label: ComputablePred.computable_iff_re_compl_re
slogan: A predicate is computable if and only if both the set of elements satisfying it and the set of elements not satisfying it are recursively enumerable, meaning there are computational procedures that can list out the elements in each set. This requires the type to have a simple encoding into natural numbers. The predicate must also be decidable, so that for any input, it can be determined whether it satisfies the predicate or not.

label: ComputablePred.halting_problem
slogan: There is no algorithm that can correctly determine, for every possible program and input, whether the program will eventually stop running or continue forever. This applies even when programs are represented as natural numbers and their behavior is defined by basic computable rules. Some problems are fundamentally unsolvable by any computational process.

label: Con
slogan: Con M is a structure that defines an equivalence relation on a type M with multiplication, where the relation is compatible with the multiplication operation: if a is related to b and c is related to d, then a * c is related to b * d. It combines an equivalence relation (from Setoid) and a multiplication operation (from Mul) so that algebraic structure is preserved under equivalence.

label: Con.quotientKerEquivRange
slogan: For any monoid homomorphism f, the quotient of the domain by the kernel congruence is isomorphic to the image of f, meaning the set of equivalence classes forms a monoid that matches the structure of the elements f actually reaches.

label: ConcaveOn.le_map_integral
slogan: If a function g is concave and continuous on a closed convex set s, and f is a function that maps almost all points into s with respect to a probability measure, then the average value of g(f(x)) is less than or equal to g applied to the average value of f(x), provided both f and g∘f are integrable.

label: ConditionallyCompleteLattice
slogan: A conditionally complete lattice is an ordered set where every nonempty subset that has an upper bound has a least upper bound, and every nonempty subset with a lower bound has a greatest lower bound. This means suprema and infima exist for bounded subsets, extending the idea of lattices beyond just pairs of elements. It provides a framework for completeness in order theory without requiring all subsets to have bounds.

label: ConditionallyCompleteLinearOrder
slogan: A ConditionallyCompleteLinearOrder is a type with a total order where every nonempty set that has an upper bound has a least upper bound, and every nonempty set that has a lower bound has a greatest lower bound. It ensures that bounded sets have well-defined suprema and infima, combining total order with conditional completeness. This supports rigorous reasoning about ordered types like the real numbers.

label: ConditionallyCompleteLinearOrderedField
slogan: A ConditionallyCompleteLinearOrderedField is a type where you can add, subtract, multiply, and divide (except by zero), with a total order such that every nonempty set that has an upper bound has a least upper bound, and multiplying by a positive number preserves strict inequalities. It includes the properties that zero is less than one and addition preserves order, making it a complete, ordered number system. This structure fully captures the essential properties of the real numbers.

label: ConditionallyCompleteLinearOrderedField.to_archimedean
slogan: Any ordered field where every bounded set has a least upper bound and a greatest lower bound must satisfy the Archimedean property, meaning no positive element is infinitely larger than another, since adding any positive element to itself enough times will eventually exceed any other given positive element.

label: Configuration.HasLines
slogan: A configuration has lines if there is a membership relation between points and lines, the configuration is nondegenerate, and every pair of points has at least one line passing through both.

label: Configuration.HasLines.card_le
slogan: In a finite, nondegenerate configuration where any two points determine exactly one line, the number of points is at most the number of lines.

label: Configuration.HasPoints
slogan: A configuration has points where every pair of lines intersects at exactly one point, and the setup is nondegenerate meaning no single line contains all points, no single point lies on all lines, and any two points determine at most one line. This structure ensures well-behaved geometric relations between points and lines. The types of points and lines can vary, and their membership relation is defined separately.

label: Configuration.Nondegenerate
slogan: A configuration is nondegenerate if no single line contains all points, no single point lies on all lines, any two points lie on at most one line together, and any two lines intersect in at most one point. The last two conditions are logically equivalent. The setup involves a type of points and a type of lines with a membership relation between them.

label: Configuration.ProjectivePlane
slogan: A projective plane is a geometric structure made of points and lines where every two points lie on exactly one line, every two lines meet at exactly one point, and there are three points that are not all on the same line. It combines the properties of having well-defined lines through points and well-defined intersection points for lines, with a nondegeneracy condition to avoid trivial cases. The structure is defined using a membership relation between points and lines, ensuring consistent behavior across different types of points and lines.

label: Configuration.ProjectivePlane.card_points_eq_card_lines
slogan: In a finite projective plane, the number of points is equal to the number of lines. This holds because every pair of points determines a unique line, every pair of lines meets at a unique point, and there are enough points and lines in general position to prevent degeneracy. The result follows by showing the number of points is both at most and at least the number of lines.

label: Configuration.ProjectivePlane.order
slogan: The order of a projective plane is defined as one less than the number of lines passing through any point, or equivalently, one less than the number of points lying on any line. It is a natural number that characterizes the size of the projective plane structure.

label: ConjAct
slogan: ConjAct takes a group G and returns a type representing the action of conjugation in that group, where each element g transforms another element x into g * x * g⁻¹. This structure captures how elements of a group can act on each other by conjugation. It is used to formalize the algebraic behavior of conjugation as a group action.

label: ConjAct.orbit_eq_carrier_conjClasses
slogan: The set of all elements you can get by conjugating a given element g in a group is exactly the same as the conjugacy class that contains g. This means two elements are conjugate if and only if one can be reached from the other by conjugation. The orbit of an element under the conjugation action is precisely its conjugacy class.

label: ConjClasses
slogan: ConjClasses is the type of equivalence classes of elements in a monoid where two elements are considered equivalent if one can be obtained from the other by conjugation, meaning a ~ b if there exists some g such that a = g * b * g^-1. It is constructed by taking the quotient of the monoid by the conjugacy relation, which is an equivalence relation. This groups together all elements that are conjugate to each other into a single class.

label: ConjClasses.card_carrier
slogan: In a finite group, the size of each conjugacy class equals the total number of group elements divided by the number of elements that leave a given element fixed under conjugation.

label: ConnectedComponents
slogan: ConnectedComponents is a function that, given a topological space, groups its points into sets where each set contains all points that are in the same connected component. Two points are in the same set if there is a connected subset containing both. The result is a type representing the space partitioned into its largest possible connected pieces.

label: ConnectedSpace
slogan: A connected space is a topological space where the only subsets that are both open and closed are the entire space and the empty set, meaning it cannot be split into two disjoint nonempty open parts. This captures the idea that the space is in one piece. It is equivalent to being a preconnected space.

label: ContDiff
slogan: A function is C^n if it can be differentiated up to n times (n a natural number or infinity) and all its derivatives are continuous, where the function maps between vector spaces over a field with a nontrivial norm. Differentiability here means the function is locally approximated by multilinear maps, and the derivative maps must be continuous and bounded in norm. This definition applies in settings like real or complex vector spaces with a well-behaved notion of size and distance.

label: ContDiff.dense_compl_range_of_finrank_lt_finrank
slogan: If a continuously differentiable function maps from a finite-dimensional real vector space to another such space of strictly higher dimension, then the set of points not in the function's image is dense in the target space.

label: ContDiffAt.exists_forall_mem_closedBall_exists_eq_forall_mem_Ioo_hasDerivAt
slogan: If a function f from a complete normed real vector space to itself is continuously differentiable at a point x₀, then for any starting point x near x₀, there exists a solution curve α defined on some open interval around t₀ such that α starts at x and its derivative at each point in that interval equals f applied to the value of α at that point.

label: ContDiffBump
slogan: ContDiffBump c represents a smooth function centered at point c in a normed space, equal to 1 inside a closed ball of radius rIn and zero outside an open ball of larger radius rOut, with values between 0 and 1 everywhere. The function is fully determined by the structure's fields rIn and rOut, which satisfy 0 < rIn < rOut. When the space supports it (via HasContDiffBump), the function can be used directly in expressions like f x.

label: ContDiffBump.convolution_tendsto_right_of_continuous
slogan: As a family of smooth bump functions gets concentrated near zero, their convolution with a continuous function g converges to g at each point. This means integrating g against these shrinking bump functions recovers the value of g in the limit. The bump functions are normalized so their integral is one, and the convergence holds under standard completeness and measurability conditions on the space.

label: ContFract
slogan: A regular continued fraction is a sequence starting with an integer h followed by positive integers b0, b1, b2, etc., where each term after h appears in the denominator of a fraction with numerator 1, forming an expression like h + 1/(b0 + 1/(b1 + 1/(b2 + ...))). It is a special case of a simple continued fraction where all the partial denominators are strictly greater than zero. This type is defined for any type α that has zero, one, and a less-than relation.

label: ContMDiff.contMDiff_tangentMap
slogan: If a function between smooth manifolds is n times continuously differentiable, then its derivative map (pushforward) is m times continuously differentiable provided that m+1 is at most n.

label: ContMDiffMap.algebra
slogan: Smooth maps between manifolds form an algebra over a normed field, meaning they can be added, multiplied, and scaled pointwise while preserving smoothness. Constant functions are smooth, and combinations of smooth functions using these operations remain smooth. This structure supports algebraic manipulation of smooth functions without losing differentiability.

label: ContMDiffSection.instAdd
slogan: Smooth sections of a vector bundle can be added together pointwise, and this addition operation is well-defined for sections that are n times continuously differentiable.

label: ContMDiffSection.instModule
slogan: The space of n times continuously differentiable sections of a vector bundle over a manifold forms a module over the field 𝕜, meaning you can add such sections together and multiply them by scalars from 𝕜 in a way that respects the algebraic structure of a module. This holds under the assumptions that the base space is a manifold modeled on a normed space, the bundle is a topological vector bundle with fiber F, and each fiber has a compatible 𝕜-vector space structure. The smoothness condition on sections is controlled by the parameter n, which can range up to infinity.

label: ContMDiffVectorBundle.pullback
slogan: If E is a C^n vector bundle over a manifold B and f is a C^n map from another manifold B' to B, then the pullback of E by f is also a C^n vector bundle over B'.

label: ContextFreeGrammar
slogan: A context-free grammar is a system that generates strings of symbols from a set of terminal symbols, using rules that replace single nonterminal symbols with sequences of terminals and nonterminals. It is defined over a type of terminals and uses finite sets of such replacement rules. Each rule specifies how one nonterminal can be rewritten as a list of symbols, which can include both terminals and nonterminals.

label: ContextFreeGrammar.Derives
slogan: Given a context-free grammar g, g.Derives u v means that the string u can be turned into the string v by applying zero or more grammar rules from g in sequence, where each rule replaces a nonterminal symbol with a sequence of symbols.

label: ContextFreeGrammar.Produces
slogan: For a context-free grammar g, g.Produces u v means that the string u can be transformed into the string v in one step by applying a single rule from g, where u and v are lists of symbols that may include both terminals and nonterminals.

label: ContextFreeGrammar.language
slogan: The language of a context-free grammar is the set of all strings made from terminal symbols that the grammar can generate by applying its production rules starting from the initial nonterminal. Each string in the language consists only of terminal symbols, and the grammar generates it through a sequence of rule applications. This set of strings is formally defined as the collection of all such terminal-only sequences that the grammar can produce.

label: ContextFreeRule
slogan: A context-free rule describes how a single nonterminal symbol can be replaced by a string of symbols, where the string is represented as a list. It takes a type of terminal symbols T and a type of nonterminal symbols N, and defines a transformation from one nonterminal to a list of terminals and nonterminals. The rule is part of a system used to define context-free grammars in formal language theory.

label: Continuous
slogan: A function between two topological spaces is continuous if the preimage of every open set in the target space is an open set in the source space. This means small changes in the input lead to small changes in the output, as defined by the topologies on the spaces. The function f is continuous when this condition holds for all open sets in the codomain.

label: Continuous.comp
slogan: If two functions are continuous, then the function you get by applying one after the other is also continuous. This means that whenever the final output set is open, the set of all inputs that lead to it through both functions is also open.

label: Continuous.ext_on
slogan: If two continuous functions from a space to a Hausdorff space agree on a dense subset, then they are equal everywhere. This is because the Hausdorff condition ensures limits are unique, and continuity forces the functions to behave consistently near limit points. Thus, the values of a continuous function on a dense set determine its values on the whole space.

label: Continuous.homeoOfEquivCompactToT2
slogan: If a function is a continuous bijection from a compact space to a Hausdorff (T2) space, then its inverse is also continuous, making the function a homeomorphism. This means the two spaces have the same topological structure. Without the T2 condition, even a continuous bijection from a compact space might not have a continuous inverse.

label: Continuous.integral_hasStrictDerivAt
slogan: If a function is continuous, then the integral from a fixed point to a variable point has a derivative at each point equal to the function's value there, meaning the rate at which the accumulated integral changes is exactly the function's height at that point.

label: Continuous.measurable
slogan: A continuous function between two topological spaces is measurable when both spaces have their Borel sigma-algebras, because the preimage of every open set is open and therefore belongs to the Borel sigma-algebra. This means that continuity guarantees the function respects the measurable structure generated by the topology.

label: Continuous.seqContinuous
slogan: A function is continuous if and only if it maps convergent sequences to convergent sequences, meaning that if a sequence of points approaches a limit, then the sequence of their images under the function approaches the image of the limit. This equivalence holds in topological spaces where the behavior of sequences fully determines the topology.

label: Continuous.tendsto
slogan: A function is continuous if, whenever you pick a point and look at a neighborhood around its image, there's a neighborhood around the original point that maps entirely into that neighborhood. This means the function preserves closeness in terms of the topology on the spaces.

label: Continuous.uniformContinuous_of_tendsto_cocompact
slogan: If a function between uniform spaces is continuous and its outputs get close to a fixed value as inputs move away from compact sets, then the function is uniformly continuous. This means that continuity together with controlled behavior at infinity ensures uniform continuity. The result depends on the topology of the spaces and the notion of convergence outside compact sets.

label: ContinuousAt
slogan: A function is continuous at a point if, for every neighborhood around the function's value at that point, there is a neighborhood around the point whose image is contained in the first neighborhood. This means the function's behavior near the input point matches the expected closeness in the output. It is defined using filters, where the preimage of neighborhoods of the output must belong to the neighborhood filter of the input point.

label: ContinuousAt.preimage_mem_nhds
slogan: If a function is continuous at a point, then the set of all inputs that map into a neighborhood of the output near that point forms a neighborhood of the input point. This means the preimage of any set close to the function's value around a point will itself be close to the input point in the domain.

label: ContinuousInv
slogan: A type has a continuous inverse if, whenever elements get close to each other in the topology, their inverses also get close, and this inverse operation plays well with open sets. This assumes the type already has a group structure and a topology where multiplication is continuous. It means the map sending each element to its inverse is a continuous function.

label: ContinuousLinearEquiv.ofBijective
slogan: If a continuous linear map between two complete normed vector spaces over nontrivially normed fields is both injective (its kernel is trivial) and surjective (its range covers the whole target space), then it has a continuous inverse and is thus a continuous linear isomorphism.

label: ContinuousLinearEquiv.ofFinrankEq
slogan: If two finite-dimensional vector spaces over a nontrivially normed field have the same dimension and their addition and scalar multiplication are continuous, then there is a continuous linear isomorphism between them whose inverse is also continuous. This map preserves both vector space operations and the topology. The result relies on the existence of a linear isomorphism and the completeness of the base field.

label: ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint
slogan: For two Hilbert spaces E and F over a real-like field, the adjoint of a bounded linear operator A from E to F is a bounded linear operator from F back to E that satisfies the inner product relation <Ax, y> = <x, A†y> for all x in E and y in F, and it has the same operator norm as A.

label: ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_adjoint
slogan: Taking the adjoint of a bounded linear operator twice gives back the original operator.

label: ContinuousLinearMap.completeSpace
slogan: If the target space is complete and the domain has a topology compatible with bounded sets, then every Cauchy net of continuous linear maps converges to a continuous linear map. This means the space of such maps is complete under the uniform structure. The result depends on the completeness of the codomain and the behavior of bounded sets in the domain.

label: ContinuousLinearMap.eq_zero_of_forall_hasEigenvalue_eq_zero
slogan: If a compact, symmetric linear operator on a complete inner product space has only zero as a possible eigenvalue, then the operator must be the zero operator.

label: ContinuousLinearMap.equivRange
slogan: If a continuous linear map between complete normed spaces is one-to-one and its image is a closed set, then the map is a homeomorphism onto its image, meaning it has a continuous inverse when restricted to its range. This result depends on the completeness of both spaces and the linearity and continuity of the map. The inverse map is also linear and continuous, making the original map an isomorphism between the domain and the range.

label: ContinuousLinearMap.exist_extension_of_finiteDimensional_range
slogan: Any continuous linear map defined on a subspace of a normed space can be extended to a continuous linear map on the whole space, provided the target space is finite-dimensional. The extension agrees with the original map on the subspace and remains linear and continuous. This means that maps into finite-dimensional spaces can always be expanded to cover the entire domain without losing their structure.

label: ContinuousLinearMap.exists_approx_preimage_norm_le
slogan: If a continuous linear map between Banach spaces is surjective, then for every element y in the target space, there is an element x in the domain such that f(x) is close to y and the size of x is at most a fixed multiple of the size of y.

label: ContinuousLinearMap.inner_map_map_of_mem_unitary
slogan: If a continuous linear map u preserves the inner product structure of a complete inner product space H over a real-like field 𝕜, meaning it maps vectors in a way that maintains their inner products, then u is unitary and satisfies inner 𝕜 (u x) (u y) = inner 𝕜 x y for all vectors x and y in H.

label: ContinuousLinearMap.isOpenMap
slogan: A continuous linear map between complete normed spaces (Banach spaces) that hits every point in the target space will send open sets in the domain to open sets in the target. This means the image of any open set under such a map is also open. The result depends on both the completeness of the spaces and the continuity of the linear map.

label: ContinuousLinearMap.isSelfAdjoint_iff_isSymmetric
slogan: A continuous linear operator on a complete inner product space over the real or complex numbers is self-adjoint if and only if it is symmetric, meaning the inner product of A applied to vector x with vector y equals the inner product of x with A applied to y for all vectors x and y.

label: ContinuousLinearMap.lpPairing
slogan: The lpPairing function takes two functions f and g from Lp and Lq spaces (with conjugate exponents p and q) and a continuous bilinear map B, then returns the integral of B(f(x), g(x)) with respect to a measure μ, resulting in a value in a normed space G. This integral defines a continuous linear map from the product of the Lp and Lq spaces into G. In a special case involving dual spaces, it gives a natural mapping from Lp of the dual into the dual of Lq.

label: ContinuousLinearMap.ofIsClosedGraph
slogan: If a linear map between two complete normed spaces has a graph that is a closed set in the product space, then the map is continuous and can be treated as a continuous linear map. This means that checking the closedness of the graph is enough to ensure the map behaves well under limits. The function uses this fact to convert a linear map with a closed graph into a continuous one.

label: ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm
slogan: The opNorm of a continuous linear map is the smallest number C such that the size of the output is always <= C times the size of the input, measuring how much the map can stretch vectors. It is defined as the infimum of all such constants C and is always a non-negative real number or infinity. This value exists for maps between normed spaces over nontrivially normed fields.

label: ContinuousLinearMap.orthogonalComplement_iSup_eigenspaces_eq_bot
slogan: For a compact self-adjoint operator on a complete inner product space, the only vector orthogonal to all eigenspaces is the zero vector.

label: ContinuousLinearMap.rayleighQuotient
slogan: The Rayleigh quotient of a continuous linear map T at a vector x is the real number obtained by taking the real part of the inner product of T(x) and x, then dividing it by the square of the norm of x. It is defined for vector spaces over the real or complex numbers equipped with an inner product and a norm. This quantity is always a real number and measures a kind of ratio between the action of the map and the size of the vector.

label: ContinuousLinearMap.spectralRadius_eq_nnnorm
slogan: For a self-adjoint continuous linear operator on a complete inner product space over the real or complex numbers, the spectral radius (the largest absolute value of its eigenvalues) is equal to the operator norm (the maximum factor by which the operator stretches vectors).

label: ContinuousLinearMap.tendsto_birkhoffAverage_orthogonalProjection
slogan: In a Hilbert space, if a continuous linear map f has norm at most 1, then the averages of the iterates of f applied to a vector x converge to the projection of x onto the subspace of vectors fixed by f. This result holds as the number of iterations goes to infinity. The convergence is with respect to the topology of the space.

label: ContinuousMap
slogan: A ContinuousMap is a function between two topological spaces such that the preimage of every open set in the target space is open in the source space, along with a proof that this continuity condition holds. It is structured as a pair of a function and the continuity evidence, enabling formal reasoning about continuous functions in topology. This setup allows for a coherent framework where continuous maps can be manipulated and composed while preserving topological structure.

label: ContinuousMap.Homotopic
slogan: Two continuous functions f0 and f1 from a space X to a space Y are called homotopic if there exists a continuous deformation from f0 to f1, meaning a continuous map from the unit interval times X to Y that starts at f0 and ends at f1. This relation captures the idea that the two functions can be smoothly transformed into each other. The existence of such a deformation is what it means for f0 and f1 to be homotopic.

label: ContinuousMap.Homotopic.comp
slogan: If two continuous functions g0 and g1 from Y to Z are homotopic, and two continuous functions f0 and f1 from X to Y are homotopic, then the composition g0(f0) is homotopic to g1(f1). This means that homotopy is preserved under composition of continuous functions.

label: ContinuousMap.Homotopic.equivalence
slogan: Being homotopic is an equivalence relation on continuous maps between topological spaces, meaning it is reflexive, symmetric, and transitive.

label: ContinuousMap.HomotopicRel
slogan: Two continuous maps f0 and f1 from a topological space X to another topological space Y are said to be homotopic relative to a subset S of X if there exists a continuous deformation from f0 to f1 that keeps all points in S fixed throughout the deformation.

label: ContinuousMap.Homotopy
slogan: A homotopy between two continuous maps f0 and f1 is a continuous function that deforms f0 into f1 over time, represented as a map from the product of the unit interval and the space X to Y. The type Homotopy f0 f1 collects all such deformations. It is recommended to work with types that behave like homotopies (via HomotopyLike) rather than directly with this type.

label: ContinuousMap.Homotopy.affine
slogan: Given two continuous functions f and g from a space X to a topological real vector space E, the affine homotopy between them is defined pointwise as a straight-line path from f(x) to g(x), where at time t it equals (1-t)*f(x) + t*g(x). This homotopy continuously deforms f into g over the unit interval. The construction ensures the resulting map is continuous in both time and space.

label: ContinuousMap.Homotopy.curry
slogan: Given a continuous deformation (homotopy) between two continuous functions from X to Y, this function produces a continuous path in the space of continuous functions from X to Y, where each point along the path corresponds to an intermediate function in the deformation. The path is parameterized by the unit interval [0,1]. This transformation is known as currying the homotopy.

label: ContinuousMap.HomotopyEquiv
slogan: A homotopy equivalence between two topological spaces X and Y consists of continuous maps from X to Y and from Y to X, such that composing them in either direction results in a map that can be continuously deformed back to the identity map on the respective space.

label: ContinuousMap.HomotopyEquiv.simplyConnectedSpace
slogan: If two topological spaces are homotopy equivalent and one is simply connected, then the other is also simply connected. This means that being simply connected is preserved under homotopy equivalence. A space is simply connected if its fundamental groupoid is equivalent to a discrete category with a single object.

label: ContinuousMap.HomotopyEquiv.simplyConnectedSpace_iff
slogan: If two topological spaces are homotopy equivalent, then one is simply connected if and only if the other is simply connected. This means that simple connectedness is preserved under homotopy equivalence.

label: ContinuousMap.Nullhomotopic
slogan: A continuous function between two topological spaces is nullhomotopic if it can be continuously deformed into a constant function, meaning there exists a homotopy connecting it to a map that sends all points to a single point in the target space.

label: ContinuousMap.compactOpen
slogan: The compact-open topology is a way to define open sets of continuous functions between two topological spaces, where a subbasis consists of functions that map a compact set in the domain into an open set in the codomain. It uses the existing topologies on the spaces and the structure of continuous functions to form a new topological space on the set of all such functions. This topology is useful for studying how continuous functions behave with respect to compactness and convergence.

label: ContinuousMap.continuousMap_mem_subalgebra_closure_of_separatesPoints
slogan: If a subalgebra A of real-valued continuous functions on a compact space X separates points, then every real-valued continuous function on X can be uniformly approximated by functions in A.

label: ContinuousMap.exists_restrict_eq
slogan: If X is a normal topological space, s is a closed subset of X, and f is a continuous function from s to a space Y that has the Tietze extension property, then there exists a continuous function g from all of X to Y that agrees with f on s.

label: ContinuousMap.instCommCStarAlgebra
slogan: If alpha is a compact topological space and A is a commutative C*-algebra, then the space of continuous functions from alpha to A, equipped with pointwise operations and the supremum norm, forms a commutative C*-algebra. This means the functions have a norm, a conjugation operation, and satisfy the C*-identity: the norm of f* times f equals the square of the norm of f. The algebra is complete, commutative, and compatible with complex scalars.

label: ContinuousMap.instNormedAlgebra
slogan: The space of continuous functions from a compact topological space to a normed algebra over a normed field forms a normed algebra, where functions are added, multiplied, and scaled pointwise, and the norm of a function is the maximum of the norms of its values. Compactness ensures this maximum is always finite, and the operations preserve continuity and norm bounds. This structure supports both algebraic manipulation and metric analysis of continuous functions.

label: ContinuousMap.instSeparableSpace
slogan: If X and Y are second-countable topological spaces and X is locally compact, then the space of continuous functions from X to Y, equipped with the compact-open topology, is separable, meaning it contains a countable dense subset. This follows from the fact that the function space is second-countable under these conditions, and second-countable spaces are always separable.

label: ContinuousMap.starSubalgebra_topologicalClosure_eq_top_of_separatesPoints
slogan: If a subset A of continuous functions on a compact space X with values in a real-like field 𝕜 is closed under addition, multiplication, scalar multiplication, and complex conjugation, contains constants, and can distinguish points of X, then every continuous function on X can be uniformly approximated by functions in A.

label: ContinuousMap.subalgebra_topologicalClosure_eq_top_of_separatesPoints
slogan: If a set of continuous real-valued functions on a compact space contains all constant functions, is closed under addition, multiplication, and scalar multiplication, and can distinguish between any two points (meaning for any two points there's a function that takes different values at them), then any continuous function on that space can be uniformly approximated by functions in the set.

label: ContinuousMap.sublattice_closure_eq_top
slogan: If a nonempty set of real-valued continuous functions on a compact topological space is closed under taking pointwise minima and maxima, and separates points strongly, then its uniform closure consists of all continuous real-valued functions on that space.

label: ContinuousMap.tendsto_of_monotone_of_pointwise
slogan: If a sequence of continuous functions increases pointwise to a continuous limit function, then the sequence converges to that limit uniformly on compact sets.

label: ContinuousMap.toLp_denseRange
slogan: On a compact space with finite measure, any function in the Lp space (where 1 ≤ p < ∞) can be approximated arbitrarily closely by continuous functions. This means the set of continuous functions is dense in the Lp space under the Lp norm. The result applies to functions taking values in a normed vector space over the real numbers.

label: ContinuousOn
slogan: A function is continuous on a subset if, at every point in that subset, the function values stay close to the value at the point whenever the inputs are close, with closeness defined by the topology of the space. This means that for each point in the subset, small changes in the input lead to small changes in the output, considering only inputs from the subset. The condition is defined using neighborhood systems from the topological structure of the domain and codomain.

label: ContinuousOn.intervalIntegrable
slogan: If a function is continuous on the closed interval between two real numbers a and b, then it is integrable over that interval with respect to any locally finite measure. This means the function has a well-defined integral from a to b, regardless of their order, as long as the function behaves continuously on the interval. The result holds for functions taking values in a normed vector space.

label: ContinuousOn.isSeparable_image
slogan: If a function is continuous on a separable subset of a space, then the set of values it takes on that subset is also separable. This means that continuous functions preserve separability when applied to separable sets. A separable set has a countable dense subset, and this property carries over to the image under the function.

label: ContinuousWithinAt
slogan: A function is continuous at a point within a subset if, for every neighborhood around the function's value, there is a neighborhood around the point (intersected with the subset) such that the function maps all points in that neighborhood into the target neighborhood. This is defined using filters, where continuity means the function's behavior respects the neighborhood structure when restricted to the subset. It depends on the topology of the spaces and uses the concept of one filter tending to another.

label: ContractibleSpace
slogan: A contractible space is a topological space that can be continuously deformed to a single point, meaning it is homotopy equivalent to the one-point space Unit. This means there exists a continuous map from the space to Unit and another from Unit back, such that their compositions are homotopic to the identity maps. Such a space has no nontrivial topological holes.

label: ContractingWith
slogan: A function is contracting with constant K if K is a non-negative real number less than 1 and the distance between the images of any two points is at most K times the distance between the points. This means the function shrinks distances by a fixed ratio smaller than 1. The definition relies on standard properties of non-negative real numbers, including the existence of 1 and the usual ordering.

label: ContractingWith.apriori_dist_iterate_fixedPoint_le
slogan: If a function shrinks distances by a constant factor less than 1, then every iterate of the function stays within a fixed distance of the final limit point, and that distance is at most the initial step size divided by (1 minus the contraction factor), scaled by the contraction factor raised to the iteration count.

label: ContractingWith.exists_fixedPoint
slogan: If a function shrinks distances between points by a factor less than one, then repeatedly applying the function to any starting point leads to a sequence that converges to a unique fixed point—a point that maps to itself. The distance from each iterate to the fixed point decreases at a rate bounded by a geometric sequence. This holds in complete spaces where all such contracting sequences have a limit.

label: ContractingWith.fixedPoint
slogan: If a function shrinks distances between points by a fixed ratio less than 1 in a nonempty space where all distances are well-defined and all Cauchy sequences converge, then repeatedly applying the function from any starting point will converge to a single unique point that the function maps to itself. This limit point is the only one unchanged by the function, and its existence is guaranteed by the space being complete and the function being a contraction. The rate of convergence is controlled by the contraction factor, a constant between 0 and 1.

label: ContractingWith.fixedPoint_isFixedPt
slogan: If a function shrinks distances by a fixed ratio less than 1 in a complete metric space that has at least one point, then repeatedly applying the function leads to a unique point that the function maps to itself. This limit point does not change when the function is applied, meaning it is a fixed point. The existence and uniqueness of this point are guaranteed by the contraction property and completeness of the space.

label: ContractingWith.isFixedPt_fixedPoint_iterate
slogan: If a function, when applied repeatedly, shrinks distances by a fixed factor less than 1, then iterating it many times from any starting point will converge to a single unique point that maps to itself, and this point remains unchanged when the function is applied.

label: ContractingWith.tendsto_iterate_fixedPoint
slogan: If a function shrinks distances between points by a fixed ratio less than 1 in a complete metric space, then starting from any point and repeatedly applying the function will produce a sequence that gets arbitrarily close to one unique fixed point of the function.

label: Convex
slogan: A set is convex if, whenever two points are in the set, every point of the form a*x + b*y (where a and b are non-negative numbers adding up to 1) is also in the set, assuming the operations are defined in a space with a semiring structure and scalar multiplication. This means the entire line segment between any two points in the set must lie within the set. The definition generalizes the idea of convexity to algebraic structures with a partial order and compatible addition and scalar multiplication.

label: Convex.add
slogan: If two sets are convex, then the set formed by adding every element of one set to every element of the other is also convex. This holds in any algebraic structure where addition is commutative and associative, there is a zero element, and scalar multiplication behaves nicely with respect to order and addition. The result follows because the line segment between any two points in the sumset can be expressed as a sum of line segments from the original convex sets.

label: Convex.add_smul
slogan: If a set is convex, then for any two points in the set, any point you get by moving partway from one point to the other (using a weighted step that's between 0 and 1 of the total distance) will also be in the set. This works in any space where points can be scaled and added using numbers from an ordered field. The result is consistent with the algebraic structure of vector spaces or modules.

label: Convex.affine_image
slogan: If a set is convex, meaning the line segment between any two points in the set stays entirely within the set, then applying an affine transformation (a linear map plus a translation) to that set results in another convex set.

label: Convex.closure_interior_eq_closure_of_nonempty_interior
slogan: If a convex set has at least one interior point, then the closure of its interior equals the closure of the whole set. This means that the set's interior points are dense in its closure, so taking limit points of just the inside gives the same result as taking limit points of the entire set.

label: Convex.contractibleSpace
slogan: Any non-empty convex set in a real topological vector space can be continuously shrunk to a single point, meaning it has no holes and is topologically simple.

label: Convex.interior
slogan: If a set is convex in a topological vector space where addition and scalar multiplication are continuous, then the interior of that set is also convex; this means any point strictly between two interior points stays inside the interior.

label: Convex.isConnected
slogan: Any nonempty convex set in a real topological vector space is connected, meaning it cannot be separated into two disjoint nonempty open parts. This is because any two points in the set can be joined by a straight line segment lying entirely within the set, making the set path connected, and hence connected. The result relies on the continuity of vector addition and scalar multiplication in the space.

label: Convex.isPathConnected
slogan: Any nonempty convex set in a real vector space with continuous addition and scalar multiplication is path connected, meaning you can draw a continuous line between any two points in the set without leaving the set. This works because the straight-line path between any two points stays within the set, thanks to convexity, and the topology ensures continuity. The space must support addition, negation, scalar multiplication, and have a well-behaved topology for this to hold.

label: Convex.lipschitzOnWith_of_nnnorm_fderiv_le
slogan: If a function is differentiable on a convex set and the norm of its derivative is at most L at every point in that set, then the function is L-Lipschitz on the set, meaning the distance between outputs is at most L times the distance between inputs.

label: Convex.norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_fderiv_le
slogan: If a function is differentiable on a convex set and the size of its derivative is bounded by a constant C at every point in the set, then the distance between the function values at any two points is at most C times the distance between those points. This means the function's change is controlled by the bound on its derivative. The result works in real or complex normed vector spaces.

label: Convex.openSegment_interior_closure_subset_interior
slogan: If a set is convex, then any point strictly between a point inside the set and a point in the closure of the set must also be inside the set.

label: Convex.radon_partition
slogan: Any set of points that are affinely dependent has a partition into two subsets such that their convex hulls share at least one common point. In simpler terms, if you have more points than the dimension of the space plus one, you can always split them into two groups whose convex spans overlap. This is known as Radon's theorem.

label: Convex.starConvex
slogan: A set is star-convex if there is a base point in the set such that, for every other point in the set, all points on the line segment from the base point to that point (formed by scaling between 0 and 1) are also in the set. This relies on scalar multiplication over a semiring and an additive commutative monoid structure. The result states that if a set is convex and contains a point, then it is star-convex with respect to that point.

label: Convex.sum_mem
slogan: If you have a finite set of points in a convex set, and you assign each point a nonnegative weight such that the weights add up to 1, then the weighted sum of those points is also inside the convex set. This means averaging points in a convex set using such weights keeps the result within the set.

label: Convex.toWeakSpace_closure
slogan: If a set in a locally convex space is convex, then its closure is the same as its weak closure, meaning the set's topological closure doesn't change when switching to the weak topology via the natural map to the weak space.

label: ConvexCone
slogan: A convex cone is a set that is closed under addition and multiplication by non-negative scalars, meaning adding any two elements in the set gives another element in the set, and multiplying any element by a non-negative number (from a semiring with a partial order) also stays in the set. It requires the underlying space to be an additive commutative monoid and supports a scalar multiplication action from a semiring that respects algebraic and order properties. This structure captures the idea of a cone that is preserved under linear combinations with non-negative coefficients.

label: ConvexOn
slogan: A function is convex on a set if, for any two points in that set, the value of the function at any weighted average of the points is less than or equal to the same weighted average of the function values at those points. This means the line segment between any two points on the graph of the function lies above or on the graph. The definition requires the function's domain and codomain to support scalar multiplication, addition, and a partial order, with scalars forming a semiring.

label: ConvexOn.convex_le
slogan: If a function is convex on a set, then the set of points where the function's value is less than or equal to a given bound is itself a convex set. This means that for any two points where the function stays below the bound, every weighted average of those points (with weights between 0 and 1) also lies in the set and satisfies the same bound. The result holds in a general algebraic setting with scalar multiplication and a compatible order.

label: ConvexOn.map_condExp_le
slogan: If a function φ is convex and lower semicontinuous on a closed set s in a Banach space, and f is a measurable function that takes values in s almost everywhere, then the value of φ at the conditional expectation of f is less than or equal to the conditional expectation of φ composed with f, almost everywhere with respect to the measure μ. This holds when the underlying measure is σ-finite on the sub-σ-algebra and both f and φ∘f are integrable.

label: ConvexOn.map_integral_le
slogan: If g is a convex and continuous function on a closed set s, and f is a function that maps almost all points into s with respect to a probability measure, then the value of g at the integral (expected value) of f is less than or equal to the integral of g composed with f, provided both f and g∘f are integrable.

label: Coplanar
slogan: A set of points is coplanar if the vectors formed by taking differences between those points span a space of dimension 2 or less. This means all the points lie in a single flat plane that can be described using only two independent directions. The definition works over any division ring and uses the vector space structure associated with an affine space.

label: Countable
slogan: A type is countable if all its elements can be listed in a sequence, such that each element is assigned a unique natural number. This means the type is either finite or can be matched one-to-one with the natural numbers. The declaration defines a property in the Lean library to identify such types.

label: CovariantDerivative
slogan: A covariant derivative is a mathematical object that defines how to differentiate sections of a vector bundle in the direction of vector fields, where the bundle has a compatible topological and algebraic structure over a manifold. The definition assumes a nonstandard argument order: the derivative of a section σ in the direction of a vector field X at a point x is written as cov σ x (X x), corresponding to ∇_X σ (x) in standard notation. It requires the base space, fiber, and total space to support continuity, addition, scalar multiplication, and local triviality as in a fiber bundle.

label: CovariantDerivative.difference
slogan: The difference between two covariant derivatives is a linear map that, at each point on a manifold, takes a tangent vector and a section of a vector bundle and returns the difference in how the two derivatives act on that section. This difference behaves like a one-form with values in linear transformations of the vector bundle. It captures how much the two derivatives disagree when differentiating sections in the direction of tangent vectors.

label: CovariantDerivative.torsion
slogan: The torsion tensor measures how much a covariant derivative on a manifold's tangent bundle fails to be symmetric in its inputs, by taking two tangent vectors and producing a third that represents the difference between their covariant derivatives in opposite orders. It is defined at each point of the manifold and operates linearly on tangent vectors from the same point. The construction assumes the manifold is finite-dimensional, complete, and modeled on a normed space over a nontrivially normed field.

label: CovariantDerivative.torsion_eq_zero_iff
slogan: A covariant derivative has zero torsion if and only if the difference between the covariant derivative of two vector fields in each direction equals their Lie bracket. This means the torsion vanishes exactly when the covariant derivative satisfies a symmetry condition with respect to the Lie bracket of vector fields. The result holds for sufficiently smooth manifolds and vector fields over complete normed fields.

label: CoxeterMatrix
slogan: A Coxeter matrix is a symmetric matrix with natural number entries where all diagonal elements are 1 and all off-diagonal elements are not 1. It is defined over a type B, representing the indexing set of the matrix. The structure captures the combinatorial data used to define Coxeter groups.

label: CoxeterMatrix.A
slogan: The Coxeter matrix A(n) is a symmetric matrix indexed by pairs of natural numbers less than n, where the diagonal entries are 1, and the off-diagonal entries are 3 if the indices are consecutive, and 2 otherwise. It represents the Coxeter-Dynkin diagram of type A_n, which is a linear chain of n nodes connected by edges labeled 3. This matrix encodes the relations of a Coxeter group of type A_n.

label: CoxeterMatrix.Group
slogan: The Coxeter group of a Coxeter matrix M is the group generated by elements s_i for each index i, with relations stating that the product of any two generators s_i and s_j raised to the power M_i,j equals the identity. These relations are imposed on the free group generated by the s_i, forming a quotient group where the Coxeter matrix dictates the orders of the products of generator pairs. If M_i,j is zero, no relation is imposed between s_i and s_j.

label: CoxeterSystem
slogan: A Coxeter system consists of a group W and a Coxeter matrix M such that W is isomorphic to the Coxeter group defined by M. The Coxeter matrix is a symmetric matrix of natural numbers with 1s on the diagonal and values not equal to 1 elsewhere. This structure captures the relationship between a group and its presentation via reflections and relations encoded in the matrix.

label: CoxeterSystem.IsReduced
slogan: A word ω in a Coxeter system is reduced if it has the shortest possible length among all words that represent the same group element. This means the number of generators in ω equals the minimal number needed to express that element. The property depends on the group, the Coxeter matrix, and the specific list of generators.

label: CoxeterSystem.length
slogan: The length of an element w in a Coxeter group is the smallest number of simple reflections whose product equals w. This is defined for groups that are part of a Coxeter system, where the group structure and reflection relations are encoded in a Coxeter matrix. The length function returns a natural number representing this minimal count.

label: CoxeterSystem.simple_mul_simple_self
slogan: In a Coxeter system, each simple generator multiplied by itself equals the identity element of the group.

label: Cube.boundary
slogan: The boundary of an N-dimensional cube consists of all points where at least one coordinate is either 0 or 1. It is defined as the set of functions from N to the unit interval [0,1] such that at least one function value is exactly 0 or 1.

label: Cubic
slogan: The Cubic structure represents a cubic polynomial over a ring R, storing its coefficients and an associated discriminant value. The discriminant provides information about the roots of the polynomial, such as whether they are distinct or repeated. This structure supports algebraic analysis of cubic equations within a formal proof system.

label: Cubic.discr
slogan: The discriminant of a cubic polynomial is calculated from its coefficients using basic arithmetic operations in any ring. It helps determine whether the polynomial has repeated roots. The cubic must have a leading coefficient associated with a natural number at least two, ensuring the polynomial is of valid degree.

label: Cubic.discr_ne_zero_iff_roots_nodup
slogan: A cubic polynomial has a nonzero discriminant exactly when all three of its roots are different, with no repeated values, provided the polynomial breaks down completely into linear factors over the given field.

label: CuspFormClass.qExpansion_isBigO
slogan: If f is a weight k modular form for an arithmetic subgroup, then the coefficients of its q-expansion grow no faster than a constant multiple of n^(k/2) as n gets large.

label: CyclotomicField
slogan: CyclotomicField n K means K is a field that contains all the nth roots of unity and is generated by adding a primitive nth root of unity to the base field. It is the smallest field where the nth cyclotomic polynomial splits into linear factors. This makes K a splitting field for the nth cyclotomic polynomial over the base field.

label: DFA
slogan: A DFA consists of a set of states, a transition function based on input symbols, a starting state, and a set of accepting states. It models a deterministic finite automaton used in computation theory. The types for input symbols and states can vary, and the DFA type depends on these.

label: DFA.accepts
slogan: M.accepts is the set of all strings that, when processed by the DFA M starting from its initial state, end in one of the accept states. It defines the language recognized by the automaton.

label: DFA.pumping_lemma
slogan: If a string is accepted by a deterministic finite automaton and is at least as long as the number of states in the automaton, then the string can be split into three parts such that the middle part can be repeated any number of times and the resulting string will still be accepted.

label: DFA.toNFA
slogan: M.toNFA converts a deterministic finite automaton (DFA) into a nondeterministic finite automaton (NFA) by keeping the same start and accept states, and defining the NFA's transition function to produce a set containing just the single next state that the DFA would transition to.

label: DFA.toNFA_correct
slogan: Converting a deterministic finite automaton (DFA) into a nondeterministic finite automaton (NFA) using the standard method results in an NFA that accepts exactly the same language as the original DFA. This means that for any input string, the NFA will accept it if and only if the DFA would have accepted it. The conversion preserves the behavior of the automaton despite changing its structure.

label: Delone.DeloneSet
slogan: A Delone set is a subset of a metric space that has a minimum distance between points (uniform discreteness) and where every point in the space is within a bounded distance of the set (relative denseness). It is defined by specifying these two radii explicitly. The structure is built on a type equipped with a metric space structure.

label: DenselyOrdered
slogan: A type has a dense order when, given any two elements where one is less than the other, there is always a third element in between them. This requires the type to support a less-than relation and logical "and" statements. For example, if a < b, then there must exist some c such that a < c and c < b.

label: Denumerable.int
slogan: The integers can be listed in a sequence that matches each one to a unique natural number, proving they are countably infinite. This is done by using a known one-to-one pairing between integers and natural numbers. As a result, the type of integers is considered denumerable, meaning it supports a computable and complete enumeration.

label: Derivation
slogan: A derivation is a function that acts like a derivative on algebraic structures, satisfying the product rule (the value on a product is the first part times the derivative of the second plus the second times the derivative of the first) and being linear with respect to addition and scalar multiplication. It is defined between modules over a commutative semiring, where the domain is an algebra over the semiring and the codomain is a module over both the semiring and the algebra. The function must preserve zero and interact correctly with scalars from the semiring.

label: Derivation.instLieAlgebra
slogan: The set of derivations from a commutative algebra to itself forms a Lie algebra over the base ring, where the Lie bracket is given by the commutator of derivations: [D1, D2] = D1 after D2 minus D2 after D1. This bracket operation is bilinear, alternating, and satisfies the Jacobi identity, making the space of derivations a Lie algebra.

label: Derivation.map_algebraMap
slogan: A derivation sends elements of the base ring R, when embedded into the algebra A via the algebra map, to zero. This means that any element coming directly from R is treated as a constant by the derivation.

label: DerivedCategory
slogan: The derived category of an abelian category is a mathematical construction where chain complexes are treated as objects, and maps between them that induce isomorphisms on homology (quasi-isomorphisms) are formally inverted, making those complexes equivalent. It is built by localizing the category of chain complexes so that quasi-isomorphisms become isomorphisms in the new category. This allows homological algebra to be done in a setting where complexes with the same homology are identified.

label: DiffContOnCl.circleAverage
slogan: If a function from the complex numbers to a complete normed space is complex differentiable everywhere inside and on a closed disc of radius R centered at c, then the average value of the function on the circle of radius R around c equals the value of the function at the center c. This average is computed by integrating the function along the circle and dividing by the circumference. The result holds for functions that are continuously differentiable on the closed disc.

label: DiffContOnCl.circleIntegral_eq_zero
slogan: If a function is continuously differentiable on a closed disk in the complex plane, then its contour integral around the boundary of that disk is zero. The integral is taken counterclockwise around the circle centered at a point with a given radius, and the result holds because the function's smoothness ensures no net circulation.

label: Diffeomorph.toHomeomorph
slogan: A diffeomorphism between two smooth manifolds is also a homeomorphism, meaning it is a continuous bijection with a continuous inverse that preserves the topological structure.

label: Diffeomorph.trans
slogan: The composition of two smooth invertible maps (diffeomorphisms) between manifolds, each preserving the smooth structure up to order n, results in another smooth invertible map between the first and last manifold that also preserves the smooth structure up to order n.

label: Differentiable
slogan: A function is differentiable if, at every point in its domain, it can be closely approximated by a linear map in a space that supports addition, scalar multiplication, and a notion of closeness, over a field with a nontrivial norm. The required structures include a topology, an additive group, and a module structure on both the domain and codomain. The derivative, if it exists, is unique.

label: Differentiable.apply_eq_apply_of_bounded
slogan: If a function between complex normed spaces is differentiable everywhere and its outputs don't grow without bound, then the function must be constant, meaning it gives the same value for any two inputs.

label: Differentiable.continuous
slogan: If a function has a derivative, then it is continuous, meaning it has no jumps or breaks in its graph. This holds in spaces where addition, scalar multiplication, and a notion of distance are well-defined. Differentiability ensures smoothness at every point in the function's domain.

label: Differentiable.exists_const_forall_eq_of_bounded
slogan: If a function between complex normed spaces is differentiable everywhere and its outputs are bounded, then the function must be constant. This means there is some fixed value c such that the function takes the value c at every point in its domain. The result is a generalization of Liouville's theorem to functions on complex normed spaces.

label: Differentiable.exists_eq_const_of_bounded
slogan: If a function between complex normed spaces is differentiable everywhere and its outputs are bounded, then the function must be constant. This means there is some fixed value that the function returns no matter what input it receives.

label: DifferentiableAt
slogan: A function is differentiable at a point if it can be closely approximated by a continuous linear map near that point, with the error becoming very small compared to the distance from the point. This requires the function to map between vector spaces over a field with a nontrivial norm, where both spaces have a topology and a compatible additive and scalar multiplication structure. The linear approximation, if it exists, is unique.

label: DifferentiableAt.conformalAt
slogan: If a function from the complex plane to a complex normed space is complex differentiable at a point and its derivative there is nonzero, then the function preserves angles at that point, meaning it is conformal. This happens because the derivative acts as a nonzero scalar multiple of a rotation and scaling. The result connects complex differentiability with geometric angle preservation.

label: DifferentiableAt.continuousAt
slogan: If a function has a well-defined linear approximation at a point, then it must also be continuous at that point, meaning there are no jumps or breaks there. This holds in the context of normed vector spaces over a nontrivially normed field. The result follows from the fact that having a Fréchet derivative implies continuity.

label: DifferentiableOn
slogan: A function is differentiable on a set if, at every point in that set, it can be closely approximated by a linear map when restricted to that set. This requires the function to map between spaces that support addition, scalar multiplication, and a notion of distance, with the domain being a nontrivially normed field. The definition generalizes ordinary differentiability to functions defined on arbitrary subsets, not just open ones.

label: DifferentiableOn.analyticAt
slogan: If a function is complex differentiable on a set that includes a closed ball around a point, then the function can be expressed as a convergent power series near that point. This means the function is analytic at the point, with its values determined by a power series expansion in some neighborhood of the point.

label: DifferentiableOn.analyticOnNhd
slogan: If a function is complex differentiable on an open set, then near every point in that set, the function can be written as a convergent power series in some small region around that point, so it is locally analytic.

label: DifferentiableOn.circleIntegral_sub_inv_smul
slogan: If a function is differentiable on a closed disk in the complex plane, then the contour integral of the function divided by (z - w) around the boundary of the disk equals 2 * pi * i times the value of the function at the point w, provided w is inside the disk.

label: DifferentiableOn.contDiffOn
slogan: If a function is complex differentiable on an open set in the complex plane, then it is infinitely differentiable there, and all its derivatives are continuous, provided the target space is complete. This is because complex differentiability on an open set implies the function is analytic, and analytic functions are smooth. The result relies on the completeness of the space where the function takes values.

label: Differential
slogan: A Differential is a commutative ring equipped with a derivation, which is a function that satisfies the product rule: the derivative of a product is the first part times the derivative of the second plus the second part times the derivative of the first. This structure extends the ring with a way to differentiate elements while respecting addition and multiplication. The derivation also behaves linearly with respect to addition and scalar multiplication.

label: DifferentialAlgebra
slogan: A DifferentialAlgebra is a setup where one commutative ring acts on another in a way that supports both algebraic operations and differentiation, with a derivation defined on the second ring that respects multiplication (via the Leibniz rule) and is compatible with the scalar action from the first ring. The derivation must also commute with the natural map embedding the base ring into the algebra. This structure allows for a unified treatment of algebra and differentiation in a ring-theoretic setting.

label: Digraph
slogan: A digraph is a set of vertices with a relation that defines directed edges between them, where each edge goes from one vertex to another and self-loops are allowed. It is represented by a type of vertices and an adjacency relation on that type.

label: Digraph.completeDigraph
slogan: The complete digraph on a type V is a directed graph where every vertex is connected to every other vertex, including itself. In this graph, the adjacency relation holds for all pairs of vertices. It is represented as the top element in the lattice of digraphs on V.

label: DihedralGroup
slogan: DihedralGroup n is a type representing the symmetries of a regular n-sided polygon when n is not zero, including rotations and reflections; for n = 0, it represents the infinite dihedral group. Rotations are given by r i, which rotates by 2πi/n, and reflections by sr i. This group captures all ways to flip or rotate the polygon so it looks the same.

label: DihedralGroup.card_conjClasses_odd
slogan: When n is an odd natural number, the number of conjugacy classes in the dihedral group of order 2n is (n + 3) divided by 2.

label: Dioph
slogan: A set S of tuples of natural numbers is Diophantine if there is an integer polynomial p in more variables such that a tuple v is in S exactly when some extra natural number variables t can make p(v, t) equal to zero. The polynomial takes inputs split between the original tuple and the added variables. The notation uses direct sum types to combine the variable indices.

label: DirectedOn.convex_sUnion
slogan: If a collection of sets is directed by inclusion and each set in the collection is convex, then their union is also convex. This means that whenever two points lie in the union, the entire line segment between them is contained in the union. The result holds for sets in a module over a semiring with a partial order on the scalars.

label: DirichletCharacter
slogan: DirichletCharacter R n represents functions from the integers modulo n to a commutative monoid with zero R, preserving multiplicative structure and mapping zero to zero. These functions are defined only on integers coprime to n and extend to a multiplicative map on ZMod n. They are used in number theory to study arithmetic properties in modular systems.

label: DirichletCharacter.IsPrimitive
slogan: A Dirichlet character is called primitive if its level is the same as its conductor, meaning it cannot be expressed in terms of a character of smaller level. The conductor is the smallest level through which the character factors.

label: DirichletCharacter.IsPrimitive.completedLFunction_one_sub
slogan: For a primitive Dirichlet character χ of level N, the completed L-function satisfies a symmetry: the value at 1 - s equals N raised to the power (s - 1/2), multiplied by the root number of χ, and the completed L-function of the inverse character at s.

label: DirichletCharacter.LFunction
slogan: For a Dirichlet character χ modulo N, the L-function is a complex function that matches the sum of χ(n)/n^s over natural numbers n where this sum converges, and is extended to other points in the complex plane using analytic continuation via Hurwitz zeta functions. It is defined for all complex numbers s, unlike the related LSeries which is set to zero when the real part of s is less than or equal to 1.

label: DirichletCharacter.LFunction_modOne_eq
slogan: The L-function associated with the only Dirichlet character modulo 1 is the same as the Riemann zeta function. This means that for this specific character, the L-function behaves exactly like the zeta function for all complex inputs.

label: DirichletCharacter.LSeriesSummable_of_one_lt_re
slogan: The L-series associated with a Dirichlet character converges absolutely for complex numbers s where the real part of s is greater than 1. This means the infinite sum formed by the character values over natural numbers, scaled by powers of s, adds up to a finite value when the real part of s exceeds 1. The convergence is guaranteed because the character's values are bounded in size by 1.

label: DiscreteTiling.Prototile
slogan: A Prototile G X represents a shape in a space X that can be moved around by the actions of a group G to form tilings, where each transformed copy is considered part of the tiling. Copies of the tile that can be turned into each other using elements of a specified symmetry group are treated as the same tile. The structure keeps track of the tile's points in X and any symmetries that leave it unchanged.

label: DiscreteTopology
slogan: A discrete topology is a type of topological space where every subset is open, so each point is isolated. This means there are no limit points, and every function from such a space is automatically continuous. It is defined as a property of a topological space, requiring that all subsets satisfy the openness condition.

label: Dist
slogan: Dist is a class that provides a way to measure the distance between any two elements of a type, returning a non-negative real number. It sets up the foundation for defining metric-like structures where distance and related concepts such as closeness or convergence can be studied.

label: DistribLattice
slogan: A distributive lattice is a set with operations to find the least upper bound (sup) and greatest lower bound (inf) of any two elements, where sup distributes over inf in a specific inequality: for any elements a, b, and c, a sup (b inf c) is less than or equal to (a sup b) inf (a sup c). This property ensures a consistent interaction between the two operations.

label: DistribLattice.booleanAlgebraOfComplemented
slogan: If a lattice has a top and bottom element, every element has a complement, and the meet and join operations distribute over each other, then it forms a Boolean algebra where the operations behave like logical AND, OR, and NOT.

label: DistribLattice.prime_ideal_of_disjoint_filter_ideal
slogan: In a distributive lattice with a top and bottom element, if a filter and an ideal have no elements in common, then there exists a prime ideal that contains the original ideal and still has no elements in common with the filter.

label: Distribution
slogan: Distribution(Ω, F, n) is the space of continuous linear functions from smooth F-valued functions on an open set Ω to the real numbers, where continuity is defined with respect to uniform convergence on compact sets and the distribution has order at most n. For most uses, the space Distribution(Ω, F, top) is preferred, representing all F-valued distributions on Ω without restricting the order. Here, Ω is an open subset of a real normed space, F is a real topological module, and the distributions act on smooth test functions with compact support.

label: Distribution.IsVanishingOn
slogan: A function f vanishes on a set s if, whenever a test function has its tsupport (the closure of where it is nonzero) inside s, applying f to that test function gives zero. This definition works for any function from a space of functions to a type that has a zero element, not just distributions. It relies on the domain being a topological space and the notion of support being well-defined.

label: Distribution.dsupport
slogan: The distributional support of a function f is the smallest closed set such that f is zero outside of it, meaning f vanishes on the complement of this set. It is defined as the intersection of all closed sets where the function vanishes outside them. This works for any function from a space of functions to a type with a zero element.

label: DivisibleBy
slogan: DivisibleBy describes a structure where, for any element x and positive integer n, there is some element y such that adding y to itself n times gives x. It requires the type to support addition with a zero element, scalar multiplication, and a zero scalar. This captures the idea that every element can be evenly divided by any positive integer.

label: DivisionRing
slogan: A DivisionRing is a mathematical structure where you can add, subtract, multiply, and divide (except by zero), and every nonzero element has an inverse so that division is always possible. It is based on a ring and includes operations for inverse and division, with the rule that dividing by an element is the same as multiplying by its inverse. This structure ensures arithmetic behaves as expected, similar to how it does with fractions or real numbers.

label: DoubleQuot.quotQuotEquivQuotOfLE
slogan: If I and J are ideals in a commutative ring with I contained in J, then taking the quotient of R by I first, and then taking the quotient of that result by the image of J, gives a ring that is isomorphic to simply taking the quotient of R by J directly. This isomorphism preserves both addition and multiplication, meaning the two quotient constructions are algebraically the same. It allows replacing a double quotient with a single quotient when one ideal is inside the other.

label: DualNumber
slogan: DualNumber R represents numbers of the form a + b*ε where a and b are elements of type R and ε squared is zero. It is a way to work with extended numbers that include an infinitesimal-like component. The notation R[ε] is shorthand for DualNumber R.

label: DyckWord
slogan: A Dyck word is a sequence of steps, each being either "U" (up) or "D" (down), such that the total number of U's equals the number of D's and in every initial segment of the sequence, the number of U's is at least as many as the D's. This structure models balanced paths or valid parenthesis expressions.

label: DyckWord.card_dyckWord_semilength_eq_catalan
slogan: The number of Dyck words with semilength n (which have n up-steps and n down-steps) is equal to the nth Catalan number. This means the count of valid balanced sequences of parentheses of length 2n is given by the Catalan sequence. For example, there are 5 Dyck words of semilength 3, matching the third Catalan number.

label: DyckWord.equivTree
slogan: There is a one-to-one correspondence between Dyck words, which are sequences of balanced up and down steps, and rooted binary trees where each node has zero or more subtrees and the data at each node is just a placeholder value. This equivalence means each Dyck word can be uniquely translated into a tree structure and vice versa. The mapping relies on recursively decomposing a Dyck word into an "inside" part, which becomes a subtree, and an "outside" part, which represents the rest of the structure.

label: Dynamics.coverEntropy
slogan: The topological entropy of a function T on a subset F of a uniform space X is defined as the supremum, over all entourages U, of the exponential growth rate of the smallest (U, n)-refined covers of F, using the limsup to capture long-term behavior; this measures how quickly points in F become distinguishable under repeated applications of T. The result is an extended real number that quantifies the complexity or unpredictability of the system's dynamics on F.

label: EMetric.instParacompactSpace
slogan: Every pseudometric space is a paracompact space, meaning that any open cover has a locally finite refinement. This result holds for spaces equipped with an extended pseudometric. The proof follows from general topological arguments formalized in the given reference.

label: ENNReal
slogan: ENNReal is the set of nonnegative real numbers (including zero and all positive reals) with positive infinity added as a top element. It allows standard arithmetic and comparisons involving infinity, such as treating infinity as larger than any real number. This type is built by extending the NNReal type using a general construction that adds a maximum element.

label: ENNReal.HolderConjugate
slogan: Two extended nonnegative real numbers p and q are conjugate exponents if their reciprocals sum to 1 (1/p + 1/q = 1), with special rules handling cases where p or q is zero or infinite. This condition supports key inequalities in analysis, such as Hölder's inequality, in spaces of functions with finite norms. The definition works consistently even when infinity is involved, using a framework that extends nonnegative reals with an infinite value.

label: ENNReal.limsup_const_mul
slogan: If c is a fixed non-negative number (possibly infinite) and g is a function, then the limit superior of c times g is equal to c times the limit superior of g, as long as c is not infinity.
