slogan: The total complex of a bicomplex combines its objects across pairs of indices into a single complex indexed by a new shape, where each component is a coproduct of the original objects whose indices map to the same degree under a given index projection. This construction requires that the necessary coproducts exist and that the index shapes are compatible via a total complex shape. The resulting complex inherits its differential from the original bicomplex in a way that respects the categorical structure.

label: HomotopyGroup
slogan: The HomotopyGroup is the set of equivalence classes of n-dimensional loops in a topological space X based at a point x, where two loops are considered the same if one can be continuously deformed into the other without moving the boundary points. It is formed by taking all continuous maps from an n-cube to X that send the boundary to x, and identifying those that are homotopic relative to the boundary. This construction captures the algebraic structure of higher-dimensional holes in the space.

label: HomotopyGroup.Pi
slogan: The homotopy group pi_n(X, x) is the set of equivalence classes of n-dimensional loops in a topological space X based at a point x, where loops are considered the same if one can be continuously deformed into the other while keeping the boundary fixed. Each loop is a continuous map from an n-dimensional cube to X that sends the boundary to x. This structure captures information about n-dimensional holes in the space.

label: HomotopyGroup.commGroup
slogan: For a topological space X and a nontrivial type N, the set of homotopy classes of N-dimensional loops based at a point x in X forms a commutative group under composition. This means that the order in which loops are combined does not affect the result. In particular, the (n+2)-th homotopy group of a space always has commutative multiplication.

label: HopfAlgebra
slogan: A Hopf algebra is a structure built on a semiring A over a commutative semiring R, equipped with linear operations for duplicating elements (comultiplication), deleting them (counit), and inverting them (antipode), all of which must satisfy consistency conditions with the algebra's multiplication and addition. It combines algebra and coalgebra structures with an antipode map, enabling advanced operations used in areas like quantum groups and topology. The setup relies on linear maps to preserve the underlying module and ring-like properties.

label: HopfAlgebra.antipode_mul
slogan: The antipode operation in a Hopf algebra preserves multiplication, meaning the antipode of a product equals the product of the antipodes of each element. This holds for algebras over a commutative semiring. However, this property typically requires the algebra to be cocommutative, as antipodes are usually expected to reverse the order of multiplication.

label: Hyperreal
slogan: Hyperreal is a type representing hyperreal numbers, constructed as germs of sequences of real numbers under an ultrafilter that extends the cofinite filter on the natural numbers. This construction captures infinitesimal and infinite quantities by identifying sequences that agree on a "large" set of indices, as determined by the ultrafilter. The infinitude of the natural numbers ensures the filter can be extended to an ultrafilter needed for this definition.

label: Hyperreal.Infinitesimal
slogan: A hyperreal number is called infinitesimal if it is infinitely close to zero, meaning its difference from zero is smaller than any positive real number. This happens when the standard part of the hyperreal number is zero. Infinitesimal is a property that applies to certain hyperreal numbers in relation to the real number zero.

label: Hyperreal.st
slogan: The standard part function maps a hyperreal number to the nearest real number, if one exists, by discarding infinitesimal differences. It is defined only for finite hyperreals and gives a real number that the hyperreal is infinitely close to. This function goes from the type of hyperreals to the type of reals.

label: Hyperreal.stdPart_of_tendsto
slogan: If a hyperreal number x gets arbitrarily close to a real number r, then the standard part of x equals r.

label: Ideal
slogan: An ideal in a semiring is a subset that includes zero, is closed under addition, and whenever an element is in the ideal, multiplying it by any element from the semiring keeps it in the ideal.

label: Ideal.IsLasker.exists_isMinimalPrimaryDecomposition
slogan: If a ring has the property that every ideal can be written as a finite intersection of primary ideals, then for any given ideal, there exists a minimal such decomposition into primary ideals where the radicals of the primary components are distinct and no component contains the intersection of the others.

label: Ideal.IsMaximal
slogan: An ideal is maximal if it is as large as possible without being the entire ring, meaning no other proper ideal contains it except the whole ring itself. It is a property of a subset of a ring that satisfies certain algebraic closure conditions. Maximal ideals are important because they help identify when a quotient ring is a field.

label: Ideal.IsMaximal.isPrime
slogan: In a commutative ring with unity, if an ideal is maximal (meaning it is not properly contained in any other proper ideal), then it is also prime: whenever the product of two elements is in the ideal, at least one of the elements must already be in the ideal.

label: Ideal.IsMaximal.ne_top
slogan: A maximal ideal is never equal to the entire ring; it is a proper ideal that cannot be made any larger without becoming the whole ring. This means no ideal sits strictly between a maximal ideal and the full ring. In particular, a maximal ideal is always different from the top ideal (which represents the whole ring).

label: Ideal.IsMinimalPrimaryDecomposition
slogan: A finite set of ideals is a minimal primary decomposition of an ideal I if the intersection of the ideals equals I, each ideal is primary, their radical ideals are all different, and no ideal can be removed without changing the intersection.

label: Ideal.IsPrimary
slogan: An ideal is called primary if, whenever a ring element times some element of the ideal is in the ideal, then either that ring element is in a certain prime ideal linked to the ideal, or some power of it multiplies every element of the ideal to zero. This condition extends prime-like behavior by allowing nilpotent effects, and it applies to ideals in a commutative semiring.

label: Ideal.IsPrime
slogan: An ideal I in a semiring R is prime if, whenever the product of two elements a and b is in I, then at least one of a or b must already be in I. This mimics the behavior of prime numbers dividing products. The definition builds on the algebraic structure of semirings and the concept of ideals as special subsets closed under addition and multiplication by ring elements.

label: Ideal.IsPrime.comap
slogan: The preimage of a prime ideal under a ring homomorphism is also a prime ideal, as long as the homomorphism preserves the multiplicative identity and the preimage is not the entire ring. This means that if the image of an element is in the prime ideal, then the element must be in the preimage, and the preimage satisfies the condition that whenever a product is in it, at least one factor is too. The result relies on the fact that ring structure is preserved and the preimage of a proper ideal remains proper.

label: Ideal.IsPrime.inf_le'
slogan: If a prime ideal P contains the intersection of a finite collection of ideals, then P must contain at least one of those ideals. This is equivalent to saying that if the product of several ideals is contained in a prime ideal, then at least one of the ideals must already be contained in that prime ideal. The result follows from the fact that in a commutative semiring, the product of ideals is contained in their intersection, and prime ideals have the property that they must absorb at least one factor in any product they contain.

label: Ideal.IsPrime.isPrimary
slogan: In a commutative semiring, if an ideal is prime—meaning that whenever a product of two elements is in the ideal, at least one of the elements must be in the ideal—then it is also primary, which means that if a product ab is in the ideal, then either a is in the ideal or some power of b is in the ideal. This follows because the prime condition is stronger than the primary condition. The result holds for all ideals in any commutative semiring with standard algebraic properties.

label: Ideal.IsPrime.mul_notMem
slogan: If a prime ideal does not contain two elements, then it also does not contain their product. This is the contrapositive of the rule that if a product is in a prime ideal, at least one factor must be in it.

label: Ideal.LiesOver
slogan: Given a ring homomorphism from a commutative semiring A to a semiring B, an ideal P in B lies over an ideal p in A if the set of elements in A that map into P under the homomorphism is exactly p. This means p is the preimage of P under the algebra map from A to B. The relation describes how ideals in an algebra correspond to ideals in its base ring.

label: Ideal.Quotient.commRing
slogan: When you divide a commutative ring by one of its ideals, the result is a new commutative ring made of equivalence classes where two elements are the same if their difference is in the ideal, and addition and multiplication work consistently on these classes.

label: Ideal.Quotient.field
slogan: If you divide a commutative ring by a maximal ideal, the result is a field, meaning every nonzero element in the quotient has a multiplicative inverse. This is because the maximality of the ideal ensures that every nonzero element in the quotient ring can be multiplied by some other element to give 1. The field structure is built using the fact that the quotient is already a commutative ring and every nonzero element has an inverse.

label: Ideal.Quotient.isDomain_iff_prime
slogan: The quotient ring R/I has no zero divisors (meaning ab = 0 implies a = 0 or b = 0) and is not the zero ring if and only if the ideal I is prime (meaning whenever ab is in I, then a is in I or b is in I). This means the structure of the quotient ring reflects the algebraic property of the ideal. The result depends on standard ring operations and the definition of ideals and quotients.

label: Ideal.Quotient.lift
slogan: If a ring homomorphism maps every element of an ideal to zero, then it induces a unique ring homomorphism from the quotient ring, defined by sending each coset to the image of any of its representatives. This induced map is well-defined and respects both addition and multiplication. It allows constructing maps out of quotient rings by factoring through the original ring.

label: Ideal.Quotient.maximal_ideal_iff_isField_quotient
slogan: In a commutative ring, an ideal is as large as possible without being the whole ring if and only if the quotient ring formed by that ideal is a field, meaning every nonzero element in the quotient has a multiplicative inverse.

label: Ideal.adicTopology
slogan: The Ideal.adicTopology function creates a topology on a commutative ring by using the powers of a fixed ideal, where each power of the ideal defines a neighborhood around zero. This makes the ring into a topological space where addition and multiplication are continuous, and the topology is built from a descending sequence of additive subgroups. The resulting structure is nonarchimedean and respects the algebraic properties of the ring and ideal.

label: Ideal.bot_isMaximal
slogan: In a division semiring, the only ideal that contains just zero is maximal, meaning no other proper ideal lies between it and the whole ring. This is because the only ideals possible are the zero ideal and the entire ring itself. An ideal containing 1 must be the whole ring, so any proper ideal cannot contain any nonzero element.

label: Ideal.bot_prime
slogan: In a semiring where there are at least two elements and no nonzero zero divisors, the ideal containing only zero is a prime ideal. This means that if the product of two elements is zero, then at least one of them must be zero. The result relies on the semiring being nontrivial and having no zero divisors.

label: Ideal.exists_ideal_over_prime_of_isIntegral
slogan: If R is a subring of S and every element of S is integral over R, then for any prime ideal P in R, there exists a prime ideal Q in S containing a given ideal I such that the elements of Q that lie in R are exactly those in P.

label: Ideal.exists_le_maximal
slogan: In any ring, if an ideal is not the entire ring, then there is always some maximal ideal that contains it. A maximal ideal is one that is not properly contained in any other proper ideal. This result relies on the fact that ideals form a partially ordered set with a largest element, and maximal ideals are the immediate predecessors of the whole ring in this order.

label: Ideal.exists_maximal
slogan: In any nonzero semiring, there is at least one maximal ideal—a proper ideal that is not contained in any other proper ideal. This means the set of proper ideals has a largest element under inclusion. The result relies on the ring having more than one element and the algebraic structure of ideals.

label: Ideal.exists_minimalPrimes_le
slogan: In a commutative ring, every proper ideal is contained in at least one minimal prime ideal, meaning a prime ideal that does not properly contain any other prime ideal with the same property. Such minimal primes exist because the set of prime ideals containing a given ideal has minimal elements under inclusion, found using Zorn's lemma on the reverse-ordered set. The result guarantees that for any prime ideal containing a given ideal, there is a minimal prime ideal below it.

label: Ideal.finiteHeight_of_isNoetherianRing
slogan: In a commutative Noetherian ring, every ideal has finite height, meaning the longest chain of prime ideals contained in it is finite. This includes the unit ideal, which is treated as having finite height by definition. The result follows from the fact that the height of a proper ideal is bounded by the number of elements needed to generate it.

label: Ideal.height
slogan: The height of an ideal in a commutative ring is the smallest height among all prime ideals that are minimal over it, where the height of a prime ideal is the length of the longest chain of smaller prime ideals. This value is a natural number or infinity, using extended natural numbers. It measures how deeply embedded the ideal is within the ring's structure of prime ideals.

label: Ideal.height_le_iff_exists_minimalPrimes
slogan: In a commutative Noetherian ring, a prime ideal p has height at most n if and only if p is a minimal prime over some ideal that can be generated by n or fewer elements.

label: Ideal.height_le_spanRank_toENat
slogan: In a commutative Noetherian ring, the height of a proper ideal is at most the minimum number of generators needed for that ideal. This means that if an ideal can be generated by n elements, then the longest chain of prime ideals contained in it has length at most n. The result applies to all finitely generated ideals that are not the entire ring.

label: Ideal.iInf_pow_eq_bot_of_isDomain
slogan: In a commutative Noetherian domain, if an ideal is not the entire ring, then the intersection of all its powers contains only zero. This means that no nonzero element can belong to every power of the ideal. The result relies on the ring having no zero divisors and satisfying a finiteness condition on ideals.

label: Ideal.iInf_pow_eq_bot_of_isLocalRing
slogan: In a local ring that is Noetherian, the intersection of all powers of any proper ideal is zero, meaning no nonzero element can be found in every power of the ideal. This captures the idea that repeatedly multiplying a proper ideal by itself eventually "becomes" zero in the limit.

label: Ideal.instIsTwoSided
slogan: In a commutative semiring, any ideal is automatically closed under multiplication by elements from the semiring on both sides, so it is always two-sided. This means that if you multiply an element of the ideal by any element of the semiring, the result stays in the ideal regardless of the order of multiplication. The commutativity of the semiring ensures that left and right closure are equivalent.

label: Ideal.isCoprime_iff_add
slogan: Two ideals in a commutative semiring are coprime if and only if their sum equals the entire ring, which means the smallest ideal containing both is the whole ring. This happens exactly when the only common divisor of the two ideals is the unit ideal. The condition is equivalent to the ideals being codisjoint, meaning their join in the lattice of ideals is the top element.

label: Ideal.isCoprime_iff_exists
slogan: Two ideals in a commutative semiring are coprime if and only if there are elements, one from each ideal, that add up to 1. This means their sum contains the multiplicative identity, which happens exactly when they have no common factors except the whole ring. The condition is equivalent to the existence of a linear combination of elements from the ideals equaling one.

label: Ideal.isMaximal_def
slogan: An ideal is maximal if it is not the whole ring and there is no other ideal strictly between it and the entire ring; equivalently, it is a coatom in the lattice of ideals, meaning the only ideal that properly contains it is the whole ring itself.

label: Ideal.isMaximal_iff
slogan: An ideal in a semiring is maximal if and only if it does not contain 1 and, whenever an element is not in the ideal, adding it to the ideal forces the ideal to become the entire ring. This means the ideal is proper and there is no other ideal strictly between it and the whole ring. Maximal ideals are precisely those that are as large as possible without being the full ring.

label: Ideal.isPrime_bot
slogan: The zero ideal is prime if and only if the ring is not the zero ring and has no zero divisors, meaning that whenever a product of two elements is zero, at least one of them must be zero. This happens precisely when the ring is nontrivial (0 ≠ 1) and multiplication behaves like in an integral domain. In such cases, the smallest ideal—containing only zero—satisfies the prime condition.

label: Ideal.isPrime_of_maximally_disjoint
slogan: If an ideal in a commutative semiring is as large as possible without sharing any elements with a given submonoid, then that ideal is prime. This means that whenever a product of two elements is in the ideal, at least one of the elements must already be in the ideal. The result connects maximality with respect to disjointness from a submonoid to the prime property of ideals.

label: Ideal.jacobson
slogan: The jacobson of an ideal consists of all elements in the ring such that, when multiplied by any element of the ideal and added to 1, the result is a unit (an invertible element). It is formed by taking the intersection of certain subsets of the ring that are linked to the ideal, capturing elements that behave like they are "infinitesimally small" in a multiplicative way. This construction results in a new ideal that reflects deep structural properties of the original ideal and the ring.

label: Ideal.primeHeight
slogan: The height of a prime ideal is the longest possible chain of smaller prime ideals, counted by the number of steps in the chain, and it can be infinite. It measures how deep the ideal sits within the ring's structure of prime ideals. The value is a natural number or infinity, using the extended natural numbers.

label: Ideal.primeHeight_eq_zero_iff
slogan: A prime ideal has height zero if and only if it is a minimal prime ideal, meaning no other prime ideal is strictly contained within it.

label: Ideal.prod_eq_iInf_of_pairwise_isCoprime
slogan: If a finite collection of ideals in a commutative ring are pairwise coprime, then the product of these ideals is equal to their intersection. This means multiplying the ideals together gives the same result as taking all elements common to every ideal in the collection. The equality holds because pairwise coprimality ensures no overlapping structure interferes with the product.

label: Ideal.quotientInfRingEquivPiQuotient
slogan: When a ring is divided by the intersection of finitely many pairwise coprime ideals, the result is a ring that is structurally the same as the product of the rings obtained by dividing the original ring by each ideal individually; this correspondence preserves both addition and multiplication.

label: Ideal.quotientInfToPiQuotient_surj
slogan: When a ring is divided by the intersection of several ideals that are pairwise coprime, the resulting quotient ring maps onto the product of the individual quotient rings, such that every combination of elements from the individual quotients comes from a single element in the original ring.

label: Ideal.radical
slogan: The radical of an ideal in a commutative semiring is the set of all elements where, for some positive whole number power, that power of the element is in the ideal. It forms a new ideal made up of all such elements. This means if you can raise an element to some positive power and get something in the original ideal, then the element belongs to the radical.

label: Ideal.relIsoOfSurjective
slogan: For a surjective ring homomorphism f from ring R to ring S, there is a one-to-one correspondence between ideals of S and ideals of R that contain the kernel of f; this correspondence is given by mapping an ideal in R to its image under f, and an ideal in S to its preimage under f.

label: Ideal.sInf_isPrime_of_isChain
slogan: If a nonempty collection of ideals is totally ordered by inclusion and each ideal in the collection is prime, then their intersection is also a prime ideal; this means that whenever a product of two ring elements is in the intersection, at least one of the elements must lie in every ideal of the chain. The result holds in any semiring where ideals are defined and closed under the usual operations.

label: Ideal.span
slogan: Ideal.span is the smallest ideal in a semiring that includes a given set of elements, made by taking all finite sums of elements from that set multiplied by elements of the semiring. It is generated by combining the set's elements with arbitrary coefficients from the semiring. This forms a subset that is closed under addition and multiplication by any ring element.

label: Ideal.span_singleton_prime
slogan: In a commutative semiring, the ideal generated by a single nonzero element p consists of all multiples of p, and this ideal is prime exactly when p itself is a prime element. A prime element is one that is not a unit and has the property that if it divides a product, it must divide at least one factor. Thus, the ideal of multiples of p is prime if and only if p meets this standard definition of a prime element.

label: Ideal.subset_union_prime
slogan: If an ideal is contained in the union of finitely many prime ideals, then it must be entirely contained in at least one of those prime ideals. This means you can't spread an ideal across multiple prime ideals in a union without it fully lying in one of them.

label: Ideal.sup_primeHeight_of_maximal_eq_ringKrullDim
slogan: In a nonzero commutative ring, the largest chain of prime ideals contained in any maximal ideal determines the ring's Krull dimension, and the supremum of these heights across all maximal ideals equals the ring's overall Krull dimension.

label: Ideal.uniqueFactorizationMonoid
slogan: In a Dedekind domain, every nonzero ideal can be written in exactly one way as a product of prime ideals, up to the order of the factors, just like how integers have unique prime factorizations.

label: IncidenceAlgebra
slogan: The incidence algebra over a type α with coefficients in a type 𝕜 consists of functions that assign elements of 𝕜 to pairs of elements in α where the first is less than or equal to the second, using a zero element from 𝕜 and the ordering on α. It combines algebraic structure with the order relation on α. This structure supports operations like addition and convolution based on the order and the zero element.

label: IncidenceAlgebra.mu
slogan: The Möbius function mu is an element of the incidence algebra that inverts the zeta function, meaning when combined with zeta using convolution, it produces the identity element for that operation. It is defined for locally finite preorders and takes values in a ring with unity, assigning a value to each pair of comparable elements. The function is constructed recursively so that its sum over intervals matches the Kronecker delta function.

label: IncompRel
slogan: IncompRel r a b means that neither r a b nor r b a is true, so a and b are incomparable under the relation r.

label: IndiscreteTopology
slogan: A type has the indiscrete topology if the only open sets are the empty set and the entire space, with no other subsets being open. This is a special case of a topological space where the topology is as coarse as possible.

label: Infinite
slogan: A type is Infinite if it has no finite limit on the number of values it can contain, meaning it goes on forever. This is the opposite of being IsEmpty, where no values exist at all. Infinite types have endlessly many elements.

label: InfiniteGalois.IntermediateFieldEquivClosedSubgroup
slogan: There is a one-to-one correspondence between intermediate fields of an infinite Galois extension and closed subgroups of its Galois group, where each field corresponds to the subgroup of automorphisms that fix it, and each subgroup corresponds to the field it fixes. This correspondence reverses inclusion: bigger fields match smaller subgroups, and smaller fields match bigger subgroups. The mapping is an order-reversing isomorphism between the lattice of intermediate fields and the lattice of closed subgroups.

label: InformationTheory.UniquelyDecodable
slogan: A set of lists is uniquely decodable if no two different sequences of lists from the set, when concatenated, produce the same overall list. In other words, each possible string formed by joining lists from the set has only one unique way to be broken down into its original list sequence. This ensures unambiguous decoding of concatenated messages.

label: InformationTheory.integral_llr_add_sub_measure_univ_nonneg
slogan: The integral of the log-likelihood ratio between two finite measures μ and ν with respect to μ, plus the total mass of ν minus the total mass of μ, is always at least zero, provided μ is absolutely continuous with respect to ν and the log-likelihood ratio is integrable. This result supports the nonnegativity of the Kullback-Leibler divergence. It relies on the fact that the underlying function used in the divergence is nonnegative.

label: InformationTheory.klDiv
slogan: The Kullback-Leibler divergence is a measure of the difference between two probability measures, defined as the integral of the log-likelihood ratio weighted by one of the measures. It is infinite if the first measure is not absolutely continuous with respect to the second, and otherwise takes a non-negative real value. The result is expressed as an extended non-negative real number (including infinity).

label: InformationTheory.klDiv_compProd_eq_add
slogan: The Kullback-Leibler divergence between two joint measures formed by combining a measure on one space with a kernel into another space equals the sum of the divergence between the original measures and the divergence between the resulting joint measures when the first measure is fixed. This identity holds for finite measures and Markov kernels without restrictions on the underlying measurable spaces. It expresses a chain rule for KL divergence using composition-products.

label: InformationTheory.kraft_mcmillan_inequality
slogan: If a set of finite lists over a finite alphabet can be uniquely decoded (no two sequences of lists concatenate to the same string), then the sum of (1/D) raised to the length of each list in the set is less than or equal to 1, where D is the number of symbols in the alphabet.

label: InitialSeg.image_Iio
slogan: If f is an initial segment embedding between two partially ordered sets, then the image of all elements less than a under f is exactly the set of all elements less than f(a) in the target set. This means f preserves the structure of downward-open intervals. In other words, mapping the elements below a through f gives precisely the elements below f(a).

label: InitialSeg.total
slogan: For any two well-ordered sets, either the first is an initial segment of the second or the second is an initial segment of the first. This means one set can always be embedded at the beginning of the other in an order-preserving way. The result guarantees a complete ordering of well-ordered sets by initial segment inclusion.

label: Inner
slogan: Inner defines a structure for a vector space over a field 𝕜 where any two vectors can be combined using an inner product to produce a scalar value. It requires the space to support operations like vector addition and scalar multiplication, along with the inner product satisfying properties such as symmetry, linearity, and positive definiteness. This structure allows defining geometric concepts like lengths and angles in the vector space.

label: InnerProductGeometry.angle
slogan: The angle between two vectors in a real inner product space, defined as the arccosine of the normalized inner product; if either vector is zero, the angle is pi/2. This measures the smallest angle between the vectors without regard to direction. It is always a real number between 0 and pi.

label: InnerProductGeometry.angle_eq_zero_iff
slogan: The angle between two vectors is zero if and only if both vectors are nonzero and one vector is a positive scalar multiple of the other.

label: InnerProductGeometry.angle_smul_left_of_pos
slogan: The angle between a vector and another vector scaled by a positive real number is the same as the angle between the two original vectors. Scaling a vector by a positive number does not change the angle it makes with another vector.

label: InnerProductGeometry.cos_angle
slogan: The cosine of the angle between two vectors equals the inner product of the vectors divided by the product of their lengths. This holds for any vectors in a real inner product space, with the angle defined even when one vector is zero.

label: InnerProductGeometry.cos_angle_mul_norm_mul_norm
slogan: The cosine of the angle between two vectors, times the product of their lengths, equals the inner product of the vectors. This holds in any real inner product space, where angles and lengths are defined using the inner product. If either vector is zero, the angle is defined as 90 degrees (pi/2), and the formula still holds since the inner product is zero.

label: InnerProductGeometry.inner_eq_zero_iff_angle_eq_pi_div_two
slogan: Two vectors are perpendicular if and only if their inner product is zero, which happens exactly when the angle between them is 90 degrees (or pi/2 radians). This holds true in any real inner product space, with the angle defined even when one of the vectors is zero.

label: InnerProductGeometry.norm_add_sq_eq_norm_sq_add_norm_sq'
slogan: If two vectors form a right angle with each other, then the square of the length of their sum equals the sum of the squares of their individual lengths.

label: InnerProductGeometry.norm_add_sq_eq_norm_sq_add_norm_sq_iff_angle_eq_pi_div_two
slogan: The square of the length of the sum of two vectors equals the sum of the squares of their lengths if and only if the angle between them is 90 degrees (pi/2 radians). This is the Pythagorean theorem expressed in terms of vectors and angles. It holds in any real inner product space.

label: InnerProductGeometry.norm_ofLp_crossProduct
slogan: The length of the cross product of two 3D real vectors equals the product of their lengths multiplied by the sine of the angle between them.

label: InnerProductGeometry.norm_sub_sq_eq_norm_sq_add_norm_sq_iff_angle_eq_pi_div_two
slogan: The squared length of the difference of two vectors equals the sum of their squared lengths if and only if the angle between them is 90 degrees. This is the Pythagorean theorem expressed in terms of vector geometry. It holds when the vectors are perpendicular, which means their inner product is zero.

label: InnerProductGeometry.norm_sub_sq_eq_norm_sq_add_norm_sq_sub_two_mul_norm_mul_norm_mul_cos_angle
slogan: The square of the distance between two vectors x and y is equal to the sum of the squares of their lengths minus twice the product of their lengths and the cosine of the angle between them. This is the law of cosines expressed in terms of vectors. It generalizes the Pythagorean theorem to non-right triangles in inner product spaces.

label: InnerProductSpace
slogan: An InnerProductSpace is a vector space over a field like the real or complex numbers, where there is an inner product that assigns a scalar to each pair of vectors, satisfying properties like linearity, symmetry, and positive definiteness. This inner product induces a norm, allowing the definition of geometric concepts such as angles, lengths, and orthogonality. The space must also support the algebraic and metric structure of a normed vector space with completeness and ordered field properties.

label: InnerProductSpace.Core.toNormedAddCommGroup
slogan: An inner product space automatically gives rise to a normed abelian group by defining the norm of a vector as the square root of the inner product of the vector with itself, ensuring the norm is non-negative and behaves well with vector addition and scalar multiplication.

label: InnerProductSpace.HarmonicAt
slogan: A function f from a finite-dimensional real inner product space E to another normed space F is harmonic at a point x if f is twice continuously differentiable near x and its Laplacian (sum of second partial derivatives) is zero in a neighborhood around x.

label: InnerProductSpace.HarmonicAt.add
slogan: If two functions are harmonic at a point in a finite-dimensional real inner product space, then their sum is also harmonic at that point. A function is harmonic at a point if it is twice continuously differentiable near that point and its Laplacian vanishes in a neighborhood around it. This result states that harmonicity is preserved under addition.

label: InnerProductSpace.HarmonicContOnCl
slogan: A function is harmonic on a set and continuous on the closure of that set, meaning it satisfies the Laplace equation within the set and has no discontinuities when approaching the boundary. This combines smoothness and regularity conditions commonly used in harmonic analysis. The setting is finite-dimensional real inner product spaces, with the function mapping into a real normed space.

label: InnerProductSpace.HarmonicOnNhd.circleAverage_poissonKernel_smul
slogan: If a real-valued function is harmonic inside and near a closed disk in the complex plane, then its value at any point inside the disk equals the average of its values around the boundary circle, weighted by the Poisson kernel centered at that point. This average is taken over the circle of radius R centered at c, and the weighting depends on the location of the interior point w. The formula expresses the function's value at w as an integral involving the Poisson kernel and the function's values on the boundary.

label: InnerProductSpace.HarmonicOnNhd.exists_analyticOnNhd_ball_re_eq
slogan: If a real-valued function f is harmonic in a neighborhood around a point z in the complex plane, then there exists a complex-analytic function F defined in the same neighborhood such that the real part of F equals f.

label: InnerProductSpace.bounded_harmonic_on_complex_plane_is_constant
slogan: A bounded harmonic function from the complex plane into a real normed space is constant, meaning it takes the same value everywhere. This means if a function satisfies the harmonic property in a neighborhood of every point in the complex plane and its outputs don't grow without bound, then the function must be constant. Specifically, for any two complex numbers z and w, the value of the function at z equals the value at w.

label: InnerProductSpace.gramSchmidt
slogan: The gramSchmidt function processes a sequence of vectors in an inner product space one by one, removing the components that lie in the span of earlier vectors and normalizing the result, to produce an orthonormal set. This orthonormal set spans the same subspace as the original vectors. The process relies on projections and inner products, and works for any sequence indexed by a well-ordered, locally finite type.

label: InnerProductSpace.laplacianWithin_eq_iteratedFDerivWithin_stdOrthonormalBasis
slogan: The Laplacian of a function at a point in a finite-dimensional real inner product space, with respect to a set containing that point, equals the sum of the second directional derivatives in the directions of the standard orthonormal basis vectors. This formula holds when the set supports unique differentiability at the point. The standard orthonormal basis provides a concrete way to compute the Laplacian using iterated derivatives.

label: InnerProductSpace.laplacian_eq_iteratedFDeriv_orthonormalBasis
slogan: The Laplacian of a function between finite-dimensional real inner product spaces can be computed by summing the second directional derivatives in the directions of an orthonormal basis. Specifically, at each point, it is the sum over all basis vectors of the second derivative evaluated on pairs of identical basis vectors. This formula holds for any choice of orthonormal basis in the domain space.

label: InnerProductSpace.laplacian_eq_iteratedFDeriv_stdOrthonormalBasis
slogan: The Laplacian of a function between finite-dimensional real inner product spaces is equal to the sum of the second directional derivatives in the directions of the standard orthonormal basis vectors. Each term in the sum evaluates the second derivative of the function at a point, applied twice to the same basis vector. This formula uses the standard basis to express the Laplacian in terms of iterated derivatives.

label: InnerProductSpace.ofNorm
slogan: If a normed vector space satisfies the parallelogram identity — that the sum of the squares of the norms of x+y and x-y equals twice the sum of the squares of the norms of x and y — then there exists an inner product that induces this norm, making the space an inner product space over a real-like field.

label: InnerProductSpace.rankOne
slogan: The rankOne function takes two vectors and returns a continuous linear map that acts by taking the inner product of its input with one vector and then multiplying the result by the other vector. This produces a rank-one operator, meaning its output space is one-dimensional. The map is linear, continuous, and respects the inner product structure of the space.

label: Inseparable
slogan: Two points in a topological space are inseparable if they have exactly the same neighborhoods, meaning every open set containing one also contains the other, or equivalently, their closures are equal. This means no open or closed set can tell them apart. Inseparable points are topologically indistinguishable.

label: Int.ModEq
slogan: Int.ModEq(n, a, b) means that integers a and b have a difference divisible by n, so they leave the same remainder when divided by n in the usual mathematical sense. The modulo operation ensures the remainder has the same sign as the divisor. This defines a congruence relation used in modular arithmetic.

label: Int.ModEq.cancel_left_div_gcd
slogan: If a nonzero integer c times a is congruent to c times b modulo m, then a is congruent to b modulo m divided by the greatest common divisor of m and c.

label: Int.ModEq.mul_left_cancel'
slogan: If a nonzero integer c times a is congruent to c times b modulo c times m, then a is congruent to b modulo m. This means you can cancel a nonzero common factor from both sides of a modular equation when the modulus is adjusted accordingly. The result depends on the fact that multiplication respects modular equivalence and divisibility.

label: Int.ModEq.of_mul_right
slogan: If two integers are congruent modulo n, then they remain congruent modulo n even if the modulus is multiplied by another integer. In other words, if a ≡ b mod n, then a ≡ b mod (n * m) for any integer m. This result follows from properties of integer multiplication and modular equivalence.

label: Int.ModEq.pow_card_sub_one_eq_one
slogan: If p is a prime number and a is any integer not divisible by p, then a^(p-1) leaves a remainder of 1 when divided by p. This means that raising such an integer to the power (p-1) gives a result that is congruent to 1 modulo p.

label: Int.ModEq.pow_prime_eq_self
slogan: If p is a prime number, then for any integer n, n raised to the power p has the same remainder as n when divided by p. In other words, n^p - n is divisible by p. This is a modular arithmetic property known as Fermat's Little Theorem.

label: Int.ModEq.trans
slogan: If a is congruent to b modulo n, and b is congruent to c modulo n, then a is congruent to c modulo n. This means modular equivalence for integers is transitive.

label: Int.ceil
slogan: Int.ceil is a function that takes a real number from a type with ring and linear order structure, and returns the smallest integer that is greater than or equal to that number, using the floor function's existence to compute the result. It works in any system where integers can be embedded into an ordered ring and where floor operations are defined. The output is always a standard integer.

label: Int.ceil_eq_floor_add_one_iff_notMem
slogan: The ceiling of a number equals the floor of that number plus one if and only if the number is not an integer. This means that when a number is not a whole number, rounding it up gives the same result as rounding it down and then adding one.

label: Int.ediv_emod_unique
slogan: For integers a, b, q, and r, with b positive, the division a / b equals q and the remainder a % b equals r if and only if a = r + b * q, where r is nonnegative and less than b.

label: Int.ediv_emod_unique''
slogan: For any integers a, b, q, and r, where b is not zero, a divided by b equals q and a modulo b equals r if and only if a equals r plus b times q, with r being nonnegative and less than the absolute value of b. This holds even when b is negative. The result of division and remainder is uniquely determined by these conditions.

label: Int.emod_lt_of_pos
slogan: For any integer a and positive integer b, the remainder when a is divided by b is always less than b.

label: Int.fib
slogan: The Int.fib function defines the Fibonacci sequence for all integers, where fib(0) = 0, fib(1) = 1, and each subsequent number is the sum of the two preceding ones, extended to negative indices as well. It builds upon the natural number version of Fibonacci (Nat.fib) and returns integer values. Negative inputs are handled by converting them to natural numbers, with negative integers effectively treated as zero in that conversion.

label: Int.fib_add_sq_sub_fib_mul_fib_add_two_mul
slogan: For any integers x and a, the square of the (x+a)th Fibonacci number minus the product of the xth and (x+2a)th Fibonacci numbers equals (-1) raised to the absolute value of x, multiplied by the square of the ath Fibonacci number.

label: Int.fib_succ_mul_fib_pred_sub_fib_sq
slogan: For any integer n, the product of the Fibonacci numbers at positions n+1 and n-1, minus the square of the Fibonacci number at n, equals (-1) raised to the absolute value of n.

label: Int.floor
slogan: Int.floor is a function that takes a number from a type with both arithmetic operations and a total order, like the real or rational numbers, and returns the largest integer that is less than or equal to that number. It works on any type that supports addition, multiplication, subtraction, and comparison between elements, ensuring that the floor operation is consistent with basic arithmetic. When the input is already an integer, the function returns it unchanged.

label: Int.floor_eq_iff
slogan: The floor of a number b is equal to an integer a if and only if a is less than or equal to b and b is less than a plus one. This means the floor function returns the greatest integer that does not exceed the given number. The result holds for any type that supports a ring structure, a linear order, and a floor operation.

label: Int.floor_eq_on_Ico
slogan: The floor of a number a is equal to an integer n if and only if a is greater than or equal to n and less than n + 1, where the comparison happens in a ring with a linear order and a floor function. This means the floor function returns the largest integer that is not greater than a. The result holds for any type that supports both arithmetic operations and ordering.

label: Int.floor_le_ceil
slogan: For any number in an ordered ring, the largest integer less than or equal to it (floor) is always less than or equal to the smallest integer greater than or equal to it (ceiling). This follows from the definitions of floor and ceiling and the fact that the order relation is transitive. The result holds in any algebraic structure where integers can be embedded and ordered operations are defined.

label: Int.floor_mono
slogan: If one number is less than or equal to another, then the floor of the first number is also less than or equal to the floor of the second; this means the floor function preserves order.

label: Int.gcd_dvd_iff
slogan: A natural number d divides both integers a and b if and only if d divides the greatest common divisor of a and b. This means the common divisors of a and b are exactly the divisors of their gcd.

label: Int.gcd_eq_gcd_ab
slogan: For any two integers x and y, their greatest common divisor can be written as a combination of x and y multiplied by some integers, specifically x times a value called gcdA and y times a value called gcdB. The result is always a natural number, based on the absolute values of x and y. This shows that the GCD of two integers is equal to a linear combination of those integers using integer coefficients.

label: Int.gcd_least_linear
slogan: The greatest common divisor of two integers, where at least one is nonzero, is the smallest positive integer that can be written as a combination of the two integers multiplied by some integers. In other words, no smaller positive number can be formed by adding multiples of the two integers. This smallest combination equals their gcd.

label: Int.ideal_span_isMaximal_of_prime
slogan: If a natural number is prime, then the set of all integer multiples of that number forms a maximal ideal in the ring of integers, meaning no other proper ideal can strictly contain it except the whole ring.

label: Int.instCommRing
slogan: The integers form a commutative ring, meaning they support addition and multiplication that are both commutative and associative, with 0 as the additive identity, 1 as the multiplicative identity, additive inverses for every element, and multiplication distributing over addition.

label: Int.instIsStrictOrderedRing
slogan: The integers form a ring where the usual ordering is compatible with addition and multiplication, meaning adding the same number to both sides of an inequality preserves it, and multiplying by a positive number also preserves the inequality. Positive integers remain positive when multiplied, and zero is less than one. This structure ensures consistent arithmetic and ordering behavior for all integers.

label: Int.instLinearOrder
slogan: The integers support a total ordering where any two integers can be compared using ≤ or <, and this ordering is reflexive, transitive, antisymmetric, and total. This means for any integers a and b, either a ≤ b or b ≤ a holds, and standard comparison operations like min and max are well-defined and computable. The ordering follows familiar mathematical rules, with a < b meaning a ≤ b and b ≰ a.

label: Int.isCoprime_iff_gcd_eq_one
slogan: Two integers are coprime if and only if their greatest common divisor is 1, meaning they have no common positive divisors except 1. The result depends only on the absolute values of the integers.

label: Int.log
slogan: Int.log is a function that finds the largest integer n such that 2 to the power of n is less than or equal to a given positive number, effectively computing the integer part of the base-2 logarithm. It works with types that support order, addition, multiplication, and division, converting from natural number logarithm results when needed. The function is used in formal proofs to reason about powers of two and integer magnitude.

label: Int.prime_dvd_pow_sub_one
slogan: If p is a prime number and n is an integer that shares no common factors with p, then p divides n raised to the power (p-1) minus 1.

label: Int.quotientSpanNatEquivZMod
slogan: The integers modulo n are equivalent to the ring obtained by dividing the integers by the ideal consisting of all multiples of n, with a one-to-one correspondence that preserves addition and multiplication. This equivalence is based on mapping each integer to its remainder when divided by n. The structure of modular arithmetic is thus captured exactly by the quotient ring construction.

label: Irrational
slogan: A real number x is irrational if it cannot be expressed as a fraction a/b where a and b are integers and b is not zero; equivalently, x is not in the set of real numbers that come from converting rational numbers into reals using the standard embedding.

label: Irrational.beattySeq_symmDiff_beattySeq_pos
slogan: If r and s are irrational numbers greater than 1 such that 1/r + 1/s = 1, then the sets of positive integers formed by taking the floor of k*r and floor of k*s for positive integers k together contain every positive integer exactly once, with no overlaps.

label: Irreducible
slogan: An irreducible element in a monoid is a non-unit element that cannot be expressed as the product of two non-unit elements. In other words, if an element is irreducible, then whenever it is written as a product of two elements, at least one of them must be a unit. This property helps identify building blocks in algebraic structures where factorization matters.

label: Irreducible.degree_le_two
slogan: If a polynomial with real coefficients cannot be factored into simpler non-constant polynomials, then its degree is at most 2. This means such irreducible polynomials can only have degree 0, 1, or 2.

label: IsAbelianGalois
slogan: A field extension L over K is Abelian Galois if it is Galois and the group of automorphisms of L that fix K is commutative, meaning the order in which symmetries are applied does not affect the result. This commutativity implies that the structure of the extension is highly symmetric and algebraically simple. The extension must support field operations and a compatible algebra structure over the base field.

label: IsAdicComplete
slogan: A ring is adic complete with respect to an ideal if, under the topology defined by that ideal, every Cauchy sequence converges and distinct points can be separated by disjoint neighborhoods. This means the ring is both complete (all Cauchy sequences have limits) and separated (the intersection of all powers of the ideal is zero) in the adic topology. It combines algebraic structure with a strong form of topological completeness.

label: IsAdicComplete.henselianRing
slogan: A ring that is complete with respect to an ideal has the property that if a polynomial equation has a solution modulo the ideal and the derivative of the polynomial is a unit at that solution, then the solution can be lifted uniquely to the whole ring. This lifting property, known as the Henselian property, allows for approximating roots in a way similar to how Hensel's lemma works for p-adic numbers. The completeness ensures that such approximations can be refined indefinitely to get an actual solution.

label: IsAlgClosed
slogan: A field is algebraically closed if every non-constant polynomial with coefficients in the field has at least one root in the same field. This means all polynomials can be broken down into linear factors using elements of the field. In such a field, no polynomial of degree one or higher lacks a solution.

label: IsAlgClosed.equivOfTranscendenceBasis
slogan: If two algebraically closed fields have the same characteristic and their transcendence bases can be put in one-to-one correspondence, then the fields are isomorphic. This means that such fields with matching transcendence basis sizes and characteristics are structurally identical as fields. The isomorphism is built by mapping one transcendence basis to the other and extending algebraically.

label: IsAlgClosure
slogan: A field K is an algebraic closure of a commutative ring R if every element of K is a root of some nonzero polynomial with coefficients in R, and every non-constant polynomial with coefficients in K has a root in K. This means K is algebraically closed and consists entirely of elements algebraic over R. The structure requires K to be a field, R a commutative ring, and K an algebra over R with no torsion in its module structure.

label: IsAntichain
slogan: A set is an antichain if no two different elements in the set are related by a given relation; this means for all distinct pairs of elements, the relation does not hold between them. The condition is expressed using the Pairwise property applied to the complement of the relation. It checks that the negation of the relation is true for every pair of distinct elements in the set.

label: IsAntichain.sperner
slogan: In a finite set, the largest possible collection of subsets where no one subset contains another is no bigger than the number of subsets of size equal to half the total number of elements, rounded down. This maximum size is given by the binomial coefficient "n choose floor(n/2)".

label: IsArtinian
slogan: A module is called Artinian if every descending sequence of its submodules eventually stops getting smaller, meaning no infinite strictly decreasing chains of submodules exist. This is equivalent to saying that the submodules, ordered by inclusion, form a structure where every nonempty collection has a minimal element. The definition applies to modules over a semiring, using the algebraic properties of addition and scalar multiplication.

label: IsArtinianRing
slogan: A ring is called Artinian if every descending sequence of ideals eventually stabilizes, meaning that in its structure as a module over itself, there are no infinite strictly decreasing chains of ideals. This definition relies only on the ring's semiring properties, which include associative addition and multiplication, distributivity, and the existence of additive zero and multiplicative one. The condition ensures a kind of finiteness in the lattice of ideals.

label: IsArtinianRing.equivPi
slogan: An Artinian ring with no nonzero nilpotent elements is ring-isomorphic to a product of fields, one for each of its maximal ideals. This means the ring can be decomposed into simpler pieces, each corresponding to a field formed by taking the ring modulo one of its maximal ideals. The isomorphism preserves both addition and multiplication.

label: IsAtom
slogan: An element is an atom if it is above the smallest element (bot) and nothing lies strictly between it and bot. This means the element is minimal among all non-bottom elements in the order.

label: IsAtomic
slogan: A type is atomic if it has a smallest element (called bottom) and every element that isn't the smallest has a minimal non-bottom element (called an atom) below it. This means every non-bottom element is greater than or equal to at least one atom. The type must support a partial order and have a defined bottom element.

label: IsAzumaya
slogan: An Azumaya algebra is a finitely generated, projective, and faithful algebra over a commutative semiring R, such that the map sending a tensor a ⊗ b to the linear function x ↦ a * x * b gives an isomorphism between the tensor product of the algebra and its opposite and the algebra of endomorphisms of the module. This means the algebra has a strong duality property over its base ring. The structure ensures it behaves like a matrix algebra over R in a generalized sense.

label: IsBoundedBilinearMap.hasFDerivAt
slogan: If a function is bilinear and bounded, then it is differentiable everywhere, and its derivative at any point is a continuous linear map that acts on a pair of vectors by applying the bilinear map to one vector from each input along with the corresponding change in that input.

label: IsBoundedLinearMap.isLinearMap_and_continuous_iff_isBoundedLinearMap
slogan: A function between two normed spaces is linear and continuous if and only if it is bounded, meaning it preserves vector addition and scalar multiplication, doesn't amplify norms beyond a fixed constant, and small input changes lead to small output changes.

label: IsCancelMul
slogan: A type has IsCancelMul when multiplying on the left or right can be canceled, meaning if a * b = a * c then b = c, and if b * a = c * a then b = c, for all elements a, b, c. This requires the type to have a multiplication operation and combines both left and right cancellation properties.

label: IsCauSeq.series_ratio_test
slogan: If the size of each term in a sequence is eventually no more than a fixed fraction (less than 1) of the size of the previous term, then the sum of the sequence's terms converges.

label: IsChain
slogan: A chain is a set where, for any two different elements, a specified relation holds between them; it describes a subset in which all pairs of elements are related in a particular way. This means the set is totally ordered according to the given relation. The property depends on the relation being satisfied pairwise across all elements of the set.

label: IsChain.exists_maxChain
slogan: In any nonempty collection of sets where every pair of sets is comparable by inclusion, there exists a maximal chain—a chain that cannot be extended by adding more sets while preserving the inclusion order.

label: IsClopen
slogan: A set is clopen if it is open and its complement is also open, meaning the set is both open and closed in the given topological space.

label: IsClosed
slogan: A set is closed if its complement is open, meaning the points not in the set form an open set. This definition depends on the topology of the space the set is in. The declaration provides a way to state that a subset of a topological space is closed.

label: IsClosed.add_left_of_isCompact
slogan: If one set is compact and another is closed in a topological additive group where addition is continuous, then the set formed by adding every element of the compact set to every element of the closed set is also closed. This result depends on the continuity of addition and the topological properties of compactness and closedness. The operation involved is pointwise addition of sets.

label: IsClosed.isCompact
slogan: If a set is closed and lies within a compact topological space, then that set is also compact. This means that any open cover of the set has a finite subcover, provided the set is closed and the whole space is compact. The result links the properties of closedness and compactness in topology.

label: IsClosed.isComplete
slogan: In a uniform space where all Cauchy filters converge, any closed subset contains the limits of all Cauchy filters that converge within the whole space, so the subset is complete under the same uniform structure. This means completeness is preserved when restricting to closed subsets.

label: IsClosed.mem_of_tendsto
slogan: If a function gets arbitrarily close to a limit point and is often inside a closed set, then the limit point must belong to that closed set. This holds because closed sets contain all their boundary points, and the function's behavior reflects this in the limit. The result requires the function to approach the limit and the set to be topologically closed.

label: IsClosed.mono
slogan: If a set is closed in a topology with more open sets, then it is also closed in any topology with fewer open sets. This is because closed sets are complements of open sets, and reducing the number of open sets means fewer complements are required for closure. The result follows from the fact that coarser topologies have fewer open sets, hence more sets remain closed.

label: IsClosed.mul_left_of_isCompact
slogan: If s is a compact set and t is a closed set in a topological group, then the set of all products obtained by multiplying each element of s on the left with each element of t is also closed. This holds because the group's multiplication is continuous and the topological properties of compactness and closedness interact well under continuous operations.

label: IsCoatom
slogan: An element is a coatom if it is not the top element and every element strictly greater than it must be the top element. This means there are no elements strictly between a coatom and the top in the order. The definition applies to any type with a preorder and a top element.

label: IsCoercive
slogan: A function B is coercive if, whenever the size (norm) of an input vector in a real normed vector space gets very large, the absolute value of the resulting output also becomes arbitrarily large. Specifically, B takes vectors to linear maps that return real numbers, and coerciveness means the output's magnitude grows without bound as the input's magnitude increases. This captures the idea that large inputs always lead to large outputs in absolute value.

label: IsCoercive.continuousLinearEquivOfBilin
slogan: Given a complete real inner product space and a bounded bilinear form B that is coercive, the map sending each vector v to the unique vector representing the linear functional B(v, ·) via the inner product is a continuous linear isomorphism; this means it is a bijective, continuous, linear map with a continuous inverse.

label: IsCofinal
slogan: A set s is cofinal in an ordered type if for every element y, there is some element x in s such that y is less than or equal to x. This means the set s has elements that go arbitrarily far up in the order. No single element can be an upper bound for all elements of s.

label: IsCofinal.mem_of_isMax
slogan: If a subset s is cofinal in a partially ordered set and there is a maximum element a, then a must belong to s. This is because a cofinal subset must contain elements that are at least as large as every element in the set, and the maximum element cannot be exceeded. Since no element is larger than the maximum, the cofinal subset must include it.

label: IsCommJordan
slogan: A type A has a commutative Jordan multiplication if it comes with a binary operation that is commutative and satisfies the Jordan identity, meaning that for all elements a and b, the operation fulfills a*(b*a^2) = (a*b)*a^2, and this operation is part of a CommMagma structure.

label: IsCompact
slogan: A set is compact if every filter containing the set has a cluster point that lies within the set. This means that for any collection of subsets with the finite intersection property, there is a point in the set that is adherent to the behavior of the filter. The definition uses the structure of topological spaces and filters to formalize this notion of compactness.

label: IsCompact.add
slogan: If two sets are compact and addition is continuous in the space, then the set formed by adding each element of one set to each element of the other is also compact. This works in any space where addition behaves nicely with the topology. The result follows from the fact that the sum of the sets is the image of their product under the addition map, and continuous images of compact sets are compact.

label: IsCompact.exists_isLUB
slogan: If a set is nonempty and compact in a linearly ordered topological space where intervals extending to infinity are closed, then there is a smallest number that is greater than or equal to all elements of the set, and this number is actually in the set.

label: IsCompact.exists_isMaxOn
slogan: If a set is nonempty and compact, and a continuous function is defined on it, then the function reaches its highest value at some point in the set, provided the space has a linear order where upward-closed intervals are closed.

label: IsCompact.exists_isMinOn
slogan: If a nonempty set is compact and a function is continuous on that set, then the function reaches its smallest value at some point in the set. In other words, there is a point in the set where the function's value is less than or equal to its value at every other point in the set. This result depends on the set being compact and the function being continuous.

label: IsCompact.extremePoints_nonempty
slogan: In a locally convex topological vector space, every nonempty compact set has at least one extreme point — a point that cannot be expressed as an interior point of any line segment lying entirely within the set.

label: IsCompact.image
slogan: If a set is compact and a function is continuous, then the image of that set under the function is also compact. This means that continuous functions map compact sets to compact sets.

label: IsCompact.inter
slogan: If two sets are compact in a Hausdorff space, then their intersection is also compact, because compact sets in such spaces are closed and the intersection of closed sets is closed, and a closed subset of a compact set remains compact.

label: IsCompact.isBounded
slogan: In a pseudometric space, every compact set is bounded, meaning all its points lie within some finite distance of each other. This follows from the fact that compactness implies total boundedness, and a totally bounded set can be covered by finitely many bounded regions. Since finite unions of bounded sets are bounded, the whole set must be bounded.

label: IsCompact.isClosed
slogan: In a Hausdorff space, any compact set must be closed, meaning it contains all its limit points. This is because every filter that clusters near a point in the set must converge to a point within the set. The result uses properties of filters, neighborhoods, and the separation axiom to ensure no sequence or filter can approach a point outside the set.

label: IsCompact.isComplete
slogan: In a uniform space, if a set is compact, then every Cauchy filter in that set converges to a point within the set, meaning the set is complete.

label: IsCompact.isSeparable
slogan: Every compact set in a space that can be described by a pseudo-metric has a countable dense subset, meaning it is separable. This is because compact sets in such spaces are second-countable, and second-countable spaces always have a countable dense subset. The result connects compactness and separability in topological spaces with a pseudo-metric structure.

label: IsCompact.isSeqCompact
slogan: In a first-countable topological space, if a set is compact, then every sequence in that set has a subsequence that converges to a point within the set.

label: IsCompact.nonempty_iInter_of_sequence_nonempty_isCompact_isClosed
slogan: If you have a sequence of nonempty, compact, closed sets where each set is contained in the previous one, then their infinite intersection is not empty—there is at least one point common to all the sets. This holds in any topological space. The result depends on the properties of compactness and closedness.

label: IsCompact.tendsto_subseq
slogan: In a first-countable topological space, if a set is compact, then every sequence in that set has a subsequence that converges to a point within the set. This means there is always some point in the set and a strictly increasing sequence of indices such that the subsequence approaches that point. Convergence is defined in terms of neighborhoods in the topology.

label: IsCompact.uniformContinuousOn_of_continuous
slogan: If a function is continuous on a compact set in a uniform space, then it is uniformly continuous on that set. This means that when the domain is compact, continuity implies a stronger condition: the function's output doesn't change much whenever inputs are close, and this holds consistently across the whole set.

label: IsCompact.union
slogan: The union of two compact sets in a topological space is compact, meaning that if every filter with the finite intersection property has a cluster point in each set, then the same holds for their union. This is a special case of the fact that a finite union of compact sets is compact.

label: IsCompactOperator
slogan: A compact operator is a function between two topological vector spaces that maps some neighborhood of zero into a set whose closure is compact. This means the image of a small region around zero is contained in a compact set. The operator is compact if such a neighborhood exists.

label: IsCompactOperator.clm_comp
slogan: Composing a continuous linear map with a compact operator results in another compact operator, meaning the combined map still sends bounded sets to relatively compact sets. This holds because the compactness property is preserved when the output of a compact operator is further transformed by a continuous linear map. The composition remains well-behaved in terms of topology and linearity.

label: IsCompactOperator.continuous
slogan: A compact operator between normed spaces is always continuous, meaning it maps convergent sequences to convergent sequences and respects the topology of the spaces. This holds even though compactness is defined in terms of mapping bounded sets to relatively compact ones, not directly in terms of continuity. The result shows that the algebraic and topological structure of normed spaces ensures continuity automatically for such operators.

label: IsCompactOperator.hasEigenvalue_iff_mem_spectrum
slogan: For a compact operator on a Banach space, a nonzero scalar is an eigenvalue if and only if it is in the spectrum of the operator.

label: IsCompactOperator.hasEigenvalue_or_mem_resolventSet
slogan: For a compact operator T and a nonzero scalar μ, either μ is an eigenvalue of T or the operator (μI - T) has an inverse in the space of bounded operators.

label: IsCompactOperator.isCompact_closure_image_of_bounded
slogan: If a linear operator is compact, then the closure of the image of any bounded set under that operator is a compact set. This means that compact operators turn bounded sets into sets whose closures are compact. The result applies to normed or topological vector spaces where the operator is continuous and linear.

label: IsCompl
slogan: IsCompl means two elements x and y in a partially ordered set with a top and bottom element are complements if their join (least upper bound) is the top element and their meet (greatest lower bound) is the bottom element.

label: IsComplete
slogan: A space is complete if every Cauchy filter (a collection of sets where points eventually become arbitrarily close) converges to some point within the space. This means that any sequence or filter that behaves like it should have a limit actually does have a limit in the space, so no points are "missing". The completeness depends on the uniform structure that defines how close points can be to each other.

label: IsComplete.isClosed
slogan: In a uniform space that is also T0, any complete set contains all its limit points and is therefore closed; this means if a sequence or net in the set converges to some point, that point must already be in the set.

label: IsComplete.nonempty_iInter_of_nonempty_biInter
slogan: If you have a sequence of nonempty, closed, bounded sets in a complete metric space, and the diameter of these sets shrinks to zero, then there is at least one point common to all the sets. This happens because picking points from each finite intersection forms a Cauchy sequence, which must converge to a limit in the space. That limit lies in every set because they are closed.

label: IsConformalMap
slogan: A continuous linear map is called conformal if it is a nonzero scalar multiple of a linear isometry, meaning it preserves angles but may scale lengths. This means the map stretches or shrinks vectors uniformly in all directions by a nonzero factor, without distorting angles between them. The map must also be continuous and linear between two normed spaces over the same normed field.

label: IsConj
slogan: Two elements a and b in a monoid are conjugate if there exists another element c such that c multiplied by a equals b multiplied by c, meaning a can be transformed into b via multiplication by c and its inverse. This relation is defined using the SemiconjBy relation, which captures the equation c * a = b * c. Conjugacy expresses a symmetry between elements under the monoid's multiplication.

label: IsConj.setoid
slogan: IsConj.setoid defines when two elements in a monoid are considered conjugate, meaning one can be obtained from the other by multiplying with some element and its inverse. This conjugacy relation is reflexive, symmetric, and transitive, making it an equivalence relation. As a result, it allows forming equivalence classes and building a quotient type based on conjugacy.

label: IsConnected
slogan: A set is connected if it has at least one element and cannot be split into two nonempty, disjoint open subsets. This means that if the set is covered by two open sets that don't overlap, then the entire set must lie within one of them. The notion depends on the topology defined on the underlying space.

label: IsConnected.closure
slogan: If a set is connected, then its closure — which includes all the set's limit points — is also connected. This means you can't split the closure into two disjoint nonempty open parts if the original set was connected. The result holds in any topological space.

label: IsConnected.image
slogan: If a continuous function is applied to a connected set, the resulting image is also connected. This means that continuous functions do not break connected sets into separate pieces. A connected set is one that cannot be split into two disjoint nonempty open parts.

label: IsContMDiffRiemannianBundle
slogan: A Riemannian vector bundle is a family of inner product spaces parameterized by a smooth manifold, where the inner product varies continuously and smoothly with the base point. It combines the structures of a smooth vector bundle and a smoothly varying metric on each fiber. The condition IsContMDiffRiemannianBundle specifies that the bundle has a smooth dependence of the scalar product on the base space.

label: IsCovariantDerivativeOn
slogan: A covariant derivative on a vector bundle over a manifold is a function that takes a section of the bundle and returns a linear map from tangent vectors to changes in the section, defined over a subset of the manifold, such that it is additive and satisfies the Leibniz rule for differentiable sections. The function acts pointwise and respects the vector space structure of the bundle. The order of arguments in the function is arranged so that the tangent vector comes after the section and base point.

label: IsCoveringMap
slogan: A covering map is a continuous function f from a space E to a space X such that every point in X has a neighborhood whose preimage under f is a disjoint union of open sets in E, each of which is mapped homeomorphically onto the neighborhood by f, and the fibers (preimages of points) are discrete.

label: IsCoveringMap.existsUnique_continuousMap_lifts_of_range_le
slogan: If A is a path-connected and locally path-connected space, and f is a continuous map from A to X, then f can be lifted in exactly one way to a continuous map from A to the covering space E, starting at a specified point e0 above f(a0), provided that the image of the fundamental group of A under f is contained within the image of the fundamental group of E under the covering map.

label: IsCoveringMap.injective_path_homotopic_map
slogan: A covering map p : E → X ensures that different paths in E which start and end at the same points and project to the same path in X under p must actually be the same path in E, up to homotopy. This means the induced map on homotopy classes of paths is injective. In particular, the map p induces an injective function on fundamental groups.

label: IsCoveringMap.isLocalHomeomorph
slogan: A covering map between topological spaces is always a local homeomorphism, meaning each point in the domain has a neighborhood where the map restricts to a homeomorphism onto its image.

label: IsCoveringMap.liftHomotopy
slogan: Given a covering map p from space E to space X, a homotopy H in X starting at p(f(a)) for each point a in A, and a continuous map f from A to E, there exists a continuous lift of H to E starting at f. This lift is a homotopy in E that projects down to H via p. The existence of such a lift means covering maps have the homotopy lifting property.

label: IsCoveringMap.liftPath
slogan: Given a covering map p from a space E to a space X, a continuous path in X starting at p(e) can be uniquely lifted to a continuous path in E starting at the point e. This lift is a continuous function from the unit interval to E that projects down to the original path via p. The result provides an explicit construction of such a lifted path.

label: IsCoveringMap.liftPath_apply_one_eq_of_homotopicRel
slogan: If two paths in a topological space are homotopic relative to their endpoints and start at the same point in a covering space, then their lifts under a covering map end at the same point in the covering space.

label: IsCoveringMap.monodromy
slogan: For a covering map p from E to X, the monodromy maps a point in the fiber over x to the endpoint of the unique lift of a path class starting at x, and this assignment depends only on the homotopy class of the path.

label: IsCoveringMap.monodromyFunctor
slogan: Given a covering map p from a space E to a space X, the monodromy functor assigns to each point in X the set of points in E that map to it, and to each homotopy class of paths from x to y in X, a function that maps the fiber over x to the fiber over y by lifting the path. This assignment respects the composition of paths and identities, making it a functor from the fundamental groupoid of X to the category of types.

label: IsCoxeterGroup
slogan: A group is a Coxeter group if it can be described by a set of generators and relations determined by a symmetric matrix with 1s on the diagonal and other entries being natural numbers not equal to 1. This matrix, called a Coxeter matrix, encodes how the generators interact. The group is then isomorphic to the one defined by those generators and relations.

label: IsCyclic
slogan: A type is cyclic if all its elements can be produced by repeatedly applying the group operation to a single element, using integer exponents. This means every element can be written as some integer power of a fixed generator. The definition requires the type to support exponentiation with integer exponents.

label: IsCyclic.card_orderOf_eq_totient
slogan: In a finite cyclic group, the number of elements whose order is exactly d is equal to the number of integers between 1 and d that are relatively prime to d, which is given by Euler's totient function of d. This holds for any positive divisor d of the group's total size.

label: IsCyclic.commGroup
slogan: A cyclic group is one where every element can be written as a power of a single generator; because combining powers of the same element depends only on addition of exponents, which is commutative, the group operation itself must be commutative.
