This means that any cyclic group automatically satisfies the properties of a commutative group. The declaration constructs a commutative group structure from a cyclic group.

label: IsCyclic.exists_generator
slogan: A cyclic group has an element such that every group member can be written as an integer power of that element. The set of all such powers forms a subgroup containing every element of the group. This guarantees that the group is generated entirely by one element.

label: IsCyclotomicExtension.autEquivPow
slogan: The function autEquivPow gives a one-to-one correspondence between automorphisms of a cyclotomic extension field L over a field K and the multiplicative units modulo n, where each automorphism is determined by mapping a primitive nth root of unity μ to μ raised to a power k that is coprime to n. This means every symmetry of the field extension that fixes K comes from raising roots of unity to powers that are invertible modulo n. The correspondence preserves the group structure of composition and multiplication.

label: IsDedekindDomain
slogan: A Dedekind domain is a commutative ring with no zero divisors where every nonzero prime ideal is maximal, the ring is Noetherian, and it is integrally closed; equivalently, every nonzero fractional ideal has a multiplicative inverse. Such rings ensure unique factorization of ideals into prime ideals and generalize the integers in number fields. The condition can be checked either algebraically or through ideal invertibility.

label: IsDedekindDomain.flat_iff_torsion_eq_bot
slogan: A module over a commutative ring that is a Dedekind domain is flat if and only if its torsion submodule contains only the zero element, meaning no nonzero element is annihilated by a regular ring element. This means flatness is equivalent to being torsion-free in this setting.

label: IsDenseInducing.extend
slogan: If a function i from one topological space to another has a dense image and induces the topology on its domain, then any continuous function from the domain to a Hausdorff space can be uniquely extended to the whole codomain of i by taking limits along the dense image. The extension at a point b is defined as the limit of f(x) as i(x) approaches b, using the topology of the target space. This works because points in the closure of the image can be approximated by values of i(x), and the Hausdorff condition ensures the limit is unique.

label: IsDiscreteValuationRing
slogan: A discrete valuation ring is a commutative ring with no zero divisors, exactly one maximal ideal, and where every nonzero ideal is generated by a single element. It combines the properties of being a local ring, a principal ideal ring, and an integral domain. Such rings have a simple ideal structure and support a well-behaved notion of divisibility.

label: IsDomain
slogan: A domain is a nontrivial semiring where you can cancel multiplication by a nonzero element: if a ≠ 0 and a * b = a * c, then b = c, and similarly for multiplication on the right. This means the semiring has no zero divisors and at least two elements.

label: IsExposed
slogan: A set B is exposed with respect to A if there exists a continuous linear functional such that B contains exactly those points in A where this functional achieves its maximum value. This means B is the set of maximizers of some linear function over A. The base field 𝕜 has a topology and algebraic structure that support continuity and linearity.

label: IsExtreme
slogan: A set B is an extreme subset of A if B is contained in A and whenever a point in B lies on an open line segment between two points in A, then both endpoints of that segment must also be in B. This means B captures all boundary points of such segments passing through it. The condition ensures B is "closed" under taking endpoints of internal segments.

label: IsFiberBundle.isCoveringMap
slogan: If a map f from a space E to a space X has the property that every point in X has a neighborhood that lifts to a product of that neighborhood with a discrete space, then f is a covering map. This means f is continuous and each point in X has an evenly covered neighborhood. The condition relies on the existence of local trivializations respecting the topology and the discrete nature of the fiber.

label: IsField
slogan: A type R is a field if it has addition and multiplication that follow basic arithmetic rules (like a semiring) and every nonzero element has a multiplicative inverse, meaning division by any nonzero element is possible. This allows full arithmetic including reciprocals for all nonzero elements. The structure extends semirings by ensuring that all nonzero elements can be divided.

label: IsFoelner.amenable
slogan: If a group action on a measure space has a Følner sequence with respect to a non-trivial filter, then there exists a finitely additive probability measure on the space that is invariant under the group action. This means the measure assigns total size 1 to the whole space, adds properly on disjoint measurable sets, and remains unchanged when sets are transformed by the group.

label: IsFractionRing
slogan: A fraction ring is a structure where a commutative semiring R is extended to a larger semiring K such that every nonzero element of R that doesn't cause zero when multiplied (a non-zero divisor) becomes invertible in K, meaning division by such elements is possible. This extension is done via localization at the set of non-zero divisors, and K carries an algebra structure over R. The map from R to K makes every non-zero divisor in R invertible in K, and every element of K can be expressed as a fraction of an element of R by a non-zero divisor.

label: IsFractionRing.toField
slogan: If A is a commutative ring with no zero divisors (a domain) and K is its fraction ring, then K supports division by any nonzero element and forms a field. This means every nonzero element in K has a multiplicative inverse. The algebraic structure of A extends to K in a way that allows safe division.

label: IsGalois
slogan: A field extension E over F is Galois if it is both normal (every irreducible polynomial from F with a root in E splits completely in E) and separable (the minimal polynomials of elements in E have no repeated roots). This means E is the splitting field of a separable polynomial over F, and the symmetries of E that fix F form a group. The condition ensures the extension has a clean algebraic structure with no redundant or degenerate behavior.

label: IsGalois.intermediateFieldEquivSubgroup
slogan: In a finite Galois field extension, there is a one-to-one, order-reversing match between fields lying between the base and extension fields and the subgroups of the Galois group; each intermediate field corresponds to the group of automorphisms that fix it, and each subgroup corresponds to the field elements it fixes.

label: IsGreatest
slogan: IsGreatest s a means that a is an element of the set s, and every other element in s is less than or equal to a according to the ≤ relation defined for that type.

label: IsGroupLikeElem
slogan: A group-like element in a coalgebra over a commutative semiring is an element that maps to 1 under the counit and, under comultiplication, maps to the tensor product of the element with itself.

label: IsGroupLikeElem.antipode_antipode
slogan: If an element in a Hopf algebra is group-like, then applying the antipode operation twice returns the original element. This means that the antipode of the antipode of such an element is equal to the element itself. The result relies on the structure of Hopf algebras and the properties of group-like elements.

label: IsHilbertSum
slogan: A Hilbert sum of a family of Hilbert spaces is a complete Hilbert space equipped with linear isometries from each of the family's spaces, such that every element in the sum can be represented as a convergent sum of elements from the images of these isometries. The combined map from the abstract l2 space of the family to the Hilbert sum is an isometric isomorphism and covers the entire space. This setup generalizes the idea of decomposing a Hilbert space into orthogonal parts indexed by a type.

label: IsHomeomorph
slogan: A homeomorphism is a one-to-one and onto function between two topological spaces such that both the function and its inverse are continuous, meaning open sets in one space correspond exactly to open sets in the other. The condition IsHomeomorph is true for a function if it meets these requirements. It relies on the definitions of topological spaces and continuity.

label: IsIdempotentElem
slogan: An element a is idempotent if multiplying it by itself results in the same element, meaning a * a = a, for any type that has a multiplication operation defined. This property depends on the type supporting multiplication through the Mul interface. The concept applies generally to any algebraic structure where such an operation exists.

label: IsIdempotentElem.one
slogan: In a structure with multiplication and a multiplicative identity (one), the identity element satisfies one * one = one, meaning it is idempotent. This holds because multiplying one by itself returns one, as guaranteed by the identity property of multiplication.

label: IsIntegral
slogan: A value x in a ring A is integral over a subring R if there is a polynomial with coefficients in R, having 1 as its leading coefficient, such that x satisfies this polynomial when evaluated in A. This means x is a root of a monic polynomial whose coefficients come from R, using the algebra structure to interpret scalar multiplication. The rings involved are commutative, and R maps into A via a ring homomorphism that respects the algebra structure.

label: IsIntegral.add
slogan: If two elements in an algebra over a commutative ring are integral over that ring—meaning each is a root of a monic polynomial with coefficients in the ring—then their sum is also integral over the same ring.

label: IsIntegralCurve
slogan: A function γ from the real numbers to a manifold M is an integral curve of a vector field v if, at every point in time, the derivative of γ matches the direction and magnitude of v at the corresponding point on the manifold. This means γ follows the flow of the vector field v exactly. The setup assumes M has a smooth structure modeled on a normed space, and v assigns a tangent vector to each point of M.

label: IsIntegralCurveAt
slogan: IsIntegralCurveAt means that a path γ from real numbers to a manifold M follows the direction of a given vector field v near a specific point t₀, so that the derivative of γ at t₀ matches the vector field at that location. The behavior of γ far away from t₀ does not matter. This definition works within a mathematical framework that supports smooth spaces and derivatives.

label: IsIntegralCurveOn
slogan: A curve γ from the real numbers to a manifold M is an integral curve of a vector field v on a set s if, for every time t in s, the derivative of γ at t matches the vector v at the point γ(t), and γ is continuously differentiable on s; the values of γ outside s are ignored.

label: IsIntegrallyClosed
slogan: A commutative ring R is integrally closed if every element in its field of fractions that is a root of a monic polynomial with coefficients in R must already be an element of R. This means R contains all the elements of its fraction ring that are integral over it. It is equivalent to saying R is integrally closed in its own fraction ring.

label: IsInvariant
slogan: A set s is invariant under a function phi from tau to alpha if applying phi with any t from tau maps elements of s only to other elements within s. This means the image of s under phi t is always contained in s for all t in tau.

label: IsIrreducible
slogan: A set is irreducible if it is not empty and cannot be covered by two proper nonempty closed subsets. This means the set cannot be split into two smaller closed pieces that are both nonempty. The concept relies on the topology of the space and only applies to nonempty sets.

label: IsJordan
slogan: A type A has a Jordan multiplication if it comes with a binary operation * (from Mul) that satisfies the properties of a non-commutative Jordan product. This means the operation is not necessarily commutative but follows specific algebraic rules typical of Jordan algebras. The IsJordan class marks such types with this structure.

label: IsLUB
slogan: A value is the least upper bound of a set if it is greater than or equal to every element in the set and is less than or equal to any other such upper bound. This means it is the smallest possible upper bound for the set, using the standard ≤ relation. The definition relies on the concept of upper bounds and a type equipped with a ≤ ordering.

label: IsLeast
slogan: IsLeast s a means that a is an element of the set s and no other element in s is strictly less than a, according to the ≤ ordering. In other words, a is the smallest element in s.

label: IsLeast.unique
slogan: If two elements are both the smallest in a set according to a partial order, then they must be the same element, since a partial order ensures that if each is less than or equal to the other, they are equal.

label: IsLeftCancelMul
slogan: A type has the IsLeftCancelMul property if, for all elements a, b, and c, the equation a * b = a * c implies that b = c. This means multiplying on the left by any element does not lose information, so each left multiplication map is one-to-one. The type must support a multiplication operation defined by the Mul class.

label: IsLieAbelian
slogan: A Lie algebra is called abelian when the bracket of any two elements is zero, meaning the operation always gives the zero element. This implies the algebra has no non-commutative behavior. The type must support a zero element and a bracket operation between its elements.

label: IsLindelof.image
slogan: If a set is Lindelof and a function is continuous, then the image of that set under the function is also Lindelof, meaning every open cover of the image has a countable subcover.

label: IsLinearMap
slogan: A LinearMap is a function between two modules over a semiring that preserves addition and scalar multiplication, meaning f(a + b) = f(a) + f(b) and f(r * a) = r * f(a) for all elements a, b and scalars r.

label: IsLocalExtr
slogan: A point a is a local extremum of a function f if, for all points sufficiently close to a, the values of f are either all at least f(a) or all at most f(a), in terms of the preorder on the codomain and the topology on the domain. This means f(a) is either a local minimum or a local maximum near a. The condition is defined using neighborhood filters to capture "closeness" around a.

label: IsLocalExtr.deriv_eq_zero
slogan: If a real function has a local maximum or minimum at a point and is differentiable there, then its derivative at that point is zero.

label: IsLocalExtr.fderiv_eq_zero
slogan: If a function has a local maximum or minimum at a point and is differentiable there, then its derivative at that point is zero. This means the slope of the function must be flat at any local extremum where the derivative exists.

label: IsLocalExtr.hasDerivAt_eq_zero
slogan: If a real-valued function has a local maximum or minimum at a point and is differentiable there, then the derivative at that point must be zero.

label: IsLocalExtr.hasFDerivAt_eq_zero
slogan: If a function from a real normed space to the real numbers has a local minimum or maximum at a point and is differentiable there, then its derivative at that point is zero. This means the linear approximation of the function at the extremum has a slope of zero. The result holds for functions between general normed spaces using Fréchet differentiability.

label: IsLocalExtrOn
slogan: A point a is a local extremum of a function f on a set s if, for all points y near a within s, the value f(a) is either <= f(y) or f(y) <= f(a) according to the preorder, when considering the topology on the space. This is determined by checking the behavior of f in a neighborhood of a restricted to s using filters. It combines the concepts of local minima and maxima in ordered topological spaces.

label: IsLocalExtrOn.exists_linear_map_of_hasStrictFDerivAt
slogan: If a real-valued function φ has a local maximum or minimum at a point x₀ subject to the constraint that f(x) = f(x₀), and both φ and f are strictly differentiable at x₀ with f mapping into a complete normed space, then there are constants Λ and Λ₀, not both zero, such that the linear combination Λ times the derivative of f plus Λ₀ times the derivative of φ equals zero for all directions.

label: IsLocalExtrOn.exists_multipliers_of_hasStrictFDerivAt
slogan: If a function φ has a local maximum or minimum at a point x₀ subject to constraints f i x = f i x₀ for a finite set of functions f i, and all these functions are strictly differentiable at x₀, then the derivatives of φ and the f i at x₀ are linearly dependent: there are real numbers Λ i and Λ₀, not all zero, such that the linear combination Σ Λ i * f' i + Λ₀ * φ' equals zero.

label: IsLocalExtrOn.exists_multipliers_of_hasStrictFDerivAt_1d
slogan: If a real-valued function φ has a local maximum or minimum at a point x₀ subject to the constraint that another real-valued function f equals f(x₀), and both functions are strictly differentiable at x₀, then there are real numbers a and b, not both zero, such that the linear combination a times the derivative of f plus b times the derivative of φ is zero.

label: IsLocalExtrOn.linear_dependent_of_hasStrictFDerivAt
slogan: If a function φ has a local maximum or minimum at a point x₀ subject to constraints f i x = f i x₀, and all functions involved are strictly differentiable at x₀, then the derivatives of φ and the f i at x₀ are linearly dependent.

label: IsLocalHom
slogan: A local homomorphism is a function between monoids that maps non-invertible elements to non-invertible elements, preserving the structure of units. It is used especially in the context of local rings, where it ensures the maximal ideal is preserved under the map. The function must respect the monoid operations and be compatible with the notion of invertibility.

label: IsLocalMax
slogan: A point a is a local maximum of a function f if, for some neighborhood around a, the value of f at a is not exceeded by f at any nearby point, meaning f(x) <= f(a) for all x close to a, according to the topology and the preorder on the codomain. This is defined using the neighborhood filter at a and the preorder structure on the target space. The condition holds when the neighborhood filter eventually satisfies f(x) <= f(a).

label: IsLocalMin
slogan: A point a is a local minimum of a function f if, for all points near a (in the topological sense), the value of f at those points is at least as large as f(a), with respect to a given preorder. This is formalized using neighborhood filters to capture the idea that the condition holds for all points sufficiently close to a. The definition depends on the topology of the domain and the order structure of the codomain.

label: IsLocalMin.fderiv_eq_zero
slogan: If a function has a local minimum at a point and is differentiable there, then its derivative at that point is zero. This means that whenever a function reaches a low point in its immediate neighborhood and has a well-defined slope, that slope must be flat.

label: IsLocalRing
slogan: A local ring is a semiring with at least two elements where the sum of two elements can only be a unit if at least one of them is a unit, meaning non-units are closed under addition.

label: IsLocalRing.ResidueField.field
slogan: If a commutative ring has a unique maximal ideal, then the quotient of the ring by that ideal is a field, meaning every nonzero element in the quotient has a multiplicative inverse. This quotient field is known as the residue field of the local ring. The result ensures that the algebraic structure of the quotient supports division for nonzero elements, inheriting commutativity and inverse properties from the ring and maximality of the ideal.

label: IsLocalRing.maximal_ideal_unique
slogan: In a local ring, there is only one maximal ideal, and it is made up of all elements that do not have multiplicative inverses.

label: IsLocalRing.mem_maximalIdeal
slogan: In a local ring, an element is in the unique maximal ideal exactly when it has no multiplicative inverse. This means the maximal ideal is made up of all elements that cannot be inverted. The result relies on the fact that in such rings, the set of non-units forms an ideal.

label: IsLocalRing.notMem_maximalIdeal
slogan: In a local ring, an element is not in the maximal ideal if and only if it has a multiplicative inverse; equivalently, the maximal ideal consists precisely of those elements that are not invertible.

label: IsLocalRing.of_unique_max_ideal
slogan: If a commutative semiring has exactly one maximal ideal, then it is a local ring, meaning all non-unit elements form a single ideal. This unique maximal ideal contains every proper ideal, and any element not in it has a multiplicative inverse. The existence of only one such maximal ideal ensures the ring has a well-defined set of "small" elements, namely the non-units.

label: IsLocalRing.ringJacobson_eq_maximalIdeal
slogan: In a local ring, the Jacobson radical — the intersection of all maximal ideals — is exactly the unique maximal ideal, which consists of all non-units. Since there is only one maximal ideal in such a ring, the set of elements that are in every maximal ideal is just that single ideal. This identifies the Jacobson radical with the largest proper ideal of the ring.

label: IsLocalization
slogan: IsLocalization means that a ring map from a commutative semiring R to another ring S makes all elements of a given submonoid M of R invertible in S, and every element of S can be expressed as a fraction of an element of R divided by an element of M, using the algebra structure that connects R and S.

label: IsLocalization.AtPrime.isDiscreteValuationRing_of_dedekind_domain
slogan: If a ring is a Dedekind domain and you form the localization at a nonzero prime ideal, the resulting ring is a discrete valuation ring. This means the localized ring is a local Noetherian domain with exactly one nonzero prime ideal and is not a field. The result follows from the fact that localizations of Dedekind domains at prime ideals have the required properties.

label: IsLocalization.AtPrime.isLocalRing
slogan: Localizing a commutative ring at a prime ideal results in a ring where the sum of any two non-units is still a non-unit, meaning all non-units form a single maximal ideal.

label: IsLocalization.epi
slogan: If a ring homomorphism from a localization of a commutative ring maps elements in such a way that every element of the target ring can be expressed as a fraction of elements from the original ring, then this homomorphism is surjective in the categorical sense, meaning it cannot be canceled on the right when composing with other homomorphisms.

label: IsLocalization.flat
slogan: Localizing a module over a commutative ring at a multiplicative submonoid results in a flat module, meaning that tensoring with this localized module preserves exact sequences. This ensures that extending scalars via localization does not introduce unexpected torsion or collapse structure. The result applies to any module and submonoid satisfying the localization conditions.

label: IsLocalization.orderIsoOfPrime
slogan: There is a one-to-one, order-preserving correspondence between prime ideals in a localized ring and prime ideals in the original ring that do not share any elements with the multiplicative set used for localization. This bijection is given by taking images and preimages under the localization map, and it respects the inclusion of ideals.

label: IsLocalizedModule.map_exact
slogan: Localizing a sequence of module homomorphisms over a commutative semiring preserves exactness, meaning if the image of one map equals the kernel of the next before localization, the same holds after localization. This holds for modules connected by linear maps that are compatible with the localization at a submonoid. The localized maps are constructed using the natural maps induced by the localization process.

label: IsLowerModularLattice
slogan: A lower modular lattice is a type with meet and join operations where, if x is less than or equal to z, then x joined with the meet of y and z equals the meet of (x joined with y) and z. This condition ensures a consistent relationship between the operations when one element is below another.

label: IsManifold
slogan: A manifold is a topological space that near each point looks like a model space with corners, where the local coordinates (charts) are related by smooth transition maps belonging to a specified groupoid, ensuring consistent geometric behavior; it is built over a normed vector space on a nontrivially normed field, with smoothness up to a specified degree (including infinitely smooth). The structure combines topology, algebra, and analysis to support differential geometry on spaces that may have boundaries or corners. Charts map parts of the space to open sets in a model space, and the degree of

label: IsMax
slogan: A value x is the maximum in a set if every other element in the set is less than or equal to x, and no element in the set is greater than x.

label: IsMaxAntichain
slogan: A set s is a maximum antichain under relation r if no two different elements in s are comparable by r, and every other set with that same property is contained within s. This means s is the largest possible set of mutually incomparable elements. The function s may be used in specific contexts involving groups and measures to build or study such sets.

label: IsMaxOn
slogan: IsMaxOn f s x means that for all y in the set s, the value of f at x is at least as large as f at y, according to the preorder on the codomain of f. This condition holds when the principal filter of the set where f achieves its maximum includes all points in s. It expresses that f attains its maximum at x within the subset s.

label: IsMaxOn.isLocalMax
slogan: If a function f takes its maximum value at a point a within a set s, and the set s contains a neighborhood around a, then f has a local maximum at a. This means f(a) is at least as large as f(x) for all x sufficiently close to a. The result applies in any space with a topology and a preorder.

label: IsMaxOn.neg
slogan: If a function f achieves its maximum value at a point x within a set s, then the function -f achieves its minimum value at that same point x. This is true in any setting where the values form a partially ordered abelian group and negation reverses the order. The reason is that negating all function values reverses inequalities, turning maximums into minimums.

label: IsMinOn.of_isLocalMin_of_convex_univ
slogan: If a function is convex on the entire space and has a local minimum at a point, then that point is also a global minimum: the function value at that point is less than or equal to the function value at any other point.

label: IsModularLattice
slogan: A modular lattice is a type with well-defined operations for combining any two elements into their smallest common upper bound (sup) and largest common lower bound (inf), and it satisfies the condition that if a is less than or equal to c, then a combined with the lower bound of b and c gives the same result as first combining a and b above and then taking the lower bound with c. This ensures a consistent relationship between how elements are joined and met when one element lies below another.

label: IsMoritaEquivalent
slogan: Two R-algebras A and B are Morita equivalent if their module categories are equivalent as R-linear categories, meaning their structures for representing modules over R are essentially the same. This equivalence captures a deep relationship between the algebras that goes beyond simple isomorphism. The property is expressed as a proposition that depends on R being a commutative semiring and A and B being rings with R-algebra structures.

label: IsNilpotent
slogan: A type is nilpotent if, for every element in the type, raising it to some natural number power results in zero. This means repeated multiplication of any element by itself eventually becomes zero. The type must support both a zero element and exponentiation with natural numbers.

label: IsNilpotent.to_isSolvable
slogan: If a group's lower central series eventually reaches the trivial subgroup, then its derived series will also eventually reach the trivial subgroup, meaning every nilpotent group is solvable.

label: IsNoetherian
slogan: A type is Noetherian if all its submodules are finitely generated, meaning there are no infinite increasing chains of submodules. This applies to modules over a semiring, where the module has a commutative addition with zero and scalar multiplication that respects the semiring's operations. It captures the idea that substructures cannot grow indefinitely in a well-behaved algebraic system.

label: IsNoetherianRing
slogan: A Noetherian ring is a semiring where every ideal can be generated by a finite number of elements, meaning any subset closed under addition and multiplication by ring elements is produced by combining finitely many elements using ring operations. This imposes a finiteness condition that limits how complex the ideals in the ring can be.

label: IsNonarchimedeanLocalField
slogan: A nonarchimedean local field is a field with a topology defined by a nontrivial, discrete, rank-one valuation, making it locally compact, complete, and ensuring all field operations are continuous; its topology comes from a valuation that measures the size of elements, and the unit ball is compact.

label: IsOpen
slogan: A set is open if it belongs to a topology, where open sets include the empty set and the entire space, and are closed under finite intersections and arbitrary unions.

label: IsOpen.baireSpace
slogan: If a topological space is a Baire space, then any open subset of it, with the subspace topology, is also a Baire space. This means that in such an open subset, countable intersections of dense open sets are still dense. The result follows because the inclusion of an open set into the whole space preserves the necessary topological structure.

label: IsOpen.exists_eq_add_of_deriv_eq
slogan: If two functions have the same derivative at every point in an open and connected set, then they differ by a constant on that set.

label: IsOpen.isConnected_iff_isPathConnected
slogan: In a locally path connected space, an open set is connected if and only if it is path connected. This means that if the set cannot be split into two disjoint nonempty open parts, then any two points in it can be joined by a continuous path. The result equates global connectedness with the existence of paths within open sets.

label: IsOpen.is_const_of_fderiv_eq_zero
slogan: If a function has a derivative of zero at every point in an open and connected set, then the function takes the same value at all points in that set. This means the function is constant on the set, provided the domain is open and cannot be split into separate open pieces. The result holds for functions between spaces like real or complex vector spaces where derivatives are defined.

label: IsOpen.locallyConnectedSpace
slogan: If a set is open in a locally connected topological space, then the set itself, with the subspace topology, is also locally connected. This means every point in the open set has arbitrarily small connected neighborhoods within the set. The local connectedness of the whole space passes down to its open subsets.

label: IsOpen.measurableSet
slogan: In a space where the measurable sets include all open sets by design, every open set is automatically measurable. This happens when the topology's open sets are part of the sigma-algebra defining measurability. Such spaces ensure that topological and measure-theoretic concepts work together smoothly.

label: IsOpen.polishSpace
slogan: An open subset of a Polish space (a space with a complete metric and a countable base for its topology) is itself a Polish space under the subspace topology. This means the open subset has a complete metric and is second-countable. No additional conditions are needed beyond the set being open.

label: IsOpenMap
slogan: A function is called an open map if it sends every open set in its domain to an open set in the target space, where openness is defined by the given topologies on both spaces. This means that whenever you apply the function to an open set, the resulting set in the codomain is also considered open. The property depends on the topologies of both the starting and ending space.

label: IsOrderedMonoid
slogan: A type is an ordered monoid if it has a commutative monoid operation and a partial order where multiplying both sides of an inequality by the same element preserves the order; specifically, if a <= b, then a * c <= b * c for all c.

label: IsOrderedRing
slogan: An ordered ring is a set with addition and multiplication that follow basic arithmetic rules, has a partial order where adding or multiplying by positive elements preserves inequalities, and ensures that zero is less than or equal to one. The order behaves like the usual ordering on numbers, so inequalities stay consistent when performing operations. It combines algebra and order in a way that matches how numbers work in everyday math.

label: IsPGroup
slogan: A p-group is a group in which every element has an order that is a power of a fixed prime number p, meaning for each element g, some power of g equals the identity and that power is p raised to a natural number. The definition assumes the group has standard multiplication, inverses, and an identity, and uses natural number exponents in a multiplicative setting. It applies to any type equipped with a group structure and a chosen prime p.

label: IsPGroup.card_modEq_card_fixedPoints
slogan: If a finite group has size a power of a prime p, then the total number of elements in a finite set being acted on by the group is congruent modulo p to the number of elements that stay fixed under the group action.

label: IsPGroup.center_nontrivial
slogan: If a finite group's size is a power of a prime number, then there is at least one non-identity element that commutes with every other element in the group. This means the group's center contains more than just the identity.

label: IsPGroup.commutative_of_card_eq_prime_sq
slogan: If a group has exactly p^2 elements, where p is a prime number, then the group is commutative: for any two elements a and b, a * b equals b * a. This happens because the group's size forces its structure to be abelian.

label: IsPGroup.exists_le_sylow
slogan: If every element in a subgroup has an order that is a power of a prime p, then there exists a Sylow p-subgroup of the whole group that contains this subgroup.

label: IsPGroup.isNilpotent
slogan: Every finite group whose size is a power of a prime number has a nontrivial center and can be broken down into a sequence of central extensions, meaning it is nilpotent. This is proven by induction, using that quotients of such groups remain groups of prime power order. In short, all finite p-groups are nilpotent.

label: IsPathConnected.image
slogan: If a continuous function maps a path-connected set to another space, then the resulting image set is also path-connected, meaning any two points in the image can be joined by a continuous path within that set. This happens because continuous functions preserve the connected structure of the original set.

label: IsPathConnected.subset_pathComponent
slogan: If a subset of a topological space is path connected, then all its points lie within the same path component of the space, specifically the one containing any given point of the subset.

label: IsPicardLindelof
slogan: The declaration defines a condition that ensures a time-dependent vector field f has a unique solution curve starting near a point x₀, within a certain time interval and bounded region, provided f meets specific continuity and boundedness criteria. It allows the initial position of the solution to be close to, but not necessarily exactly, x₀. The parameters control the size of the region, bounds on f, and the interval over which the solution exists.

label: IsPicardLindelof.exists_eq_forall_mem_Icc_hasDerivWithinAt
slogan: There exists a function α defined on a closed time interval [tmin, tmax] such that α starts at a given point x near x₀ and its derivative at each time t equals f(t, α(t)), provided f satisfies certain smoothness and boundedness conditions near x₀ over that interval. The function α follows the direction field given by f at every point in the interval. This guarantees a local solution to the differential equation passing through x at time t₀.

label: IsPicardLindelof.exists_eq_forall_mem_Icc_hasDerivWithinAt₀
slogan: There exists a function α that starts at x₀ when time t equals t₀, and for every time t between tmin and tmax, the derivative of α at t exists and equals f(t, α(t)), provided f satisfies certain continuity, boundedness, and Lipschitz conditions near x₀ over the interval [tmin, tmax].

label: IsPicardLindelof.exists_forall_mem_closedBall_eq_forall_mem_Icc_hasDerivWithinAt
slogan: If a time-dependent vector field f satisfies certain smoothness and boundedness conditions near a point x0, then for every initial position close to x0, there exists a unique solution curve starting at that position, defined on a given time interval, whose derivative at each time matches the vector field at that point in space and time.

label: IsPicardLindelof.exists_forall_mem_closedBall_eq_hasDerivWithinAt_lipschitzOnWith
slogan: If a time-dependent vector field satisfies certain smoothness and boundedness conditions near a point, then there exists a unique solution curve starting near that point, defined for a short time interval, and the solution depends in a Lipschitz continuous way on the initial position.

label: IsPreconnected.image
slogan: If a function is continuous on a preconnected set, then the set of values it takes on that set is also preconnected. This means continuous functions map preconnected sets to preconnected sets. You can't turn a preconnected set into a disconnected one by applying a continuous function.

label: IsPrimitiveRoot.geom_sum_eq_zero
slogan: If a is a primitive root of unity of order k greater than 1 in a commutative ring with no zero divisors, then the sum 1 + a + a^2 + ... + a^(k-1) equals zero. This happens because a is not equal to 1, so (a - 1) is not zero, and multiplying the sum by (a - 1) gives zero, forcing the sum to be zero. The result holds in any integral domain.

label: IsPrincipalIdealRing
slogan: A ring is called a principal ideal ring if every ideal in the ring is generated by just one element, meaning each ideal is made up of all multiples of that element. This applies to rings built on a semiring structure, where ideals act like submodules. Such rings have a simpler ideal structure, which makes algebraic work easier.

label: IsProperMap.isCompact_preimage
slogan: If a function is proper, then the inverse image of any compact set under that function is also compact. This means that when a set in the output space is compact, all the points mapping into it from the input space form a compact set. Proper maps ensure compactness is preserved going backward.

label: IsPurelyInseparable
slogan: A purely inseparable field extension is one where every element in the larger field, when raised to a high enough power, lands in the smaller base field, and this usually happens in fields where the characteristic is a prime number. The condition means that the minimal polynomial of each element has just one root, so there are no distinct conjugate elements. This declaration defines a property to recognize such extensions in algebraic structures with compatible ring and scalar multiplication operations.

label: IsQuotientMap.of_surjective_continuous
slogan: A continuous and surjective function from a compact space to a Hausdorff space is a quotient map, meaning the topology on the target space is fully determined by the function: a set in the target is open if and only if its preimage in the source is open.

label: IsReduced
slogan: A type has the IsReduced property if, for any nonzero element, raising it to any natural number power never gives zero. This means the only element that can become zero through repeated exponentiation is zero itself. It ensures no nonzero element acts nilpotent under the power operation.

label: IsRegularLocalRing
slogan: A regular local ring is a Noetherian local ring where the maximal ideal can be generated by a number of elements equal to the dimension of the ring. It is a property assigned to commutative rings that are both local and Noetherian. This property holds when the minimal number of generators of the maximal ideal matches the Krull dimension of the ring.

label: IsRiemannianManifold
slogan: A space is called a Riemannian manifold if it has a distance function that comes from measuring the lengths of smooth paths, where the length of each path is computed using an inner product on the tangent space at each point. The tangent spaces must already have an inner product, and the distance between two points must equal the infimum of the lengths of all C^1 paths connecting them. This is a property (not a structure) that can be satisfied by a space with the right combination of topology, smooth structure, and geometry.

label: IsSaddlePointOn
slogan: A pair (a, b) is a saddle point of a function f on sets X and Y if, for every x in X and every y in Y, the value f(a, y) is less than or equal to f(x, b), using the preorder relation on the codomain of f. The elements a and b do not need to be in X and Y, respectively. This means f achieves a minimum with respect to the first argument and a maximum with respect to the second at (a, b), in a pairwise comparison across X and Y.

label: IsSelfAdjoint
slogan: An element x is self-adjoint if it equals its star, meaning x = star(x), where star is an operation defined on a type, such as complex conjugation or the adjoint of an operator. The property IsSelfAdjoint(x) holds when this equality is true. This applies to any type equipped with a star operation.

label: IsSelfAdjoint.hasEigenvector_of_isMaxOn
slogan: For a self-adjoint operator T, if a nonzero vector x0 maximizes the Rayleigh quotient on a sphere centered at the origin, then x0 is an eigenvector of T, and the corresponding eigenvalue is the maximum value of the Rayleigh quotient over all nonzero vectors.

label: IsSelfAdjoint.mem_spectrum_eq_re
slogan: If a complex number is in the spectrum of a self-adjoint element in a C*-algebra, then that number must be real.

label: IsSelfAdjoint.val_re_map_spectrum
slogan: The spectrum of a selfadjoint element in a C*-algebra consists only of real numbers. This means that every complex number in the spectrum is equal to its own real part. The set of spectrum values is unchanged when each value is replaced by its real part.

label: IsSemiprimaryRing.isNoetherian_iff_isArtinian
slogan: For a semiprimary ring, a module over that ring satisfies the ascending chain condition on submodules if and only if it satisfies the descending chain condition on submodules. This means that in such rings, being Noetherian and Artinian are equivalent properties for modules.

label: IsSemisimpleModule
slogan: A semisimple module is one where every submodule has a complementary submodule such that together they form the whole module as a direct sum. This means the module can be broken down into independent parts, and the collection of all submodules forms a complemented lattice. The module must be over a ring, with standard addition and scalar multiplication satisfying the usual algebraic rules.

label: IsSemisimpleRing
slogan: A ring is semisimple if it can be expressed as a finite product of matrix rings over division rings, meaning it decomposes into simpler algebraic pieces that resemble linear transformations over fields. In such rings, every module breaks down into a direct sum of simple modules. This reflects a strong structural property where the ring's representation theory is completely reducible.

label: IsSemisimpleRing.exists_algEquiv_pi_matrix_divisionRing
slogan: If a ring is semisimple, then it is algebraically equivalent to a product of matrix rings over division rings, where each matrix ring consists of square matrices of some positive size and the entries come from a division ring.

label: IsSemisimpleRing.exists_ringEquiv_pi_matrix_divisionRing
slogan: If a ring is semisimple, then it is isomorphic to a product of matrix rings over division rings, where each matrix ring consists of square matrices of a certain size and the entries come from a corresponding division ring. The sizes of the matrices are positive integers, and the isomorphism preserves the ring structure. This means the ring can be decomposed into simpler components that resemble linear algebra over division rings.

label: IsSemisimpleRing.isSemisimpleModule
slogan: If a ring is semisimple, then every module over that ring can be broken down into a direct sum of simple modules. This means all modules over such a ring have a particularly nice structure, built from irreducible components. The result follows from the ring's decomposition into matrix rings over division rings.

label: IsSeqClosed
slogan: A set is sequence-closed if whenever a sequence of points in the set converges to a limit in the space, that limit is also in the set. This means the set contains all points that can be approached by sequences within it. Convergence is defined using neighborhood filters and the behavior of sequences at infinity via the atTop filter.

label: IsSeqCompact
slogan: A set is sequentially compact if every sequence in the set has a subsequence that converges to a point in the set, meaning the subsequence eventually stays arbitrarily close to the limit according to the topology. This is formalized using the idea that the function mapping natural numbers to later and later indices is strictly increasing, and the values of the sequence along this subsequence get eventually close to the limit, expressed using filters: the subsequence tends to the limit under the neighborhood filter of the point and the at-top filter on natural numbers. The at-top filter capture

label: IsSigmaCompact.isLindelof
slogan: A set that can be written as a countable union of compact sets is always Lindelof, meaning every open cover of the set has a countable subcover. This is because compact sets are Lindelof, and a countable union of Lindelof sets remains Lindelof. The result holds in any topological space.

label: IsSimpleGroup
slogan: A group is simple if it has more than one element and its only normal subgroups are the whole group and the subgroup containing just the identity. This means there are no nontrivial normal subgroups inside it. Simplicity in groups indicates a kind of algebraic indivisibility.

label: IsSimpleModule
slogan: A simple module is a nonzero module over a ring that has no submodules other than the zero submodule and the whole module itself. It is an additive commutative group with a scalar multiplication operation that satisfies the module axioms. The condition means the module has no nontrivial substructures closed under addition and scalar multiplication.

label: IsSimpleRing.exists_ringEquiv_matrix_divisionRing
slogan: If a ring is simple and satisfies the descending chain condition on ideals, then it is isomorphic to a ring of square matrices over some division ring, where the size of the matrices is at least 1.

label: IsSimpleRing.matrix
slogan: If a ring has no nontrivial two-sided ideals and is not the zero ring, then the ring of square matrices over that ring also has no nontrivial two-sided ideals and is not the zero ring, so it is simple. This means that forming matrices over a simple ring results in another simple ring. The result depends on how two-sided ideals in matrix rings correspond to those in the original ring.

label: IsSl2Triple
slogan: An IsSl2Triple describes three elements h, e, f in a Lie ring L that satisfy specific bracket relations, meaning they behave like the standard generators of the Lie algebra sl₂, with h acting diagonally and e, f as raising and lowering operators. These relations ensure the three elements generate a subalgebra isomorphic to sl₂. The structure is used to study representations and symmetries in Lie theory.

label: IsSolvable
slogan: A group is solvable if it has a sequence of subgroups, each normal in the next, with abelian quotient groups. This property applies to algebraic structures with a multiplication operation, inverses, and an identity. The function G mentioned is unrelated and refers to a complex-valued function on the upper half-plane.

label: IsSolvableByRad
slogan: A value in a field extension E of a field F is solvable by radicals if it can be obtained from elements of F using a finite sequence of field operations and taking roots. This means the value comes from repeatedly adding, subtracting, multiplying, dividing, and extracting n-th roots starting from elements in F. The definition builds this idea inductively, step by step, within the framework of field extensions.

label: IsStrictOrder
slogan: A strict order is a relation where no element is related to itself, and if one element is related to a second and the second to a third, then the first is related to the third. It combines the properties of being irreflexive and transitive. The declaration defines a class for such a relation on a type.

label: IsStrictOrderedRing
slogan: A strict ordered ring is a set with addition and multiplication where the operations follow basic arithmetic rules, the order relation is preserved when adding or multiplying by positive elements, and zero is less than one; it also requires that the set has more than one element and that inequalities become strictly stronger when multiplying by positive values. Adding the same value to both sides of an inequality preserves the order, and if two sums are equal then the original terms must be equal too when one is less than or equal to the other. Multiplying by a positive element always increase

label: IsStrictTotalOrder
slogan: A strict total order is a relation that is transitive and irreflexive (meaning no element is less than itself, and if one element is less than a second and the second less than a third, then the first is less than the third), and for any two elements, exactly one of the following is true: the first is less than the second, the second is less than the first, or the two are equal.

label: IsTopologicalDivisionRing
slogan: A topological division ring is a set with operations for addition, multiplication, and division (except by zero) where all these operations, including taking reciprocals of nonzero elements, are continuous with respect to a given topology. It is a division ring and a topological space such that algebra and topology are compatible. This means that limits and open sets work well with all arithmetic operations, including inversion for nonzero values.

label: IsTopologicalGroup
slogan: A topological group is a set with both a group structure and a topology where multiplying elements and taking inverses are continuous operations, so algebra and closeness fit together smoothly. It also has a natural way to define uniform closeness using the group operation and identity element. This makes the space a uniform group, where left and right translations behave well with respect to limits and neighborhoods.

label: IsTopologicalGroup.completeSpace_rightUniformSpace_iff_leftUniformSpace
slogan: In a topological group, the space is complete with respect to the right uniform structure if and only if it is complete with respect to the left uniform structure, meaning completeness on one side implies completeness on the other. This equivalence holds because the group's inversion operation provides a uniform equivalence between the two structures. As a result, the space has no "missing" limit points in one uniformity if it doesn't in the other.

label: IsTopologicalGroup.of_nhds_one
slogan: A group with a topology is a topological group if multiplication and inversion are continuous at the identity element, and the topology is translation-invariant and conjugation-invariant at the identity; this ensures the group operations are continuous everywhere.

label: IsTopologicalGroup.regularSpace
slogan: A topological group is a group with a topology where multiplication and inversion are continuous, and this declaration states that such a space is regular: any point and any disjoint closed set can be separated by disjoint open sets, and every neighborhood of a point contains the closure of a smaller neighborhood around that point.

label: IsTopologicalGroup.rightUniformSpace
slogan: The right uniform space of a topological group is defined by using neighborhoods of the identity element to determine when two points are close, based on whether the product of one with the inverse of the other lies in such a neighborhood. This structure creates a uniformity that reflects the group's topology and algebraic properties. Closeness between points x and y is measured by how near x * y^-1 is to the identity.

label: IsTopologicalRing
slogan: A topological ring is a set with both a ring structure and a topology such that addition, multiplication, and negation are continuous operations. This means that algebraic operations behave well with respect to limits and open sets. It extends the idea of a topological semiring by including continuous negation.

label: IsTranscendenceBasis
slogan: A transcendence basis is a set of elements in an algebra over a commutative ring such that no nontrivial polynomial with coefficients in the ring evaluates to zero when applied to these elements, and every element of the algebra can be expressed algebraically in terms of them. The elements are algebraically independent, meaning they do not satisfy any polynomial relation, and their algebraic span covers the whole algebra. This generalizes linear independence to polynomial independence in ring extensions.

label: IsUltrametricDist
slogan: IsUltrametricDist is a property of a distance function where the distance between any two points is at most the maximum of their distances to a third point. This means the distance satisfies a stronger version of the triangle inequality. It applies to types that already have a standard non-negative distance function defined.

label: IsUnifLocDoublingMeasure.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div
slogan: For almost every point in a set S, if you have a sequence of closed balls whose radii shrink to zero and the point stays within a fixed multiple of the radius from each ball's center, then the ratio of the measure of S intersected with each ball to the measure of the whole ball tends to 1. This means that at small scales, the set S fills up almost all of the balls around almost every point in S, when the measure is uniformly locally doubling. The result holds in a pseudo-metric space with standard measure-theoretic and topological conditions.

label: IsWellOrder
slogan: A well-order is a relation that is transitive, meaning if a is less than b and b is less than c then a is less than c; trichotomous, meaning any two elements are comparable and only one of a less than b, b less than a, or a equals b can be true; and well-founded, meaning there are no infinite descending sequences and every non-empty set has a smallest element. This structure supports proof by induction and ensures a consistent, total order.

label: IsZGroup
slogan: A Z-group is a group where every Sylow subgroup is cyclic, meaning each of these subgroups can be generated by a single element. This property depends on the group structure and the cyclic nature of its Sylow subgroups.

label: IsZGroup.of_squarefree
slogan: If a finite group has a number of elements that is squarefree (meaning no prime factor appears more than once in its factorization), then every Sylow subgroup of the group is cyclic, which means the group is a Z-group.

label: IsZLattice
slogan: A Z-lattice is a subgroup of a real vector space that consists of all integer linear combinations of a finite set of vectors, making it a discrete and countable additive group. It is closed under addition and integer scaling, and sits inside a normed space with a discrete topology. The IsZLattice class captures this idea by combining module, normed space, and topological properties to ensure the lattice is well-behaved and structured.

label: Isometry
slogan: An isometry is a function between two spaces with distances defined (where distances can be infinite or zero even for distinct points) such that the distance between any two points in the source space equals the distance between their images in the target space. It preserves the metric structure exactly.

label: Isometry.dist_eq
slogan: An isometry is a function between two spaces with distance measures where the distance between any two points stays the same after applying the function. This means if you take any pair of points, the distance between them is exactly the same as the distance between their images. The spaces involved allow for distinct points to have zero distance, and the function must preserve all distances perfectly.

label: Isometry.injective
slogan: An isometry is a function that preserves distances between points, and such a function cannot map two different inputs to the same output. This means if two points have the same image under an isometry, then they must be the same point to begin with.

label: IsometryEquiv
slogan: An IsometryEquiv is a bijective function between two pseudo-metric spaces where the distance between any two points in one space equals the distance between their corresponding points in the other space. It ensures that both the function and its inverse preserve distances, making the two spaces metrically identical. This combines a one-to-one correspondence (Equiv) with the structure-preserving property of isometries in the context of extended pseudometric spaces.

label: IteratedWreathProduct
slogan: IteratedWreathProduct takes a group G and a natural number n, and returns the wreath product of G with itself, repeated n times. It constructs a new group by iteratively combining G with itself using the wreath product operation. The result is a group type built from n layers of G.

label: KaehlerDifferential
slogan: The module of Kähler differentials for a commutative R-algebra A is formed by taking the tensor product A ⊗[R] A and quotienting out the ideal generated by all elements of the form a ⊗ 1 - 1 ⊗ a, which represent formal differences that behave like da. This construction yields a module where each element da corresponds to the derivative of a, and it supports a universal derivation map that is compatible with the algebraic operations. The resulting object captures the notion of differentials in a purely algebraic way, independent of limits or topology.

label: KaehlerDifferential.D
slogan: KaehlerDifferential.D defines a function that takes elements from a ring S and maps them to their differentials in a module over S, where the map satisfies the product rule and linearity. It constructs this module by taking formal symbols for differentials and imposing relations so that constants have zero differential and the Leibniz rule holds. The result is an algebraic version of the idea of a differential, capturing how elements change relative to a base ring R.

label: KuratowskiEmbedding.exists_isometric_embedding
slogan: Every separable metric space can be embedded into the space of bounded sequences (l-infinity of the natural numbers) in a way that preserves all distances exactly. This means there exists a function from the space into l-infinity that is an isometry, so the distance between any two points in the original space equals the distance between their images in the sequence space.

label: LDL.lower_conj_diag
slogan: Every positive definite matrix S can be broken down into the product of a lower-triangular matrix L, a diagonal matrix D, and the conjugate transpose of L, such that S = L * D * L^H. The matrices L and D are constructed from S in a way that ensures this equality holds. This decomposition is always possible when S is positive definite and the underlying index set is finite and suitably ordered.

label: LSeries
slogan: The LSeries of a function f at a point s is the sum of f(n) divided by n to the power s for all natural numbers n, provided this sum converges absolutely; otherwise, it is zero. The function f maps natural numbers to complex numbers, and the result is a complex number. This sum is computed using a limiting process over finite subsets of the natural numbers.

label: LSeriesSummable_of_abscissaOfAbsConv_lt_re
slogan: If the real part of a complex number s is greater than the abscissa of absolute convergence of a function f from natural numbers to complex numbers, then the L-series of f converges absolutely at s.

label: LSeries_convolution
slogan: The L-series of the Dirichlet convolution of two complex sequences f and g is equal to the product of their individual L-series, provided that the real part of the complex variable s is large enough for both L-series to converge absolutely.

label: Lagrange.basis
slogan: Lagrange.basis returns a polynomial that is 1 at a specific point v(i) and 0 at all other points v(j) for j in a finite set s, provided the points are distinct; it is used to build polynomials that interpolate values at given nodes.

label: Lagrange.eq_interpolate
slogan: If a polynomial has degree less than the number of points in a set and those points have distinct values, then the polynomial is uniquely determined by its values at those points and can be reconstructed using Lagrange interpolation. The interpolated polynomial matches the original polynomial exactly. This holds over any field where the evaluation points are injective on the given finite index set.

label: Lagrange.eq_interpolate_iff
slogan: A polynomial f of degree less than the number of points in a finite set s, where the function v maps each index to a field value, takes the value r i at each point v i if and only if f is exactly the polynomial constructed by Lagrange interpolation from s, v, and r, provided the values of v on s are distinct.

label: Lagrange.funEquivDegreeLT
slogan: Lagrange interpolation gives a one-to-one correspondence between functions defined on a finite set s and polynomials over a field whose degree is less than the size of s, provided the points assigned to s are distinct. This correspondence is linear and preserves the structure of function values when mapped to polynomials.

label: Lagrange.interpolate
slogan: Given a finite set of nodes and a function that assigns values to these nodes, the interpolate function returns a polynomial that passes through all the specified points, meaning it takes the assigned value at each node. The polynomial has degree less than the number of points and is built using Lagrange basis polynomials. This mapping from value functions to polynomials is linear over the field.

label: Lagrange.interpolate_eq_sum
slogan: The Lagrange interpolation formula constructs a polynomial that passes through a given set of points by summing terms, where each term is a scaled product of linear factors; the scaling factor for each point is the value at that point divided by the product of differences between that point's input and all other inputs; the polynomial is built using constants and the variable X, combined through multiplication and addition.

label: Language
slogan: A language is a collection of strings formed from symbols in a given alphabet. It is defined as a set of sequences where each sequence consists of elements from a specified type representing the alphabet. The type of the language corresponds to the type of the alphabet used to form the strings.

label: Language.IsContextFree
slogan: A language is context-free if it can be generated by a context-free grammar, meaning there exists some context-free grammar that produces exactly the strings in that language.

label: Language.IsContextFree.reverse
slogan: If a language can be generated by a context-free grammar, then the language formed by reversing all its strings (such as turning "abc" into "cba") is also context-free. This is because reversing the production rules of the grammar produces a new grammar that generates the reversed strings. Thus, the set of context-free languages is closed under the reversal operation.

label: Language.IsRegular
slogan: A language is regular if there exists a deterministic finite automaton (DFA) with a finite number of states that accepts exactly the strings in that language. This means the language can be recognized by a simple machine that reads input symbols and transitions between states, ending in an accepting state for valid strings. Regular languages are built from finite alphabets and consist of finite sequences of symbols.

label: Language.IsRegular.add
slogan: If two languages are regular, then their union is also a regular language. This means that whenever there are finite automata that recognize each of the two languages, there exists another finite automaton that recognizes all strings in either language. The union of languages is treated as addition in the algebraic structure of languages.

label: Language.IsRegular.compl
slogan: If a language is regular, then its complement is also regular. This means that for any language recognized by a finite automaton, the set of strings not in that language can also be recognized by some finite automaton. The result follows from the fact that deterministic finite automata can be complemented by flipping their accept states.

label: Language.IsRegular.inf
slogan: If two languages are regular, then their intersection is also a regular language. This means that if there are finite automata that recognize each of the two languages, there exists a finite automaton that recognizes the strings common to both languages.

label: Language.instKStar
slogan: The Kleene star of a language L is the set of all strings that can be formed by concatenating zero or more strings from L. For any alphabet α, this operation is available on languages over α. It allows building new strings by joining together any number of strings that are already in the language.

label: Language.instMul
slogan: The product of two languages combines any string from the first language with any string from the second by concatenating them. This operation is defined as multiplication for languages, where each resulting string is formed by appending a string from the first language to one from the second. The alphabet used for both languages must be the same.

label: Language.isRegular_iff_finite_range_leftQuotient
slogan: A language is regular if and only if there are only finitely many distinct sets of strings that can follow a given prefix to form a string in the language. These sets, called left quotients, represent all possible suffixes that complete a prefix into a valid string. The finiteness of these sets completely characterizes whether a language can be recognized by a finite automaton.

label: Language.kstar_def
slogan: The Kleene star of a language l is the set of all strings that can be formed by concatenating a finite list of strings from l, including the empty string when no strings are used. A string x is in the Kleene star of l if there exists a list L of strings such that x is the concatenation of all strings in L and every string in L is in l. This definition captures the idea of repeated concatenation of strings from the language.

label: Language.leftQuotient
slogan: The left quotient of a string x with respect to a language L is the set of all strings y such that the concatenation of x and y (written x ++ y) is in L. It represents all possible suffixes that, when added to x, produce a string in the language. This operation is defined for any alphabet and works with lists of symbols.

label: Language.mem_inf
slogan: A string is in the intersection of two languages if and only if it is in both languages. This means membership in the combined language requires the string to be present in each individual language. The operation uses logical and to express that both conditions must hold.

label: Language.reverse
slogan: The reverse of a language is the set of all strings obtained by reversing each string in the original language. For example, if a language contains the string "abc", its reverse contains "cba". This operation applies to every string in the language, producing a new language with the reversed strings.

label: Lattice
slogan: A lattice is a type with a partial order where every pair of elements has both a least upper bound (sup) and a greatest lower bound (inf). It combines the properties of a semilattice_sup, which provides sup, and a semilattice_inf, which provides inf. These operations ensure that any two elements can be combined in a way that respects the order structure.

label: LatticeHom
slogan: A LatticeHom is a function between two lattices that preserves both the meet (inf) and join (sup) operations, so that the image of the meet or join of two elements is the same as the meet or join of their images.

label: LaurentPolynomial
slogan: A Laurent polynomial with coefficients in a semiring R is a finite combination of positive and negative powers of a variable, where coefficients follow arithmetic rules similar to natural numbers. It is built using a structure that assigns coefficients to integer powers, with only finitely many nonzero terms. This construction supports addition and multiplication, generalizing polynomials to allow negative exponents.

label: LaurentSeries
slogan: LaurentSeries R represents formal Laurent series with coefficients in a type R that has a zero element, where each series is a sum of terms indexed by integers. It is defined using Hahn series over the integers, meaning the powers of the variable can be any integers, positive or negative, but only finitely many negative powers can have nonzero coefficients. The structure allows operations like addition and multiplication to be defined term-wise, respecting the zero element in R.

label: LeftCancelMonoid
slogan: A LeftCancelMonoid is a set with an associative multiplication and an identity element, such that if a * b = a * c, then b = c for any elements a, b, c. It combines the structure of a monoid with the rule that left multiplication can always be canceled. This ensures that multiplying on the left does not map different elements to the same result.

label: LeftCancelMonoid.groupOfFinite
slogan: If a monoid has the left cancellation property and contains only finitely many elements, then every element in it has some positive power that equals the identity, and this structure guarantees that the monoid is actually a group.

label: LieAlgebra
slogan: A Lie algebra is a module over a commutative ring equipped with a Lie bracket operation that is bilinear, alternating, and satisfies the Jacobi identity. The bracket measures non-commutativity and interacts with scalar multiplication in a compatible way. It combines the linear structure of a module with the algebraic properties of a Lie ring.

label: LieAlgebra.Basis
slogan: A basis for a semisimple Lie algebra picks out a special Cartan subalgebra and a base for the corresponding root system. It is defined over a Lie algebra L with coefficients in a commutative ring R, indexed by a finite type. This structure helps decompose the Lie algebra into root spaces relative to the chosen Cartan subalgebra.

label: LieAlgebra.ExtendScalars.instLieAlgebra
slogan: If you have a Lie algebra over a commutative ring R and extend scalars to a larger ring A using a tensor product, the result is a new Lie algebra over A, with the bracket defined by extending the original bracket linearly. This construction uses the module structure of the tensor product and preserves the Lie algebra axioms. The new bracket satisfies bilinearity, alternation, and the Jacobi identity over the extended scalars.

label: LieAlgebra.Extension
slogan: A Lie algebra extension of M by N over a commutative ring R is a short exact sequence of Lie algebra homomorphisms 0 -> N -> L -> M -> 0, where L is a Lie algebra containing N as an ideal and mapping onto M. This structure captures how one Lie algebra can be built from two others in a way that preserves their algebraic properties. The type LieAlgebra.Extension collects all such possible extensions for fixed R, M, and N.

label: LieAlgebra.HasCentralRadical
slogan: A Lie algebra has central radical when its largest solvable ideal (the radical) is exactly the same as its center, meaning all elements in the radical commute with every element in the algebra. This property is often associated with reductive Lie algebras in characteristic zero. The definition depends on the underlying commutative ring and the Lie algebra structure.

label: LieAlgebra.IsKilling.isSimple_iff_isIrreducible
slogan: A Lie algebra with a non-degenerate Killing form is simple if and only if its associated root system cannot be split into independent, non-trivial subsystems that are invariant under the root reflections. This means the algebra's structure is irreducible exactly when its root system is irreducible. The result holds for finite-dimensional Lie algebras over fields of characteristic zero with a Cartan subalgebra and a triangularizable adjoint action.

label: LieAlgebra.IsSemisimple
slogan: A Lie algebra is semisimple if it can be written as a direct sum of non-abelian ideals that cannot be broken down further, and each of these ideals is a simple Lie algebra. This means the algebra has no non-zero solvable ideals and is built entirely from simple components. Some definitions instead use "semisimple" to mean having only a trivial radical, which may differ in positive characteristic.

label: LieAlgebra.IsSemisimple.isSimple_of_isAtom
slogan: If a Lie algebra is semisimple, then any nonzero ideal that is minimal among nonzero ideals (an atom) must itself be a simple Lie algebra.

label: LieAlgebra.IsSimple
slogan: A Lie algebra is simple if it has no nontrivial ideals under the adjoint action and is not Abelian, meaning its bracket operation is not identically zero. It is a non-Abelian Lie ring that is irreducible as a module over itself via the adjoint map. This property is defined over a commutative ring R and requires L to be a Lie algebra over R.

label: LieAlgebra.IsSolvable
slogan: A Lie algebra is called solvable if repeatedly taking the derived subalgebra eventually results in the zero algebra after finitely many steps. This property depends on the Lie bracket operation and the underlying algebraic structure of the Lie ring. The condition is expressed as a logical proposition for a given Lie algebra over a commutative ring.

label: LieAlgebra.SemiDirectSum
slogan: The semi-direct sum of two Lie algebras K and L over a commutative ring R is a new Lie algebra built from pairs (k, l) with k in K and l in L, where the Lie bracket is modified by a homomorphism psi from L to the Lie derivations of K. This homomorphism twists the bracket operation so that elements of L act on K via derivations. The resulting structure combines K and L in a way that generalizes the direct sum but allows for non-trivial interaction between the two algebras.

label: LieAlgebra.SpecialLinear.sl
slogan: The special linear Lie algebra consists of all square matrices over a commutative ring where the sum of the diagonal elements (the trace) is zero. These matrices form a Lie subalgebra under the commutator bracket, meaning they are closed under matrix subtraction, scalar multiplication, and the operation [A, B] = A*B - B*A. This structure is defined for matrices with finitely many rows and columns indexed by a type with decidable equality.

label: LieAlgebra.ad
slogan: For any associative algebra over a commutative ring, the map sending an element x to the linear transformation given by taking the commutator [x, y] = x*y - y*x is a Lie algebra homomorphism; this map is linear and preserves the Lie bracket structure.

label: LieAlgebra.ad_lie
slogan: For any element x in a Lie algebra over a commutative ring, the operation that sends y to the bracket [x, y] is a linear map that preserves the Lie bracket structure, satisfying [x, [y, z]] = [[x, y], z] + [y, [x, z]] for all elements y and z. This identity reflects the fact that taking brackets with x respects the algebra's bracket operation. The map is known as the adjoint action of x.

label: LieAlgebra.ad_pow_lie
slogan: For an element x in a Lie algebra, repeatedly applying the map that sends y to [x, y] and then taking the nth power of this map applied to the bracket [y, z] equals a sum over all pairs (i,j) that add to n, where each term is the binomial coefficient "n choose i" times the bracket of the ith power of the map on y and the jth power on z.

label: LieAlgebra.center
slogan: The center of a Lie algebra is the set of all elements that have a zero Lie bracket with every element in the algebra. This set forms a Lie ideal and is the largest submodule where the algebra's bracket action is trivial. It consists of all elements annihilated by the action of the entire algebra.

label: LieAlgebra.derivedSeries
slogan: The derived series of a Lie algebra is a sequence of nested Lie ideals where each term is formed by taking the Lie bracket of the previous term with itself, starting from the entire algebra. Each subsequent ideal in the series is contained in the previous one, capturing how repeated brackets reduce the structure. This series helps determine whether the Lie algebra is solvable by checking if the sequence eventually reaches zero.

label: LieAlgebra.isEngelian_of_isNoetherian
slogan: If a Lie algebra over a commutative ring is Noetherian, meaning its submodules are all finitely generated, then it has the property that any representation where each element acts nilpotently must result in a nilpotent action overall. This means the algebra's structure forces global nilpotency in such representations. Being Noetherian ensures this strong algebraic behavior.

label: LieAlgebra.ofAssociativeAlgebra
slogan: Any associative algebra over a commutative ring can automatically become a Lie algebra by defining the Lie bracket as the commutator [x, y] = x*y - y*x, using the algebra's existing multiplication and subtraction; this bracket satisfies all the Lie algebra axioms, including bilinearity and the Jacobi identity, while respecting scalar multiplication.

label: LieAlgebra.radical
slogan: The radical of a Lie algebra is the largest solvable ideal that contains all other solvable ideals. It is formed by taking the supremum (least upper bound) of all solvable ideals in the Lie algebra. This object itself is a Lie ideal over the same ring and module structure.

label: LieDerivation.IsKilling.exists_eq_ad
slogan: In a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over a field where the Killing form is non-singular, every derivation can be expressed as the adjoint action of some element in the algebra. This means that all such derivations are inner derivations. There exists some element x in the Lie algebra such that applying the adjoint map ad(x) gives the same result as the derivation.

label: LieDerivation.ad_ker_eq_center
