This series includes only the odd powers of x, scaled by 2 and divided by their exponents. The equality holds as long as |x| < 1.

label: Real.hasSum_pow_div_log_of_abs_lt_one
slogan: If the absolute value of a real number x is less than 1, then the infinite sum of x^(n+1)/(n+1) for n starting at 0 converges to -log(1 - x). This means the series adds up exactly to the negative natural logarithm of (1 - x) when |x| < 1.

label: Real.infinite_rat_abs_sub_lt_one_div_den_sq_of_irrational
slogan: If a real number is irrational, then there are infinitely many rational numbers p/q such that the absolute difference between the irrational number and p/q is less than 1 divided by q squared.

label: Real.instCompleteSpace
slogan: The real numbers are complete, meaning every Cauchy sequence of real numbers converges to a real number. This ensures that sequences that get arbitrarily close to each other will always have a limit within the real numbers. There are no missing points or gaps in the real number line where such limits should be.

label: Real.instConditionallyCompleteLinearOrder
slogan: The real numbers have a total order where every nonempty set with an upper bound has a least upper bound, and every nonempty set with a lower bound has a greatest lower bound. This means suprema and infima exist for all bounded sets, ensuring the order is conditionally complete. The structure supports standard comparisons, bounds, and operations like min and max.

label: Real.instField
slogan: The real numbers form a field, meaning they support addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division (except by zero) with all the usual algebraic rules. This structure extends the real numbers' existing commutative ring properties by adding multiplicative inverses for nonzero elements. Rational numbers can be embedded into the reals, allowing fractions to be used naturally in real number arithmetic.

label: Real.instIsStrictOrderedRing
slogan: The real numbers have a consistent system of addition, multiplication, and less-than ordering where multiplying both sides of an inequality by a positive number preserves the inequality. This means if a is less than b and c is positive, then a times c is less than b times c. The real numbers satisfy the rules of a strictly ordered ring, ensuring arithmetic and order work together as expected.

label: Real.integral_rpow_mul_exp_neg_mul_Ioi
slogan: For any real number a greater than 0 and any positive real number r, the integral from 0 to infinity of t raised to the power (a - 1), multiplied by e to the power of -r times t, equals (1/r) raised to the power a, multiplied by the gamma function of a. This formula links an improper integral involving a power and an exponential decay to the gamma function. The integration is performed over the positive real line using Lebesgue measure.

label: Real.isEquivalent_sin
slogan: The sine of a real number is approximately equal to the number itself when the input is close to zero, and the difference between sin(x) and x becomes very small compared to x as x approaches zero. This means sin(x) behaves like the identity function near zero in terms of limits. It follows from the fact that the derivative of sin(x) at 0 is 1.

label: Real.isTopologicalBasis_Ioo_rat
slogan: The collection of all open intervals (a, b) with rational endpoints forms a basis for the standard topology on the real numbers, meaning every open set in the real line can be expressed as a union of such intervals. This works because rational numbers are dense in the reals, so any open interval around a real number contains one with rational endpoints. The result uses the fact that rationals can be embedded into the reals while preserving order.

label: Real.linearOrder
slogan: The real numbers have a total ordering, so any two real numbers can be compared using "less than or equal to," and this ordering supports consistent min and max operations.

label: Real.log
slogan: The real logarithm function takes a positive real number and returns the power to which e must be raised to get that number. It is defined only for inputs greater than zero and is the inverse of the exponential function. For example, if e^y = x, then log(x) = y.

label: Real.log_exp
slogan: For any real number x, taking the natural logarithm of e raised to the power x gives back x. This works because the exponential function always produces a positive result, and the logarithm is defined to reverse that operation.

label: Real.log_injOn_pos
slogan: The natural logarithm function is one-to-one when restricted to positive real numbers, so no two different positive real numbers have the same logarithm. This is because the logarithm function is strictly increasing for positive inputs.

label: Real.log_lt_log
slogan: If 0 < x and x < y, then log(x) < log(y), meaning the natural logarithm function increases as its input increases for positive real numbers.

label: Real.log_lt_log_iff
slogan: For positive real numbers x and y, the natural logarithm of x is less than the natural logarithm of y if and only if x is less than y. This means the log function increases as its input increases, preserving the order of positive real numbers. The result relies on the fact that the exponential function is strictly increasing and that log is its inverse.

label: Real.log_mul
slogan: For any two nonzero real numbers x and y, the logarithm of their product equals the sum of their logarithms: log(x * y) = log(x) + log(y). This holds because the exponential function, which is the inverse of the logarithm, turns addition into multiplication. The condition that x and y are nonzero ensures that their absolute values are positive, so the logarithm is defined.

label: Real.log_neg
slogan: The natural logarithm of a real number is negative when the number is between 0 and 1. This applies only to positive numbers less than 1, since the logarithm of 1 is 0 and the function increases as the input grows.

label: Real.log_pow
slogan: The logarithm of a positive real number raised to a natural number power is equal to that power times the logarithm of the number. This means taking a power inside a logarithm turns it into a multiplication outside. For example, log(x^n) = n * log(x) when x is positive and n is a natural number.

label: Real.log_rpow
slogan: For any positive real number x and any real number y, the natural log of x to the power y equals y times the natural log of x. This means you can bring the exponent down as a multiplier when taking the log of a power. The rule works because the log and exponential functions are inverses and the exponential function always gives positive results for real inputs.

label: Real.logb
slogan: Real.logb takes two positive real numbers, a base b (not equal to 1) and a value x, and returns the logarithm of x with respect to base b by dividing the natural logarithm of x by the natural logarithm of b. This computation relies on the natural logarithm function and standard division for real numbers. The result is the exponent to which b must be raised to get x.

label: Real.logb_eq_iff_rpow_eq
slogan: For positive real numbers b and y, where b is not 1, the base-b logarithm of y equals x if and only if b raised to the power x equals y.

label: Real.logb_mul
slogan: For any positive real numbers x and y, and a positive base b not equal to 1, the logarithm of x times y in base b is the same as the sum of the logarithm of x in base b and the logarithm of y in base b. This means taking the log of a product gives the sum of the logs, as long as the numbers are positive and the base is valid. The result follows from how logarithms are defined using natural logs and division.

label: Real.metricSpace
slogan: The real numbers are equipped with a metric space structure where the distance between two numbers is the absolute value of their difference, ensuring positive distances for distinct points, symmetry, and the triangle inequality. This metric induces a topology that is Hausdorff and completely normal, meaning distinct points and closed sets can be separated by open sets, and it aligns with the usual order and uniform structure of the real line.

label: Real.negMulLog_zero
slogan: The function -x * log(x) approaches 0 as x gets closer to 0 from the positive side, even though log(x) goes to negative infinity. This result shows that the product of a value going to zero and a logarithm going to negative infinity can still converge to zero. It is useful in areas like analysis and information theory, especially when handling limits involving entropy or logarithmic behavior near zero.

label: Real.nonempty_algEquiv_or
slogan: For any field F that is an algebraic extension of the real numbers, either there exists an algebra isomorphism from F to the real numbers or an algebra isomorphism from F to the complex numbers. This means every algebraic extension of the reals is structurally equivalent to either the reals or the complex numbers. The result follows from the fact that the complex numbers are algebraically closed and two-dimensional over the reals.

label: Real.not_summable_one_div_natCast
slogan: The sum of the series 1 + 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/4 + ... does not approach a finite real number; instead, it grows indefinitely. This means the harmonic series, formed by summing the reciprocals of the natural numbers, diverges and cannot be assigned a finite sum in the real numbers.

label: Real.ofDigits
slogan: Real.ofDigits takes a base b and a sequence of digits (each between 0 and b-1) and returns the real number formed by interpreting that sequence as the fractional part of a base-b number, like 0.d0d1d2... in base b, computed as the infinite sum of digit[i] / b^i.

label: Real.ofDigits_const_last_eq_one'
slogan: In any base b greater than 1, an infinite sequence of the largest digit (b-1) after the decimal point represents the number 1; for example, 0.999... in base 10 equals 1, and this holds similarly in other bases.

label: Real.ofDigits_digits
slogan: For any real number x between 0 (inclusive) and 1 (exclusive) and any integer base b greater than 1, converting x into its base-b digit sequence and then reconstructing the number from those digits gives back x.

label: Real.pi_gt_d4
slogan: The number pi is greater than 3.1415. This means pi lies somewhere above 3.1415 on the number line, giving a clear lower bound for its value.

label: Real.pi_gt_d6
slogan: pi is greater than 3.141592, meaning this decimal value is a proven lower bound for the actual value of pi.

label: Real.pi_gt_sqrtTwoAddSeries
slogan: Pi is greater than a sequence formed by repeatedly taking square roots of two added together in a nested way, multiplied by a power of two. This sequence builds a lower bound for pi using only square roots and arithmetic. Each step gets closer to pi but always stays less than it.

label: Real.pi_lt_d20
slogan: pi is less than 3.14159265358979323847, meaning its value is strictly smaller than this decimal number.

label: Real.pi_lt_d4
slogan: pi is less than 3.1416, meaning the mathematical constant pi has a value strictly smaller than 3.1416.

label: Real.pseudoMetricSpace
slogan: The real numbers are equipped with a pseudometric space structure where the distance between any two numbers is the absolute value of their difference, satisfying properties like non-negativity, symmetry, and the triangle inequality.

label: Real.rpow_def_of_pos
slogan: For any positive real number x and any real number y, x raised to the power y is equal to e raised to the power of y times the natural logarithm of x. This definition relies on the real exponential and logarithm functions, with the logarithm only defined when x is positive. The result is always a real number when x is greater than zero.

label: Real.rpow_inv_natCast_pow
slogan: For any non-negative real number x and any positive natural number n, if you raise x to the power 1/n and then raise that result to the power n, you get x back. This means taking the n-th root of x and then raising it to the n-th power returns the original value of x.

label: Real.rpow_logb
slogan: For positive real numbers b and x, where b is not 1, raising b to the power of the base-b logarithm of x gives x. This identity follows from the inverse relationship between exponentiation and logarithms in real analysis.

label: Real.sigmoid
slogan: The sigmoid function takes a real number x and returns 1 divided by (1 plus the exponential of -x), which is a smooth, S-shaped function that maps any real input to a value between 0 and 1.

label: Real.sigmoid_pos
slogan: The sigmoid function of any real number is always greater than zero. This is because the sigmoid is defined as 1 divided by (1 plus the exponential of the negative input), and since the exponential function is always positive, the denominator is always greater than 1, making the result a positive fraction.

label: Real.sin_add
slogan: The sine of the sum of two real numbers x and y is equal to the sine of x times the cosine of y plus the cosine of x times the sine of y. This formula is proven by using the complex number definitions of sine and cosine, and relies on the fact that real numbers can be embedded into the complex plane without changing their trigonometric behavior. The identity holds because the complex sine and cosine functions follow the same addition rule, which applies to real numbers as a special case.

label: Real.sin_lt
slogan: For any positive real number x that is less than pi, the sine of x is always less than x itself.

label: Real.sin_sq_add_cos_sq
slogan: For any real number x, the sum of the square of its sine and the square of its cosine is always equal to one. This identity, sin(x)^2 + cos(x)^2 = 1, holds universally for all real values of x.

label: Real.sinc
slogan: The Real.sinc function returns sin(x) divided by x for any real number x, and returns 1 when x is 0 to avoid division by zero and ensure smooth behavior at that point. It uses standard real number operations including sine, division, zero, and one, with equality checks supported for all inputs. This makes sinc a well-defined, continuous function across all real numbers.

label: Real.sqrt
slogan: Real.sqrt is a function that takes a real number and returns its non-negative square root, but only makes sense for inputs that are zero or positive. It works by converting the input to a non-negative real, taking the square root there, and converting back to a real number. The function respects the usual ordering, so larger inputs give larger outputs.

label: Real.strictConcave_binEntropy
slogan: The binary entropy function, defined as -p * log(p) - (1-p) * log(1-p) for p between 0 and 1, is strictly concave on the interval [0, 1], meaning that the function always lies above any straight line connecting two of its points on this interval.

label: Real.tanh
slogan: The function Real.tanh calculates the hyperbolic tangent of a real number by dividing its hyperbolic sine by its hyperbolic cosine, and the result is always a real number between -1 and 1. It behaves the same as the complex tanh function when the real number is treated as a complex number with zero imaginary part.

label: Real.tendsto_euler_sin_prod
slogan: As n gets larger, the expression pi * x * (1 - x^2/1^2) * (1 - x^2/2^2) * ... * (1 - x^2/(n-1)^2) gets arbitrarily close to sin(pi * x), for any real number x. This means the sine of pi times x can be approximated as an infinite product involving squared terms of integers.

label: Real.tendsto_exp_div_pow_atTop
slogan: As x approaches positive infinity, the expression (e^x)/(x^n) also goes to positive infinity for any fixed natural number n. This means that exponential growth eventually overtakes polynomial growth. The result is stated for real numbers and relies on properties of limits and the order structure of the reals.

label: Real.tendsto_harmonic_sub_log
slogan: As n gets very large, the difference between the nth harmonic number and the natural logarithm of n gets arbitrarily close to the Euler-Mascheroni constant.

label: Real.tendsto_one_add_div_pow_exp
slogan: As n approaches infinity, the expression (1 + t/n) raised to the power n gets arbitrarily close to exp(t) for any real number t.

label: Real.tendsto_prod_pi_div_two
slogan: The infinite product formed by multiplying pairs of fractions (2/1 * 2/3 * 4/3 * 4/5 * 6/5 * 6/7 * ...) gets closer and closer to pi/2 as more terms are included. Each term in the product comes from even and odd integers in a specific repeating pattern. This convergence is expressed using limits in the context of filters, where the sequence approaches the value pi divided by two.

label: Real.tendsto_sigmoid_atTop
slogan: As x gets larger and larger, the value of the sigmoid function approaches 1.

label: Real.tendsto_tsum_powerSeries_nhdsWithin_lt
slogan: If a real power series converges at x = 1, then as x approaches 1 from values less than 1, the sum of the series approaches the same limit as the sum of the coefficients. This means the function defined by the power series is left-continuous at x = 1.

label: Real.tsum_eq_tsum_fourier
slogan: The sum of a continuous function f over all integer shifts x + n equals the sum of its Fourier transform values multiplied by complex exponentials at x, provided both sums converge appropriately. This is the most general form of Poisson's summation formula for real-valued functions. It connects the periodic summation of a function to the periodic summation of its Fourier transform.

label: Real.tsum_eq_tsum_fourier_of_rpow_decay
slogan: If a continuous function f and its Fourier transform both decay at least as fast as |x|^(-b) for some b > 1 as |x| gets large, then the sum of f(x + n) over all integers n equals the sum of the Fourier transform of f at integers n multiplied by complex exponentials at x. This identity holds for all real numbers x and is a version of Poisson's summation formula. The decay condition ensures that both sums converge.

label: Real.uniformContinuous_abs
slogan: The absolute value function on the real numbers is uniformly continuous, meaning that for any small distance, there is a fixed distance such that whenever two real numbers are within that distance, their absolute values are also within the small distance, no matter where the numbers are on the real line. This relies on the fact that the real numbers have a well-defined order, addition, and metric structure. The result follows from general properties of metric spaces and the inequality that the absolute value of the difference of absolute values is at most the absolute value of the difference o

label: Real.volume_Icc
slogan: The length of a closed interval [a, b] on the real line is given by b minus a, or zero if a is greater than b. This length is represented as an extended nonnegative real number, where finite values are embedded using the ofReal function. The measure used is the standard Lebesgue measure, which assigns to each interval its usual length.

label: Real.volume_Icc_pi
slogan: The volume of a closed rectangular box in n-dimensional real space, defined by intervals from a to b in each coordinate direction, equals the product of the lengths of those intervals, with any negative length treated as zero; the result is an extended nonnegative real number.

label: Real.young_inequality
slogan: For any real numbers a and b, and for positive real numbers p and q such that 1/p + 1/q = 1, the product a*b is less than or equal to (|a|^p)/p + (|b|^q)/q.

label: Real.zero_at_infty_fourier
slogan: As the frequency goes to infinity, the Fourier transform of an integrable function on the real line tends to zero. This means that high-frequency components of the function become negligible in the limit. The result holds for functions taking values in a complex normed space.

label: RealRMK.integral_rieszMeasure
slogan: The integral of a continuous real-valued function with compact support over a locally compact Hausdorff space, with respect to a specific measure, equals the value of a given positive linear functional applied to that function. This measure is uniquely determined up to normalization. The result links positive linear functionals to regular Borel measures.

label: RegularExpression
slogan: A regular expression is defined as a type that can match strings in specific ways: it can match nothing, the empty string, a single character, any repetition of a pattern, a choice between two patterns, or a sequence of two patterns. Each operation corresponds to basic building blocks of pattern matching. The type depends on an underlying alphabet of characters.

label: RegularSpace
slogan: A regular space is a topological space where, for any point and a closed set not containing that point, there are two non-overlapping open sets, one containing the point and the other containing the closed set. This ensures that points and closed sets can be separated by open neighborhoods. It is a condition that makes the topology well-behaved with respect to separation.

label: RegularWreathProduct
slogan: The regular wreath product of groups Q and D is a group built from pairs where the first part is a function from Q to D and the second part is an element of Q; the group operation combines these pairs by shifting the input of one function using the inverse of the other's Q element. It forms a new group using pointwise multiplication adjusted by the group action of Q on the functions.

label: Relation.Comp
slogan: Relation.Comp describes when two elements a and c are related through a chain of two relations: there exists some intermediate element b such that a is related to b by the first relation and b is related to c by the second.

label: Relation.ReflTransGen
slogan: Relation.ReflTransGen r a b means that element b is reachable from element a by following zero or more steps of the relation r, where zero steps means a equals b. It captures all pairs connected through repeated application of r, including direct equality. This forms the smallest reflexive and transitive relation containing r.

label: Relation.SymmGen
slogan: Relation.SymmGen takes a relation r on a type and creates a new relation where if a is related to b, then b is also related to a, ensuring symmetry. It includes all original pairs and their reverses to form the smallest symmetric relation that contains the original. The result is a relation that is symmetric by construction.

label: Relation.TransGen
slogan: TransGen r is the smallest transitive relation that includes the relation r, meaning that if r connects a to b and b to c, then TransGen r connects a to c. It holds between two elements a and z if there is a chain of r-related steps from a to z of length at least one. The relation is defined for any type α and any binary relation r on α.

label: Relator.LeftTotal
slogan: Relator.LeftTotal means that for every element in the first type, there exists at least one element in the second type such that the given relation between them is true. It ensures the relation covers all elements of the first type.

label: Rep
slogan: Rep is a structure that represents how a group or monoid can act on a module over a ring by mapping its elements to linear transformations in a way that preserves the algebraic structure. It forms a category where the objects are these representations and the morphisms are linear maps that respect the group or monoid action. This allows algebraic objects to be studied through their actions on vector spaces or modules.

label: Rep.indResAdjunction
slogan: The indResAdjunction states that for a group homomorphism φ from G to H and a commutative ring k, there is a natural one-to-one correspondence between linear maps from the induced representation of a G-module to an H-module and linear maps from the original G-module to the restricted H-module. This correspondence shows that inducing a representation is left adjoint to restricting one, in the category of group representations over k.

label: Rep.indResHomEquiv
slogan: The function Rep.indResHomEquiv provides a one-to-one correspondence between linear maps from the induced representation of a G-module A to an H-module B and linear maps from A to the restricted version of B along a group homomorphism φ : G → H. This correspondence is linear, natural, and respects the module structures, meaning it preserves composition and commutes with the action of the groups involved. It essentially links how representations transform under induction and restriction in a way that maintains their algebraic relationships.

label: Rep.res
slogan: Rep.res takes a representation of a monoid G over a commutative ring k and restricts it to a representation of another monoid H, using a monoid homomorphism from H to G, by composing the representation maps with this homomorphism. The result is a new representation on the same underlying module but with the action defined through the smaller monoid H. This restriction process preserves the structure of representations and intertwining maps, making it compatible with the category of representations.

label: Representation.Equiv
slogan: A Representation.Equiv is a bijective linear map between two representations of a monoid that preserves both the module structure and the action of the monoid, meaning applying the map commutes with the representation's transformation for every group element. It is an invertible intertwining map that respects addition, scalar multiplication, and the monoid's operation. This equivalence ensures the two representations are structurally identical in how they represent the monoid's action on the modules.

label: Representation.IntertwiningMap
slogan: A Representation.IntertwiningMap is a linear function between two modules that respects both the module structure and the action of a monoid, meaning applying the function after the monoid action gives the same result as applying the monoid action after the function. It requires the modules to be over a commutative ring and the monoid to act linearly on both spaces. This map preserves the symmetry encoded by the monoid across the two representations.

label: Representation.IsIrreducible
slogan: A representation is called irreducible if it is not zero and its only subrepresentations are the zero subspace and the whole space itself, meaning no proper nonzero subspaces are preserved under the group action. This applies to actions of a monoid on a vector space over a field, where the structure respects addition and scalar multiplication. The condition is equivalent to saying that the lattice of subrepresentations has no intermediate elements between zero and the full space.

label: Representation.IsIrreducible.bijective_or_eq_zero
slogan: A nonzero linear map between two irreducible representations that commutes with the group action is either an isomorphism or the zero map; there are no other possibilities. This means the map either fully preserves the structure and matches the spaces perfectly, or it sends every element to zero. The reason is that the image of such a map must be a subrepresentation, and irreducible representations have no nontrivial subrepresentations.

label: Representation.IsIrreducible.finrank_eq_one_of_isMulCommutative
slogan: If a representation is irreducible and the group it acts on has commutative multiplication, and the vector space is finite-dimensional over an algebraically closed field, then the space must be one-dimensional. This means the only possible invariant subspaces are trivial, and commutativity forces the entire space to be as small as possible. The result follows from the structure of modules over commutative algebras.

label: Representation.IsSemisimpleRepresentation
slogan: A representation is semisimple if, whenever there is a subrepresentation, there exists another subrepresentation such that together they form the whole space and their intersection is trivial. This means every subrepresentation can be complemented in a way that preserves the structure of the representation.

label: Representation.averageMap
slogan: For a finite group acting on a module over a commutative ring where the group order is invertible, the averageMap function builds a linear map that averages the group's action over all its elements. This map projects any vector onto the subspace of vectors unchanged by the group action, using the group algebra's average element applied through the representation. The result is a linear endomorphism of the module.

label: Representation.card_inv_mul_sum_char_mul_char_eq_finrank
slogan: For two finite-dimensional representations of a finite group, the average over the group of the product of one character with the conjugate of the other equals the dimension of the space of intertwining maps between them.

label: Representation.directSum
slogan: The directSum function builds a representation of a monoid on a direct sum of modules by combining individual representations on each module in the family, so that the monoid acts component-wise. It ensures the action is linear and respects the monoid's multiplication and identity. Each element of the direct sum transforms by applying the corresponding representation to each nonzero component.

label: Representation.dual
slogan: Given a group action on a module, the dual representation defines a corresponding group action on the space of linear maps from that module to its base ring, where each group element acts by transforming the input of a linear map before evaluation. This new action respects the group structure and module linearity. The dual space thus becomes a representation in a natural way.

label: Representation.ind
slogan: Representation.ind constructs a new representation of a group from a representation of a subgroup by using a tensor product with the group algebra, effectively extending the action to the whole group. It ensures the resulting module has a compatible group action that respects the original structure. The method relies on linear maps and tensor products to preserve algebraic properties during the extension.

label: Representation.isProj_averageMap
slogan: The averageMap function in a group representation takes any vector and returns a new vector that is invariant under the group action, meaning it doesn't change when any group element acts on it. If the input vector is already invariant, the function returns it unchanged. This works for finite groups when the group size has a multiplicative inverse in the ring.

label: Representation.tprod
slogan: The tprod function takes two representations of a monoid over modules and builds a new representation on the tensor product of those modules, where each group element acts by applying the original representations separately on each component of a tensor. This action is linear and respects the group's multiplication and identity. The resulting object is a valid representation because it preserves the monoid structure through the tensor product of the actions.

label: Representation.trivial
slogan: The trivial representation sends every element of a monoid to the identity map on a module, so no element changes the module's structure. It is defined for any module over a commutative semiring and ensures the monoid action is compatible with the module's linearity. This representation always exists and respects the algebraic properties of the involved structures.

label: RiemannHypothesis
slogan: The RiemannHypothesis is a logical proposition stating that all non-trivial zeros of the riemannZeta function have real part equal to 1/2. It is one of the most famous unsolved problems in mathematics, and proving it would have profound implications for the distribution of prime numbers. A proof of this statement would also qualify for a million-dollar prize.

label: Ring
slogan: A Ring is a mathematical structure where you can add, subtract, multiply, and negate elements, with addition being commutative, multiplication being associative, and multiplication distributing over addition; it includes a zero and a one, supports integer literals, and follows standard arithmetic rules. It combines the features of an additive commutative group and a semiring. The structure allows consistent conversion of integers into its elements via a ring homomorphism.

label: Ring.DirectLimit
slogan: The direct limit of a directed system of commutative rings is a ring formed by combining all the rings in the system, identifying elements that are mapped to each other through the directed structure. It is constructed so that compatible elements across the rings are glued together in a consistent way. This resulting ring satisfies a universal property with respect to maps from the original system.

label: Ring.KrullDimLE
slogan: Ring.KrullDimLE n R means that in the commutative semiring R, there is no chain of prime ideals with more than n strict inclusions, where prime ideals are ordered by inclusion. It expresses that the longest such chain has at most n steps from one prime ideal to another properly containing it. This measures the dimension of the ring by the height of its lattice of prime ideals.

label: Ring.KrullDimLE.isField_of_isDomain
slogan: If a commutative ring with unity has no nonzero zero divisors and its longest chain of prime ideals has length at most zero, then every nonzero element has a multiplicative inverse, making the ring a field. This means the only ideals are the zero ideal and the whole ring, and the ring supports division by any nonzero element.

label: Ring.choose
slogan: The Ring.choose function computes the binomial coefficient "r choose n" in algebraic structures that support addition, multiplication, and clean division by factorials, generalizing the natural number version of combinations. It works for elements r in a ring R and a natural number n, relying on the ring having properties that ensure operations like exponentiation and division by factorials are well-defined. This operation models choosing n items from r without replacement, extended to work beyond natural numbers.

label: Ring.choose_succ_succ
slogan: For any element r in a binomial ring R and any natural number k, the binomial coefficient of (r + 1) choose (k + 1) is equal to the sum of (r choose k) and (r choose (k + 1)). This generalizes Pascal's identity to binomial rings. It mirrors the familiar property of binomial coefficients in combinatorics.

label: Ring.isField_iff_isSimpleOrder_ideal
slogan: A commutative semiring is a field if and only if its only ideals are the zero ideal and the whole ring, with no ideals in between. This means the ring has a simple ideal structure, where the lattice of ideals has no intermediate elements. In other words, a ring allows division by nonzero elements precisely when it lacks nontrivial ideals.

label: Ring.jacobson
slogan: The Jacobson radical of a ring R is the intersection of all maximal ideals in R, or the entire ring if there are no maximal ideals. It consists of those elements that are annihilated by every homomorphism into simple modules. This gives a measure of how far the ring is from being semisimple.

label: Ring.jacobson_eq_sInf_isMaximal
slogan: The Jacobson radical of a ring is the set of elements that are in every maximal ideal of the ring. It equals the intersection of all maximal ideals, where a maximal ideal is a largest proper ideal not contained in any other proper ideal. This intersection is well-defined because the set of maximal ideals has a greatest lower bound under inclusion.

label: Ring.krullDimLE_zero_and_isLocalRing_tfae
slogan: A ring has Krull dimension at most zero if and only if it is a local ring where every element is either a unit or nilpotent, the maximal ideal contains all non-units, and there is exactly one prime ideal. In such a ring, the nilradical is maximal and there are no chains of distinct prime ideals of length greater than zero. This means the ring's ideal structure is as simple as possible, with no hierarchy among prime ideals.

label: RingAut
slogan: RingAut R represents the set of all bijective functions from a ring R to itself that preserve both addition and multiplication. These functions can be composed, and together they form a group. The type requires R to support both addition and multiplication operations.

label: RingCon.comapQuotientEquivRange
slogan: Given a ring homomorphism f from N to M and a congruence relation c on M, the quotient of N by the preimage of c under f is isomorphic to the image of the composed map from N to the quotient of M by c. This establishes a ring isomorphism between the quotient structure on N and the range of a related homomorphism. The result captures the essence of the second isomorphism theorem for rings in terms of congruences and homomorphic images.

label: RingEquiv
slogan: A RingEquiv is a one-to-one correspondence between two types with addition and multiplication, where the mapping and its inverse preserve both operations, so the structure of a ring is fully maintained when moving between the types.

label: RingHom
slogan: A RingHom is a function between two rings that preserves addition, multiplication, and the multiplicative identity (one), ensuring the full ring structure is respected. It combines the properties of preserving both additive and multiplicative operations, including mapping zero to zero and one to one. This makes it a complete structure-preserving map between rings in algebra.

label: RingHom.Flat
slogan: A ring homomorphism f from R to S is called flat if, when S is viewed as a module over R using f, it satisfies the flatness property, meaning tensoring with S preserves exact sequences. This relies on R and S being commutative rings and f respecting their ring structures. The flatness condition ensures that S behaves well with respect to certain algebraic operations involving R-modules.

label: RingHom.injective
slogan: A ring homomorphism from a simple ring to a nontrivial ring is injective, meaning it maps different elements to different elements. If two elements in the source ring have the same image under the homomorphism, then they must be the same element. This holds when the target ring has more than one element and the source ring has no nontrivial ideals.

label: RingHom.ker
slogan: RingHom.ker takes a ring homomorphism and returns the set of elements in the source ring that map to zero in the target ring, which forms an ideal. This ideal is constructed by taking the preimage of the zero ideal under the homomorphism. It applies to any structure-preserving map between semirings that respects addition, multiplication, and the multiplicative identity.

label: RingHom.map_det
slogan: Applying a ring homomorphism to every entry of a square matrix and then computing the determinant gives the same result as first computing the determinant and then applying the homomorphism to that value.

label: RingHom.quotientKerEquivOfSurjective
slogan: If a ring homomorphism maps every element in its codomain and has a well-defined inverse for each output, then the ring formed by taking the domain modulo the kernel (elements that map to zero) is isomorphic to the codomain. This isomorphism preserves both addition and multiplication, meaning the two rings have identical algebraic structure. The surjectivity of the homomorphism ensures that this correspondence covers the entire codomain.

label: RingHom.quotientKerEquivRange
slogan: Every ring homomorphism can be broken down into two steps: first, take the source ring and divide out the kernel (the elements that map to zero), and then map the result isomorphically onto the image of the homomorphism in the target ring. This means the quotient of the source ring by the kernel is structurally identical to the subring of outputs in the target. The isomorphism preserves both addition and multiplication.

label: RingQuot
slogan: RingQuot defines a new ring by taking an existing semiring and treating all elements of a given ideal as zero, so that arithmetic operations still work correctly in the resulting structure. It ensures that addition and multiplication are preserved in a consistent way after this simplification. The relation r specifies which elements are considered equivalent to zero in the new ring.

label: RootPairing.Base
slogan: A base of a root pairing is a subset of the indexing set that corresponds to a linearly independent set of roots, such that every root can be expressed as a linear combination of these with all coefficients either nonnegative or nonpositive integers. It generalizes the concept of a simple system in root system theory. This definition is stricter for non-reduced root pairings than the usual one in informal literature.

label: RootPairing.Base.IsPos
slogan: A root is considered positive with respect to a base if it can be written as a linear combination of base roots using only non-negative integer coefficients. This means the root lies "on the same side" as the base in the root system structure. The condition relies on the algebraic setup of modules over a commutative ring with characteristic zero.

label: RootPairing.Base.cartanMatrix
slogan: The Cartan matrix is an integer-valued matrix defined for a crystallographic root system with a chosen base, where each entry is the pairing between a root and a coroot from the base. It is indexed by the elements of the base and takes values in the integers. This matrix encodes the geometric structure of the root system relative to its base.

label: RootPairing.Base.height
slogan: The height of a root, with respect to a given base, is the sum of the integer coefficients when the root is expressed as a combination of base elements.

label: RootPairing.Base.toWeightBasis
slogan: A base of a root system provides a set of roots that form a basis for the vector space (or module) in which the root system lives, meaning every element of the space can be uniquely expressed as a linear combination of these roots. This basis is indexed by the support of the base and works over the underlying ring or field. The function converts such a base into a formal basis object for the module.

label: RootPairing.Equiv
slogan: An equivalence of root pairings is a structure-preserving map between two root pairings where the linear maps between weight and coweight spaces are bijective, meaning they are invertible and preserve roots, coroots, and the pairing structure. It ensures the indexing sets and root system data correspond perfectly in both directions. Such equivalences capture when two root pairings are essentially the same in structure.

label: RootPairing.InvariantForm.exists_apply_eq_or
slogan: In a reduced irreducible finite crystallographic root system, there are at most two distinct lengths for the roots, meaning every root's squared length equals one of two possible values.

label: RootPairing.IsCrystallographic
slogan: A root pairing is crystallographic if, for every root and its corresponding coroot, the result of their pairing is an integer. This means the evaluation of each root with its coroot must always be a whole number. The structure involves modules over a commutative ring, with roots and coroots indexed by a common set.

label: RootPairing.IsReduced
slogan: A root pairing is called reduced if any two roots that are linearly dependent are just negatives of each other. This means no root can have a nontrivial scalar multiple (other than -1) also be a root. The condition ensures a minimal, non-redundant set of roots in the pairing.

label: RootPairing.mapsTo_reflection_root
slogan: The reflection associated with a root in a root pairing maps the set of all roots to itself, meaning that applying the reflection to any root results in another root within the same set.

label: RootPairing.weylGroup
slogan: The Weyl group of a root pairing is the subgroup of automorphisms generated by reflections associated with the roots. It is formed by taking all combinations of these reflections and their inverses within the automorphism group. This group captures the symmetries of the root pairing structure.

label: Sat.Valuation.satisfies
slogan: Sat.Valuation.satisfies checks if a truth assignment makes a logical clause true by evaluating each literal: positive literals stand for variables and negative ones for their negations, using the assignment to determine truth values. It returns true if at least one literal in the clause is true under the assignment. This is used to verify that a clause is satisfied in the process of checking SAT solver proofs.

label: Sat.Valuation.satisfies_fmla
slogan: A valuation assigns true or false to each variable in a propositional logic formula, and satisfies_fmla checks whether the formula evaluates to true under that assignment. The formula is represented as a list of clauses, where each clause is a list of integers representing literals. This relation returns true if the given valuation makes all clauses true, meaning the formula is satisfied.

label: SchauderBasis
slogan: A SchauderBasis is a sequence of vectors in a normed vector space over a nontrivially normed field, indexed by the natural numbers, such that every vector in the space can be uniquely expressed as a conditionally convergent series of scalar multiples of these basis vectors, where convergence is defined using limits of partial sums over initial segments of the sequence.

label: SchwartzMap
slogan: A SchwartzMap is a smooth function between two real normed spaces such that the function and all its derivatives decay faster than any inverse power of the norm of the input.

label: SchwartzMap.convolution
slogan: The convolution of two Schwartz functions is a bilinear operation that takes a pair of rapidly decaying smooth functions and produces another such function, using a continuous linear map to combine their values. This operation is continuous in the first argument and respects the vector space structure of Schwartz functions. It is defined in the context of finite-dimensional real inner product spaces and involves scalar multiplication compatibility over complex and real numbers.

label: SchwartzMap.derivCLM
slogan: The derivative of a Schwartz function (a smooth function whose values and all derivatives decay rapidly at infinity) is also a Schwartz function, and this operation is represented as a continuous linear map over a field 𝕜 that behaves like the real or complex numbers. This map takes Schwartz functions from the real line to a normed space F and returns another Schwartz function of the same type. The derivative operation preserves the structure of the Schwartz space and is linear and continuous with respect to the topology of that space.

label: SchwartzMap.fourierTransformCLE
slogan: The Fourier transform is a continuous, linear, and invertible map between two topological modules E and F over a semiring R, where the transform and its inverse are additive, homogeneous, and continuous, and compose to the identity on both sides. This means the Fourier transform establishes a structure-preserving isomorphism between the function spaces E and F. The conditions ensure it behaves well with respect to algebraic operations and topology.

label: SchwartzMap.fourierTransformCLM
slogan: The Fourier transform is defined as a continuous linear map that takes rapidly decaying smooth functions (Schwartz functions) on a finite-dimensional real inner product space to other such functions, preserving the structure of the space. It operates within the context of complex and real normed spaces, and is parameterized by a scalar field that behaves like the real or complex numbers. This map is specifically designed for use in distribution theory and harmonic analysis.

label: SchwartzMap.integral_inner_fourier_fourier
slogan: The integral of the inner product of the Fourier transforms of two Schwartz functions over all points is equal to the integral of the inner product of the functions themselves over all points. This means the Fourier transform preserves the inner product structure for Schwartz functions. It is a version of Plancherel's theorem in the context of functions that decay rapidly along with their derivatives.

label: SchwartzMap.laplacian_eq_fourierMultiplierCLM
slogan: The Laplacian of a Schwartz function f is equal to -4 times pi squared times the result of applying a Fourier multiplier operation to f, where the multiplier is the squared norm of the input variable. This means differentiation in physical space corresponds to multiplication by a quadratic function in frequency space. The identity holds for smooth, rapidly decaying functions on finite-dimensional real inner product spaces with values in a complete complex normed space.

label: SchwartzMap.tsum_eq_tsum_fourier
slogan: For a Schwartz function f on the real line, the sum of f(x + n) over all integers n equals the sum of the Fourier transform of f evaluated at integers n, multiplied by the complex exponential exp(2 * pi * i * n * x), also summed over all integers n.

label: ScottContinuous
slogan: A function is Scott continuous if, for every directed set with a least upper bound, the image of that set under the function also has a least upper bound and the function maps the original least upper bound to the least upper bound of the image. This means the function preserves the limit-like structure of directed suprema in preorders. It depends on the notions of preorders, directed sets, set images, nonempty sets, and least upper bounds.

label: ScottContinuousOn
slogan: A function is Scott continuous on a set if, for every directed subset that has a least upper bound, the image of that subset under the function also has a least upper bound and the function maps the original least upper bound to the least upper bound of the image. This ensures the function preserves the limit structure of directed sets in preorders. It depends on the notions of preorder, directed set, least upper bound, and image of a set.

label: SecondCountableTopology
slogan: A second-countable topology is a topological space where the open sets can all be formed by combining elements from a countable collection of basic open sets. It requires both the structure of a topological space and the existence of a countable basis. This is expressed as a property that combines the topological space condition with the requirement that a countable base exists.

label: SemidirectProduct
slogan: The semidirect product combines two groups, N and G, into a new group using a map φ that describes how elements of G act as symmetries on N. The group operation multiplies pairs (n1, g1) and (n2, g2) by applying φ to transform n2 before multiplying in N, while multiplying g1 and g2 directly in G. This construction generalizes the direct product by allowing a nontrivial interaction between the two groups.

label: Semigroup
slogan: A semigroup is a set with a multiplication operation where the order of operations doesn't matter as long as the sequence of elements stays the same—specifically, (a * b) * c always equals a * (b * c). The multiplication must combine any two elements of the set to produce another element of the same set, using the * operator. No requirement is made for an identity element or inverses—only that multiplication is associative.

label: Seminorm
slogan: A seminorm is a function that assigns a non-negative real number to each element of an additive group, respects scalar multiplication, and satisfies the triangle inequality, but does not require that only the zero element has zero length. It is defined on a type equipped with addition, negation, zero, and scalar multiplication by elements of a seminormed ring. This structure generalizes notions of size in vector-like spaces where scaling and addition are defined.

label: Seminorm.continuous_from_bounded
slogan: If a linear map between two topological vector spaces is bounded with respect to families of seminorms, and the target space's topology is defined by continuous seminorms, then the map is continuous. This means that boundedness relative to continuous seminorms guarantees continuity of the linear map. The result holds when the source and target spaces are equipped with topologies induced by their respective seminorm families.

label: Seminorm.convexOn
slogan: A seminorm assigns a non-negative value to vectors in a way that respects scaling and addition, and the set of vectors where the seminorm is finite forms a convex set, meaning any weighted average of two such vectors (with non-negative weights adding to one) also has a finite seminorm value.

label: SeminormFamily
slogan: A SeminormFamily is a set of functions from a module over a seminormed ring to the real numbers, where each function satisfies subadditivity and absolute homogeneity, and the module's underlying type is an additive commutative group.

label: SeminormFamily.moduleFilterBasis
slogan: A family of seminorms on a module over a normed field gives rise to a filter basis at zero, where the basic neighborhoods are sets that bound finitely many seminorms by positive numbers, and these sets are closed under addition, symmetric, and absorbent. The resulting topology makes addition and scalar multiplication continuous, ensuring the module has a compatible topological structure. This filter basis respects the algebraic operations and the norm on the field, turning the module into a topological module.

label: Semiring
slogan: A semiring is a set with addition and multiplication that work like they do on natural numbers: addition is commutative and associative, multiplication is associative, multiplication distributes over addition, there's an additive zero and a multiplicative one, and anything times zero is zero. It supports converting natural numbers into its elements and combines a commutative monoid under addition with a monoid under multiplication. This structure allows basic algebraic operations without requiring subtraction or negative numbers.

label: SemistandardYoungTableau
slogan: A semistandard Young tableau is a way of filling a Young diagram with natural numbers so that numbers in each row do not decrease from left to right and numbers in each column strictly increase from top to bottom. The filling is represented as a function from pairs of natural numbers (row, column) to natural numbers, where entries outside the diagram are zero. A Young diagram itself is a collection of cells arranged in rows and columns such that if a cell is present, all cells above and to the left are also included.

label: SeparatedNhds
slogan: Two subsets of a topological space are separated by neighborhoods if there are two disjoint open sets, each containing one of the subsets, such that no point belongs to both open sets. This means each subset is completely contained in its own open set, and these open sets do not intersect. The condition depends only on the topology and the arrangement of the subsets within the space.

label: SeparatedNhds.of_isCompact_isCompact
slogan: If two compact sets in a Hausdorff space have no points in common, then there are open sets containing each of them that also do not overlap. This means you can always separate disjoint compact sets in a Hausdorff space with non-overlapping open neighborhoods. The result depends on the space being Hausdorff, where distinct points can be separated by open sets.

label: SeparationQuotient
slogan: The separation quotient groups together points in a topological space that cannot be told apart by open sets, meaning they belong to exactly the same open sets. It forms a new space where these indistinguishable points are identified, resulting in a T0 space where distinct points can always be separated by some open set. This construction uses an equivalence relation based on topological indistinguishability.

label: SeparationQuotient.t2Space_iff
slogan: A topological space is Hausdorff if and only if its separation quotient, formed by grouping together topologically indistinguishable points, is also Hausdorff; this means distinct equivalence classes in the quotient can be separated by disjoint open sets. The condition holds because the quotient map is surjective and preimages of neighborhoods under this map preserve disjointness. Essentially, the original space is T2 exactly when its quotient space is T2.

label: SeqContinuous
slogan: A function is sequentially continuous if, whenever a sequence in the domain gets arbitrarily close to a point, the function values on that sequence get arbitrarily close to the function's value at that point. This means that for any target neighborhood around the output, the outputs of the sequence eventually stay inside that neighborhood. The definition uses filters to formalize convergence: the function maps sequences converging to a point to sequences converging to the image of that point.

label: SequentialSpace
slogan: A sequential space is a topological space where a set is closed exactly when it includes the limits of all sequences of points inside it. This means the topology can be fully understood by looking at which sequences converge and where they converge to. It connects the idea of closed sets with the behavior of convergent sequences.

label: Set.Countable
slogan: A set is countable if its elements can be matched one-to-one with natural numbers, meaning they can be listed in a sequence; this includes both finite sets and sets that are infinite but can still be enumerated.

label: Set.Countable.measure_zero
slogan: In a space where no single point has positive size according to the measure, any set that contains at most countably many points must have total measure zero. This means that if a measure assigns zero to each individual point, then any countable collection of such points also has measure zero.

label: Set.Countable.mono
slogan: If a set s2 is countable and s1 is a subset of s2, then s1 is also countable. This is because the inclusion map from s1 into s2 is injective, and injective functions preserve countability.

label: Set.Countable.prod
slogan: If two sets can be listed in a sequence (are countable), then the set of all pairs formed by taking one element from each set is also countable. This is because there is a systematic way to list all such pairs without missing any, ensuring the resulting set remains countable.

label: Set.Countable.union
slogan: A union of two countable sets is also countable. This means if each set can be listed in a sequence (or is finite), then their combination using union (∪) can still be listed in a sequence. The result holds because both the sets and the way they are indexed are countable.

label: Set.Definable
slogan: A subset of a finite product of a structure M is definable over a set A if there is a first-order formula, using symbols from a language L and parameters from A, such that the elements of the subset are exactly those that satisfy the formula when interpreted in M.

label: Set.Definable₁
slogan: A set s of elements from a structure M is definable over a subset A using a first-order language L if there is a first-order formula in L with parameters from A that exactly describes which elements of M are in s. This is the one-dimensional case of definability, where we are only considering subsets of the single structure M, not higher-dimensional products. The definition depends on having a language L and an interpretation of that language in M.

label: Set.Finite
slogan: A finite set is one that contains only a limited number of distinct elements, and there exists a natural number that counts exactly how many elements are in it. Such a set can be completely listed, and its size is well-defined. The property of being finite is expressed as a logical condition on sets.

label: Set.Finite.convexHull_eq_image
slogan: The convex hull of a finite set of points is the set of all weighted averages of those points, where the weights are nonnegative and add up to one. This set of combinations can be seen as the image of a standard simplex under a linear map that builds these weighted sums. The result applies when the set is finite and the space allows linear operations over an ordered field.

label: Set.Finite.countable
slogan: If a set has only finitely many elements, then its elements can be listed in a sequence using natural numbers, meaning it is countable. This is because any finite set can be matched one-to-one with a finite subset of the natural numbers, which is itself countable.

label: Set.Icc
slogan: Set.Icc a b is the set of all elements x where a is less than or equal to x and x is less than or equal to b, for any type that has a preorder. It uses the setOf function to collect all such x that satisfy the condition a <= x <= b. This forms a closed interval including both endpoints a and b.

label: Set.Infinite
slogan: A set is infinite if it is not finite, meaning its elements cannot be counted by any natural number. This definition relies on the concept that a finite set has a specific number of elements, and infinite sets are those that do not meet this condition. It applies to any type of set where finiteness can be determined.

label: Set.Infinite.exists_subset_countable_infinite
slogan: Every infinite set contains a subset that is countably infinite, meaning there is always a way to find a part of the set that can be matched one-to-one with the natural numbers. This subset is both infinite and countable. The existence of such a subset follows from the fact that infinite sets allow for injective mappings from the natural numbers into them.

label: Set.Nontrivial.infsep_exists_of_finite
slogan: If a set in a pseudometric space is finite and has at least two distinct points, then there exist two points in the set, different from each other, such that the distance between them equals the smallest positive distance between any two points in the set.

label: Set.OrdConnected
slogan: A set is ordConnected if it contains all points between any two of its points according to the order, and it cannot be divided into two separate nonempty open parts. This means the set is both order-convex and topologically connected. The type must support a preorder and a compatible topology.

label: Set.PairwiseDisjoint.isPartition_of_exists_of_ne_empty
slogan: If a collection of sets is pairwise disjoint, every element of the type belongs to at least one set in the collection, and the empty set is not in the collection, then the collection is a partition.

label: Set.Subset
slogan: A set B is a subset of a set A if every element of B is also an element of A. This means that having an object in B guarantees it is also in A. The relation is a fundamental way to compare sets based on their elements.

label: Set.Subset.antisymm
slogan: If two sets are subsets of each other, then they are equal. This is because sets are equal whenever they contain exactly the same elements. The subset relation is well-defined for sets, making such comparisons valid.

label: Set.Subset.antisymm_iff
slogan: Two sets are equal if and only if each is a subset of the other; this means that whenever every element of the first set is in the second and vice versa, the sets contain exactly the same elements.

label: Set.Subset.refl
slogan: For any set A, every element of A is also an element of A, so A is always a subset of itself.

label: Set.Subset.trans
slogan: If one set is contained within a second, and the second is contained within a third, then the first set is also contained within the third. This applies to any three sets in a chain of inclusion. The subset relation is transitive.

label: Set.add
slogan: Set.add creates a new set by adding every element from one set to every element from another set, using the type's addition operation. The result is the set of all possible sums of pairs from the two sets. This works for any type that supports addition.

label: Set.chainHeight
slogan: The chainHeight of a set s with respect to a relation r is the supremum of the sizes of all chains in s, where a chain is a subset in which every pair of distinct elements is related by r. It returns a value in the extended natural numbers (including infinity). This measures the longest possible chain of related elements within the set.

label: Set.compl
slogan: The complement of a set is defined as the set of all elements that do not belong to the original set, using a function that collects elements for which the "not in" condition holds.

label: Set.countable_iUnion
slogan: If you have a countable collection of sets, and each set in the collection is countable, then the union of all these sets is also countable. This means that combining countably many countable sets results in a set that is still countable. The result relies on the fact that you can systematically list all elements from all sets using the countability of the index set and each individual set.

label: Set.countable_infinite_iff_nonempty_denumerable
slogan: A set is countably infinite if and only if it is nonempty and can be put into a one-to-one correspondence with the natural numbers. This means the set has infinitely many elements and they can be listed in a sequence that includes each element exactly once. The existence of such a listing is equivalent to the set being both countable and infinite.

label: Set.countable_setOf_finite_subset
slogan: Any collection of finite subsets of a countable set is itself countable, meaning that if the elements of a set can be listed in a sequence, then all its limited-size subcollections can also be arranged in a sequence. This follows because injective functions preserve countability, and finite subsets can be mapped injectively into countable structures.

label: Set.diagonal
slogan: The diagonal of a set S is the collection of all pairs (x, x) such that x is an element of S. It is a subset of the Cartesian product S × S, where both elements in each pair are identical. This is defined using a set builder notation based on the property that the two components of the pair are equal.

label: Set.diff
slogan: Set.diff is a function that takes two sets and returns a new set containing only the elements that are in the first set but not in the second. It works by collecting all elements that satisfy being in the first set and not in the second, using the setOf function. This is the standard set difference operation.

label: Set.disjoint_iff_inter_eq_empty
slogan: Two sets are disjoint if and only if their intersection is the empty set, meaning they have no elements in common. This is equivalent to saying that the only way two sets can be disjoint is when there is nothing shared between them. The empty set, which has no elements, represents this lack of overlap.

label: Set.empty_def
slogan: The empty set is defined as the set of all elements x such that the condition False holds, which no element can satisfy. It is written as {} or ∅ and exists for every type, representing a collection with no members. This relies on the fact that False has no proofs, so no element can belong to this set.

label: Set.empty_subset
slogan: The empty set, denoted by {} or ∅, is a subset of every set. This means that no matter what elements a set contains, the set with no elements is always considered to be contained within it. The notations {} and ⊆ are supported for expressing empty sets and subset relationships in set operations.

label: Set.eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem
slogan: A set is equal to the empty set if and only if no element of its type is a member of it.

label: Set.eq_empty_of_forall_notMem
slogan: If no element of a given type is in a set, then that set must be equal to the empty set. This means the only set with no members is the empty set, denoted {} or ∅. It relies on standard set notation and the definition of the empty collection for any type.

label: Set.ext
slogan: Two sets are equal when every element of one set is also an element of the other, and vice versa. This means that if an object belongs to one set exactly when it belongs to the other, the sets are the same. The order or description does not matter—only the elements themselves.

label: Set.ext_iff
slogan: Two sets are equal if and only if every element of one set is also an element of the other, and vice versa.

label: Set.extremePoints
slogan: A point x is an extreme point of a set A if it does not lie in the interior of any open line segment between two distinct points of A, except when the segment is degenerate (from x to x). The set of all such extreme points of A is given by the function extremePoints. This definition applies in contexts where points can be scaled and added, such as in vector spaces over semirings.

label: Set.forall_mem_empty
slogan: For any type and any property, the statement that all elements of the empty set have that property is always true, since there are no elements in the empty set. This makes any universal claim about the elements of the empty set vacuously true. The empty set contains nothing, so there is nothing to check.

label: Set.graphOn
slogan: Set.graphOn takes a function f and a set s, then returns the set of all pairs (x, f(x)) where x is an element of s; this forms the graph of f restricted to the domain s.

label: Set.image_preimage
slogan: For any function f and set S, applying f to the set of points that map into S gives a result that is always contained in S; if all such points are included, the result equals the portion of S that f can actually reach. This means the image of the preimage of S under f is exactly the intersection of S with the range of f. The relationship between taking images and preimages forms a Galois connection, reflecting an order-preserving duality between sets in the domain and codomain.

label: Set.image_preimage_eq
slogan: If a function f covers all elements of a set S in its output, then taking all inputs that map into S and applying f to them gives back exactly the set S. This holds when every element in the target set has at least one input that maps to it. In simple terms, f maps the preimage of S onto S completely when f is surjective.

label: Set.image_preimage_subset
slogan: For any function f and set s, applying f to all elements that map into s gives a set that is contained in s. In other words, the image of the preimage of s under f is always a subset of s.

label: Set.inclusion
slogan: If one set s is contained in another set t, then every element of s is also an element of t, and the inclusion function maps each element of s to the corresponding element in t while preserving this membership. This function allows treating elements of a subset as elements of the larger set. It relies on the standard subset relation and subtype properties to ensure correctness.

label: Set.indicator
slogan: Set.indicator is a function that, given a set s and a function f, returns a new function which equals f(x) when x is in s and returns zero otherwise. It relies on classical logic to determine whether an element belongs to the set, and requires the output type to support a zero value. This is useful for creating functions that are non-zero only on a specified subset.

label: Set.instEmptyCollection
slogan: The declaration allows the symbol ∅ or {} to represent an empty set for any type α, meaning a collection with no elements. It works by implementing a typeclass called EmptyCollection for sets. This makes the empty set notation available in expressions involving sets of any type.

label: Set.inter
slogan: The Set.inter operation takes two sets of the same type and returns a new set containing only the elements that appear in both sets. It requires the type to have decidable equality so that membership can be checked. This operation is what allows the use of the ∩ symbol to compute set intersections.

label: Set.inter_assoc
slogan: For any three sets A, B, and C, the intersection of A and B taken together with C gives the same result as intersecting A with the intersection of B and C. In other words, (A ∩ B) ∩ C equals A ∩ (B ∩ C). This means parentheses can be rearranged when computing intersections without changing the result.

label: Set.inter_eq_left
slogan: If set A is a subset of set B, then the intersection of A and B is equal to A; this means A ∩ B = A holds true exactly when every element of A is also in B.

label: Set.inter_union_distrib_left
slogan: The intersection of set A with the union of sets B and C is the same as the union of the intersection of A and B with the intersection of A and C. In symbols, A ∩ (B ∪ C) = (A ∩ B) ∪ (A ∩ C). This rule shows how intersection distributes over union when applied from the left.

label: Set.mem_inter_iff
slogan: An element is in the intersection of two sets if and only if it is in both of those sets. This means being in the intersection is the same as being in the first set and also being in the second set. The word "and" is used to require both conditions at once.

label: Set.ncard_powerset
slogan: The number of subsets of a finite set is exactly two raised to the power of the number of elements in that set. This means if a set has n elements, it has 2^n subsets in total. The result only applies to finite sets and uses ordinary natural number exponentiation.

label: Set.pi
slogan: Set.pi defines the Cartesian product of a family of sets indexed by a type, where each element of the product is a function that assigns to every index an element from the corresponding set. It collects all such functions whose value at each index lies in the specified set for that index. This generalizes finite Cartesian products to arbitrary, possibly infinite, index sets.

label: Set.powerset
slogan: Set.powerset is a function that takes a set and returns the collection of all its subsets, meaning each element of the result is a set that contains only elements from the original set.

label: Set.powersetCard
slogan: Set.powersetCard takes a type α and a natural number n, and returns the set of all finite subsets of α that have exactly n elements. It is used to represent all possible combinations of n elements from α. This is similar to selecting all n-element subcollections from a collection without duplicates.

label: Set.powerset_empty
slogan: The powerset of the empty set is the set that contains only the empty set. This means the only subset of the empty set is the empty set itself. So, the collection of all subsets of ∅ has exactly one element, which is ∅.

label: Set.preimage
slogan: The preimage of a set S under a function f is the set of all elements x such that f(x) is in S. It is formed by collecting every x from the domain of f that maps into S. This operation is commonly used in set theory, measure theory, and algebra.

label: Set.prod
slogan: Set.prod takes two sets and returns the set of all ordered pairs where the first element is from the first set and the second is from the second set. This creates the Cartesian product of the two sets, forming a new set whose elements are pairs of the original types. For example, if the sets contain elements of type α and β, the result is a set of elements of type α × β.

label: Set.range
slogan: Set.range f is the set of all outputs produced by applying the function f to every possible input. It consists of all values y such that y equals f(x) for some x. This is the same as the set of elements y where there exists an x with f(x) = y.

label: Set.rangeFactorization
slogan: Every output in the range of a function f comes from applying f to some input x, and the range is precisely the collection of all such outputs. The function Set.rangeFactorization maps each input to its corresponding value in the range, confirming that every element of the range is reachable in this way. This means the range of f is made up exactly of the values f(x) for inputs x in the domain.

label: Set.rangeFactorization_surjective
slogan: The function Set.rangeFactorization f maps inputs to the range of f in such a way that every element in the range is hit by some input, ensuring the map is surjective. This means for every element in the output set, there is some input that produces it. The result guarantees that the image of the function fully covers its range.

label: Set.restrict
slogan: Set.restrict takes a set s and a function f defined on a type, and returns a new function that only applies f to elements within the set s, ensuring all inputs are restricted to those that belong to s. It is used to limit the domain of a function to a specific subset of its original type. The result is a function that operates on the restricted subset while preserving the output type.

label: Set.sInter
slogan: Set.sInter takes a collection of sets and returns a new set containing only the elements that are present in every set within the collection. It computes the intersection of all sets in the given collection. This operation is defined for any type of elements and works within the framework of set-theoretic operations.

label: Set.sUnion
slogan: The sUnion function takes a collection of sets and returns a single set that contains all elements from every set in the collection. It works by combining all sets in the collection using the union operation, which includes any element that is in at least one of the sets. This union is defined as the supremum (least upper bound) of the sets in the context of a lattice ordered by inclusion.

label: Set.sUnion_eq_univ_iff
slogan: The union of a collection of sets equals the set of all possible elements if and only if every element is in at least one set from the collection.

label: Set.singleton
slogan: Set.singleton is a function that takes an element 'a' of any type and returns a set containing only that element, written as {a}. It allows Lean to support standard mathematical notation for single-element sets by using a type class instance that defines how such sets are constructed. This works together with other operations like inserting elements or creating empty sets.

label: Set.ssubset_def
slogan: A set A is a strict subset of set B if all elements of A are in B, but B contains at least one element not in A. This means A is contained in B and A is not equal to B. The condition is written as A ⊂ B and is equivalent to (A ⊆ B and not B ⊆ A).

label: Set.ssubset_iff_subset_ne
slogan: A set A is a strict subset of set B if and only if A is contained in B but A is not equal to B. This means every element of A is in B, yet B has at least one element not in A. The strict subset relation is defined in terms of subset and inequality.

label: Set.subset_def
slogan: A set s is a subset of set t if and only if every element x in s is also an element of t. This means s ⊆ t is equivalent to saying that for all x, if x is in s, then x must be in t. The subset relation is defined using universal quantification over the elements of the sets.

label: Set.union_assoc
slogan: For any three sets A, B, and C, combining A and B first and then adding all elements from C gives the same result as combining A with the combination of B and C. This means the way sets are grouped during unions does not affect the final set.

label: Set.union_comm
slogan: The union of two sets A and B is the same regardless of order, so A ∪ B equals B ∪ A. This means combining set A with set B gives the same result as combining set B with set A. The equality holds because both unions contain exactly the same elements.

label: Set.union_empty
slogan: The union of any set with the empty set is just the set itself. Adding nothing to a set doesn't change what's in it. This works for sets of any type of elements.

label: SetRel.dom
slogan: SetRel.dom returns the set of all elements that are related to something in a given relation. It collects every element x for which there exists some y such that the relation holds between x and y. This is done using setOf to gather all such x based on the relation's condition.
