slogan: In a Hausdorff space (T2 space), any two different points can be separated by non-overlapping open sets, and this property guarantees that every single-point set is closed, which means the space also satisfies the T1 condition.

label: T35Space
slogan: A T3.5 space is a topological space that is both completely regular and T0, meaning it can separate points from closed sets using continuous real-valued functions and also distinguishes between topologically indistinguishable points.

label: T35Space.instT3space
slogan: A T3.5 space is a topological space that is both completely regular and T0, and this declaration states that every T3.5 space is also a T3 space. Being a T3 space means that for any point and a closed set not containing it, there are disjoint open sets separating them. This follows because completely regular spaces are already regular, and regular T0 spaces are T3.

label: T3Space
slogan: A T3 space is a topological space where every point can be separated from any disjoint closed set by non-overlapping open sets, and any two distinct points have at least one open set containing one but not the other. This combines the properties of regularity and the T0 separation axiom. Such a space ensures both good separation between points and between points and closed sets.

label: T4Space
slogan: A T4 space is a topological space where all single points are closed sets, and any two disjoint closed sets can be separated by disjoint open sets. This means the space satisfies both the T1 and normal space conditions. It combines separation properties to ensure strong control over how points and closed sets can be isolated from each other.

label: T4Space.instT35Space
slogan: Every T4 space, which is a normal space where points are closed, is also a T3.5 space, meaning it can separate points from disjoint closed sets using continuous real-valued functions and satisfies the T0 separation axiom. This follows because normal spaces that are R0 are completely regular, and T4 spaces are both normal and T1 (hence R0 and T0). Thus, the conditions for being a T3.5 space are met.

label: TangentBundle
slogan: The TangentBundle combines a manifold and its tangent spaces into a single space, where each point is a pair consisting of a point on the manifold and a tangent vector at that point. It uses the topology and normed structure of the underlying model space to define a new space that captures both position and direction. This construction relies on the manifold having a system of smooth charts and a compatible normed vector space structure.

label: TangentSpace
slogan: The tangent space at a point on a manifold is the set of all possible directions in which you can take directional derivatives at that point, forming a vector space that models infinitesimal changes. It is built using local coordinate charts that map parts of the manifold to a normed vector space over a nontrivially normed field, preserving both the topological and algebraic structure. This allows the tangent space to reflect how functions on the manifold change smoothly near the point.

label: TangentSpace.vectorBundle
slogan: The tangent space of a smooth manifold forms a vector bundle, meaning it has a consistent structure where each point on the manifold has a tangent space that varies smoothly and supports linear operations. This structure is built using local coordinate charts and their derivatives to define how tangent spaces are glued together across the manifold. The field and normed space conditions ensure the necessary algebraic and topological properties for smoothness and continuity.

label: TannakaDuality.FiniteGroup.equiv
slogan: A finite group G is isomorphic to the group of automorphisms of the forgetful functor from its category of finite-dimensional representations over a domain k to the category of finite-dimensional k-modules. This means the group can be completely recovered from its representation category. The isomorphism holds for any commutative ring k that is also a domain.

label: TemperedDistribution
slogan: The space of tempered distributions consists of continuous linear functions that map Schwartz functions to a normed space, where the functions are treated as vectors and the mappings respect both linearity and convergence. These mappings are equipped with a topology defined by pointwise convergence, meaning a sequence of mappings converges when it converges at each input function. The definition involves real and complex vector spaces with compatible normed group and space structures.

label: TemperedDistribution.delta
slogan: The Dirac delta distribution is a continuous linear map that takes a Schwartz function and returns its value at zero. It is defined on the space of tempered distributions over a real normed vector space, mapping to the complex numbers. This object represents a generalized function used in analysis and physics to model point sources or impulses.

label: TemperedDistribution.derivCLM
slogan: The derivative of a tempered distribution in one dimension is defined as a continuous linear map over the complex numbers, taking tempered distributions to tempered distributions. It is constructed by duality from the derivative on Schwartz functions, preserving continuity and linearity. This map respects the structure of tempered distributions as continuous linear functionals on Schwartz functions.

label: TemperedDistribution.fourier_apply
slogan: The Fourier transform of a tempered distribution applied to a Schwartz function equals the original distribution applied to the Fourier transform of that Schwartz function. This means the Fourier transform of a distribution is defined by shifting the transform to the test function. It holds for functions on finite-dimensional real inner product spaces with values in a complex normed space.

label: TemperedDistribution.fourier_delta_zero
slogan: The Fourier transform of the Dirac delta distribution at zero is equal to the constant function 1, interpreted as the volume measure in the context of tempered distributions. This means that when you apply the Fourier transform to the delta distribution, you get a distribution that acts like integrating against the constant function 1. In simple terms, the total "mass" spread out over all space by the Fourier transform of delta is uniform and equal to the volume.

label: TemperedDistribution.instFourierTransform
slogan: The declaration states that the Fourier transform is defined as an operation on tempered distributions, meaning it specifies how to transform a continuous linear map from Schwartz functions to a normed space, in a way that respects the structure of these spaces when the domain is a finite-dimensional real inner product space and the codomain is a complex normed space.

label: TemperedDistribution.smulLeftCLM
slogan: Multiplying a tempered distribution by a function that grows at most polynomially results in another tempered distribution, and this operation is continuous and linear over the complex numbers. The map that performs this multiplication is itself a continuous linear operator on the space of tempered distributions. This works when the distributions take values in a complex normed space and are defined on a real normed group.

label: TendstoLocallyUniformly
slogan: A function F from a parameter space to functions on α with values in β converges locally uniformly to a limit function f if, for every point in α, there is a neighborhood around it where F eventually gets and stays uniformly close to f, meaning the closeness is measured by the uniform structure of β and holds across the entire neighborhood for sufficiently advanced parameters. This uses filters to formalize "sufficiently advanced" behavior and combines local topology with uniform closeness. The condition ensures that convergence is uniform on some neighborhood of each point.

label: TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn.differentiableOn
slogan: If a sequence of holomorphic functions converges uniformly on small neighborhoods within an open set in the complex plane, and the space they map into is complete, then the limit function is also holomorphic on that open set.

label: TendstoUniformly
slogan: TendstoUniformly describes a sequence of functions F from a set α to a uniform space β converging to a function f such that, for any desired level of closeness, all functions in the sequence beyond some point in the index set ι remain uniformly close to f across the entire domain α, as defined by the uniform structure on β.

label: TendstoUniformly.continuous
slogan: If a sequence of continuous functions converges uniformly to a limit function on a topological space, and infinitely many of the functions in the sequence are continuous, then the limit function is also continuous. Uniform convergence ensures that continuity is preserved in the limit. This holds in the general setting of uniform spaces, where closeness and convergence are defined using filters.

label: TendstoUniformly.tendstoLocallyUniformly
slogan: If a sequence of functions converges uniformly on a space, then it also converges uniformly in a neighborhood of each point. This means that uniform convergence implies local uniform convergence everywhere.

label: TendstoUniformlyOn
slogan: A sequence of functions f_n converges uniformly on a set s if, for any given level of closeness (defined by the uniform structure), there is some index after which all the functions in the sequence stay that close to the limit function at every point in s. This means the convergence happens evenly across the whole set, not just at specific points. The condition uses a filter to express that the desired closeness eventually holds for all later functions in the sequence.

label: TendstoUniformlyOn.continuousOn
slogan: If a sequence of functions converges uniformly on a set and infinitely many of them are continuous on that set, then the limit function is also continuous on that set. Uniform convergence ensures that continuity is preserved in the limit. This holds in spaces where closeness is defined by a uniform structure.

label: TensorAlgebra
slogan: The TensorAlgebra construction takes a module M over a commutative semiring R and builds an algebra containing all finite combinations of tensors made from elements of M, with multiplication defined by concatenating tensors. This algebra has the property that any linear map from M to another R-algebra can be uniquely extended to a homomorphism from the tensor algebra. It is the most general (freest) R-algebra generated by M.

label: TensorProduct
slogan: The tensor product of two modules over a commutative semiring is constructed by taking formal sums of pairs of elements and then imposing relations that ensure bilinearity, meaning addition and scalar multiplication distribute properly across both components. It is built as a quotient of a free additive monoid, where the equivalence relation enforces the expected algebraic rules for tensor products. This allows any bilinear map on the original modules to be uniquely represented as a linear map on the resulting tensor product.

label: TensorProduct.addCommMonoid
slogan: The tensor product of two modules over a commutative semiring has a well-defined addition operation that is commutative, associative, and has a zero element. This means you can add elements in the tensor product in any order, and the result will follow the usual rules of addition. The additive structure comes from the modules and the semiring they are built over.

label: TensorProduct.assoc
slogan: The function TensorProduct.assoc gives a natural way to reorganize the grouping of three modules in a tensor product, showing that (M ⊗ N) ⊗ P is structurally the same as M ⊗ (N ⊗ P) in terms of their module operations. It provides an invertible linear map between these two groupings that preserves addition and scalar multiplication. This allows free rearrangement of parentheses when working with tensor products of modules over a commutative semiring.

label: TensorProduct.comm
slogan: The tensor product of two modules M and N over a commutative semiring R has a natural linear equivalence to the tensor product of N and M, meaning the order of the modules can be swapped. This equivalence maps each element a ⊗ b to b ⊗ a and extends linearly to all tensors. It preserves addition and scalar multiplication, and its inverse is the map that swaps the order back.

label: TensorProduct.instInnerProductSpace
slogan: If E and F are inner product spaces over a real-like type 𝕜, then their tensor product over 𝕜 also forms an inner product space using the same base type 𝕜. This instance defines how to equip the tensor product of two spaces with an inner product derived from the inner products on the original spaces. The construction relies on the algebraic and topological structure of the base type and the properties of bilinear maps.

label: TensorProduct.lift
slogan: Given two modules over a commutative semiring and a bilinear map from their Cartesian product to another module, there is a unique linear map from the tensor product of the two modules to the target module that matches the original bilinear map on simple tensors. This universal property allows bilinear operations to be represented as linear operations on the tensor product. The function TensorProduct.lift constructs this linear map explicitly.

label: TensorProduct.lift.equiv
slogan: The function TensorProduct.lift.equiv gives a one-to-one match between linear maps from the tensor product M ⊗ N to P and bilinear maps from M and N to P, meaning every linear map on the tensor product comes from a unique bilinear map on M and N. This correspondence works for modules over commutative semirings and respects the linear structure, allowing free translation between bilinear operations and linear maps on tensors. It shows that defining a linear map out of M ⊗ N is equivalent to defining a bilinear map from M and N.

label: TensorProduct.map
slogan: Given two linear maps f and g between modules over commutative semirings, TensorProduct.map produces a linear map between the tensor products of the source modules and target modules, sending each simple tensor a ⊗ b to f(a) ⊗ g(b). This map is built using the universal property of tensor products to ensure linearity. It allows linear transformations to be applied separately on each component of a tensor product.

label: TensorProduct.map_surjective
slogan: If two linear maps are surjective, then the map they induce on the tensor product of their domains is also surjective, meaning every element in the resulting tensor product can be obtained by applying the induced map to some element in the source tensor product.

label: TensorProduct.mk
slogan: TensorProduct.mk provides a way to build elements of the tensor product of two modules over a commutative semiring by pairing elements from each module in a way that respects addition and scalar multiplication. It ensures that the pairing behaves linearly in both arguments, forming the foundation for constructing bilinear maps. The result is an object in the tensor product space that supports standard algebraic operations like addition and scaling.

label: TensorProduct.tmul
slogan: The tmul function takes an element from each of two modules over a commutative semiring and produces their tensor product as an element in the resulting tensor product space. It works by forming a formal pair of the elements and then applying quotienting rules that enforce bilinearity. This allows bilinear operations to be represented as linear ones in the new module.

label: TensorProduct.toMatrix_map
slogan: When you turn a linear map on tensor products into a matrix using bases, the result is the Kronecker product of the matrices of the individual linear maps. This means applying two linear transformations separately on tensor factors and then combining them as a matrix gives the same result as building their Kronecker product. The bases used must be finite and have decidable equality, and all structures must be modules over a commutative ring.

label: TestFunction
slogan: TestFunction represents smooth functions from an open subset of a real normed vector space E to another real normed vector space F, where the functions are n-times continuously differentiable and have compact support. The value of n can be any natural number or infinity. These functions are bundled with their smoothness and support properties for use in distribution theory.

label: TestFunction.continuous_iff_continuous_comp
slogan: A linear map from the space of n-times differentiable functions with compact support on an open set Ω to a locally convex topological vector space is continuous if and only if it remains continuous when restricted to functions supported in any compact subset K of Ω. This means continuity can be checked piecewise on compactly supported subspaces. The result relies on the topology of test functions being defined as the direct limit of these subspaces.

label: TopCat
slogan: TopCat is a type that represents the category of topological spaces, where each object is a topological space and each morphism is a continuous function between such spaces. It is defined in the Mathlib library's topology category module. The type lives in universe u + 1 and organizes topological spaces into a category for use in formal category theory.

label: TopCat.Homotopy.congr_homologyMap_singularChainComplexFunctor
slogan: If two continuous maps between topological spaces are homotopic, then they produce the same map on singular homology groups with coefficients in any given abelian group or algebraic object R. This means homotopy equivalent maps cannot be distinguished by their effect on homology. The result holds for any category of coefficients that supports the necessary algebraic structure.

label: TopCat.Presheaf
slogan: A presheaf on a topological space X with values in a category C is a contravariant functor from the category of open sets of X to C. This definition packages all such functors into a category, where objects are presheaves and morphisms are natural transformations between them. The type depends on the universe levels of C, X, and the ambient category theory setup.

label: TopCat.Presheaf.IsSheaf
slogan: A presheaf F on a topological space X is a sheaf if, for every open cover of an open set U, any compatible family of sections over the open sets in the cover comes from a unique section over U. This condition is defined using Grothendieck topologies so it works generally, without requiring extra structure on the category C where F takes values. Equivalent definitions exist that involve equalizers, limits, or unique gluings when the category has additional properties.

label: TopCat.Presheaf.germ
slogan: The germ of a section of a presheaf F over an open set U at a point x in U is a map from the sections of F over U to the stalk of F at x, capturing the local behavior of the section near x. It is defined using the colimit that forms the stalk, by including the open neighborhood U into the system of all neighborhoods of x. This map is part of the universal cocone over the diagram of restrictions to neighborhoods of x.

label: TopCat.Presheaf.isIso_iff_stalkFunctor_map_iso
slogan: A morphism between two sheaves is an isomorphism if and only if the induced map on the stalk at every point is an isomorphism, provided the target category has enough colimits and the forgetful functor preserves limits, filtered colimits, and reflects isomorphisms.

label: TopCat.Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheafPairwiseIntersections
slogan: A presheaf is a sheaf if and only if for every open cover, the value on the whole set is the limit of the values on the individual sets and their pairwise intersections. This means that sections over the whole set correspond exactly to compatible families of sections over the cover and its overlaps. The condition using equalizer diagrams is equivalent to the one using limits over pairwise intersections.

label: TopCat.Presheaf.pushforward
slogan: Given a continuous map f from topological space X to Y and a category C, the pushforward operation turns a presheaf on X with values in C into a presheaf on Y with values in C by precomposing with the map that sends open sets in Y to their preimages in X. This defines a functor from the category of presheaves on X to the category of presheaves on Y.

label: TopCat.Presheaf.stalk
slogan: The stalk of a presheaf F at a point x is the colimit of the values of F over all open neighborhoods of x, taken in the category C. It captures the local behavior of the presheaf near x by combining sections over every neighborhood of x. This construction requires the category C to have all colimits.

label: TopCat.Sheaf
slogan: A TopCat.Sheaf C X represents a presheaf of objects from a category C over a topological space X that satisfies the sheaf condition, meaning it correctly glues local data into global data. It uses the Grothendieck topology defined on the open sets of X, where covers are collections of open sets whose union is the whole open set. This structure ensures that compatible local sections of the presheaf can be uniquely combined into a single global section.

label: TopCat.Sheaf.pullback
slogan: Given a continuous map f from topological space X to Y, and a category A with sufficient structure (like limits, colimits, and a forgetful functor preserving them), the pullback functor takes a sheaf of objects of A over Y and produces a corresponding sheaf of objects of A over X, by precomposing with the map induced by f on open sets.

label: TopCat.Sheaf.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction
slogan: For a continuous map f between topological spaces X and Y, and a well-behaved category A, the pullback of sheaves along f is left adjoint to the pushforward along f. This means there is a natural correspondence between morphisms from the pullback of a sheaf on Y to a sheaf on X and morphisms from the original sheaf on Y to the pushforward of the sheaf on X. The result holds under technical conditions ensuring the categories of sheaves have enough structure.

label: TopCat.isoOfHomeo
slogan: A homeomorphism between two topological spaces gives an isomorphism in the category of topological spaces by turning the continuous forward and inverse maps into morphisms that compose to the identity on each space. This means that if two spaces are homeomorphic, they are equivalent in the categorical sense, with each map preserving the topological structure. The isomorphism is built using the continuous functions from the homeomorphism and its inverse.

label: TopCat.sheafToTop
slogan: The sheafToTop function constructs a sheaf of continuous functions from a topological space X to another topological space T, where the sheaf assigns to each open set of X the set of continuous functions from that open set to T. This sheaf satisfies the sheaf condition, meaning that continuous functions can be glued together uniquely when they agree on overlaps. It is built from the presheaf of continuous functions by verifying that continuity is a local condition.

label: TopCat.toSSetObjEquiv
slogan: For a topological space X and an object n from the opposite of the simplex category, the set (toSSet.obj X).obj n is equivalent to the set of continuous maps from the standard simplex (with dimension based on n) to X. The standard simplex is formed from points in real vector space indexed by Fin (n.unop.len + 1) that are non-negative and sum to one. This equivalence matches each element of the simplicial set associated to X with a continuous function from a geometric simplex into X.

label: TopologicalSpace
slogan: A topological space is a set with a defined collection of open subsets that include the empty set and the whole set, and are closed under finite intersections and any unions.

label: TopologicalSpace.Clopens.instBooleanAlgebra
slogan: The set of all subsets that are both open and closed in a topological space can be combined using operations like union, intersection, and complement, and these operations follow the rules of a Boolean algebra, with the empty set as the smallest element and the whole space as the largest.

label: TopologicalSpace.Countable.to_separableSpace
slogan: If a topological space has only countably many points, then it is separable because the whole space is a countable set and is dense in itself.

label: TopologicalSpace.IsCompletelyMetrizableSpace
slogan: A topological space is completely metrizable if there exists a metric that induces its topology and under which every Cauchy sequence converges to a point in the space. This means the space can be given a complete metric without changing its open sets. It does not require the metric to be specified, only that such a complete metric exists.

label: TopologicalSpace.IsSeparable.iUnion
slogan: A separable space has a countable dense subset, and if you take a countable union of separable subspaces, the resulting space is also separable as long as each subspace is part of the union.

label: TopologicalSpace.IsSeparable.image
slogan: If a topological space has a countable dense subset and a function is continuous, then the image of that space under the function also has a countable dense subset. This means separable spaces remain separable after applying continuous mappings.

label: TopologicalSpace.IsSeparable.of_separableSpace
slogan: A topological space is separable if it has a countable dense subset, meaning some countable set of points meets every nonempty open set. If a space is a separable space, then any subset of it inherits this property. In particular, the whole space being separable means there is a countable set whose closure is the entire space.

label: TopologicalSpace.IsTopologicalBasis
slogan: A topological basis is a set of subsets of a space such that every open set can be formed by combining some of these subsets, and whenever two of them overlap, their overlap is covered by other subsets from the same collection. It must also cover the entire space and satisfy a condition that overlapping sets have their intersection covered by smaller basis sets. This allows defining a topology by focusing only on a simpler generating set of open sets.

label: TopologicalSpace.MetrizableSpace
slogan: A metrizable space is a topological space where the open sets come from a metric, meaning distance between points defines the topology and distinct points always have positive distance; it is also a T0 space, so for any two different points, at least one has an open neighborhood not containing the other. This is stronger than being pseudo-metrizable, where the topology comes from a distance function that allows distinct points to be zero distance apart.

label: TopologicalSpace.NoetherianSpace
slogan: A Noetherian space is a topological space where every increasing sequence of open sets eventually stops growing, meaning no infinite strictly larger sequences of open sets can exist. This is equivalent to saying that every non-empty family of open sets has one that is maximal under inclusion.

label: TopologicalSpace.NoetherianSpace.exists_finite_set_isClosed_irreducible
slogan: In a Noetherian topological space, every closed set can be written as a union of finitely many closed irreducible subsets. There is a finite collection of such irreducible closed sets that serve as building blocks for all closed sets in the space.

label: TopologicalSpace.NoetherianSpace.exists_finset_irreducible
slogan: In a Noetherian topological space, every closed set can be written as a union of finitely many irreducible closed sets. These irreducible sets are the basic building blocks, meaning they cannot be split into smaller nonempty closed parts. The result guarantees that such a finite decomposition always exists.

label: TopologicalSpace.NoetherianSpace.finite_irreducibleComponents
slogan: In a Noetherian topological space, there are only finitely many irreducible components, which are the largest irreducible closed subsets, and these components together cover the whole space.

label: TopologicalSpace.OpenNhds
slogan: The OpenNhds type represents all open sets containing a given point x in a topological space, where the space is part of the TopCat category of topological spaces and continuous maps. It is used to work with neighborhoods of a point in a categorical setting. Each neighborhood is an open set that includes the point.

label: TopologicalSpace.Opens.instFrame
slogan: The open sets of a topological space form a structure where you can take arbitrary unions and finite intersections, and these operations satisfy the distributive laws of a frame. This means the collection of open sets behaves like a complete lattice in which intersection distributes over union, even for infinite collections. The structure is built from a minimal set of axioms that ensure this algebraic behavior.

label: TopologicalSpace.Opens.instIsManifoldSubtypeMem
slogan: An open subset of a manifold inherits the structure of a manifold in a natural way, because it keeps the same local coordinate charts and topology as the original space, restricted to the subset. This means smoothness and dimension are preserved on the open set. The declaration ensures this restricted structure satisfies the formal conditions for being a manifold.

label: TopologicalSpace.SecondCountableTopology.to_separableSpace
slogan: A second-countable topological space has a countable collection of open sets such that every open set can be written as a union of sets from this collection, and this ensures the space contains a countable dense subset. The statement confirms that such spaces are separable by selecting one point from each nonempty basis set to form a dense set. This construction relies on the fact that the basis is countable and each basis set is nonempty.

label: TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace
slogan: A separable space is a topological space that has a countable set of points such that every nonempty open set contains at least one of them. This means the space can be "approximated" by a countable sequence of points, even if the space itself is uncountable. The existence of such a set is guaranteed by classical logic, though it may not be explicitly constructed.

label: TopologicalSpace.coinduced
slogan: The coinduced topology on a set Y, given a function f from X to Y and a topology on X, is the largest topology on Y that makes f continuous. A subset of Y is open in this topology if and only if its preimage under f is open in X. This means open sets in Y are exactly those whose inverse images are open in the original space X.

label: TopologicalSpace.induced
slogan: The induced topology on a set X, given a function f from X to a topological space Y, is defined by calling a subset of X open if it is the preimage under f of an open set in Y. This ensures that the open sets in X are exactly those that come from open sets in Y via the function f. The resulting collection of open sets satisfies the axioms of a topology: the whole space is open, and both arbitrary unions and finite intersections of open sets remain open.

label: TopologicalSpace.instPartialOrder
slogan: The declaration sets up a way to compare topological spaces by saying one is "less than or equal to" another if it has fewer or the same open sets. This creates a partial order based on how coarse or fine the topologies are. A topology with fewer open sets is considered coarser, and thus smaller in this ordering.

label: TopologicalSpace.instSecondCountableTopologyOfLindelofSpaceOfPseudoMetrizableSpace
slogan: If a topological space has a pseudo-metric and every open cover has a countable subcover (Lindelof), then its topology has a countable basis. This means the space is second-countable, so all its open sets can be described using a countable collection of basic open sets. The existence of a pseudo-metric and the Lindelof property together ensure this countable basis exists.

label: TopologicalSpace.instSeparableSpaceForallOfCountable
slogan: A topological space made from a countable product of separable spaces is itself separable, meaning it has a countable dense subset. This means that if each factor space has a countable set whose closure is the whole space, and there are only countably many such spaces, then the product space also has a countable set that is dense. The result ensures separability is preserved under countable products.

label: TopologicalSpace.isSeparable_range
slogan: If a topological space has a countable dense subset and a function from it is continuous, then the set of all output values of that function also has a countable dense subset. This means separability is preserved under continuous mappings.

label: TopologicalSpace.le_def
slogan: One topology is less than or equal to another if every open set in the first is also open in the second, meaning it is coarser. This defines a partial order on topologies based on the inclusion of their open sets. The ordering compares how fine or coarse topologies are by looking at which has more open sets.

label: TopologicalSpace.mkOfNhds
slogan: Given a function that assigns to each point a collection of neighborhoods (as a filter), a topology is created where a set is open if it includes a neighborhood of each of its points. The whole space is always a neighborhood of every point, and any set containing a neighborhood of a point is also a neighborhood. This builds a valid topological space from neighborhood data using filter properties like closure under supersets and finite intersections.

label: TopologicalSpace.ofClosed
slogan: A topology can be defined by specifying a collection of closed sets that includes the empty set and the whole space, is closed under finite unions and arbitrary intersections, and corresponds to the complements of open sets. This construction ensures the closed-set axioms are equivalent to the usual open-set definition of a topological space. The function takes a collection of sets satisfying these closure properties and returns a topological space structure.

label: TopologicalSpace.separableSpace_iff_countable
slogan: A topological space with the discrete topology is separable if and only if the underlying type is countable, meaning its elements can be listed in a sequence. In a discrete space, the only dense set is the whole space, so separability requires that the entire set of points be countable. This links the concept of separability to the size of the space in terms of countability.

label: Topology.IsOpenEmbedding.separableSpace
slogan: If a function is continuous, injective, and maps open sets to open sets (an open embedding), and the space it maps into has a countable dense subset, then the space it comes from must also have a countable dense subset. The openness and injectivity of the function ensure that separability is preserved in the source space. This result depends on the fact that preimages of dense sets under injective open maps remain dense and countable.

label: TotallyBounded
slogan: A set is totally bounded if, for every way of defining "closeness" in the space, the whole set can be covered by finitely many small subsets, each containing points that are close to each other by that definition.

label: TotallyBounded.image
slogan: If a set is totally bounded in a uniform space, then applying a uniformly continuous function to it results in another totally bounded set. This means that uniformly continuous functions preserve total boundedness. The image of the set under the function can still be covered by finitely many small sets, no matter how strict the notion of "small" is.

label: TotallyBounded.isBounded
slogan: In a pseudometric space, if a set can be covered by finitely many small balls of any given radius, then the set itself has finite size in the sense that it fits within some bounded region. This is because each small ball is bounded, and a finite union of bounded sets remains bounded. Thus, total boundedness implies boundedness.

label: TotallyDisconnectedSpace
slogan: A totally disconnected space is a topological space in which the only connected subsets are those with at most one element. This means no subset containing two or more points can be connected. The property is defined for any type equipped with a topology.

label: TotallySeparatedSpace
slogan: A totally separated space is a topological space where any two different points can be put into separate open sets that don't overlap, and this means the only connected parts of the space are single points.

label: TotallySeparatedSpace.of_discrete
slogan: A space where every subset is open (discrete topology) is totally separated, meaning any two different points can be placed in separate, non-overlapping open sets. This is possible because each point by itself forms an open set, allowing complete separation.

label: Transcendental
slogan: An element x in a ring A is transcendental over a commutative ring R if no nonzero polynomial with coefficients in R evaluates to zero at x. This means x does not satisfy any nontrivial polynomial equation with coefficients from R. It is the opposite of being algebraic, where such a polynomial equation exists.

label: Transcendental.irrational
slogan: If a real number cannot be the root of any nonzero polynomial with rational coefficients, then it cannot be written as a fraction of two integers. Such a number is irrational, meaning it is not equal to any rational number. This applies to numbers like pi or e, which are known to be transcendental.

label: Tree.height_le_numNodes
slogan: The height of a tree is at most the total number of nodes it has. This means you can't have more levels in a tree than the number of nodes present. The result comes from how tree height and node count are defined recursively, using basic properties of natural numbers.

label: Tree.numLeaves_eq_numNodes_succ
slogan: In any tree, the number of leaf nodes (nodes with no children) is exactly one more than the total number of nodes in the tree. This means if you count all the nodes, including internal ones, the number of leaves equals that count plus one. The result holds for all trees built using empty trees and nodes with child subtrees.

label: Tree.treesOfNumNodesEq_card_eq_catalan
slogan: The number of distinct binary trees with n nodes is equal to the nth Catalan number. This means the size of the set of all such trees matches the value given by the Catalan sequence. For example, there is 1 tree with 0 nodes and 1 tree with 1 node, matching the first two Catalan numbers.

label: Trivialization
slogan: A trivialization is a structure that describes a local equivalence between a space Z and a product space B × F, where Z maps to a base space B with fiber F, such that the mapping is continuous, invertible, and preserves open sets over an open subset of B. It acts like a homeomorphism on restricted open domains, specifically between the preimage of an open set in B and the corresponding product of that set with F, matching points in Z to pairs in B × F while leaving the B component unchanged. This concept formalizes the idea of locally "untwisting" a fiber bundle into a simple product structure

label: Tropical
slogan: Tropical(R) turns a type R into a new type where the operations are replaced with tropical operations, meaning addition becomes taking the minimum and multiplication becomes regular addition. This is used to study algebraic structures in tropical mathematics.

label: Turing.TM0.Cfg
slogan: A Turing machine's configuration includes its current state and the tape, where the tape holds symbols with one symbol currently being read, and the rest arranged as lists to the left and right of it, automatically filled with blanks when extended. The tape can grow in either direction as the machine operates. This setup ensures the machine always has a defined symbol to read, even when moving into previously untouched areas.

label: Turing.TM0.eval
slogan: Turing.TM0.eval runs a Turing machine on a given list of symbols as input and returns the final state of the tape if the machine stops, represented as a list that ignores extra blanks at the end; if the machine does not halt, no result is returned. The machine operates using a set of rules for changing states and moving or writing symbols, starting from an initial state and a blank tape. The result is wrapped in a Part type to indicate that it may not always produce an output.

label: Turing.TM0.step
slogan: The step function for a Turing machine takes a current machine state and tape configuration, then returns the next configuration after applying the machine's rules, or nothing if the machine halts. It uses the machine's current state and the symbol under the tape head to determine whether to write a symbol, move left or right, and transition to a new state. The tape is extended with blank symbols as needed when moving beyond its current bounds.

label: Turing.TM2Computable
slogan: A function f from type α to type β is TM2Computable if there exists a Turing machine that can compute f, given that both α and β have finite encodings into strings over finite alphabets. This means the inputs and outputs of f can be represented using finite symbol sets, and the machine processes these encoded inputs to produce the corresponding encoded outputs. The structure ties together the function, its input/output encodings, and the Turing machine that computes it.

label: Turing.TM2ComputableInPolyTime
slogan: A function can be computed by a Turing machine within a time limit defined by a polynomial, given that inputs and outputs are encoded using finite alphabets. The machine processes encoded inputs and produces encoded outputs, with the running time bounded by a polynomial function of the input length. This combines a Turing machine, a finite encoding scheme, and a proof that the computation finishes in polynomial time.

label: Turing.TM2ComputableInTime
slogan: A function f from type α to type β is computable in a certain time if there is a Turing machine that computes f, using finite encodings for input and output, and always finishes within a number of steps bounded by a function of the input length. The time it takes depends only on how long the input is, not on the input's contents. This structure ties together the machine, the time limit, and the proof that the machine correctly computes f within that limit.

label: TuringDegree
slogan: TuringDegree is the type of equivalence classes of partial functions from natural numbers to natural numbers, where two functions are considered equivalent if each can be computed using the other as an oracle. This means functions are grouped together when they have the same level of computational difficulty. The structure is built from a preorder on partial functions defined by Turing reducibility.

label: TuringReducible
slogan: A function f from natural numbers to partial natural numbers is said to be Turing reducible to another such function g if, assuming we can use g as an oracle (i.e., we can query it for values during computation), f can be computed by a partial recursive function. This means f's computation may rely on answers from g, but must follow an algorithmic process. The reducibility captures the idea that f is no more complex than g in terms of computability.

label: TwoSidedIdeal
slogan: A two-sided ideal is a subset of a ring (without requiring a multiplicative identity or associativity) that is closed under addition, additive inverses, and both left and right multiplication by any ring element. It allows the formation of a quotient ring where addition and multiplication are still well-defined. Such ideals are used to analyze ring homomorphisms and construct factor rings in non-unital, non-associative contexts.

label: Ultrafilter
slogan: An ultrafilter is a maximal filter on a set where every subset is either fully included or fully excluded, and it is not the trivial empty filter. It extends the concept of a filter by ensuring no larger proper filter can contain it. Ultrafilters are used to formalize ideas of convergence and largeness in mathematics.

label: Ultrafilter.exists_le
slogan: In a complete lattice of filters, every nontrivial filter (one that contains at least one set) has an ultrafilter below it in the order; that is, every such filter can be refined into an ultrafilter. This relies on the existence of minimal non-bottom elements (atoms) in the lattice. The result guarantees that ultrafilters are always present beneath any filter that isn't the smallest possible one.

label: Uncountable
slogan: A type is uncountable if its elements cannot be listed in a sequence or matched one-to-one with the natural numbers, meaning it has too many elements to be countable. This property is used to identify types that are larger than the set of natural numbers.

label: UniformCauchySeqOn.tendstoUniformlyOn_of_tendsto
slogan: If a sequence of functions gets uniformly close to itself on a set and converges pointwise there, then it converges uniformly on that set.

label: UniformContinuous
slogan: A function is uniformly continuous if it ensures that whenever two outputs are close in the target space, the corresponding inputs are close in the source space, with closeness defined by the uniform structures on both spaces. This condition must hold consistently across the entire domain. The definition uses filters to formalize that the preimages of entourages in the target are entourages in the source.

label: UniformContinuous.comp_cauchySeq
slogan: If a function is uniformly continuous and you apply it to a sequence where the terms eventually stay close together (a Cauchy sequence), then the new sequence you get will also have terms that eventually stay close together. This result holds because uniform continuity ensures that closeness in the input space is preserved in the output space, and it uses the structure of filters to define what "close" means in general spaces.

label: UniformContinuous.continuous
slogan: If a function between two uniform spaces preserves uniform closeness (meaning points that are close in the domain map to points that are close in the codomain in a consistent way), then it also preserves continuity (meaning the preimage of every open set is open). This is because the topology generated by a uniformly continuous function is coarse enough to satisfy the definition of continuity. Uniform continuity is therefore a stronger condition than continuity.

label: UniformEquicontinuous.uniformContinuous
slogan: If a family of functions is uniformly equicontinuous, then each function in the family is uniformly continuous, meaning that for every small distance in the target space, there is a single small distance in the domain that works uniformly across all functions to keep images of nearby points close.

label: UniformEquiv
slogan: A UniformEquiv is a one-to-one mapping between two uniform spaces where both the function and its inverse keep the uniform structure intact, meaning they preserve how points are considered close to each other. It ensures that properties like uniform continuity and completeness are maintained when moving between the spaces. This combines a bijective equivalence (like from Equiv) with compatibility for uniform space features.

label: UniformOnFun.instCompleteSpace
slogan: If a type has at least one element, then the space of functions from that type to a complete uniform space is complete when equipped with the uniform convergence topology. This means every uniformly Cauchy sequence of functions converges to a function in that space. The completeness comes from the fact that the uniform structure on the function space is inherited from the complete codomain.

label: UniformSpace
slogan: A uniform space is a set equipped with a structure that formalizes the idea of points being uniformly close to each other, enabling definitions of uniform continuity and completeness, and it extends the concept of a topological space by using filters to describe consistent neighborhood behavior across the space. This structure allows the formation of product spaces like α × β while preserving uniform properties. It builds on topological spaces and uses filters to define uniformity.

label: UniformSpace.Completion
slogan: The completion of a uniform space is a new space formed by grouping together Cauchy filters that get arbitrarily close, ensuring every such sequence has a limit. This new space keeps the original notion of closeness and becomes complete, meaning all Cauchy filters converge. If the original space distinguishes points well, the completed space will also keep points separate.

label: UniformSpace.firstCountableTopology
slogan: If the uniformity filter in a uniform space has a countable basis, then the neighborhood filter at each point also has a countable basis, making the topology first-countable. This is because the neighborhood filter at a point is the preimage of the uniformity filter under the map that pairs points with that fixed point, and taking preimages preserves countable generation. Thus, the topology around each point can be described by a sequence of nested neighborhoods.

label: UniformSpace.isCompact_iff_isSeqCompact
slogan: In a topological space where the open sets can be described by a generalized metric (allowing distinct points to have zero distance), a set is compact exactly when every sequence in it has a subsequence that converges to a point in the set. This means compactness and sequential compactness are equivalent under this condition. The equivalence depends on the space having a countable neighborhood basis at each point, which is ensured by the pseudo-metrizable structure.

label: UniformSpace.secondCountable_of_separable
slogan: If a uniform space has a countable dense subset, then its topology has a countable base, meaning all open sets can be built from a countable collection. This links separability to second-countability in uniform spaces.

label: UniqueFactorizationMonoid
slogan: A UniqueFactorizationMonoid is a structure where every nonzero element that isn't a unit can be broken down in exactly one way into irreducible elements (like primes), up to reordering and multiplying by units, provided multiplication is commutative, zero behaves normally, cancellation works for nonzero factors, and there are no infinite descending chains of divisors. It ensures a well-defined and unique factorization property similar to prime factorization in integers. This applies to algebraic systems with a zero element and a well-behaved multiplication operation.

label: UniqueFactorizationMonoid.factors
slogan: In a unique factorization monoid, every nonzero non-unit element can be broken down in a unique way (up to order and unit multiples) into a product of prime elements, and the factors function returns this collection of prime factors as a multiset. Multiplying all the elements in this multiset gives back the original element, ignoring units and order. The result is well-defined because multiplication is commutative and associative.

label: UniqueFactorizationMonoid.iff_exists_prime_mem_of_isPrime
slogan: An integral domain has unique factorization if and only if every nonzero prime ideal contains at least one prime element.

label: UniqueFactorizationMonoid.radical
slogan: The radical of an element a in a unique factorization monoid is the product of all distinct prime factors of a. It is computed by multiplying together each prime that divides a exactly once, ignoring multiplicity. This assumes the element comes from a commutative monoid with zero and a normalization structure.

label: UnitAddTorus.mFourierCoeff
slogan: The mFourierCoeff function computes the n-th Fourier coefficient of a function defined on a multi-dimensional torus (made from several copies of the unit circle), by integrating the product of the function with a complex exponential over the torus. The result is a vector in a complete normed complex vector space. The integration uses a normalized measure so that the total volume of the torus is 1.

label: Unitary.spectrum_subset_circle
slogan: For a unitary element in a complete normed algebra over a normed field, all points in its spectrum have norm exactly 1, meaning the spectrum lies within the unit circle centered at 0.

label: Unitization
slogan: Unitization creates a new algebra by adding a multiplicative identity to an algebra that might not have one, using pairs made of a scalar and an element from the original algebra. This new algebra is built using the Prod type, combining a scalar from a ring R and an element from the original algebra A. The result is a type that behaves like R × A, with operations defined to ensure the scalar part provides the missing identity.

label: Units
slogan: A unit in a monoid is an element that has an inverse, so multiplying the element by its inverse in either order gives the identity. The Units structure gathers all such invertible elements from a monoid and forms a group using the monoid's multiplication. This group includes only those elements that can be "undone" by another element under multiplication.

label: Units.instGroup
slogan: The units of a monoid, which are the elements that have multiplicative inverses, themselves form a group under multiplication. This means they are closed under multiplication, include an identity element, and every unit has an inverse that is also a unit. The group structure is built using the existing multiplication and inversion operations defined on the monoid's units.

label: UniversalEnvelopingAlgebra
slogan: The universal enveloping algebra takes a Lie algebra over a commutative ring and constructs an associative algebra where the Lie bracket operation becomes the commutator of elements. It is formed by starting with the tensor algebra of the Lie algebra and then imposing relations that force the commutator to match the original bracket. This allows Lie algebra problems to be studied using tools from associative algebras.

label: UniversalEnvelopingAlgebra.lift
slogan: The function UniversalEnvelopingAlgebra.lift converts a linear map from a Lie algebra to an associative algebra that respects the Lie bracket into a unique algebra homomorphism from the universal enveloping algebra, such that this homomorphism agrees with the original map on the Lie algebra elements. It ensures every compatible Lie algebra map extends uniquely to an algebra map. This property makes the universal enveloping algebra the most general algebra containing the Lie algebra in a way that preserves the bracket structure.

label: UpperHalfPlane
slogan: The upper half plane is the set of complex numbers with positive imaginary part, represented as a type in the UpperHalfPlane namespace. It is defined using the standard ordering on real numbers to require the imaginary component to be greater than zero. This type is used to work with complex numbers in the upper half of the complex plane.

label: UpperHalfPlane.dist_eq
slogan: The distance between two points z and w in the upper half-plane is equal to twice the inverse hyperbolic sine of the Euclidean distance between the corresponding complex numbers, divided by twice the square root of the product of their imaginary parts.

label: UpperHalfPlane.instMetricSpace
slogan: The upper half plane, consisting of complex numbers with positive imaginary part, is equipped with a metric space structure that defines distances in a way compatible with its standard topology. This metric ensures that the resulting topological structure matches the subspace topology inherited from the complex plane. The hyperbolic metric is used, and the topology derived from the metric is made definitionally equal to the existing topology on the upper half plane.

label: UpperSemicontinuous
slogan: A function is upper semicontinuous if, for every real number c, the set of points where the function value is less than c is an open set. This means the function does not suddenly jump upwards when moving to nearby points. The definition works for functions from a topological space to a set with a preorder.

label: Valuation
slogan: A valuation is a function that assigns values from an ordered monoid with zero to elements of a ring, preserving multiplication, sending zero to zero, and respecting the ring's structure to measure size or divisibility. It behaves like a generalized norm or absolute value, where the value of a product equals the product of the values, and larger values correspond to smaller size in a topological sense. The target space has a total order, a zero element, and multiplication that respects the order.

label: ValuationRing
slogan: A ValuationRing is a commutative ring with no zero divisors where, for any two elements a and b, either a divides b or b divides a. This means that any pair of elements has a strong divisibility relationship, creating a highly ordered multiplicative structure. It is defined on a type that already satisfies the properties of a commutative ring and an integral domain.

label: ValuationRing.isLocalRing
slogan: A valuation ring is a commutative ring where for every element x, either x or 1 - x has a multiplicative inverse, and this property guarantees the ring has exactly one maximal ideal, making it a local ring. The non-units in such a ring form an ideal, and the ring is nontrivial. This declaration asserts that any type satisfying the conditions of a valuation ring automatically meets the definition of a local ring.

label: ValuationSubring
slogan: A valuation subring is a special kind of subring inside a field, where for any element in the field, either the element or its inverse is in the subring. It is a local ring that is maximal with respect to domination by other local subrings. Such subrings correspond exactly to the largest possible local subrings under this ordering.

label: VectorBundle
slogan: A vector bundle is a structure where each point in a base space has a vector space attached to it, and nearby these vector spaces look like a product space with linear maps between them, all while maintaining compatible topological and algebraic properties. It requires the base and total spaces to be topological, the fibers to be topological vector spaces over a nontrivially normed field, and the local trivializations to preserve linearity. The total space is formed by pairing base points with elements from their respective fibers.

label: VectorBundle.prod
slogan: The product of two vector bundles over the same base space forms a new vector bundle, where the fiber over each point is the product of the fibers from the original bundles. This means that if you have two vector bundles with compatible topological and linear structures, their pointwise product also has the structure of a vector bundle. The total space of the product bundle consists of pairs of elements from the total spaces of the original bundles.

label: VectorBundle.pullback
slogan: If you have a vector bundle over a base space and a continuous map from another space to that base, then you can construct a new vector bundle over the new space by pulling back the original bundle along the map, and this pulled-back bundle still satisfies all the conditions of a vector bundle.

label: VectorField.leibniz_identity_mlieBracket
slogan: The Lie bracket of three vector fields satisfies the identity [U, [V, W]] = [[U, V], W] + [V, [U, W]], meaning the bracket operation follows a specific algebraic rule similar to the product rule in calculus. This holds for smooth vector fields on a manifold over a normed field. The identity is valid when the vector fields are sufficiently differentiable.

label: VectorField.lieBracket
slogan: The Lie bracket of two vector fields V and W at a point x is computed as the difference between the directional derivative of W along V and the directional derivative of V along W, specifically DW(x)(V(x)) - DV(x)(W(x)). It measures how the vector fields fail to commute under differentiation. This operation takes two vector fields and produces another vector field.

label: VectorField.mlieBracket
slogan: The Lie bracket of two vector fields on a manifold is a new vector field that measures how the flows of the original fields fail to commute. At each point, it produces a tangent vector representing the infinitesimal difference between following one vector field and then the other versus the reverse order. This operation is defined using the geometric structure of the manifold and the properties of the vector fields.

label: VectorField.mlieBracketWithin
slogan: The Lie bracket of two vector fields within a set measures how their directional derivatives fail to commute at a point, by taking the difference between the derivative of one field along the other and vice versa, all computed relative to the given set. It results in another vector at that point. This operation is defined on a manifold using the local structure of charts and tangent spaces over a normed field.

label: VectorField.mlieBracket_self
slogan: The Lie bracket of a vector field with itself is always zero, meaning that the operation measuring the difference between how two vector fields change along each other vanishes when both fields are the same.

label: VectorField.mpullback
slogan: The pullback of a vector field transfers a vector field from one manifold to another using a given map between them, computing the result by applying the inverse of the derivative when possible. If the derivative of the map is not invertible at a point, the pullback returns zero as a default value. This operation relies on the smooth structures of both manifolds and the properties of tangent spaces over normed fields.

label: VectorFourier.fourierIntegral
slogan: The Fourier transform integral takes a function f from a vector space V to a normed space E, a measure on V, a bilinear form L mapping V and W to a commutative ring 𝕜, and an additive character e from 𝕜 to the unit circle, and produces a new function that maps each element w of W to an element of E by integrating f against the character e composed with L using the given measure. This integral generalizes the classical Fourier transform to vector spaces with suitable algebraic and measure structures. The result is a function that captures frequency information of f relative to the pairing defin

label: VectorFourier.fourierIntegral_add
slogan: The Fourier transform of the sum of two integrable functions is equal to the sum of their individual Fourier transforms, given appropriate continuity and measurability conditions on the spaces and mappings involved.

label: VectorFourier.fourierIntegral_continuous
slogan: The Fourier integral of a function that is integrable with respect to a measure is a continuous function. This means if a function is sufficiently well-behaved to be integrated, its Fourier transform will vary smoothly without jumps or breaks.

label: VectorFourier.fourierIntegral_fderiv
slogan: The Fourier transform of the derivative of a function is the same as multiplying the Fourier transform of the function by a factor involving -L, w, and v, which scales the result based on the bilinear form L and the frequency variable. This relationship holds under conditions of differentiability and integrability of the function and its derivative. The result connects differentiation in the original space to multiplication in the frequency domain.

label: VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_average
slogan: For almost every point in a metric space equipped with a measure and a Vitali family, the average of an integrable function over smaller and smaller sets around that point gets arbitrarily close to the function's value at the point. This convergence happens in the sense that the difference between the averages and the function value tends to zero. The result holds under general conditions on the space, measure, and function, including local finiteness of the measure and completeness of the target space.

label: VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_average_norm_sub
slogan: For almost every point in a metric space, the average of the distance between a locally integrable function's values and its value at that point, taken over smaller and smaller neighborhoods around the point, approaches zero as the neighborhoods shrink. This holds when the neighborhoods are part of a Vitali family, which guarantees they cover the space well and contract nicely. As a result, the function's integral averages converge to the function's value almost everywhere.

label: VonNeumannAlgebra
slogan: A von Neumann algebra is a collection of bounded linear operators on a Hilbert space that is closed under adjoints, closed under multiplication and addition, and equal to its double commutant — meaning it contains exactly those operators that commute with all operators that commute with its elements. It is defined as a *-subalgebra of operators on a fixed Hilbert space H, where H is complete, complex, and equipped with an inner product. This structure bundles the algebra with the space it acts on, rather than being defined abstractly.

label: VonNeumannAlgebra.centralizer_centralizer
slogan: In a Hilbert space, the set of bounded operators that commute with all operators that commute with a given von Neumann algebra is exactly the original algebra itself. This means a von Neumann algebra is completely determined by its commutation relations. The result reflects the double commutant property that defines von Neumann algebras.

label: VonNeumannAlgebra.commutant
slogan: The commutant of a von Neumann algebra is the set of all bounded linear operators on a Hilbert space that commute with every operator in the algebra, and this commutant itself forms a von Neumann algebra. It is defined on a complete complex inner product space and inherits the algebraic and topological structure of the original space. This construction reflects the symmetry in the double commutant property, where taking the commutant twice returns the original algebra.

label: VonNeumannAlgebra.commutant_commutant
slogan: In a complex Hilbert space, the set of bounded linear operators that commute with all operators that commute with a given von Neumann algebra is exactly the original algebra itself. Taking the commutant twice therefore returns the same set of operators. This double commutant property characterizes von Neumann algebras as being closed under this operation.

label: WStarAlgebra
slogan: A WStarAlgebra is a C* algebra that has a Banach space predual, following Sakai's definition of a von Neumann algebra. It is called "abstract" to distinguish it from concrete von Neumann algebras, which are represented as weakly closed *-subalgebras of bounded operators on a Hilbert space. The definition currently only requires the existence of such a predual, without selecting a specific one.

label: WeakDual
slogan: The WeakDual is the coarsest topology on the space of continuous linear maps from a topological module E over a commutative semiring 𝕜 to 𝕜 itself, such that for every element x in E, the evaluation map sending a linear functional v to the value v(x) is continuous. It is built using the weak topology induced by these evaluation functionals. This setup applies in contexts where both 𝕜 and E have compatible topological and algebraic structures.

label: WeakDual.gelfandTransform
slogan: The Gelfand transform maps each element of a topological algebra A over a field k to a continuous function on the space of algebra homomorphisms from A to k, where the function's value at each homomorphism is the result of applying that homomorphism to the element. This mapping preserves the algebraic structure of A, meaning it respects addition, multiplication, and scalar multiplication by elements of k. The character space consists of all nonzero algebra homomorphisms from A to k that are also continuous.

label: WeakDual.isCompact_closedBall
slogan: In the dual space of a normed vector space, every closed ball is compact when equipped with the weak-star topology, provided the base field is proper. This means that any set of continuous linear functionals whose norm is bounded by a fixed radius forms a compact set in this topology. The result is a version of the Banach-Alaoglu theorem stating that bounded closed sets in the dual space are compact in the weak-star sense.

label: WeakDual.isCompact_polar
slogan: In a normed space over a field where closed balls are compact, the set of all continuous linear functionals that map a neighborhood of zero into values no larger than 1 in absolute value forms a compact set in the weak dual topology. This means that functionals which are uniformly bounded on a neighborhood of the origin have a compact collection under the topology of pointwise convergence. The result holds when the field has a nontrivial norm and the space satisfies standard algebraic and topological conditions.

label: WeakDual.metrizable_of_isCompact
slogan: If a subset of the dual space of a separable normed space is compact in the weak-* topology, then that subset is metrizable, meaning its topology can be defined by a metric.

label: WeakSpace
slogan: The WeakSpace definition sets up a topology on a space E over a commutative semiring 𝕜 such that the coarsest topology is used, making all linear functionals (maps from E to 𝕜) continuous. It combines algebraic structures like modules and topological spaces to ensure continuity of vector space operations. This setup is used to study dual spaces and weak topologies in functional analysis.

label: WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Point.add
slogan: Given two points on an elliptic curve defined by y^2 = x^3 + a*x + b over a field, their sum is computed using arithmetic in the field: if the points are distinct and not negatives, the line through them intersects the curve at a third point, and reflecting that point over the x-axis gives the sum; if the points are the same, the tangent line is used instead; and if one point is the zero point or the points are negatives, the result is the other point or the zero point accordingly. The x and y coordinates of the sum are calculated using formulas involving the slope of the line. This addition o

label: WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Point.instAddCommGroup
slogan: Points on an elliptic curve defined by the equation y^2 = x^3 + a*x + b can be added together in a way that is commutative and associative, includes a zero point, and every point has an inverse, forming a group under this addition. The addition operation is defined for points in affine coordinates over a field where equality of elements can be decided. This structure supports standard group operations like adding points and negating them.

label: WeierstrassCurve.Affine.slope
slogan: Given two distinct points (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) on an elliptic curve defined by y^2 = x^3 + a*x + b over a field, the slope of the line between them is (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1), computed using standard arithmetic in the field, as long as x1 and x2 are not equal.

label: WeierstrassCurve.HasGoodReduction
slogan: A Weierstrass equation over a field has good reduction when its discriminant has valuation equal to 1, meaning it remains nonsingular after reducing modulo the prime of the ring. This applies to equations that are minimal, where the discriminant's valuation is as large as possible among equivalent forms. The setting involves a discrete valuation ring with fraction field and a curve defined over that field.

label: WeierstrassCurve.exists_variableChange_isCharThreeNF
slogan: For any elliptic curve defined by a Weierstrass equation over a field of characteristic 3, there exists a change of variables that transforms it into one of two simplified forms: either Y squared equals X cubed plus a2 times X squared plus a6, or Y squared equals X cubed plus a4 times X plus a6.

label: WeierstrassCurve.exists_variableChange_isCharTwoNF
slogan: For any elliptic curve defined over a field of characteristic 2, there exists a change of variables that transforms the curve into one of two standard simplified forms used in characteristic 2, depending on its j-invariant. This transformation preserves the structure of the curve while putting it into a normal form suitable for analysis. The existence of such a transformation is guaranteed and can be effectively computed when equality in the field is decidable.

label: WeierstrassCurve.exists_variableChange_of_j_eq
slogan: If two elliptic curves over a separably closed field have the same j-invariant, then one can be transformed into the other by a change of variables defined over that field.

label: WellFounded.has_min
slogan: Every nonempty set has an element such that no other element in the set is smaller under a well-founded relation, meaning there is always a minimal element in the set with respect to the relation.

label: WellFounded.induction
slogan: If a relation r on a type a is well founded, meaning there are no infinite descending chains, then to prove a property C holds for some element a, it suffices to show that whenever C holds for all elements y that are "smaller" than x (via r y x), then C also holds for x. This allows proofs by induction based on the structure of the relation.

label: WellFounded.induction_bot
slogan: If a relation has no infinite descending chains, then to prove a property holds for all elements, it is enough to show that whenever the property holds for all strictly smaller elements, it also holds for the current one; this supports inductive reasoning starting from minimal elements.

label: WellFounded.min
slogan: Given a well-founded relation and a nonempty set, the function WellFounded.min returns an element from the set that is minimal, meaning no other element in the set is smaller according to the relation.

label: WellFounded.wellFounded_iff_has_min
slogan: A relation is well-founded exactly when every nonempty set has an element that is not greater than any other element in the set under that relation. This means there is always a minimal element in each nonempty set, with no smaller elements related by the relation. The condition holds both ways: if such minimal elements always exist, the relation is well-founded, and vice versa.

label: WellFoundedGT.monotone_chain_condition
slogan: If a type has a partial order where the greater-than relation is well-founded, then any increasing sequence of elements in that type must eventually stop changing, meaning it becomes constant after some point. This means there are no infinite strictly decreasing sequences in the type. The result connects the structure of sequences to the foundational properties of the order.

label: WellFoundedLT.fix
slogan: This function enables recursive definitions on a type where a less-than relation is well-founded, meaning there are no infinite descending chains. It constructs a function by letting you define the value at each element using the values at all smaller elements, relying on the LT typeclass to determine the order. The recursion is guaranteed to terminate because the ordering is well-founded.

label: WellFoundedLT.induction
slogan: If a type has a less-than relation with no infinite descending chains, then to prove a property holds for all elements, it is enough to show that whenever the property holds for all elements smaller than a given element, it also holds for that element. This supports proof by induction based on the less-than ordering.

label: WellOrder
slogan: A well order is a way of arranging the elements of a set so that every non-empty subset has a smallest element, with no infinitely decreasing sequences. It is transitive, antisymmetric, total, and ensures every pair of elements can be compared. This structure is defined using the IsWellOrder class, which captures these properties through a strict, well-founded relation.

label: WellQuasiOrdered
slogan: A well quasi-order is a reflexive and transitive relation on a type such that in any infinite sequence, some earlier element is related to a later one. This rules out infinite decreasing sequences and infinite sets of incomparable elements. It guarantees that infinite sequences eventually show a consistent pattern.

label: WithSeminorms
slogan: A type E is equipped with a family of seminorms over a normed field 𝕜, making it a topological space where the topology is defined by the seminorms; E also has a vector space-like structure with addition and scalar multiplication, and satisfies the properties of a locally convex space.

label: WithSeminorms.continuous_iff_continuous_comp
slogan: A function between two vector spaces with families of seminorms is continuous if and only if composing it with each seminorm in the target space gives a continuous function on the source space. This means checking continuity reduces to verifying that the function behaves continuously through each individual seminorm. The result holds for linear maps over normed fields where the seminorms define the topology.

label: WithSeminorms.separating_iff_T1
slogan: A topological vector space with a topology defined by a family of seminorms is T1 (meaning all points are closed) if and only if for every nonzero vector, at least one seminorm in the family gives it a positive value. This condition ensures that distinct vectors can always be distinguished by at least one seminorm.

label: WithSeminorms.tendsto_nhds
slogan: A sequence converges to a point in a topology defined by a family of seminorms if and only if, for every seminorm in the family and every positive tolerance, the seminorm applied to the difference between the sequence terms and the limit is eventually less than that tolerance. This means convergence happens when the sequence gets uniformly close to the limit with respect to all seminorms at once. The condition uses filters to express "eventually" and relies on the idea that finite maxima of seminorms control the topology.

label: WithTop.lattice
slogan: WithTop.lattice provides a way to combine sup and inf operations on a type that includes a top element, ensuring that both least upper bounds and greatest lower bounds exist for any pair of elements. It builds on the existing sup and inf structures of the original type and extends them to handle the top value correctly. This allows full lattice operations in the presence of an added maximum element.

label: WittVector
slogan: WittVector p R represents the ring of p-typical Witt vectors over a commutative ring R, where p is a prime number. When p is invertible in R, this ring behaves like the infinite product of copies of R indexed by natural numbers. If R has characteristic p, then WittVector p R becomes a ring of characteristic zero, with a key example being the p-adic integers when R is the integers modulo p.

label: YoungDiagram
slogan: A Young diagram is a finite set of cells arranged on a grid of natural number coordinates, where each cell is represented as a pair (i, j) indicating its row and column. If a cell is included, then all cells above it in the same column and to the left in the same row must also be included. This structure is modeled using finite sets of pairs of natural numbers that are closed downward under the componentwise ordering.

label: ZFSet.IsOrdinal
slogan: A set is a von Neumann ordinal if it is transitive and its elements are also transitive under the membership relation (∈); this means that whenever an element belongs to another element of the set, it also belongs directly to the set. This condition ensures the set is well-ordered by ∈. The property does not require explicitly checking all elements are in the set, as equivalence to a simpler transitivity condition is proven.

label: ZFSet.IsOrdinal.mem
