slogan: If a set x is an ordinal and y is an element of x, then y is also an ordinal. This means ordinals are transitive in the sense that their elements are themselves ordinals.

label: ZFSet.IsOrdinal.subset_iff_eq_or_mem
slogan: If two sets are ordinals, then one is a subset of the other if and only if they are equal or the first is an element of the second.

label: ZFSet.choice
slogan: ZFSet.choice is a function that takes a nonempty ZFC set and returns an element from it, acting as a choice function for the universe of ZFC sets. It ensures that for any nonempty set in the ZFSet type, one of its members can be selected. This reflects the axiom of choice within the formalization of set theory in Lean.

label: ZFSet.choice_mem
slogan: If x is a nonempty ZFC set (meaning it has no empty elements) and y is a member of x, then the choice function applied to x selects an element from y. This means the choice function consistently picks elements from the members of x. The result is guaranteed to be inside the corresponding member set y.

label: ZFSet.empty
slogan: ZFSet.empty is the empty set in ZFC set theory, represented as a set with no elements. It is constructed by converting an empty pre-set into a ZFC set using the ZFSet.mk function. This empty set is part of the universe of sets defined by quotienting pre-sets under extensional equivalence.

label: ZFSet.eq_empty
slogan: A set is equal to the empty set if and only if it has no elements, meaning nothing belongs to it.

label: ZFSet.ext
slogan: Two ZF sets are equal if they have exactly the same elements, meaning that every element of one set is also an element of the other and vice versa. This is the principle of extensionality, which defines set equality based on membership. The declaration asserts that this property holds for the universe of ZFC sets constructed from pre-sets by identifying extensionally equivalent ones.

label: ZFSet.isOrdinal_notMem_univ
slogan: The collection of all ordinal numbers cannot itself be a set, because if it were, it would contain itself and lead to a logical contradiction. This means ordinals form a proper class rather than a set. In simpler terms, there are too many ordinals to fit into a single set.

label: ZFSet.mem_image
slogan: A set y is an element of the image of a definable function f applied to a set x if and only if there exists an element z in x such that f(z) equals y. This means the image of x under f consists exactly of the values f(z) for all z in x. The function f must be definable so that it respects set equivalence in ZFC set theory.

label: ZFSet.mem_irrefl
slogan: No set can be a member of itself in ZFC set theory. This means that for any set x, the statement "x ∈ x" is always false. The result follows from the fact that the membership relation is well-founded, which prevents infinite descending chains like x ∈ x.

label: ZFSet.mem_pair
slogan: An element x is a member of the pair set {y, z} if and only if x is equal to y or x is equal to z.

label: ZFSet.regularity
slogan: Every non-empty set has an element that is disjoint from it, meaning there is an element in the set that shares no common elements with the original set.

label: ZFSet.sep
slogan: The expression {x ∈ a | p x} denotes the set of all elements x that are members of a and satisfy the property p. It is a way to form a new set by selecting elements from an existing set a based on a condition p. This operation is known as set separation or restricted comprehension in set theory.

label: ZFSet.subset_def
slogan: A set x is a subset of a set y if and only if every element of x is also an element of y. This means x ⊆ y is defined by the condition that whenever z is in x, then z must also be in y. The relation uses the standard membership symbol ∈ to compare sets within the ZF set theory framework.

label: ZFSet.vonNeumann
slogan: The von Neumann hierarchy assigns a set V_o to each ordinal o, where V_0 is empty, V_(a+1) is the powerset of V_a, and for limit ordinals, V_a is the union of all V_b with b < a.

label: ZLattice.covolume
slogan: The covolume of a Z-lattice is the volume of a fundamental region that the lattice tiles through translations in a real vector space, calculated using a given measure. It is obtained by measuring disjoint translated copies of this region and summing their sizes, then converting the result from extended non-negative reals to a real number. This value quantifies the average space associated with each lattice point.

label: ZLattice.rank
slogan: The rank of a Z-lattice, which is a discrete subgroup of a finite-dimensional vector space over a normed field, equals the dimension of the vector space. This means the number of independent integer-linear combinations needed to generate the lattice matches the usual linear algebra dimension of the space. The result depends on the lattice being discrete and the underlying space being finite-dimensional and proper.

label: ZMod
slogan: ZMod n represents the integers modulo n, where numbers wrap around when they reach n, creating a cyclic number system. Arithmetic in ZMod n behaves as if done on a clock with n positions. This allows working with remainders in a structured way.

label: ZMod.AddAutEquivUnits
slogan: The function ZMod.AddAutEquivUnits maps each additive automorphism of the integers modulo n to a unit in the same ring, establishing a one-to-one correspondence between these automorphisms and the multiplicative units modulo n. Each automorphism corresponds to multiplication by a unit, and the mapping preserves the group structure on both sides.

label: ZMod.cauchy_davenport
slogan: If s and t are nonempty sets of integers modulo a prime p, then the number of distinct sums you can make by adding an element of s to an element of t is at least the smaller of p and |s| + |t| - 1.

label: ZMod.chineseRemainder
slogan: If two natural numbers have no common factors other than 1, then doing arithmetic modulo their product is essentially the same as doing it separately modulo each number. This means a number modulo m*n can be represented by its remainders modulo m and modulo n, and operations like addition and multiplication work the same in both settings. The mapping from a number mod m*n to its pair of remainders mod m and mod n is reversible and preserves the structure of the arithmetic.

label: ZMod.commRing
slogan: For any natural number n, the type ZMod n represents integers modulo n and supports a commutative ring structure, meaning addition, subtraction, and multiplication are well-defined and follow standard algebraic rules like commutativity, associativity, and distributivity.

label: ZMod.dft
slogan: The discrete Fourier transform on the integers modulo N (where N is nonzero) is a linear transformation that maps functions from ZMod N to a complex vector space E into other functions of the same type, preserving the structure of complex linearity. It is defined using complex exponentials and provides a reversible way to analyze periodic functions on a finite cyclic group. This transformation is expressed as a bijective linear map, meaning every function has a unique Fourier transform and inverse.

label: ZMod.dft_apply
slogan: The discrete Fourier transform of a function Φ defined on integers modulo N is computed by summing, over all integers j modulo N, the product of a complex exponential (based on -j*k) and the value of Φ at j. The complex exponential comes from the standard additive character, which maps j to exp(-2*pi*i*j*k/N). This formula holds for any nonzero N and for functions taking values in a complex vector space.

label: ZMod.dft_dft
slogan: Applying the discrete Fourier transform twice to a function on integers modulo N scales the original function by N and reverses its input, so that the result at position j is N times the original value at position -j.

label: ZMod.erdos_ginzburg_ziv
slogan: In the integers modulo n, any list of at least 2n - 1 elements contains a subset of exactly n elements that add up to zero modulo n.

label: ZMod.euler_criterion
slogan: For an odd prime number p and an integer a not divisible by p, a has a square root modulo p if and only if a raised to the power (p-1)/2 leaves a remainder of 1 when divided by p.

label: ZMod.exists_sq_eq_neg_one_iff
slogan: In the integers modulo a prime number p, there exists a number whose square is congruent to -1 modulo p if and only if p is 2 or p leaves a remainder of 1 when divided by 4. This means -1 has a square root in this modular system exactly when p equals 2 or p % 4 equals 1. The result applies only when working modulo a prime number.

label: ZMod.exists_sq_eq_neg_two_iff
slogan: There is a number in the integers modulo p whose square is congruent to -2 modulo p if and only if p is an odd prime that leaves a remainder of 1 or 3 when divided by 8. This applies only when p is a prime number not equal to 2.

label: ZMod.exists_sq_eq_two_iff
slogan: There is a number in the integers modulo p whose square is 2 if and only if p is an odd prime that leaves a remainder of 1 or 7 when divided by 8. This applies only when p is a prime number not equal to 2.

label: ZMod.frobenius_zmod
slogan: If p is a prime number, then raising any element of the integers modulo p to the p-th power gives back the same element, so the map sending each element to its p-th power is the identity function on the field of integers modulo p.

label: ZMod.gauss_lemma
slogan: For an odd prime p and an integer a not divisible by p, the Legendre symbol (a/p) is 1 if the number of integers x between 1 and (p-1)/2 such that the remainder of a*x modulo p is greater than p/2 is even, and -1 if that count is odd.

label: ZMod.instField
slogan: When p is a prime number, the integers modulo p form a field, meaning every nonzero element has a multiplicative inverse. This allows division by any nonzero element in the system. The structure supports arithmetic operations with wraparound behavior defined by modulo p.

label: ZMod.instIsAddCyclic
slogan: The integers modulo n form an additive group where every element can be written as a multiple of 1, meaning repeated addition of 1 generates all elements. This group is cyclic because the integers map onto it surjectively and the integers themselves are generated by 1 under addition. As a result, ZMod n is always an additively cyclic group for any natural number n.

label: ZMod.intCast_zmod_eq_zero_iff_dvd
slogan: An integer k becomes zero when converted to the integers modulo n if and only if k is divisible by n. In other words, casting k to ZMod n gives 0 exactly when n divides k.

label: ZMod.invDFT_apply
slogan: The inverse discrete Fourier transform of a function Ψ defined on integers modulo N is computed by averaging, over all integers j modulo N, the values of Ψ at j multiplied by a complex exponential factor that depends on j, k, and N. Specifically, the value at k is (1/N) times the sum of exp(2πi * j * k / N) * Ψ(j) over all j. This reconstructs the original function from its Fourier transform using complex weights.

label: ZMod.invDFT_def
slogan: The inverse discrete Fourier transform of a function Ψ from integers modulo N to a complex vector space E is given by averaging, over all integers j modulo N, the values of Ψ at j multiplied by the complex number exp(2 * pi * i * j * k / N), scaled by 1/N. This formula reconstructs the original function from its Fourier coefficients. The transform is defined for nonzero N and relies on complex linearity and modular arithmetic.

label: ZMod.isCyclic_units_iff
slogan: The multiplicative group of integers modulo n is cyclic if and only if n is 0, 1, 2, 4, a power of an odd prime, or twice a power of an odd prime.

label: ZMod.isSquare_of_jacobiSym_eq_one
slogan: If an integer a has a Jacobi symbol of 1 modulo an odd prime p, then a is a perfect square modulo p, meaning some integer squared is congruent to a mod p.

label: ZMod.isUnit_iff_coprime
slogan: In the integers modulo n, a number m has a multiplicative inverse if and only if the greatest common divisor of m and n is 1. This means m can be inverted modulo n precisely when m and n share no common factors other than 1. The result holds for natural numbers m and n, with m interpreted modulo n.

label: ZMod.pow_card
slogan: In the integers modulo a prime number p, raising any number to the power p gives back the same number. This works because there are exactly p distinct values in the system, and arithmetic wraps around every p steps. The result holds for all values, including zero, due to the properties of modular arithmetic with a prime modulus.

label: ZMod.pow_card_sub_one_eq_one
slogan: In arithmetic modulo a prime number p, any nonzero number raised to the power p-1 equals 1. This is because there are exactly p-1 nonzero elements, and their multiplicative behavior cycles in a way that ensures this result. It is a special case of Fermat's Little Theorem in modular arithmetic.

label: ZMod.pow_totient
slogan: If a is an integer that has no common factors with n other than 1, then raising a to the power of the number of such integers less than n gives a result that leaves a remainder of 1 when divided by n. This holds in the system of integers modulo n, where arithmetic wraps around every n numbers. The reason is that the invertible elements modulo n form a finite group whose size is given by Euler's totient function.

label: ZMod.ringEquivOfPrime
slogan: If p is a prime number and R is a finite ring with exactly p elements, then the ring of integers modulo p is structurally identical to R, meaning there is a one-to-one mapping between them that preserves both addition and multiplication.

label: ZMod.wilsons_lemma
slogan: For any prime number p, the product of all integers from 1 to p-1 is congruent to -1 modulo p.

label: ZSpan.fundamentalDomain
slogan: The fundamental domain of the integer span of a basis is the set of all linear combinations of the basis vectors where each coefficient is at least 0 and less than 1. This set contains exactly one representative from each coset of the integer span in the real vector space. It represents a unit cell that repeats periodically to cover the entire space under integer translations.

label: ZeroAtInftyContinuousMap
slogan: A ZeroAtInftyContinuousMap is a continuous function from a topological space to a type that has a zero element, where the function values get arbitrarily close to zero as the input moves toward infinity. It describes functions that vanish at infinity in a general topological setting. This type combines continuity with the condition that the function approaches zero outside large compact sets.

label: ZeroAtInftyContinuousMap.instNonUnitalCommCStarAlgebra
slogan: The space of continuous functions that vanish at infinity from a topological space to a non-unital commutative C*-algebra forms a non-unital commutative C*-algebra under pointwise operations, with the supremum norm and a compatible involution. This structure has a norm satisfying the C*-identity, commutative multiplication, and no multiplicative unit. It supports complex scalar multiplication and is complete with respect to the norm topology.

label: Zsqrtd.norm_mul
slogan: The norm of the product of two elements in the ring Z[sqrt(d)] is equal to the product of their norms. This means that for any two numbers of the form a + b*sqrt(d), multiplying them and then computing the norm gives the same result as computing each norm first and then multiplying those integers. The norm here is defined as a*a - d*b*b for an element a + b*sqrt(d).

label: abs_dist_sub_le
slogan: The absolute value of the difference between the distance from x to z and the distance from y to z is at most the distance from x to y. This means that moving one endpoint of a distance measurement changes the distance by no more than the distance moved. It follows from the triangle inequality in spaces where distance is symmetric and satisfies the triangle law, even if distinct points can be zero distance apart.

label: abs_le_abs_of_nonneg
slogan: If a number a is at least zero and less than or equal to another number b that is also at least zero, then the absolute value of a is less than or equal to the absolute value of b. This is because the absolute value of a non-negative number is the number itself, and the less-than-or-equal-to relation is transitive. The result holds in any algebraic structure with addition, negation, zero, and a lattice order where addition preserves order when added on the left.

label: abs_norm_sub_norm_le
slogan: The absolute value of the difference between the sizes of two elements is at most the size of their difference, in any group with a norm that behaves like length. This means that changing an element by some amount changes its norm by no more than the size of the change.

label: abs_real_inner_div_norm_mul_norm_le_one
slogan: The absolute value of the inner product of two vectors, divided by the product of their lengths, is always less than or equal to 1. This is true for any two vectors in a real inner product space. It follows from the fact that the absolute value of the inner product is at most the product of the norms of the vectors.

label: absurd
slogan: If you have a statement and its opposite both true, then any other statement can be concluded. This principle allows deriving any conclusion from contradictory assumptions. It works for any proposition and any type of result.

label: accPt_iff_frequently
slogan: A point x is an accumulation point of a set C if and only if, in every neighborhood around x, there are frequently points from C other than x itself; this means that for every neighborhood of x, there exists some y not equal to x such that y is in both the neighborhood and C.

label: accPt_iff_frequently_nhdsNE
slogan: A point x is an accumulation point of a set C if and only if, in every neighborhood around x excluding x itself, there are frequently points from C. This means that no matter how small the neighborhood around x, there is always some point from C (different from x) inside it. The condition is stated using filters: the set C intersects the punctured neighborhoods of x in a frequent way.

label: ack
slogan: The ack function is a two-argument function on natural numbers that grows very quickly and is defined recursively: it returns n + 1 when the first argument is 0, otherwise it reduces the first argument and adjusts the second argument recursively. It is an example of a function that is computable but not primitive recursive.

label: add_assoc
slogan: For any three elements a, b, and c in a type where addition is defined, the sum of a + b + c is the same whether you group a and b first or b and c first. This means addition is associative.

label: add_comm
slogan: For any type with a commutative addition operation, adding two elements a and b gives the same result regardless of order, so a + b is always equal to b + a.

label: add_pow_char
slogan: In a commutative semiring where adding 1 to itself p times gives 0, and p is a prime number, the p-th power of the sum of two elements equals the sum of their p-th powers, provided the elements commute. This means (x + y)^p = x^p + y^p holds under these conditions. The rule works because the binomial coefficients for intermediate terms vanish due to the prime characteristic.

label: ae_eq_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq
slogan: If two functions that are locally integrable on a finite-dimensional real vector space have the same integral against every smooth compactly supported test function, then they are equal almost everywhere with respect to the given measure.

label: ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero
slogan: If a function that is locally integrable over a finite-dimensional real vector space has the property that its integral is zero whenever it is multiplied by any smooth, compactly supported real-valued function, then the function itself must be zero almost everywhere with respect to the given measure.

label: affineSpan_pair_le_of_mem_of_mem
slogan: If two points are in an affine subspace, then the smallest affine subspace containing those two points is contained within the original subspace. This means any line segment or affine combination between the two points lies entirely in the subspace. The result follows from the fact that affine spans are the minimal subspaces containing their defining points.

label: algebraicClosure
slogan: The algebraic closure of a field F within a larger field E is the set of all elements in E that are roots of polynomials with coefficients in F, forming a field that sits between F and E. It is built by taking elements that satisfy monic polynomials over F, ensuring every element is algebraic over F. This intermediate field contains all possible solutions to polynomial equations from F inside E.

label: algebraicClosure.isAlgClosure
slogan: The algebraic closure of a field F is an extension field where every polynomial with coefficients in F has a root, and this result confirms that the constructed extension is indeed algebraic over F and algebraically closed, meaning all elements are roots of polynomials from F and all polynomials over the extension split completely.

label: alternatingGroup
slogan: The alternating group on a finite type is defined as the subgroup of all even permutations within the group of all permutations of that type. It consists of those permutations whose sign is +1, forming a subgroup under composition. For a finite set with n elements, this corresponds to the usual alternating group A_n.

label: alternatingGroup.commutator_perm_le
slogan: The commutator subgroup of the symmetric group on a finite type is contained within the alternating group. This means every element that can be written as a product of commutators of permutations is an even permutation. In other words, the subgroup generated by all commutators lies inside the group of even permutations.

label: alternatingGroup.isSimpleGroup_five
slogan: The alternating group on 5 elements, which consists of all even permutations of five items, is simple because it has no nontrivial normal subgroups—any normal subgroup containing a non-identity element must be the entire group. This is shown by checking each possible cycle type of a non-identity element and proving that its normal closure is the whole group. The result relies on properties of permutations, conjugacy, and subgroup structure.

label: alternatingGroup.kleinFour
slogan: The alternatingGroup.kleinFour is the subgroup of even permutations generated by those that swap two pairs of elements. When the type has exactly four elements, this subgroup behaves like the Klein Four group. It is formed by taking all combinations of such double transpositions within the alternating group.

label: alternating_series_error_bound
slogan: For an alternating series where the terms get smaller in absolute value and approach zero, the difference between the partial sum up to term n and the full sum is no larger than the absolute value of the next term, f(n).

label: and_assoc
slogan: The statement (a and b) and c is logically equivalent to a and b and c, meaning that the grouping of conditions joined by "and" does not affect the overall truth value.

label: and_comm
slogan: The logical conjunction of two propositions a and b is equivalent to their conjunction in the opposite order; that is, if both a and b are true, then both b and a are true, regardless of the order.

label: and_iff_not_or_not
slogan: The statement "a and b" is true exactly when it is not true that either a is false or b is false. This means both a and b must be true if neither one is false. The equivalence holds when the truth of a and b can each be decided.

label: and_imp
slogan: If a and b together imply c, then having a implies that having b also implies c, and vice versa. This means that proving c from both a and b is the same as proving c from a after assuming b. The logical connection between the propositions stays the same either way.

label: and_not_self_iff
slogan: A statement and its negation cannot both be true at the same time; the conjunction of a proposition and its negation is always false.

label: and_or_left
slogan: The statement says that having a true and either b or c true is the same as having either both a and b true, or both a and c true. In other words, "a and (b or c)" is equivalent to "(a and b) or (a and c)".

label: asymm_of_isTrans_of_irrefl
slogan: If a relation is transitive and never relates an element to itself, then it cannot relate two elements in both directions; if a is related to b, then b cannot be related to a.

label: asymptoticCone
slogan: The asymptotic cone of a set s in an affine space consists of all directions v such that, no matter how far out you go, there are always points of s in directions close to v. It captures the idea of the set extending infinitely in certain directions. This is defined using a filter that describes behavior at infinity near each direction v.

label: banach_steinhaus
slogan: If a collection of continuous linear maps from a Banach space to a normed space is bounded at each point, then the operator norms of these maps are uniformly bounded by some constant.

label: banach_steinhaus_iSup_nnnorm
slogan: If a family of continuous linear operators between certain normed spaces is pointwise bounded in norm, then the supremum of their operator norms is finite. This means that uniform boundedness of the operators on each individual vector implies uniform boundedness across all vectors. The result holds when the domain space is complete and the norms take values in the extended nonnegative real numbers.

label: basisOfLinearIndependentOfCardEqFinrank
slogan: If a set of vectors is linearly independent and has exactly as many elements as the dimension of the space, then it spans the whole space and is a basis.

label: basisOfTopLeSpanOfCardEqFinrank
slogan: If a finite set of vectors in a module spans the whole module and the number of vectors equals the module's finite rank, then those vectors form a basis. This means they are linearly independent and every element of the module can be uniquely written as a combination of them. The result applies to modules with the Orzech property over a semiring.

label: basis_toMatrix_mul_linearMap_toMatrix_mul_basis_toMatrix
slogan: If you convert a linear map to a matrix using bases, multiply it by change-of-basis matrices, and then convert back, the result is the same as converting the linear map directly using the new bases. This holds when all bases are finite and their elements can be compared for equality. The matrix multiplication correctly accounts for changes in both the input and output bases.

label: bernstein
slogan: The bernstein function returns a continuous real-valued function on the interval [0,1], defined as the Bernstein polynomial of degree n corresponding to index v, which is built from binomial coefficients and powers of x and (1-x). This polynomial is treated as a continuous map using the topology of the real numbers. It is derived from an algebraic polynomial expression by restricting it to the unit interval and viewing it as a continuous function.

label: bernsteinApproximation
slogan: The bernsteinApproximation function takes a natural number n and a continuous function f from the interval [0,1] to a topological vector space E, and returns a new continuous function that approximates f by averaging its values at points k/n using Bernstein polynomials. This approximation is built by summing terms of the form (bernstein polynomial of degree n at point x) multiplied by f(k/n). The result is a sequence of polynomials that converge uniformly to f on [0,1] as n increases.

label: bernsteinPolynomial.derivative_succ
slogan: The derivative of the (ν+1)-th Bernstein polynomial of degree n over a commutative ring R is equal to n times the difference between the ν-th and (ν+1)-th Bernstein polynomials of degree n-1. This expresses how the derivative of a Bernstein basis polynomial can be written as a linear combination of lower-degree Bernstein polynomials. The formula relies on standard polynomial differentiation and the algebraic properties of binomial coefficients.

label: bernsteinPolynomial.sum
slogan: The sum of all Bernstein polynomials of degree n over a commutative ring R, evaluated at each integer from 0 to n, equals the constant polynomial 1. Each Bernstein polynomial is built from binomial coefficients and powers of X and (1 - X). Adding them all together results in 1, regardless of the ring R.

label: biUnion_connectedComponent_pathComponent_eq
slogan: In a topological space, the set of all points that can be reached by a continuous path from a given point covers the same region as the largest connected set containing that point. Every connected component is made up of path-connected parts, and together these parts fill the entire connected component. As a result, the union of all path-connected components within a connected component equals that connected component.

label: boolRingCatEquivBoolAlg
slogan: There is a one-to-one correspondence between Boolean rings and Boolean algebras that preserves their structure, meaning each Boolean ring can be viewed as a Boolean algebra and vice versa, with operations and identities matching up exactly. This correspondence is an isomorphism of categories, so the two types of structures are interchangeable in a precise mathematical sense.

label: borel
slogan: The borel function creates a measurable space from a topological space by using the open sets to generate the smallest sigma-algebra that includes them. This sigma-algebra is built with the generateFrom function, ensuring all open sets are measurable. As a result, measure theory and integration can be applied naturally on topological spaces.

label: cantorSet
slogan: The Cantor set is the set of real numbers in the interval [0, 1] that remain after repeatedly removing the open middle third of every interval, done infinitely many times. It is defined as the intersection of all pre-Cantor sets, where each pre-Cantor set is built by dividing the previous set into thirds and keeping only the left and right parts. This results in a set of points that can be expressed in base 3 without the digit 1.

label: card_comm_eq_card_conjClasses_mul_card
slogan: The number of pairs of elements in a finite group that commute equals the number of conjugacy classes multiplied by the size of the group.

label: card_sylow_modEq_one
slogan: For a finite group whose size is a power of a prime number p, the number of its Sylow p-subgroups leaves a remainder of 1 when divided by p.

label: catalan
slogan: The Catalan numbers are defined recursively such that the (n+1)th number is the sum over i from 0 to n of the product of the ith Catalan number and the (n-i)th Catalan number. Each term in the sum multiplies two earlier values in the sequence. The sequence starts with a base case where the zeroth Catalan number is 1.

label: catalan_two
slogan: The second Catalan number is equal to 2. This follows from the recursive definition of Catalan numbers, where each number is built from products of earlier terms in the sequence, starting with the base case of 1 for the zeroth term.

label: cauchySeq_of_edist_le_geometric
slogan: If the distance between consecutive terms of a sequence is bounded by a geometric sequence with ratio less than 1, then the sequence is Cauchy, meaning its terms eventually become arbitrarily close to each other. This holds in any space where distance can be infinite, as long as the bounding constants are finite and the ratio is strictly less than 1.

label: cauchySeq_tendsto_of_complete
slogan: In a complete uniform space, if a sequence is Cauchy (its terms eventually stay close to each other), then it converges to some point in the space. This means that as the sequence progresses, it gets arbitrarily close to a specific limit point.

label: cfc_map_spectrum
slogan: For a normal element a in a C*-algebra and a continuous function f defined on the spectrum of a, the spectrum of the operator f(a), obtained via continuous functional calculus, is exactly the set of values f takes on the spectrum of a.

label: char_dvd_card_solutions
slogan: If a polynomial over a finite field has fewer variables than its total degree, and the field has characteristic p, then the number of solutions to the polynomial equation is divisible by p.

label: char_dvd_card_solutions_of_fintype_sum_lt
slogan: If you have a finite set of polynomials in several variables over a finite field of characteristic p, and the sum of their total degrees is less than the number of variables, then the number of common solutions is divisible by p.

label: char_dvd_card_solutions_of_sum_lt
slogan: If you have a finite set of polynomials over a finite field of characteristic p, and the sum of their degrees is less than the number of variables, then the number of common solutions is divisible by p.

label: chartAt
slogan: chartAt takes a point in a topological space M that is modeled on a space H and returns a local homeomorphism around that point, mapping an open neighborhood in M to an open set in H, such that the map and its inverse are continuous and preserve the local topological structure.

label: chudnovskySum
slogan: chudnovskySum is the sum of an infinite series of rational terms, each computed by the chudnovskyTerm function, that converges to the reciprocal of pi. The sum is defined as the limit of partial sums over natural numbers using standard real number arithmetic. Each term in the series involves factorials and powers, and the series is known for its fast convergence in computing 1/pi.

label: closure
slogan: The closure of a set in a topological space is the intersection of all closed sets that contain it, and is itself a closed set. It represents the smallest closed set that includes all the points of the original set.

label: closure_Ioo
slogan: In a linearly ordered space where there is always an element between any two distinct elements, and where the topology is defined by the order, the smallest closed set containing all points strictly between a and b is the set that includes all points from a to b, inclusive. This means the closure of the open interval (a, b) is the closed interval [a, b], provided a is not equal to b.

label: closure_convexHull_extremePoints
slogan: In a locally convex topological vector space, every compact convex set equals the closure of all points that can be formed by taking averages of its extreme points. An extreme point is one that cannot be placed inside a line segment between two other distinct points of the set. This means the shape of a compact convex set is determined by its "corner" points, even if those corners are not obvious.

label: closure_empty
slogan: The closure of the empty set is the empty set, because the empty set is already closed in any topological space and no points can be added to it. This follows from the definition of closure as the smallest closed set containing a given set.

label: closure_pi_set
slogan: The closure of a product of sets in the product topology is the same as the product of the closures of each individual set. A point is in this closure if and only if each of its components is in the closure of the corresponding set in its space. This holds for the standard product topology where projections are continuous.

label: commGroupOfCyclicCenterQuotient
slogan: If a group homomorphism has a kernel contained in the center of the group and the image is cyclic, then the original group must be abelian; this declaration provides a commutative group structure in such cases. It uses the fact that when the quotient by the center is cyclic, all elements of the group commute. The result constructs an abelian group instance directly from these conditions.

label: commutator
slogan: The commutator of two subgroups is the smallest subgroup containing all elements made by multiplying a, b, a inverse, and b inverse in that order, where a comes from the first subgroup and b from the second. It measures how much the subgroups don't commute under the group's operation. This subgroup is built using the group's multiplication and inverse operations.

label: commute_iff_eq
slogan: Two elements a and b in a multiplicative structure commute if and only if a * b equals b * a. This means the order of multiplication does not matter exactly when the two products are equal. The statement asserts that commutativity is equivalent to this equality.

label: compactSpace_of_completeLinearOrder
slogan: Any type with a complete linear order has a natural topology based on that order, and in this topology, the entire space is compact. This means that every closed interval from the smallest to the largest element covers all elements, and the whole set behaves like a closed, bounded interval in the real numbers. The topology ensures that the space satisfies the finite subcover property for open covers.

label: compl_inf
slogan: In a Boolean algebra, the complement of the meet (intersection) of two elements equals the join (union) of their individual complements. This means that negating the infimum of two elements distributes as the supremum of their negations.

label: compl_sup_distrib
slogan: In a Heyting algebra, the complement of the join of two elements is the same as the meet of their complements.

label: completeBipartiteGraph
slogan: The complete bipartite graph on two types of vertices, V and W, is a simple graph where each vertex from V is connected to every vertex from W, but no vertices within V or within W are connected. The vertices are represented as a sum type V ⊕ W, and two vertices are adjacent if and only if one comes from V and the other from W. Any bipartite graph can be seen as a subgraph of such a complete bipartite graph.

label: completeLatticeOfCompleteSemilatticeSup
slogan: If a type has a partial order and every subset has a least upper bound, then greatest lower bounds for all subsets can also be defined by taking the least upper bound of all lower bounds; this makes the type a complete lattice. The existence of all suprema implies the existence of all infima when infima are defined in this way. Thus, any complete semilattice with suprema can be made into a complete lattice.

label: completedRiemannZeta_one_sub
slogan: The completed Riemann zeta function has a symmetry such that its value at 1 minus s is always equal to its value at s, for any complex number s. This means the function is symmetric around the point s = 1/2 in the complex plane.

label: completedZeta_eq_tsum_of_one_lt_re
slogan: For a complex number s with real part greater than 1, the completed Riemann zeta function equals pi raised to the power of -s/2, multiplied by the gamma function of s/2, and then multiplied by the sum over all positive integers n of 1 divided by n to the power s. This sum converges and represents the zeta function in a symmetric form. The equation links the completed zeta function directly to this infinite series.

label: conformalAt_iff_differentiableAt_or_differentiableAt_comp_conj
slogan: A complex function is conformal at a point if and only if it is either holomorphic or antiholomorphic at that point, and its derivative is not zero. Being holomorphic means the function is complex differentiable, while being antiholomorphic means the function composed with complex conjugation is complex differentiable. The function must have a nonzero derivative to preserve angles locally.

label: congrArg
slogan: If two inputs a1 and a2 are equal, then applying the same function f to both gives equal results: f a1 = f a2. This allows replacing equal values inside larger expressions. It works for any function f from type α to type β.

label: conj_pow
slogan: For any elements a and b in a group and any natural number i, conjugating b by a and then raising the result to the i-th power gives the same outcome as first raising b to the i-th power and then conjugating by a. This means that taking powers and conjugating commute. Specifically, (a * b * a^-1)^i equals a * (b^i) * a^-1.

label: connectedComponent
slogan: The connected component of a point in a topological space is the union of all preconnected sets that contain the point, forming the largest set around the point that cannot be divided into two separate nonempty open parts. It consists of all elements that can be reached through preconnected subsets including the point. This set is constructed by gathering all such elements and taking their union.

label: connectedComponentSetoid
slogan: The connectedComponentSetoid defines when two points in a topological space are considered equivalent by checking if they are in the same connected component, meaning there's no way to separate them using disjoint open sets. It uses the structure of the space and the definition of connected components to create this equivalence relation. This allows forming a new type where points in the same connected part are treated as equal.

label: connectedComponent_disjoint
slogan: In a topological space, the connected components of two different points are disjoint sets, meaning they share no points in common. Each connected component is the largest connected set containing its points, and distinct components do not overlap. If two components are not equal, then they have an empty intersection.

label: connectedComponent_subset_iInter_isClopen
slogan: If a set is both open and closed and contains a point, then it must contain the whole connected component of that point; therefore, the connected component of a point is contained in every clopen set that includes the point.

label: constant_of_derivWithin_zero
slogan: If a function from the real numbers to a normed vector space is differentiable on a closed interval and its derivative is zero at every point in the interior of that interval, then the function takes the same value at all points in the interval. In other words, the function is constant on the interval. This result relies on the mean value theorem and the fact that a zero derivative implies no change in the function's value.

label: continuousAt_def
slogan: A function is continuous at a point if, whenever the output is close to the function's value at that point, the input is close to the point itself. This is formalized by saying that for every set containing an open set around the function's value, the set of inputs that map into it must include an open set around the original point. The definition uses neighborhood filters to capture the idea of "closeness" in topological spaces.

label: continuousAt_iff_continuous_left_right
slogan: A function is continuous at a point if and only if it is both left-continuous and right-continuous at that point, meaning the function's limit from the left and from the right must both equal its value at the point. This is equivalent to saying the function is continuous when restricted to the sets of points less than or equal to the point and greater than or equal to the point. The result holds in any linearly ordered topological space.

label: continuousAt_iff_punctured_nhds
slogan: A function is continuous at a point if and only if, as the input approaches that point but stays different from it, the output gets arbitrarily close to the function's value at the point. This means continuity at a point depends only on the function's behavior near, but not exactly at, the point. The condition is expressed using filters: the function must map the punctured neighborhood filter at the point into the neighborhood filter of the function's value.

label: continuousAt_iff_ultrafilter
slogan: A function is continuous at a point if and only if, for every ultrafilter that converges to that point, the image of the ultrafilter converges to the function's value at that point. This means continuity at a point can be checked by looking at how ultrafilters near the point behave under the function. Convergence is defined using neighborhood filters in topological spaces.

label: continuous_apply
slogan: A function into a product space is continuous if and only if each of its component functions, obtained by projecting onto individual factors, is continuous. This means continuity for such a function is determined by how it behaves when composed with the standard projection maps. The product topology ensures that this condition holds by making projections continuous by definition.

label: continuous_id
slogan: The identity function, which sends every point in a topological space to itself, is continuous because the preimage of any open set is that same open set, and hence is open.

label: continuous_iff_continuousAt
slogan: A function is continuous if and only if it is continuous at every point, meaning that for each point in the domain, the preimage of every neighborhood of its image contains a neighborhood of the point. This is equivalent to saying the preimage of every open set in the codomain is an open set in the domain. Continuity at a point depends on the topologies of both the domain and codomain.

label: continuous_iff_image_closure_subset_closure_image
slogan: A function is continuous if and only if, for every set, applying the function to the closure of the set gives results that are contained within the closure of the image of the set. This means continuity is equivalent to the function preserving the relationship between sets and their limit points. In simple terms, a function is continuous when it maps points near a set to points near the image of that set.

label: continuous_iff_isClosed
slogan: A function between topological spaces is continuous if and only if the preimage of every closed set is closed. This means that instead of checking open sets, continuity can be verified by seeing whether pulling back closed sets results in closed sets. The equivalence works because complements of open sets are closed, and preimages preserve set complements.

label: continuous_iff_seqContinuous
slogan: A function between two topological spaces is continuous if and only if it maps convergent sequences to convergent sequences, preserving their limits, provided the domain space is a sequential space where closed sets are determined by limits of sequences. This means checking continuity using sequences is sufficient in such spaces. The equivalence relies on the topology of the domain being fully described by its convergent sequences.

label: continuous_of_continuousAt_one
slogan: A function between topological groups is continuous everywhere if it sends the identity element to the identity element and is continuous at that point, meaning the preimage of every neighborhood of the identity in the target group contains a neighborhood of the identity in the source group. Continuity at the identity, combined with the group structure, ensures continuity throughout the space.

label: continuous_of_discreteTopology
slogan: In a space where every subset is open (discrete topology), any function from that space to another topological space is continuous because the preimage of an open set is always open. This happens since all subsets being open means there are no restrictions on the function for continuity to hold.

label: continuous_of_linear_of_bound
slogan: If a function between two normed modules preserves addition and scalar multiplication, and if the size of its output is always at most a constant times the size of its input, then the function is continuous. This means linear maps with bounded growth are automatically continuous. The continuity follows because such a bound ensures the function is Lipschitz.

label: contractible_iff_id_nullhomotopic
slogan: A topological space Y is contractible if and only if the identity map on Y is homotopic to a constant map. This means the space can be continuously shrunk to a single point. The identity map being nullhomotopic captures this idea of continuous deformation to a constant function.

label: convexHull
slogan: The convexHull function takes a set of points and returns the smallest convex set containing it, where a set is convex if any weighted average of its points (with non-negative weights adding to one) stays in the set. It works in spaces that support addition, scalar multiplication, and ordering, like modules over semirings, by using the structure of closed sets under intersection. This smallest convex set is built by taking the intersection of all convex sets that contain the original set.

label: convexHullAddMonoidHom
slogan: The convexHullAddMonoidHom function takes a set and returns its convex hull, and it respects set addition and the zero set: the convex hull of the sum of two sets equals the sum of their convex hulls, and the convex hull of the zero set is just the zero set. It ensures that forming convex hulls behaves well with the algebraic structure of addition and zero in vector-like spaces. This function works in settings where there is a combination of addition, scalar multiplication, and a linear order compatible with arithmetic.

label: convexHull_add
slogan: The convex hull of the sum of two sets is the same as the sum of their convex hulls. This means you can add all points from two sets together first and then take the convex hull, or take the convex hulls first and then add them pointwise, and end up with the same set.

label: convexHull_eq_union
slogan: The convex hull of a set s is the union of the convex hulls of all affinely independent subsets of s. In other words, every point in the convex hull of s can be expressed as a convex combination of points from some affinely independent subset of s. This means the overall convex hull is built by combining the convex hulls of smaller, simpler subsets.

label: convexHull_min
slogan: The convex hull of a set is the smallest convex set containing it, meaning any convex set that includes the original set must also include its convex hull. If a set t is convex and contains all points of s, then t must contain the convex hull of s. This makes the convex hull the minimal convex set containing s with respect to inclusion.

label: convexHull_sum
slogan: The convex hull of the sum of a finite collection of sets equals the sum of the convex hulls of those sets. This means combining the smallest convex sets containing each individual set gives the same result as forming the smallest convex set containing all possible sums of points from the original sets. The result holds in vector spaces or similar structures with commutative addition and scalar multiplication.

label: convexJoin
slogan: The convexJoin of two sets s and t consists of all points lying on line segments that connect any point in s to any point in t, using weighted averages with non-negative coefficients that sum to one. It is formed within the same space as the original sets and combines the sets by filling in the straight-line paths between them. This construction generalizes the idea of joining two shapes with line segments between their points.

label: convexOn_norm
slogan: The norm function on a real vector space is convex on any convex set, meaning that for any two vectors in the set and any weight between 0 and 1, the norm of their weighted average is at most the same weighted average of their norms. This property follows from the triangle inequality and the fact that scaling a vector scales its norm by the absolute value of the scalar.

label: convexOn_univ_norm
slogan: The norm function is convex over the entire space of a real normed vector space, meaning that for any two vectors and any weight between 0 and 1, the norm of the weighted average of the vectors is less than or equal to the weighted average of their norms. This holds for all vectors because the universal set includes every element and the norm satisfies the triangle inequality and scalar multiplication properties.

label: convex_ball
slogan: In a real normed space, any open ball (the set of points within a fixed distance from a center point) is convex, meaning that if two points are inside the ball, then every point on the line segment between them is also inside the ball. This happens because the norm's convexity ensures that distances along the segment do not exceed the ball's radius.

label: convex_iff_add_mem
slogan: A set is convex if and only if for any two points in the set, any weighted average of those points using non-negative weights that add up to one is also in the set. This means that if you take two elements from the set and form a point on the line segment between them, that point must stay in the set. The weights used are scalars from a semiring with a partial order, and the operation is defined using scalar multiplication on an additive commutative monoid.

label: convex_iff_ordConnected
slogan: A set in a linearly ordered field is convex if and only if it contains every point between any two of its points, meaning the set is order-connected. This equivalence means that being closed under intervals (in the order sense) is the same as being closed under linear combinations between points. The result applies when the field has a strict order compatible with its algebraic operations.

label: convex_iff_pointwise_add_subset
slogan: A set is convex if and only if, for any two non-negative scalars that add up to one, the set contains all combinations of its points scaled by those scalars and then added together. This means that any weighted average of two points in the set must also lie in the set. The condition is expressed using scalar multiplication and pointwise set addition.

label: convex_sInter
slogan: The intersection of any family of convex sets is also convex: if every set in a collection has the property that the line segment between any two of its points stays within the set, then the common intersection of all these sets has the same property. This holds in a general algebraic setting with scalar multiplication over a semiring that has a partial order and an additive structure.

label: countable_iff_exists_injective
slogan: A set is countable exactly when there is a one-to-one function mapping its elements into the natural numbers. This means no two distinct elements of the set map to the same natural number. Such a function ensures the set can be listed or enumerated in some order.

label: countable_iff_exists_surjective
slogan: A type is countable if and only if there is a surjective function from the natural numbers onto it, meaning every element of the type can be reached by applying the function to some natural number. This requires the type to have at least one element.

label: cross_anticomm
slogan: The cross product of vector v with vector w is equal to the negative of the cross product of w with v, for any two vectors in 3-dimensional space over a commutative ring. This means swapping the order of the vectors in the cross product negates the result.

label: cross_apply
slogan: The cross product of two vectors a and b in 3-dimensional space over a commutative ring R is computed component-wise as (a1*b2 - a2*b1, a2*b0 - a0*b2, a0*b1 - a1*b0), where each vector is represented as a function from the indices 0,1,2 to R.

label: cross_cross
slogan: For any three 3-dimensional vectors u, v, and w over a commutative ring R, the cross product of (u cross v) with w equals (u cross (v cross w)) minus (v cross (u cross w)). This identity expresses a kind of distributive property of the cross product over itself, similar to the Jacobi identity. It holds because the cross product in three dimensions satisfies the algebraic rules of a Lie bracket.

label: cross_cross_eq_smul_sub_smul'
slogan: For vectors u, v, and w in 3-dimensional space over a commutative ring, the cross product of u with the cross product of v and w equals (u dot w) times v minus (v dot u) times w.

label: csSup_Icc
slogan: The supremum of the closed interval [a, b] is b, as long as a is less than or equal to b. This means b is the smallest number that is greater than or equal to every element in the interval. Since b is included in the interval and is the largest such element, it is the least upper bound.

label: den_dvd_of_is_root
slogan: If a fraction in lowest terms is a root of a polynomial with integer coefficients, then the denominator of that fraction divides the leading coefficient of the polynomial.

label: dense_iInter_of_isOpen
slogan: In a Baire space, if you have a countable family of open sets and each one is dense (meaning they get arbitrarily close to every point), then their intersection is also dense. This means the common elements shared by all these sets still come arbitrarily close to every point in the space. The result depends on the space being a Baire space and the sets being both open and dense.

label: dense_liouville
slogan: The set of Liouville numbers is dense in the real numbers, meaning that in every open interval, no matter how small, there is a Liouville number. A Liouville number is a real number that can be approximated very closely by rational numbers, with the approximation improving faster than any fixed power of the denominator. This result follows from the fact that the set of Liouville numbers is residual and the real line is a Baire space.

label: dense_sInter_of_isOpen
slogan: In a Baire space, if you have a countable family of open sets that are each dense (meaning they come arbitrarily close to every point), then the intersection of all these sets is also dense. This means that even after intersecting infinitely many such open and densely spread sets, the resulting set still gets arbitrarily close to every point in the space.

label: derangements
slogan: A derangement is a set of permutations of a type where no element is mapped to itself; in other words, every element is moved to a different position by the permutation.

label: deriv.lhopital_zero_atTop
slogan: If two functions f and g both approach 0 as x goes to positive infinity, and their derivatives exist and g' is nonzero near infinity, then the limit of f(x)/g(x) as x goes to infinity equals the limit of f'(x)/g'(x), provided the latter limit exists.

label: deriv.lhopital_zero_nhds
slogan: If two real functions f and g both approach zero as x approaches a, and if f and g are differentiable near a (except possibly at a) with the derivative of g not zero near a, then the limit of f(x)/g(x) as x approaches a equals the limit of (f'(x)/g'(x)) as x approaches a, provided the latter limit exists.

label: deriv_add
slogan: If two functions are differentiable at a point, then their sum is also differentiable at that point, and the derivative of the sum is simply the sum of their individual derivatives. This holds for functions between spaces that support norms and scalar multiplication over a field with a nontrivial norm. The derivative is understood as the best linear approximation to the function at that point.

label: deriv_comp
slogan: If a function f is differentiable at a point x, and a function g is differentiable at f(x), then the composition g(f(x)) is differentiable at x, and its derivative is the product of the derivative of g at f(x) and the derivative of f at x. This holds for functions between normed vector spaces over nontrivially normed fields. The rule for computing the derivative of the composition is known as the chain rule.

label: deriv_div
slogan: If two functions are differentiable at a point and the denominator function is not zero there, then their quotient is also differentiable at that point, and its derivative is given by the standard quotient rule: (num' * den - num * den') / den^2, where num and den are the numerator and denominator functions, and the primes denote their derivatives. This holds in normed vector spaces over a nontrivially normed field where division is well-defined. The derivative of the quotient is computed using the derivatives of the numerator and denominator at that point.

label: deriv_fun_inv''
slogan: If a function c is differentiable at a point x and c(x) is not zero, then the function 1/c(x) is also differentiable at x, and its derivative is -deriv(c)(x) divided by c(x) squared.

label: deriv_mul
slogan: If two functions are differentiable at a point, the derivative of their product at that point is the first function at that point times the derivative of the second, plus the second function at that point times the derivative of the first. This rule applies in spaces that are normed algebras over a field with a nontrivial norm.

label: derivedSeries
slogan: The derived series of a group G is a sequence of subgroups where the first subgroup is G itself, and each subsequent subgroup is generated by the commutators of the previous subgroup with itself. This process measures the degree of non-commutativity in the group by repeatedly isolating the elements that reflect failure to commute. The series progresses by applying this commutator operation iteratively at each step.

label: derivedSet
slogan: The derived set of a set A in a topological space is the collection of all points where every neighborhood around them contains at least one point of A different from the point itself. It consists of all accumulation points of A.

label: differentiableAt_complex_iff_differentiableAt_real
slogan: A function from the complex numbers to a complex normed space is complex-differentiable at a point if and only if it is real-differentiable there and its real derivative satisfies the Cauchy-Riemann condition, meaning that applying the derivative to the imaginary unit i gives the same result as multiplying the derivative of 1 by i.

label: differentiableAt_riemannZeta
slogan: The Riemann zeta function has a complex derivative at every point except s = 1. This means it is smooth and well-approximated by a linear function near any point in the complex plane as long as that point is not 1. The function behaves nicely in terms of calculus everywhere except at that single point.

label: differentiableWithinAt_complex_iff_differentiableWithinAt_real
slogan: A function from the complex numbers to a complex normed space is complex-differentiable at a point within a set if and only if it is real-differentiable there and its real derivative satisfies the Cauchy-Riemann condition, meaning multiplying the derivative of 1 by the imaginary unit i gives the same result as applying the derivative to i.

label: dimH
slogan: The Hausdorff dimension of a set in a metric space is the smallest value d such that the d-dimensional Hausdorff measure of the set is zero. It is expressed as an extended nonnegative real number (including infinity). This dimension quantifies how the set fills space, capturing fractal or irregular structures.

label: dimH_countable
slogan: Any countable set in a metric space has Hausdorff dimension zero. This means that if a set contains only finitely or countably many points, it does not fill space in a way that gives it positive fractal dimension. The result follows from the fact that single points have zero dimension and the dimension of a countable union of such sets is the supremum of their dimensions.

label: dimH_def
slogan: The Hausdorff dimension of a set s in a metric space is the supremum of all real numbers d such that the d-dimensional Hausdorff measure of s is infinite. It is defined using the measurable structure of the space and captures how "large" the set is in terms of scaling and dimension. This value can be a nonnegative real number or infinity.

label: dimH_iUnion
slogan: The Hausdorff dimension of a countable union of sets in a metric space is equal to the supremum of the Hausdorff dimensions of those individual sets. This means the overall dimension is determined by the "largest" dimension among the sets. The space allows infinite distances, and dimensions are expressed as nonnegative real numbers or infinity.

label: dimH_singleton
slogan: The Hausdorff dimension of a set containing just one point in a metric space is zero. This is because any set with at most one point has a Hausdorff dimension of zero. The result follows from the general property that singleton sets are subsingletons.

label: discrim
slogan: The discrim function calculates the discriminant of a quadratic expression using the formula b*b - 4*a*c, where a, b, and c are coefficients from any ring-like type that supports basic arithmetic and natural number literals such as 2. It works in any algebraic structure with addition, multiplication, and additive inverses, ensuring the operations follow standard algebraic rules. The result helps determine whether the roots of a quadratic equation are real, repeated, or complex.

label: discrim_eq_sq_of_quadratic_eq_zero
slogan: If a quadratic equation a*x^2 + b*x + c = 0 holds in a commutative ring, then its discriminant b^2 - 4*a*c is equal to the square of the quantity (2*a*x + b). This identity links the solution of the quadratic to the structure of the discriminant. It works for any commutative ring where natural numbers can be embedded.

label: discrim_le_zero
slogan: If a quadratic expression is always greater than or equal to zero for all values of x, then its discriminant must be less than or equal to zero, meaning the equation has at most one real root or none.

label: dist_add_dist_eq_iff
slogan: In a strictly convex space, the sum of the distances from point a to b and from b to c equals the distance from a to c if and only if point b lies on the line segment between a and c.

label: dist_comm
slogan: In a pseudo metric space, the distance between any two points x and y is always equal to the distance between y and x, ensuring symmetry. This holds even if distinct points have zero distance, which is allowed in pseudo metric spaces.

label: dist_le_range_sum_dist
slogan: The distance from f(0) to f(n) in a pseudometric space is less than or equal to the sum of the distances between consecutive points f(i) and f(i+1) for i from 0 to n-1. This sum is taken over the finite set of indices from 0 to n-1. The inequality holds for any sequence of points indexed by natural numbers.

label: dist_nonneg
slogan: The distance between any two points in a pseudometric space is always at least zero. This means distances cannot be negative, as defined by the properties of pseudometric spaces and the ordering of real numbers.

label: dist_pi_def
slogan: The distance between two points in a product of finitely many pseudometric spaces is defined as the largest distance between their coordinates, taken across all index positions. This maximum distance is computed using non-negative real numbers and is well-defined because the index set is finite. The result is converted to a real number when needed.

label: dist_pos
slogan: The distance between two points is greater than zero if and only if the points are different; the distance is zero when the points are the same. This is based on the definition of a metric space and properties of real numbers.

label: dist_self
slogan: In a pseudometric space, the distance from any point to itself is always zero. This means that for any point x, dist(x, x) = 0. The distance function returns real numbers, and zero is a valid real number.

label: dist_triangle
slogan: In a pseudometric space, the distance between any two points x and z is at most the sum of the distances from x to y and from y to z, using ordinary real number addition and comparison.

label: domain_mvt
slogan: If a function is differentiable on a convex set containing two points x and y, then there is some point z on the line segment between x and y where the derivative of the function at z, when applied to the direction (y - x), equals the total change in the function value from x to y.

label: dotProduct
slogan: The dotProduct function takes two vectors (functions from a finite type to a type with multiplication and addition) and returns the sum of the products of their corresponding elements. It works by multiplying the values at each index and adding up the results over all indices in the finite type. The operation requires that the elements can be multiplied together and that their type supports addition with a zero element.

label: dot_self_cross
slogan: The dot product of a vector v with the cross product of v and another vector w is always zero, meaning the cross product is perpendicular to v. This holds for vectors in 3-dimensional space over any commutative ring.

label: doublyStochastic
slogan: A doubly stochastic matrix is a square matrix where all entries are nonnegative and each row and column sums to 1, meaning multiplying it on the left or right by a vector of all 1s results in a vector of all 1s.

label: doublyStochastic_eq_convexHull_permMatrix
slogan: The set of doubly stochastic matrices—square matrices with nonnegative entries where each row and column adds up to 1—is exactly the set of all weighted averages of permutation matrices, where each permutation matrix has exactly one 1 in each row and column and zeros elsewhere.

label: dualTensorHomEquiv
slogan: There is a one-to-one correspondence between linear maps from the tensor product of the dual of a finite-dimensional free module M and another module N, and bilinear maps from M and N into N. This means every linear transformation on the tensor space can be uniquely matched with a bilinear operation combining elements of M and N in a way that respects linearity in both arguments. The result works over any commutative semiring and depends on M having a finite basis.

label: dvd_add
slogan: If a number divides two other numbers, then it also divides their sum. For example, if a divides both b and c, then a divides b + c. This holds in algebraic structures where addition and multiplication are defined and multiplication distributes over addition from the left.

label: dvd_def
slogan: A value x divides y if there exists some z such that y equals x times z. This means divisibility is defined in terms of multiplication within a structure where multiplication is associative. The relation holds in any semigroup, requiring only that the operation * is closed and associative.

label: dvd_refl
slogan: In a monoid, every element divides itself because multiplying it by the identity element gives the element back. This means for any element a, there is some element b such that a times b equals a, specifically b = 1. The divisibility relation is supported in any commutative monoid, and the property follows from the fact that multiplying by one does not change the element.

label: dvd_trans
slogan: If a divides b and b divides c, then a divides c, provided the elements are in a semigroup where multiplication is associative. This property relies on the fact that (a * b) * c = a * (b * c). Divisibility here means one element can be multiplied by another to get a third.

label: eVariationOn
slogan: The eVariationOn function measures the total extended distance a function f travels over a subset s of a linearly ordered set, by taking the supremum of the sum of distances between consecutive values of f along all finite increasing sequences in s. This variation is assigned an extended non-negative real value (including infinity), using the edist metric in the target space. It captures how much f oscillates or changes over s, with larger values indicating greater variation.

label: eVariationOn.comp_eq_of_monotoneOn
slogan: The total variation of a function f composed with another function φ over a set t is the same as the total variation of f over the image of t under φ, provided φ is monotone on t. This means that reparameterizing the input of f by a monotone function does not change the accumulated distance f travels. The result holds for functions into a space with an extended metric.

label: eigenvalue_mem_ball
slogan: Every eigenvalue of a square matrix is contained in at least one Gershgorin disc, where each disc is centered at a diagonal entry and has a radius equal to the sum of the absolute values of the other entries in that row.

label: eisensteinSeries
slogan: eisensteinSeries computes a complex-valued function defined on the upper half-plane, built by summing terms involving integer pairs that satisfy certain modular conditions, where the weight k is an integer, and the level N and congruence condition a specify which pairs contribute to the sum. The function uses modular arithmetic via ZMod N and indexed integers (Fin 2 → ℤ) to restrict summation to specific residue classes. Each term in the sum is formed using powers of linear combinations of integers and the imaginary part of the input complex number.

label: em
slogan: For any statement p, either p is true or p is false, with no third option. This means every statement must be either true or not true. The principle is known as the law of excluded middle.

label: eq_affineCombination_of_mem_affineSpan
slogan: If a point lies in the affine span of a set of points, then that point can be written as a weighted sum of finitely many points from the set, where the weights add up to one.

label: eq_equivalence
slogan: Equality is a relation that is reflexive, symmetric, and transitive, meaning everything is equal to itself, equal terms can be swapped, and equalities can be chained through a common term.

label: eq_of_derivWithin_eq
slogan: If two functions have the same derivative at every point in the interval from a to b, including a but not necessarily b, and they are equal at the point a, then they are equal at every point from a to b, including b.

label: euler_four_squares
slogan: Euler's four-square identity states that the product of two sums of four squares is itself a sum of four squares, and this holds in any commutative ring. Specifically, given elements a, b, c, d, x, y, z, w in a commutative ring, the square of four particular combinations of these elements adds up to the product of the sum of their squares. This identity shows how sums of four squares are closed under multiplication.

label: even_iff_two_dvd
slogan: A number in a semiring is even if and only if it can be divided by 2 with no remainder. This means being even is equivalent to 2 dividing the number, using the standard divisibility relation. The result holds for any type with a semiring structure, where operations like addition and multiplication are well-behaved.

label: eventually_residual_liouville
slogan: The set of real numbers that can be approximated extremely well by rational numbers (Liouville numbers) makes up a large or "residual" set within the real numbers, meaning it is the intersection of countably many dense open sets.

label: exists_birkhoff_representation
slogan: For any finite distributive lattice, there exists a set and an injective function from the lattice into the power set of that set, such that the lattice operations are preserved. This means the structure of the lattice can be represented using subsets and set operations. The representation is built using the lattice's sup-irreducible elements.

label: exists_continuous_zero_one_of_isClosed
slogan: In a normal topological space, for any two disjoint closed sets, there is a continuous function from the space to the real numbers that is 0 on one set, 1 on the other, and takes values between 0 and 1 everywhere.

label: exists_countable_union_perfect_of_isClosed
slogan: Every closed set in a second-countable topological space can be expressed as the union of a countable set and a perfect set, where a perfect set is closed and has no isolated points.

label: exists_deriv_eq_slope
slogan: There is a point strictly between a and b where the derivative of the function f equals the average rate of change of f from a to b, if f is continuous on the closed interval [a, b] and differentiable on the open interval (a, b).

label: exists_deriv_eq_zero
slogan: If a real-valued function is continuous on a closed interval [a, b] and differentiable on the open interval (a, b), and if the function values at a and b are equal, then there is some point strictly between a and b where the derivative of the function is zero. This point is where the function reaches a local maximum or minimum. The result guarantees such a point exists but does not say where it is.

label: exists_dual_vector
slogan: For any nonzero vector in a real normed space, there is a continuous linear functional with norm 1 that maps the vector to its norm. This functional is built by extending a linear map defined on the span of the vector using the Hahn-Banach theorem.

label: exists_embedding_euclidean_of_compact
slogan: If a compact manifold has a finite covering by supports of bump functions, then it can be smoothly embedded into some finite-dimensional Euclidean space in a way that is closed and has injective derivatives at every point.

label: exists_eq_const_mul_intervalIntegral_of_nonneg
slogan: If f is continuous on the closed interval between a and b, and g is integrable and nonnegative on the open interval between a and b, then there exists some point c in that closed interval such that the integral of f times g equals f evaluated at c multiplied by the integral of g.

label: exists_extension_norm_eq
slogan: There exists a linear functional defined on the whole space that extends a given one on a subspace, matches it exactly on that subspace, and has the same norm. This holds for normed vector spaces over certain fields where the norm behaves like the real or complex numbers. The result ensures that bounded linear functionals can be extended without increasing their norm.

label: exists_extension_of_le_sublinear
slogan: There is a linear function g that agrees with a given linear function f on its domain and is everywhere bounded above by a sublinear function N, as long as f is bounded above by N on its domain. The sublinear function N scales linearly with positive scalars and satisfies the triangle inequality. Such an extension g exists on the entire space while preserving the bound g(x) <= N(x) for all x.

label: exists_finite_inj_algHom_of_fg
slogan: If A is a finitely generated algebra over a field k, then there is some number s and an injective algebra homomorphism from the polynomial ring k[X_0, ..., X_{s-1}] into A such that A is finitely generated as a module over the image of that polynomial ring.

label: exists_hasDerivAt_eq_slope
slogan: If a function is continuous on a closed interval [a, b] and differentiable on the open interval (a, b), then there is some point c between a and b where the derivative of the function equals the average rate of change of the function from a to b.

label: exists_hasDerivAt_eq_zero
slogan: If a function is continuous on a closed interval [a, b], differentiable on the open interval (a, b), and takes the same value at both endpoints a and b, then there is some point strictly between a and b where the derivative of the function is zero.

label: exists_hasDerivWithinAt_eq_of_ge_of_le
slogan: If a function is differentiable on a closed interval [a, b] with a <= b, and its derivative at a is less than or equal to some value m which is in turn less than or equal to the derivative at b, then there exists some point c between a and b where the derivative equals m. This means the derivative function takes on every value between its values at the endpoints.

label: exists_hasDerivWithinAt_eq_of_gt_of_lt
slogan: If a function is differentiable on a closed interval [a, b] and its derivative at a is less than m and at b is greater than m, then there exists some point c between a and b where the derivative equals m. This means the derivative satisfies the intermediate value property on the interval.

label: exists_hilbertBasis
slogan: In a complete inner product space over the real or complex numbers, there exists a Hilbert basis, which is a maximal orthonormal set whose linear span is dense in the space.
