slogan: In a monoid, if one element multiplies another on the left to give the identity, and a possibly different element multiplies the same element on the right to give the identity, then those two elements must be the same. This means left and right inverses are always equal when both exist. The result uses associativity and the property that multiplying by the identity does nothing.

label: legendreSym
slogan: The legendreSym function takes a prime number p and an integer a, and returns 1 if a is a perfect square modulo p, -1 if it is not, and 0 if a is divisible by p. It works by performing arithmetic in the system of integers modulo p and uses the multiplicative structure to determine whether a has a square root modulo p. The result is an integer derived from the behavior of powers in the finite field of integers mod p.

label: legendreSym.at_neg_one
slogan: For an odd prime p, -1 is a quadratic residue modulo p if and only if p mod 4 equals 1; in this case the Legendre symbol of -1 is 1, otherwise it is -1.

label: legendreSym.eq_one_iff
slogan: The Legendre symbol (a/p) equals 1 exactly when a is a nonzero quadratic residue modulo an odd prime p, meaning there exists some integer b such that b squared is congruent to a modulo p. It is 0 if a is divisible by p, and -1 if a is not a quadratic residue mod p. This result characterizes when a quadratic equation of the form x^2 ≡ a mod p has a solution.

label: legendreSym.quadratic_reciprocity
slogan: For two different odd prime numbers p and q, whether p is a square modulo q and whether q is a square modulo p are related by a simple sign rule: the product of the Legendre symbols (p/q) and (q/p) is 1 if either p or q is congruent to 1 modulo 4, and -1 if both are congruent to 3 modulo 4.

label: legendreSym.quadratic_reciprocity_one_mod_four
slogan: If p and q are odd primes and p leaves a remainder of 1 when divided by 4, then the Legendre symbol (q/p) equals (p/q), meaning whether q is a square modulo p depends on whether p is a square modulo q in the same way.

label: legendreSym.quadratic_reciprocity_three_mod_four
slogan: For two different odd prime numbers p and q, if both have a remainder of 3 when divided by 4, then the Legendre symbol (q/p) is the negative of (p/q); otherwise, they are equal. This means whether a prime is a square modulo another prime depends on their remainders modulo 4. The rule simplifies the relationship between quadratic residues modulo different primes.

label: leibniz_lie
slogan: In a structure with addition and a bracket operation, the bracket satisfies a product-like rule where applying it twice in a nested way splits into two terms: one with the brackets reordered and one with the order of operations swapped, following a specific algebraic identity involving three elements. This rule mirrors how derivatives act on products, but in an algebraic setting with non-commutative operations. The setup requires compatible bracket operations between three types and a shared addition operation on one of them.

label: lie_jacobi
slogan: In a Lie ring, for any elements x, y, and z, the sum of the brackets [x, [y, z]], [y, [z, x]], and [z, [x, y]] equals zero, reflecting a cyclic symmetry in the way the bracket operation interacts with nested elements. This identity ensures the consistency of the bracket under repeated operations. It is known as the Jacobi identity.

label: lie_skew
slogan: In a Lie ring, the bracket of two elements x and y satisfies -[y, x] = [x, y], meaning swapping the order negates the result; this, along with [x, x] = 0, reflects the skew-symmetric nature of the operation.

label: lineDeriv
slogan: The line derivative of a function f at a point x in the direction v is the rate at which f changes along the line x + t*v as t approaches 0, if that rate exists; otherwise it is zero. It describes the linear approximation f(x + t*v) ≈ f(x) + t * lineDeriv(k, f, x, v) for small t. The function maps between vector spaces over a normed field k, with appropriate algebraic and topological structure.

label: linearIndependent_iff_notMem_span
slogan: A family of vectors is linearly independent if and only if no single vector in the family is in the span of the others; that is, each vector cannot be written as a linear combination of the remaining vectors.

label: linearIndependent_monoidHom
slogan: A set of monoid homomorphisms is linearly independent if the only way a finite linear combination of them can be the zero map is when all the scalar coefficients are zero. This means no nontrivial sum of scaled homomorphisms can produce the zero homomorphism. The result holds over a commutative domain where scalar multiplication and addition are defined.

label: liouville_liouvilleNumber
slogan: For any integer m greater than or equal to 2, the number formed by summing 1 divided by m raised to the power of i factorial (for all natural numbers i) is a Liouville number, meaning it can be approximated extremely closely by rational numbers in a non-trivial way.

label: lipschitzGroup
slogan: The lipschitzGroup is the smallest subgroup of invertible elements in the Clifford algebra that includes all elements of the form ι Q m, where ι maps vectors from a module M into the Clifford algebra built from a quadratic form Q. It is closed under multiplication and inverses, and contains only those elements needed to satisfy the group properties starting from those images. This group captures algebraic elements related to reflections and rotations in the geometric structure defined by Q.

label: lipschitzWith_of_nnnorm_deriv_le
slogan: If a function is differentiable everywhere and the size of its derivative is no more than a constant C at all points, then the function is C-Lipschitz, meaning the distance between output values is at most C times the distance between input values.

label: lipschitzWith_one_norm
slogan: A function between seminormed groups is Lipschitz with constant 1 if the distance between the outputs is always less than or equal to the distance between the inputs, as measured by the norm. This means the function does not stretch distances, and the constant 1 is treated as a non-negative real number. The result depends on the standard metric structure of the real numbers and the properties of norms in additive groups.

label: littleWedderburn
slogan: Any finite division ring, where division by nonzero elements is always possible, must automatically be a field, meaning multiplication is commutative. This result states that finiteness forces such a structure to have commutative multiplication.

label: locallyConnectedSpace_iff_connectedComponentIn_open
slogan: A topological space is locally connected if and only if, for every point and every open set containing that point, the connected component of the point within that open set is itself open. This means that around each point, the connected parts of any open neighborhood can be chosen to form an open set. Local connectedness is characterized by the openness of these connected components inside open sets.

label: logDeriv_mul
slogan: The logarithmic derivative of the product of two differentiable functions at a point equals the sum of their logarithmic derivatives at that point, as long as both functions are nonzero there. This holds when the functions map into a normed algebra over a nontrivially normed field.

label: lowerCentralSeries
slogan: The lower central series of a group is a sequence of subgroups starting with the whole group, where each next subgroup is made up of all products of commutators between elements of the previous subgroup and elements of the original group. Each subgroup in the sequence is smaller than or equal to the one before it, capturing increasing levels of non-commutativity. The series helps determine how close the group is to being abelian, with abelian groups having the trivial subgroup appear early in the sequence.

label: lp.completeSpace
slogan: If each E i is a complete normed abelian group and p is at least 1, then the space of p-summable functions from α to the E i is also complete, meaning every Cauchy sequence in this function space converges to a limit within the space.

label: lp.instInnerProductSpace
slogan: The lp.instInnerProductSpace declaration states that if you have a family of inner product spaces over a real-like field, then the lp space of functions indexed by this family, with p=2, naturally forms an inner product space. This means that square-summable functions taking values in these spaces inherit a well-defined inner product, built from the pointwise inner products of the components. The norm in this space comes from the square root of the sum of squared norms, as in the standard L2 space construction.

label: lp.norm_eq_ciSup
slogan: The norm of a bounded function f in the lp space with p=infinity is equal to the least upper bound of the norms of f(i) across all indices i.

label: lp.norm_eq_tsum_rpow
slogan: The norm of a function f in an lp space is equal to the p-th root of the sum of the p-th powers of the norms of its values at each point, where p is a positive real number and the sum is taken over all indices. This holds when each value of f lies in a normed abelian group and the extended real p is converted to a real number. The infinite sum is defined as the limit of finite sums converging unconditionally.

label: lp.tsum_mul_le_mul_norm
slogan: For two functions f and g defined on the same index set, if their norms are in conjugate lp spaces (meaning the exponents p and q satisfy 1/p + 1/q = 1), then the sum of the pointwise products of their norms is finite and bounded above by the product of their lp norms. This ensures both that the infinite sum of |f(i)| * |g(i)| converges and that its value does not exceed ||f|| * ||g||.

label: lt_asymm
slogan: In a preorder, if a is less than b, then b cannot be less than a. This means the less-than relation is asymmetric.

label: lt_irrefl
slogan: In a preorder, no element can be less than itself, meaning the less-than relation is irreflexive. This means that for any element a, it is not true that a < a. While every element is less than or equal to itself, it cannot be strictly less than itself.

label: lt_trichotomy
slogan: For any two elements a and b in a linearly ordered set, one and only one of the following must be true: a is less than b, a equals b, or b is less than a. This means every pair of elements can be compared, and their relationship is strictly one of these three possibilities.

label: lucas_lehmer_sufficiency
slogan: If p is a natural number greater than 1 and the Lucas-Lehmer test for p returns true, then the Mersenne number 2^p - 1 is prime.

label: lucas_primality
slogan: If a number p satisfies that a^(p-1) ≡ 1 mod p, and for every prime factor q of p-1, a^((p-1)/q) is not congruent to 1 mod p, then p is prime. This works because the number a has multiplicative order p-1 modulo p, which can only happen if p is prime.

label: map_compl'
slogan: In a Boolean algebra, if a function preserves the lattice operations and the top and bottom elements, then applying the function to the complement of an element is the same as taking the complement of the function's result. This means the function respects complementation.

label: matPolyEquiv
slogan: There is a one-to-one correspondence between matrices with polynomial entries and polynomials with matrix coefficients, where both forms support the same algebraic operations like addition, multiplication, and scalar multiplication. This correspondence is reversible and preserves the full algebra structure over a commutative semiring. Converting between these two representations maintains all arithmetic properties.

label: max_min_distrib_left
slogan: In a totally ordered set, taking the maximum of an element with the minimum of two others gives the same result as taking the minimum of the maximum of the element with each of the two others. This means max and min distribute over each other when the elements can all be compared.

label: measurable_of_tendsto_metrizable
slogan: If a sequence of measurable functions from a measurable space into a topological space converges pointwise to a limit function, and the topology of the target space can be defined by a pseudometric, then the limit function is also measurable. This means that the preimage of any Borel set under the limit function is measurable in the domain. The result uses the natural numbers' order structure and filter-based convergence to establish measurability.

label: measure_zero_of_dimH_lt
slogan: If a measure is absolutely continuous with respect to d-dimensional Hausdorff measure, and a set has Hausdorff dimension less than d, then the measure of that set is zero.

label: mellin
slogan: The mellin function computes the Mellin transform of a function f that maps positive real numbers to a complex normed space, by integrating f(t) multiplied by t^(s-1) over the interval (0, infinity) with respect to the Lebesgue measure, where s is a complex number. This integral is defined using standard measure theory and restricts the domain to positive reals via set Ioi. The result is an element of the same space as the codomain of f.

label: mellinInv
slogan: The mellinInv function computes the inverse Mellin transform of a complex-valued function by integrating f(s) multiplied by x^s along the vertical line Re(s) = σ in the complex plane, using the Lebesgue integral with respect to the real part of s. The result is scaled by 1/(2 * pi), where pi is the usual mathematical constant, and involves the imaginary unit i to form the complex exponential. It operates on functions taking complex inputs and returning values in a normed space over the complex numbers, relying on standard measure and normed space structures.

label: mellin_inversion
slogan: The inverse Mellin transform of the Mellin transform of a function f at a point x > 0 gives back the original function value f(x), provided certain conditions on convergence, integrability, and continuity are met.

label: mem_closure_iff_nhds
slogan: A point is in the closure of a set if and only if every neighborhood of the point has a nonempty intersection with the set. This means the point is "close" to the set in the sense that no open set around it can completely avoid the set.

label: meromorphicOrderAt
slogan: The order of a meromorphic function f at a point z0 is an integer or infinity, representing the exponent n such that f(z) = (z - z0)^n times a nonzero analytic function near z0; it is infinity if f is zero near z0, and 0 if f is not meromorphic at z0.

label: meromorphicOrderAt_eq_int_iff
slogan: The order of a meromorphic function f at a point z0 is equal to an integer n if and only if near z0, the function f(z) can be written as (z - z0)^n times a function g(z), where g is analytic and nonzero at z0.

label: mersenne
slogan: The mersenne function takes a natural number p and returns the value of 2 raised to the power p, minus 1. This result is a Mersenne number.

label: mfderiv
slogan: The mfderiv of a function between two manifolds at a point is the derivative of the function in local coordinates, mapping tangent vectors at the input point to tangent vectors at the output point. It uses coordinate charts to convert the function into one between normed spaces, applies the standard derivative, and then translates the result back to the tangent spaces of the manifolds. If the function isn't differentiable at the point, the derivative is defined to be zero.

label: mfderiv_comp
slogan: The derivative of the composition of two functions between manifolds is the composition of their derivatives, so the linear map for the combined function is obtained by applying the derivative of the outer function after the derivative of the inner function. This composite derivative is continuous and respects the smooth structure of the manifolds. If either function is not differentiable at the point, the derivative of the composition is zero.

label: minpoly
slogan: The minpoly function gives the smallest degree monic polynomial (with coefficients in a base ring A) that evaluates to zero when a given element x from an extension ring B is plugged in, provided x is integral over A. It uses the algebraic map from A to B to embed coefficients and relies on the well-foundedness of polynomial degrees to ensure minimality. This polynomial is unique and generates all other polynomials that vanish at x.

label: minpoly.irreducible
slogan: The minimal polynomial of an element that is integral over a commutative ring is irreducible, meaning it cannot be written as a product of two non-constant polynomials unless one of them is a unit. This holds when the base ring is a domain, and the polynomial is monic and non-zero. Irreducibility follows from the minimality of the polynomial and the algebraic properties of polynomial evaluation.

label: mk_eq_mk_of_basis
slogan: If two modules over a semiring have bases that are in bijection, then the cardinalities of these bases are equal after adjusting for universe levels. This means that the size of a basis is well-defined for modules satisfying the invariant basis number property. The result ensures that no module can have two finite bases of different sizes.

label: mt
slogan: If a implies b, and b is false, then a must also be false.

label: mul_add
slogan: Multiplying a value by a sum gives the same result as multiplying the value by each term in the sum separately and then adding the results. This property holds for any type that supports addition, multiplication, and left distributivity. Specifically, for elements a, b, and c, the equation a * (b + c) = a * b + a * c is always true.

label: mul_assoc
slogan: In a semigroup, multiplying three elements a, b, and c gives the same result whether you first multiply a and b or b and c, so (a * b) * c equals a * (b * c).

label: mul_comm
slogan: For any type with a commutative magma structure, the order of multiplication does not matter: multiplying a and b gives the same result as multiplying b and a. This means a * b is always equal to b * a for all elements a and b in the type.

label: mul_eq_zero
slogan: In a system with multiplication and zero where multiplying nonzero elements never gives zero, the product of two elements is zero exactly when at least one of them is zero. This means a * b = 0 if and only if a = 0 or b = 0.

label: mul_inv_cancel
slogan: In a group, multiplying any element by its inverse (in any order) results in the identity element; specifically, a times a inverse equals one.

label: mul_left_injective
slogan: If multiplying two elements by the same nonzero element on the left gives the same result, then the two elements must be equal, provided the type supports multiplication and right cancellation. This means that left multiplication by a nonzero element is injective.

label: mul_lt_mul_left_of_neg
slogan: If you multiply two numbers by the same negative value on the left and the result for the first number is smaller than the result for the second, then the first number must have been larger than the second; this is because multiplying by a negative number on the left reverses the order of inequalities in certain algebraic structures.

label: mul_neg_of_pos_of_neg
slogan: If a positive number multiplies a negative number, the result is negative, provided multiplication by positive elements preserves strict order and zero acts as an absorbing element.

label: mul_self_eq_mul_self_iff
slogan: In a ring where multiplication is commutative and there are no zero divisors, the square of two elements are equal if and only if the elements are the same or one is the negative of the other.

label: mul_self_eq_zero
slogan: In a system with multiplication and zero where no two nonzero things multiply to zero, a number times itself equals zero if and only if the number is zero.

label: neg_neg
slogan: For any element a in a type where negation is defined, applying negation twice gives back a; that is, -(-a) = a.

label: neg_one_mul
slogan: Multiplying negative one by any element gives the same result as negating that element, so -1 * x equals -x for all x. This holds in algebraic structures that have a multiplicative identity and a negation operation that distributes over multiplication.

label: neg_one_pow_eq_pow_mod_two
slogan: For any natural number n, (-1) raised to the power n equals (-1) raised to the power (n mod 2), so the result is 1 if n is even and -1 if n is odd.

label: neg_sub
slogan: The negation of the difference between two elements a and b is the same as the difference of b and a; in other words, -(a - b) equals b - a. This holds in algebraic structures where subtraction is defined as adding the negative and where negation undoes itself when applied twice.

label: nhds
slogan: The nhds function gives the neighborhood filter of a point in a topological space by taking the infimum of all principal filters generated by open sets that contain the point. This means it collects all sets that include an open set around the point, representing the notion of "being near" that point. It uses the InfSet instance for filters to combine these principal filters into a single filter.

label: nhdsWithin
slogan: nhdsWithin x s represents the collection of sets that contain a neighborhood of the point x intersected with the set s, meaning it includes all sets that eventually include points near x and also within s. It is formed by taking the infimum (overlap) of the neighborhood filter of x and the principal filter of s. This captures the idea of "closeness" to x while staying inside the subset s.

label: nhds_hasBasis_absConvex
slogan: In a locally convex vector space over a normed field, every neighborhood of zero contains a smaller neighborhood that is both convex and balanced (invariant under small scalar multiples and convex combinations), and these smaller sets form a basis for the neighborhood filter at zero. Such sets are called absolutely convex, and they reflect how the topology aligns with the vector space operations. This means the local structure near zero can be described entirely using sets that preserve both convexity and balance.

label: nilpotent_iff_finite_ascending_central_series
slogan: A group is nilpotent if and only if there is a finite sequence of subgroups starting from the trivial subgroup, each normal in the next, with consecutive quotients being central, such that the last subgroup in the sequence is the entire group. This happens exactly when the upper central series reaches the whole group after finitely many steps. The condition means the group can be built up from the trivial subgroup through a finite number of central extensions.

label: nilradical
slogan: The nilradical of a commutative semiring is the set of all elements that become zero when raised to some positive power. It forms an ideal and consists exactly of the nilpotent elements of the semiring. This ideal is also the radical of the zero ideal.

label: norm_add_sq_eq_norm_sq_add_norm_sq_of_inner_eq_zero
slogan: If two vectors have an inner product of zero (they are perpendicular), then the squared norm of their sum equals the sum of their squared norms. This is the vector form of the Pythagorean theorem, valid in any inner product space.

label: norm_add_sq_real
slogan: The square of the length of the sum of two vectors in a real inner product space equals the sum of the squares of their lengths plus twice their dot product.

label: norm_eq_sqrt_re_inner
slogan: The length of a vector in an inner product space is equal to the square root of the real part of the inner product of the vector with itself. This means the norm, or size, of a vector can be computed using the inner product. Since the inner product of a vector with itself is always non-negative, taking its square root gives a well-defined real number.

label: norm_eq_sqrt_real_inner
slogan: The length of a vector in a real inner product space is equal to the square root of the inner product of the vector with itself, using the standard non-negative real square root. This links the geometric idea of vector length to the algebraic operation of the inner product. The space must support both a norm and an inner product that are compatible with real number arithmetic.

label: norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_deriv_le_segment
slogan: If a function is differentiable on a closed interval from a to b, and the size of its derivative is no more than a constant C at every point in the interval, then the distance between the function's values at any point x in the interval and at a is at most C times the length of the interval from a to x.

label: norm_inner_eq_norm_iff
slogan: In an inner product space, the absolute value of the inner product of two nonzero vectors equals the product of their norms if and only if one vector is a nonzero scalar multiple of the other. This means the vectors point in exactly the same or opposite directions. The equality holds precisely when the vectors are parallel.

label: norm_inner_le_norm
slogan: The absolute value of the inner product of two vectors is always less than or equal to the product of their norms. This means that how "aligned" two vectors are is limited by their lengths. It's a key inequality in inner product spaces, often based on the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality.

label: norm_mul
slogan: In a normed ring, the norm of the product of two elements is always less than or equal to the product of their norms. This means that multiplying two elements does not increase their combined size beyond the product of their individual sizes. The norm respects multiplication in this way by design.

label: norm_pow
slogan: For any element in a normed ring where the norm of 1 is 1 and the norm of a product is at most the product of the norms, the norm of the element raised to a natural power equals the norm of the element raised to that same power. This means taking powers and taking norms commute under these conditions.

label: norm_smul_inv_norm
slogan: When you scale a nonzero vector by the inverse of its norm, the resulting vector has norm 1. This means dividing a vector by its own length normalizes it to unit length. The property holds in normed vector spaces over real-like fields.

label: norm_sub_norm_le
slogan: The absolute value of the difference between the sizes of two elements is no larger than the size of their difference. This holds in any group with a norm that behaves like a distance measure.

label: not_and
slogan: The statement not_and says that the negation of a and b being true is equivalent to saying that if a is true then b must be false. In other words, if it's not the case that both a and b hold, then whenever a holds, b cannot hold. This expresses a logical relationship between negation and implication.

label: not_and_or
slogan: The statement "not (a and b)" is the same as saying "not a or not b". This means if it is not true that both a and b are true, then at least one of them must be false.

label: not_and_self
slogan: It is not possible for a proposition and its negation to both be true at the same time. This means that assuming both a statement and its opposite leads to a contradiction. In simpler terms, something cannot be both true and false simultaneously.

label: not_imp_not
slogan: If a is something that must be either true or false, then "if a is false, then b is false" means the same thing as "if b is true, then a is true".

label: not_or
slogan: The statement says that if it is not true that either p or q holds, then neither p nor q individually holds. This is equivalent to saying the negation of a disjunction is the conjunction of the negations. In plain terms, denying "p or q" means both p must be false and q must be false.

label: not_small_cardinal
slogan: There is no largest cardinal number, because for any cardinal, a larger one can always be found. This means the collection of all sets is too big to be a set itself.

label: not_small_ordinal
slogan: There is no set that can contain every ordinal number because the collection of all ordinals is too large to be a set. This means the ordinals do not form a "small" type, as no one-to-one mapping from all ordinals into any set is possible.

label: not_summable_one_div_on_primes
slogan: The sum of the reciprocals of all prime numbers does not converge to a finite value; instead, it grows without bound. In other words, adding 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/5 + 1/7 + 1/11 + ... continues to increase indefinitely.

label: numDerangements
slogan: numDerangements is a function that takes a natural number n and returns the number of derangements, which are permutations of an n-element set where no element appears in its original position.

label: numDerangements_tendsto_inv_e
slogan: As n gets very large, the fraction of permutations of n elements in which no element stays in its original position approaches 1 divided by e, where e is the base of the natural logarithm.

label: num_dvd_of_is_root
slogan: If a fraction in lowest terms is a root of a polynomial with integer coefficients, then the numerator of that fraction divides the constant term of the polynomial.

label: odd_iff_exists_bit1
slogan: A number is odd if and only if it can be written in the form 2 times some other number plus 1. This means oddness is the same as having a remainder of 1 when divided by 2, as long as the number system supports basic arithmetic and 2 is not zero.

label: omegaLimit
slogan: The omega-limit of a set s under a function phi with respect to a filter f is the intersection of the closures of all images of s under phi(u) for u in f. It captures the long-term behavior of the set s as it evolves under phi according to the limiting structure defined by f. This set consists of all points in the topological space that are limits of sequences (or nets) generated by applying phi to elements of s along the filter f.

label: onePointEquivSphereOfFinrankEq
slogan: The one-point compactification of a finite-dimensional real vector space is homeomorphic to a sphere when the dimension of the space plus one equals the number of elements in a given finite type. This homeomorphism maps the extended space, with a point at infinity, to a sphere of radius 1 centered at the origin. The result connects the topological structure of vector spaces with that of spheres in a precise dimension.

label: one_add_mul_le_pow
slogan: If a number x is at least -2, then 1 plus x times any natural number n is less than or equal to (1 plus x) raised to the power n, in any ring with a strict linear order. This uses standard addition, multiplication, and exponentiation, where natural numbers are converted into the ring via canonical casting. The inequality holds due to properties of ordered rings and natural number exponents.

label: or_and_left
slogan: a or (b and c) is equivalent to (a or b) and (a or c). This means that if a is true or both b and c are true, then either a is true or b is true, and separately, either a is true or c is true, and vice versa.

label: orderOf
slogan: The order of an element in a monoid is the smallest positive number n such that multiplying the element by itself n times gives the identity element; if no such number exists, the order is undefined and treated as infinite. It is calculated by finding the minimal period of the function that repeatedly multiplies the element.

label: orderOf_dvd_card
slogan: In a finite group, the smallest positive number of times you need to multiply an element by itself to get the identity divides the total number of elements in the group. This number, called the order of the element, is always a factor of the group's size. The result comes from looking at the cyclic subgroup generated by the element and using the fact that its size equals the element's order.

label: orderOf_dvd_natCard
slogan: In a finite group, the number of times you must multiply an element by itself to reach the identity always divides the total number of elements in the group. This means the order of any element is a factor of the group's size. The result relies on the group being finite and the order being the smallest positive power that gives the identity.

label: orderOf_eq_card_of_zpowers_eq_top
slogan: If an element's integer powers generate the entire group, then the order of that element (the smallest positive exponent giving the identity) equals the total number of elements in the group. This means the cyclic subgroup formed by the element's powers has the same size as the whole group.

label: ordinaryHypergeometric
slogan: The ordinary hypergeometric function 2F1(a,b,c,x) is defined as the sum of a specific formal multilinear series constructed from parameters a, b, c in a field 𝕂 and evaluated at x in a topological ring 𝔸, where the series sum uses the topology of 𝔸. The function returns zero when the series does not converge. This definition relies on algebraic and topological structures to ensure the series and its sum are well-defined.

label: orthonormal_iff_ite
slogan: A set of vectors is orthonormal if and only if the inner product of any two vectors in the set is 1 when they are the same and 0 when they are different, using a conditional (if-else) expression to distinguish these cases based on whether their indices are equal, and this equivalence holds in inner product spaces where equality of indices is decidable.

label: oscillation
slogan: The oscillation of a function at a point is the smallest value that bounds how far apart the function's outputs can be near that point, using an extended metric that allows infinity. It is calculated by looking at the diameters of the function's image over smaller and smaller neighborhoods around the point and taking the greatest lower bound of those diameters. A smaller oscillation means the function behaves more steadily near the point, approaching continuity.

label: padicNorm
slogan: The padicNorm function takes a prime number p and a rational number q, and returns a rational number equal to p raised to the negative of the p-adic valuation of q. This valuation is the exponent of p in the prime factorization of q, accounting for numerator and denominator. The result measures the size of q in the p-adic sense, where numbers divisible by higher powers of p have smaller p-adic norm.

label: padicNormE
slogan: The padicNormE function assigns a size to a rational number based on a prime p, by measuring how many times p divides the number and returning p raised to the negative of that count. Numbers more divisible by p have smaller values under this norm, reflecting their "smallness" in the p-adic sense. This norm is used to build the p-adic numbers by completing the rationals with respect to this notion of distance.

label: padicValNat
slogan: padicValNat p n is the largest natural number k such that the prime p raised to the power k divides the natural number n. It finds this value by computing how many times p can repeatedly divide n evenly. If p does not divide n at all, the result is zero.

label: padicValNat.mul
slogan: For a prime number p and nonzero natural numbers a and b, the highest power of p that divides the product a * b is the sum of the highest powers of p that divide a and b individually. This means the p-adic valuation of a * b equals the sum of the p-adic valuations of a and b. The result depends on p being prime and a, b both being nonzero.

label: padicValRat
slogan: padicValRat takes a prime number p and a rational number q, and returns the exponent of p in the prime factorization of q, calculated as the difference between the exponents of p in the numerator and denominator of q, using the p-adic valuation for integers. It computes this by applying padicValInt to the numerator and denominator of the fraction. The result is an integer that represents how many times p divides the rational number, counting multiplicity and sign.

label: parallelepiped
slogan: A parallelepiped is the set of all points you can get by adding up multiples of basis vectors, where each multiple is a number between 0 and 1. It's like a skewed box in n-dimensional space, built from a given set of vectors. The shape includes all combinations of the form sum of (coefficient * vector), with every coefficient in the range [0,1].

label: parallelogram_law
slogan: In an inner product space, the sum of the squares of the lengths of the diagonals of a parallelogram formed by two vectors equals twice the sum of the squares of the lengths of the two adjacent sides. This identity is expressed using the inner product to compute squared lengths and holds for any pair of vectors. It reflects a fundamental relationship between vector addition and the geometry of norms.

label: parallelogram_law_with_norm
slogan: In an inner product space, for any two vectors x and y, the sum of the squares of the norms of x+y and x-y equals twice the sum of the squares of the norms of x and y. This means ||x + y||^2 + ||x - y||^2 = 2*(||x||^2 + ||y||^2), where the norm comes from the inner product.

label: partialFunEquivPointed
slogan: The declaration defines an equivalence between the category of partial functions and the category of pointed types, making the correspondence between partial functions and pointed objects into a precise, structure-preserving mapping. It extends the idea that a partial function can be represented by a total function into an option type with a base point, now treated as a functorial relationship. This means converting between partial functions and pointed types works consistently with composition and identity.

label: pathComponent
slogan: The pathComponent of a point x in a topological space is the set of all points that can be connected to x by a continuous path, meaning there is a continuous function from [0,1] to the space that starts at x and ends at the other point. This set groups together all points that are path-connected to x. It is defined using the property that two points are joined if such a path exists between them.

label: pathConnectedSpace_iff_connectedSpace
slogan: A topological space is path-connected if and only if it is connected and every point has arbitrarily small path-connected neighborhoods. This means the space consists of a single piece and locally resembles a path-connected space around each point. The equivalence shows that global path connectivity follows from connectedness combined with local path connectivity.

label: pinGroup
slogan: The pin group of a quadratic form Q is the set of elements that are both in the Lipschitz group and in the unitary group of the Clifford algebra associated with Q, forming a submonoid of that algebra. It consists of invertible elements preserving the structure defined by Q under multiplication. This group is constructed as the intersection of these two larger groups within the Clifford algebra.

label: poissonKernel
slogan: The poissonKernel function takes three complex numbers c, w, and z, and returns a real number that represents the value of the Poisson kernel at those points. It is used in complex analysis to compute harmonic functions inside a disk from their boundary values. The kernel is defined using the norm and subtraction operations on complex numbers, along with division on real numbers.

label: polynomialFunctions_closure_eq_top
slogan: Polynomial functions on a closed interval [a, b] in the real numbers are dense in the space of all continuous real-valued functions on that interval, meaning any continuous function can be uniformly approximated by polynomials.

label: pow_eq_pow_iff_modEq
slogan: Two natural number exponents give the same power of an element in a left-cancellative monoid if and only if the exponents differ by a multiple of the element's order. This means the powers of the element repeat in cycles whose length is determined by the order. The equality of powers depends only on whether the exponents are congruent modulo the order.

label: primorial
slogan: The primorial of a natural number n is the product of all prime numbers less than or equal to n. For example, the primorial of 5 is 2 * 3 * 5 = 30. This function is defined for natural numbers and returns a natural number.

label: projectivizationSetoid
slogan: The projectivizationSetoid defines an equivalence relation on the nonzero elements of a vector space V over a division ring K, where two elements are considered equivalent if one is a scalar multiple of the other by a unit. This relation captures the idea that vectors that are scaled versions of each other represent the same point in projective space. The quotient of this relation forms the projectivization of V.

label: quadraticChar_sum_zero
slogan: The sum of the values of the quadratic character over all elements of a finite field equals zero, as long as the field's characteristic is not 2. The quadratic character assigns 1 to nonzero squares, -1 to non-squares, and 0 to zero, and its sum over the entire field cancels out due to symmetry. This result relies on the fact that the character is a nontrivial multiplicative function and the field has a multiplicative group structure.

label: quadratic_eq_zero_iff
slogan: A quadratic equation a*x^2 + b*x + c = 0 has solutions if and only if the discriminant b^2 - 4*a*c is a perfect square, and when it is, the solutions are x = (-b + s)/(2*a) or x = (-b - s)/(2*a), where s is a square root of the discriminant and a is not zero.

label: quadratic_eq_zero_iff_discrim_eq_sq
slogan: A quadratic equation a*x^2 + b*x + c = 0 with coefficients in a commutative ring (like integers) has a solution x if and only if its discriminant (b^2 - 4*a*c) is equal to the square of (2*a*x + b). This means the equation has a root precisely when the discriminant matches the square of a specific linear expression involving the root. The result applies in any setting where there are no zero divisors and 2 is not zero.

label: quotient_norm_mk_eq
slogan: The norm of the equivalence class of an element in a quotient of a normed additive group is equal to the greatest lower bound of the norms of the differences between that element and any element in the subgroup. This means the size of a coset representative is the smallest distance from the original point to any point in the coset. The quotient norm is thus defined by minimizing the distance over all possible representatives.

label: re_inner_eq_norm_add_mul_self_sub_norm_sub_mul_self_div_four
slogan: The inner product of two vectors in a real inner product space can be calculated as one fourth of the difference between the squared norm of their sum and the squared norm of their difference. This means you can find the inner product using only vector addition, subtraction, and norm measurements.

label: realPart_add_I_smul_imaginaryPart
slogan: Every complex number equals its real part plus the imaginary unit i times its imaginary part. This means any complex number can be broken down into its real and imaginary components using scalar multiplication and addition. The imaginary unit i is defined such that i times i equals -1.

label: real_inner_comm
slogan: In a real inner product space, the inner product of two vectors is symmetric, meaning that swapping the order of the vectors does not change the result. This is because the inner product of y and x equals the inner product of x and y for any vectors x and y. The property holds due to the conjugate symmetry of inner products and the fact that real numbers are unchanged under conjugation.

label: real_inner_le_norm
slogan: For any two vectors in a real inner product space, the absolute value of their inner product is at most the product of their lengths. This means the inner product cannot exceed the product of the norms of the vectors. The result is a fundamental inequality in geometry and analysis.

label: real_inner_self_eq_norm_mul_norm
slogan: In a real inner product space, the inner product of a vector with itself is equal to the square of its norm. This means that measuring the vector's size using the inner product gives the same result as squaring its length. The equation inner x x = ||x|| * ||x|| holds for all vectors x in such a space.

label: resolvent
slogan: The resolvent function takes an element a from an algebra over a commutative semiring and a scalar r, then returns the inverse of (1 - r*a) when that element is invertible, using the algebra's ring structure and the embedding of scalars via algebraMap. It is defined only when (1 - r*a) is a unit in the algebra. The result is an element of the same algebra.

label: resolventSet
slogan: The resolvent set of an element a in an algebra over a commutative semiring R is the set of all scalars r in R such that the element (r embedded into the algebra) minus a has a two-sided inverse in the algebra. In other words, a scalar r is in the resolvent set if shifting a by r results in an invertible element. This set identifies the scalars for which the element behaves in a nonsingular or regular way within the algebra.

label: riemannZeta
slogan: The riemannZeta function takes a complex number s and returns a complex number, representing the Riemann zeta function ζ(s). It is defined for complex inputs and plays a central role in number theory, particularly in the study of prime numbers.

label: riemannZeta_eulerProduct
slogan: For complex numbers s where the real part of s is greater than 1, the infinite product over all primes p of the terms (1 - p^(-s))^(-1) converges to the value of the Riemann zeta function at s, meaning that as you include more primes in the product, the result gets arbitrarily close to zeta(s).

label: riemannZeta_eulerProduct_tprod
slogan: For complex numbers s where the real part is greater than 1, the infinite product over all prime numbers p of the terms (1 - p^(-s))^(-1) equals the value of the Riemann zeta function at s, with the product defined as a topological infinite product using finite approximations.

label: riemannZeta_ne_zero_of_one_le_re
slogan: The Riemann zeta function is never zero when the real part of the input is at least 1. Although the function has a pole at s = 1, the value used in this context is defined and not zero. This result applies to the entire region where the real part of s is greater than or equal to 1.

label: riemannZeta_neg_nat_eq_bernoulli
slogan: For any natural number k, the Riemann zeta function at -k equals (-1) raised to the power k, multiplied by the (k+1)-th Bernoulli number, and divided by (k+1). The Bernoulli number is treated as a rational number, and the result is expressed as a complex number through standard casting. This gives an exact formula for zeta at negative integers using Bernoulli numbers.

label: riemannZeta_neg_two_mul_nat_add_one
slogan: The Riemann zeta function equals zero at every negative even integer, specifically at values like -2, -4, -6, and so on, which are written as -2*(n+1) for natural numbers n.

label: riemannZeta_one_sub
slogan: If s is not a nonpositive integer and not equal to 1, then the Riemann zeta function at 1 - s equals 2 times (2 pi) to the power of -s, times the gamma function of s, times the cosine of (pi times s divided by 2), times the zeta function at s.

label: riemannZeta_residue_one
slogan: As the complex number s approaches 1, the product of (s - 1) and the Riemann zeta function ζ(s) approaches 1, meaning ζ(s) has a simple pole at s = 1 with residue 1.

label: riemannZeta_two
slogan: The sum of the reciprocals of the squares of the positive integers equals pi squared divided by six. This value is the result of evaluating the Riemann zeta function at 2. Pi is understood here as the real number approximately 3.14159.

label: riemannZeta_two_mul_nat
slogan: For any positive natural number k, the value of the Riemann zeta function at 2*k is equal to (-1) raised to the power (k+1), multiplied by 2 raised to (2*k - 1), multiplied by pi raised to (2*k), multiplied by the (2*k)-th Bernoulli number, and divided by the factorial of (2*k).

label: riemannZeta_zero
slogan: The Riemann zeta function evaluated at 0 equals -1/2.

label: riemannianMetricVectorSpace
slogan: The standard Riemannian metric on a real inner product space is defined by using the given inner product on each tangent space of the vector space, resulting in a smoothly varying metric that assigns lengths and angles in a way consistent with the space's linear structure.

label: riesz_lemma
slogan: In a normed vector space, for any proper closed subspace and any number r less than 1, there is a unit vector that is at least r times its norm away from every vector in the subspace. This means you can always find a vector of length 1 that is almost completely outside the subspace, in terms of distance. The result depends on the structure of norms, subspaces, and metric properties.

label: riesz_lemma_of_norm_lt
slogan: In a normed vector space, if there is a proper closed subspace, then for any real number R greater than the norm of some fixed element c with norm greater than 1, there exists a vector x0 with norm at most R such that the distance from x0 to every point in the subspace is at least 1.

label: ringKrullDim
slogan: ringKrullDim is a function that takes a commutative semiring and returns the length of the longest strictly increasing chain of prime ideals, measured as a natural number or infinity, with the result being a value in the extended natural numbers that includes infinity and a bottom element. This length is determined by ordering prime ideals by inclusion and finding the supremum of chain lengths in this order. The output type allows for finite lengths, infinity, and a minimal bottom value.

label: ringKrullDim_nonneg_of_nontrivial
slogan: For any commutative semiring with at least two elements, the Krull dimension is always greater than or equal to zero. This means the length of the longest chain of prime ideals is never negative, and is measured as a number in the set of extended natural numbers (including infinity). The result follows from the fact that the prime spectrum is nonempty and has a well-defined order structure.

label: roth_3ap_theorem_nat
slogan: If a subset of the natural numbers from 1 to n contains no three-term arithmetic progression, then as n gets very large, the proportion of numbers it includes must become arbitrarily small.

label: round
slogan: The round function takes a number from a type that supports arithmetic and ordering, like real or rational numbers, and returns the closest integer to that number, rounding up when the fractional part is 0.5 or more. For integers, it simply returns the same number since they are already whole. It works in any system that has a ring structure, a linear order, and a well-defined floor operation.

label: sbtw_of_sbtw_of_sbtw_of_mem_affineSpan_pair
slogan: If two lines are drawn from vertices of a triangle to points on the opposite sides, and these lines intersect at a point p, then p lies strictly between the vertex and the point on the opposite side for each line.

label: schnirelmannDensity
slogan: The Schnirelmann density of a set of natural numbers is the greatest lower bound of the ratio of the number of elements in the set up to n divided by n, as n runs through all positive integers. It measures how densely the set is distributed among the natural numbers.

label: second_derivative_symmetric
slogan: If a function is differentiable and its derivative is also differentiable at a point, then the second derivative is symmetric: applying it to two vectors in either order gives the same result.

label: separate_convex_open_set
slogan: If a convex open set contains the origin and a point lies outside this set, then there exists a continuous linear functional that maps the point to 1 and maps every point in the set to a value less than 1.

label: setOf
slogan: setOf is a function that takes a property p on elements of a type α and returns the set of all elements in α for which p is true.

label: sierpinskiSpace
slogan: The sierpinskiSpace declaration defines a topology on the two-element set of logical truth values, where the open sets are the empty set, the whole set, and the set containing only true (or 1). This topology is built by generating the smallest collection of open sets that includes the singleton {true} and follows the rules for unions and intersections in a topological space. It gives a simple example of a space that is not discrete but still satisfies the basic axioms of topology.

label: sigNeg
slogan: The function sigNeg computes the largest possible finite dimension of a subspace where a given quadratic form is negative-definite, returning 0 if the space is infinite-dimensional. It is defined for modules over a commutative ring with a linear order, where the form outputs values in an ordered ring. This is similar to counting the maximum number of independent directions in which the quadratic form behaves like a negative sum of squares.

label: similar_of_side_side
slogan: If two triangles have two pairs of sides that are proportional and share a common angle, then the triangles are similar, provided the corresponding sides are non-zero.

label: smoothSheafCommRing
slogan: The smoothSheafCommRing is a structure that assigns to each open set of a manifold M the ring of smooth functions from that open set to a commutative ring R, where R has a compatible smooth structure. These function rings are glued together in a way that respects overlaps between open sets, forming a sheaf of commutative rings over M. It combines the topology of the manifold with smooth, algebraic operations on functions.

label: solvableByRad
slogan: solvableByRad defines the intermediate field of elements in an extension field E over a base field F that can be expressed using radicals. It includes all elements of E that are built from elements of F using field operations and roots. This set forms a subfield of E containing F.

label: solvableByRad.isSolvable
slogan: If an element can be expressed using radicals over a field F, then the Galois group of its minimal polynomial over F is solvable. This means that whenever a number is built from field operations and roots starting from F, the symmetries of its defining polynomial form a solvable group. The result connects solvability by radicals to group-theoretic solvability in field extensions.

label: solvable_of_ker_le_range
slogan: If a group homomorphism f maps from G' to G, and another homomorphism g maps from G to G'', and the kernel of g is contained in the image of f, then the group G is solvable provided both G' and G'' are solvable. This means that solvability of G can be deduced from the solvability of the domain and codomain when the kernel of the second map lies inside the range of the first. The result connects solvability of a group to the structure of homomorphic images and kernels.

label: solvable_of_surjective
slogan: If a group homomorphism maps one group onto another group in a surjective way and the kernel of this map is solvable, then the target group is also solvable. This means that solvability is preserved when taking homomorphic images, as long as the kernel is solvable.

label: solvable_prod
slogan: If two groups are solvable, then the direct product of these groups, formed by pairing their elements and operating componentwise, is also solvable. The solvability of the product group follows directly from the solvability of each individual group.

label: span_gcd
slogan: In a Bezout ring, the set of all multiples of the greatest common divisor of two elements is the same as the set of all linear combinations of those two elements. This means the ideal generated by the gcd of x and y equals the ideal generated by x and y together.

label: span_singleton_inf_span_singleton
slogan: In a principal ideal domain, the set of elements common to the ideals generated by two elements n and m is exactly the ideal generated by their least common multiple. This means an element is divisible by both n and m if and only if it is a multiple of lcm(n, m). The result links ideal intersection with divisibility through the least common multiple.

label: specializationPreorder
slogan: In a topological space, a point x is said to be less than or equal to a point y if every open set containing y also contains x; this relation, which captures the idea that y is in the closure of x, defines a preorder on the space.

label: spectralRadius
slogan: The spectral radius of an element in an algebra over a normed field is the least upper bound of the norms of elements in its spectrum, treated as a value in the extended non-negative real numbers (including zero and infinity). If the spectrum is empty, the spectral radius is zero; if the spectrum is unbounded, the spectral radius is infinity. In Banach algebras, the spectrum is always bounded, so the spectral radius is finite.

label: spectrum
slogan: The spectrum of an element a in an algebra A over a commutative semiring R is the set of scalars r in R such that a minus r (embedded into A) is not invertible. It consists of all r for which the shifted element a - r fails to have a multiplicative inverse in A. This set is the complement of the resolvent set, where the shift would result in an invertible element.

label: spectrum.map_polynomial_aeval_of_degree_pos
slogan: If a polynomial has positive degree and you evaluate it at an element of an algebra over an algebraically closed field, then the spectrum of the resulting element consists exactly of the values you get by evaluating the polynomial at points in the spectrum of the original element. This holds under structure-preserving maps between algebras. The result links polynomial evaluation with spectral mapping in algebraic contexts.

label: spectrum.norm_eq_one_of_unitary
slogan: If u is a unitary element in a complete C*-algebra over a normed field, then every element z in the spectrum of u has norm 1.

label: spinGroup
slogan: The spin group of a quadratic form Q is the set of elements that are in both the pin group of Q and the even part of the Clifford algebra associated with Q, and it forms a submonoid under multiplication. It consists of invertible even-degree elements preserving the structure defined by Q.

label: sq_add_sq_mul_sq_add_sq
slogan: The product of two sums of two squares is itself a sum of two squares, specifically (x1^2 + x2^2)(y1^2 + y2^2) = (x1*y1 - x2*y2)^2 + (x1*y2 + x2*y1)^2, and this holds in any commutative ring.

label: sq_sub_sq
slogan: If two elements a and b in a commutative ring commute, then a squared minus b squared equals the product of a plus b and a minus b. This identity follows from the basic rules of algebra and the fact that multiplication is commutative for the elements involved.

label: squeeze_zero
slogan: If a real-valued function is always between 0 and another function that approaches 0, and both bounds go to 0, then the function in between also approaches 0. This holds in settings where limits are defined by filters, such as in metric or topological spaces. The result is a special case of the squeeze theorem for limits.

label: standardBorel_of_polish
slogan: Every Polish space, when its Borel sets are considered as measurable sets, forms a standard Borel space. This means that the combination of a complete, separable metric topology and its associated Borel sigma-algebra always results in a well-behaved measurable space. As a result, such spaces support robust measure-theoretic constructions used in analysis and probability.

label: star_star
slogan: For any element x in a type equipped with an involutive star operation, applying star twice returns x. This means that star(star(x)) is always equal to x.

label: stdOrthonormalBasis
slogan: For a finite-dimensional inner product space over a real-like field, there is a standard orthonormal basis whose vectors are indexed from 0 to n-1, where n is the dimension of the space. Each vector in this basis has length 1, and any two different vectors are perpendicular to each other. This basis allows every vector in the space to be uniquely expressed as a combination of these basis vectors.

label: stdSimplex.sum_eq_one
slogan: Any point in the standard simplex is a list of non-negative numbers indexed by a finite set, and their sum always equals 1. This holds for values in any semiring with a partial order, as long as the sum is taken over all indices in the finite type. The result follows from the definition of the simplex as the set of such vectors with total sum 1.

label: stdSimplex_fin_two
slogan: The standard simplex on two points consists of all pairs of nonnegative numbers that add up to one, meaning any such pair can be written as (a, 1-a) where a is between 0 and 1. This set is exactly the line segment connecting the points (1,0) and (0,1) in the plane. The result follows by checking that both coordinates satisfy the conditions of being nonnegative and summing to one.

label: stereographic
slogan: The stereographic projection maps points from the unit sphere in a normed vector space E, minus a chosen unit point v, to the orthogonal complement of the line spanned by v, in a way that is continuous and has a continuous inverse on open sets. It provides a one-to-one correspondence between the sphere without v and a flat space of one lower dimension. This mapping preserves topological structure locally around each point in its domain.

label: stereographic'
slogan: stereographic' defines a continuous invertible mapping from an open part of the unit sphere in an (n+1)-dimensional real inner product space to n-dimensional Euclidean space, constructed by projecting from a point on the sphere and then applying a linear isometry to align the result with standard Euclidean coordinates. The mapping and its inverse are both continuous, and the domain and range are open sets. This provides a way to locally represent points on the sphere using ordinary n-dimensional coordinates.

label: stoneCechExtend
slogan: Any continuous function from a topological space to a compact Hausdorff space can be extended in exactly one way to a continuous function from the Stone-Cech compactification of the domain to the same target space, and this extension agrees with the original function on points from the original space.

label: subgroupIsFreeOfIsFree
slogan: A subgroup of a free group is itself a free group. This means that if a group has a basis allowing every element to be uniquely expressed as a product of basis elements and their inverses, then any subgroup of that group also has such a basis. The result follows from structural properties of groups and isomorphisms, using category-theoretic constructions to establish the subgroup's freeness.

label: subgroup_solvable_of_solvable
slogan: If a group is solvable, then every subgroup of that group is also solvable. This means that whenever a group has a chain of normal subgroups with abelian quotients, any smaller subgroup will have the same kind of chain. Solvability is thus inherited by subgroups.

label: sum_four_sq_mul_sum_four_sq
slogan: The product of two sums of four squares is itself a sum of four squares, where each term is a specific combination of products of the original numbers. This identity holds in any commutative ring and matches the way quaternions multiply. The formula shows exactly how to express the product as a sum of four squared terms.

label: sum_range_pow
slogan: The sum of the p-th powers of the first n natural numbers (from 0 to n-1) is equal to a formula involving Bernoulli numbers, binomial coefficients, and powers of n, divided by p+1. Each term in the formula uses a Bernoulli number multiplied by a binomial coefficient and a power of n. This is known as Faulhaber's formula.

label: summable_condensed_iff_of_nonneg
slogan: For a sequence of nonnegative real numbers that decreases as n increases, the sum of the sequence converges if and only if the sum of a condensed version—where each term is 2^k times the value of the original sequence at index 2^k—also converges. This equivalence allows convergence to be tested using the simpler, sparser sum. The result only applies when all terms are nonnegative and the sequence is non-increasing.

label: summable_of_ratio_test_tendsto_lt_one
slogan: If the limit of the ratio of the sizes of consecutive terms in a sequence is less than 1, then the infinite sum of the terms converges. This means that when the terms get smaller quickly enough—specifically, their sizes shrink at a rate similar to a geometric sequence with ratio less than 1—the total sum is finite. The result applies in complete normed spaces where sizes and limits are well-defined.

label: sup_inf_le
slogan: In a lattice, the join (sup) of an element a with the meet (inf) of b and c is less than or equal to the meet of the joins (a with b) and (a with c). This means combining a with the common lower bound of b and c gives a result no greater than the common upper bound of the pairs (a,b) and (a,c). The inequality follows from basic lattice order properties.

label: szemeredi_regularity
slogan: For any finite graph and any small positive number ε, there exists a partition of the graph's vertices into roughly equal-sized groups such that most pairs of groups are ε-uniform (meaning their edge distribution is regular), and the number of groups is bounded by a value depending only on ε and a given minimum number of groups.

label: t1Space_iff_t0Space_and_r0Space
slogan: A topological space is T1 if and only if it is both T0 (any two distinct points can be separated by an open set containing one but not the other) and R0 (if two points are topologically indistinguishable, then they are actually the same point).

label: t2Space_iff_of_isOpenQuotientMap
slogan: A space is Hausdorff if and only if the set of pairs (x, y) where x equals y is closed in the product space, and for an open quotient map, the quotient space is Hausdorff exactly when this diagonal set's preimage is closed in the original space.

label: t2_iff_isClosed_diagonal
slogan: A topological space is Hausdorff if and only if the set of all pairs (x, x) — where both elements are the same — is closed in the product topology. This means that distinct points (x, y) with x != y can be separated by disjoint open sets exactly when the diagonal is a closed subset of the product space.

label: t2_iff_ultrafilter
slogan: A topological space is Hausdorff if and only if any ultrafilter converges to at most one point, meaning that if an ultrafilter converges to two points, then those points must be the same. This captures the idea that in a Hausdorff space, limits of ultrafilters are unique. The condition uses ultrafilters because they provide a strong and maximal notion of convergence.

label: tangentConeAt
slogan: The tangent cone at a point x in a subset s of a topological vector space is the set of all vectors that can be approached as limits of rescaled directions from x to nearby points in s, where the scaling factors go to zero. A vector v is in the tangent cone if there are points in s, getting arbitrarily close to x, such that when you subtract x from them and multiply by larger and larger positive scalars, the result converges to v. This describes the possible directions in which one can move away from x while staying close to the set s.

label: tangentMap
slogan: The tangentMap function takes a smooth map between two manifolds and produces a map between their tangent bundles, transforming tangent vectors at each point by applying the derivative of the original function in local coordinates. If the function isn't differentiable at a point, the derivative acts as zero there. It relies on the structure of normed spaces, charts, and smooth transitions defined by model with corners to ensure consistency.

label: taylorWithin
slogan: The taylorWithin function computes the Taylor polynomial of a function f at a point x0, using derivatives of f taken within a specified set s, up to degree n. It returns this polynomial as an object in a module of polynomials with real coefficients and values in a normed vector space E. The polynomial is built by summing terms of the form ((x - x0)^k / k!) times the k-th derivative of f at x0 in the set s.

label: taylor_isLittleO
slogan: If a function is n times continuously differentiable on a convex set containing a point x0, then near x0 the difference between the function and its nth degree Taylor polynomial is negligible compared to (x - x0)^n as x approaches x0 within that set.

label: taylor_mean_remainder
slogan: If a function f has n+1 continuous derivatives on the interval from x0 to x, and another function g is continuous on that interval and differentiable inside it with nonzero derivative, then the difference between f(x) and its nth-degree Taylor polynomial centered at x0 equals a remainder term involving the (n+1)th derivative of f at some point x' between x0 and x, scaled by a ratio that depends on g and its derivative at x'.

label: taylor_mean_remainder_bound
slogan: If a function f has n+1 continuous derivatives on the interval from a to b, then the difference between f(x) and its nth degree Taylor polynomial centered at a is bounded by C times (x - a)^(n+1) divided by n factorial, where C is a bound on the (n+1)th derivative of f over the interval.

label: taylor_mean_remainder_lagrange
slogan: If a function f is n+1 times continuously differentiable on the closed interval from x0 to x and n+1 times differentiable on the open interval between them, then the difference between f(x) and its nth degree Taylor polynomial centered at x0 is equal to the (n+1)th derivative of f at some point between x0 and x, multiplied by (x - x0)^(n+1) and divided by (n+1)!.

label: taylor_tendsto
slogan: As x approaches x0 within a convex set s, the difference between f(x) and its nth-order Taylor polynomial at x0, divided by (x - x0)^n, tends to 0. This means the Taylor polynomial approximates f near x0 with an error that vanishes faster than (x - x0)^n. The function f must be n-times continuously differentiable on s.

label: tendstoLocallyUniformlyOn_iff_tendstoUniformlyOn_of_compact
slogan: For a compact set, a sequence of functions converges uniformly on that set if and only if it converges locally uniformly on it. This means that when the domain is compact, uniform convergence and locally uniform convergence are the same. The result applies in uniform spaces and links local and global convergence behavior over compact subsets.

label: tendstoLocallyUniformly_iff_forall_isCompact
slogan: A function converges locally uniformly if and only if it converges uniformly on every compact set in the space. This means that for each compact subset, the function values eventually stay uniformly close to the limit function across the whole subset, regardless of the point chosen. The equivalence holds in spaces where every point has a compact neighborhood.

label: tendstoUniformlyOn_tsum
slogan: If a sequence of functions is bounded by a summable sequence of real numbers and converges uniformly on a set, then the sum of the limit function over the index set equals the limit of the sums of the functions in the sequence, with all sums converging in a complete normed abelian group.

label: tendsto_atTop_ciSup
slogan: If a function is increasing and its values don't go above some fixed bound, then as the input grows larger and larger, the function values get arbitrarily close to the smallest number that is still an upper bound for all its values. This limit is exactly the supremum of the set of all function values. The result applies in spaces where such least upper bounds exist for bounded increasing sequences.

label: tendsto_fib_succ_div_fib_atTop
slogan: As n gets very large, the ratio of the (n+1)th Fibonacci number to the nth Fibonacci number gets arbitrarily close to the golden ratio, which is (1 + sqrt(5)) / 2. This means that the sequence of ratios of consecutive Fibonacci numbers converges to that value. The statement uses filters to formalize the idea of convergence at infinity.

label: tendsto_iff_norm_sub_tendsto_zero
slogan: A function approaches a limit in a normed group if and only if the norm of the difference between the function's values and the limit approaches zero. This means convergence is equivalent to the size of the difference shrinking to zero. It connects limits with the behavior of the norm.

label: tendsto_integral_exp_smul_cocompact
slogan: As the frequency parameter grows large in the dual space of a finite-dimensional real vector space, the integral of a function multiplied by a complex exponential tends to zero. This means high-frequency oscillations cause the weighted average of the function to cancel out when integrated against a Haar measure. The result holds for functions taking values in a complex normed space.

label: tendsto_nhds_of_cauchySeq_of_subseq
slogan: If a sequence is Cauchy in a uniform space and some subsequence of it converges to a point, then the whole sequence converges to that same point. Convergence means that eventually all terms of the sequence are arbitrarily close to the limit, as defined by the topology of the space. This result uses the structure of filters and uniform spaces to generalize the idea of limits.

label: tendsto_nhds_unique
slogan: If a function approaches two points in a space where distinct points have disjoint neighborhoods, then those two points must be the same. This means that in such spaces, a function can have at most one limit at a given filter. The result relies on the fact that the space is Hausdorff, ensuring limits are unique when they exist.

label: tendsto_pi_nhds
slogan: A function into a product space converges to a point if and only if each of its coordinate functions converges to the corresponding coordinate of that point. This means convergence in the product topology is determined entirely by convergence in each factor space. The result connects limits in product spaces with limits in individual spaces using neighborhood filters and projections.

label: tendsto_riemannZeta_sub_one_div
slogan: As s approaches 1, the difference between the Riemann zeta function at s and 1/(s-1) approaches the Euler-Mascheroni constant gamma.

label: totallyBounded_convexHull
slogan: If a set in a real normed space can be covered by finitely many small neighborhoods of any given size, then the same is true for the set of all convex combinations of its points. This means forming the convex hull preserves the property of being totally bounded.

label: transcendental_liouvilleNumber
slogan: For any natural number m greater than or equal to 2, the number formed by summing 1 divided by m raised to the power of i factorial for all natural i is transcendental, meaning it cannot be a root of any non-zero polynomial with integer coefficients. This number is known as a Liouville number. The result follows from showing that such numbers can be approximated extremely well by rational numbers, which forces them to be transcendental.

label: trapezoidal_integral
slogan: The trapezoidal_integral function estimates the integral of a real-valued function f from a to b by dividing the interval into N trapezoids and summing their areas, using N+1 equally spaced evaluations of f. It computes this approximation by averaging the function values at the endpoints of each subinterval and multiplying by the width of the subintervals. The result is a numerical approximation of the definite integral based on the trapezoidal rule.

label: triple_product_eq_det
slogan: The triple product of three vectors u, v, and w (computed as u dotted with the cross product of v and w) equals the determinant of the 3x3 matrix formed by using u, v, and w as its rows. This holds for vectors with components in any commutative ring.

label: tsum_geometric_of_lt_one
slogan: If a real number r is greater than or equal to 0 and less than 1, then the infinite sum of r raised to the powers of 0, 1, 2, and so on equals 1 divided by (1 minus r). This sum is interpreted as the limit of partial sums in the real numbers with their usual topology and arithmetic. The result holds because the series converges under the standard definition of infinite sums for real-valued functions.

label: tsum_geometric_two
slogan: The sum of the infinite series (1/2)^0 + (1/2)^1 + (1/2)^2 + ..., where each term is one over two raised to a natural number power, equals 2. This means adding up all these diminishing terms gets arbitrarily close to 2 and does not exceed it. It is a specific case of a geometric series with ratio 1/2, starting from n=0.

label: tsum_mul_tsum_eq_tsum_sum_antidiagonal_of_summable_norm
slogan: If the sums of the absolute values of two sequences converge, then the product of their infinite sums equals the sum of all products of pairs of terms whose indices add up to the same number, summed over all such index pairs.

label: tsum_pow_div_one_sub_eq_tsum_sigma
slogan: For a number r with absolute value less than 1 and any non-negative integer k, the infinite sum over positive integers n of (n^k * r^n) / (1 - r^n) equals the infinite sum over positive integers n of the sum of the k-th powers of the divisors of n times r^n.

label: tsum_sq_fourierCoeff
slogan: For a complex-valued square-integrable function on the circle, the sum of the squared magnitudes of its Fourier coefficients equals the integral of the squared magnitude of the function over the circle, using normalized Haar measure.

label: uniformity
slogan: A uniform space has a filter called uniformity that describes pairs of points which are "close" to each other, and this closeness is used to define uniform properties like continuity and convergence; the filter is defined on the product type α × α, representing pairs of elements from the space.

label: unitInterval
slogan: The unit interval is the set of all real numbers x such that 0 <= x and x <= 1, including both endpoints. It is defined using the closed interval from 0 to 1 on the real number line. This set is built using the standard ordering of real numbers and the predefined values of 0 and 1.

label: unitInterval.sigmoid
slogan: The sigmoid function maps any real number to a value between 0 and 1, inclusive, and this version specifically returns a result within the unit interval [0, 1]. It is based on the standard real-valued sigmoid function, which is always nonnegative and at most 1. The function ensures the output is formally treated as an element of the unit interval.

label: upperBounds
slogan: upperBounds is a function that, given a set s of elements of some type α equipped with a ≤ relation, returns the set of all elements that are greater than or equal to every element in s. In other words, an element x is in upperBounds s if x is at least as large as every element in s according to the ≤ relation.

label: variationOnFromTo
slogan: The variationOnFromTo function calculates the signed total distance traveled by the function f between points a and b, only counting values in the set s, and returns this as a real number. It measures how much f moves along a path restricted to s within the interval from a to b, using the metric space structure of E. The result is always a finite real number, even though the underlying variation might be infinite.

label: volume_iUnion_setOf_liouvilleWith
slogan: The set of real numbers that can be approximated by rational numbers extremely closely, in the sense that for some exponent p greater than 2 the difference between the number and a fraction m/n is less than C/n^p for infinitely many n, has zero length in the usual measure on the real line. In other words, such numbers form a negligible set in terms of Lebesgue measure.

label: volume_setOf_liouville
