slogan: The set of all real numbers that can be approximated extremely closely by rational numbers (called Liouville numbers) takes up no space on the real line, meaning their total length is zero. This is measured using the standard notion of length for sets of real numbers. In other words, almost every real number is not a Liouville number.

label: wellApproximable
slogan: In a seminormed group A, given a sequence of positive distances δ(n), the set wellApproximable A δ consists of all points that are within distance δ(n) of some element of order n for infinitely many n.

label: wellFounded_iff_isEmpty_descending_chain
slogan: A relation is well-founded exactly when there are no infinite descending sequences of elements where each is related to the next; this means the collection of all such infinite descending chains contains no elements at all.

label: wellFounded_iff_principalSeg
slogan: A relation is well-founded if and only if every principal initial segment — the set of elements strictly less than a given element — is well-founded. This means checking for infinite descending chains in the whole relation is equivalent to checking them in each of these smaller segments. The result holds for transitive relations, linking global well-foundedness to local well-foundedness in substructures.

label: zero_add
slogan: For any element a in a type that has an additive identity (zero), adding zero to a results in a. This means 0 + a is always equal to a.

label: zero_pow
slogan: If you raise zero to any positive natural number power in a structure that supports multiplication with a zero element, the result is always zero. This means multiplying zero by itself one or more times always gives zero.

label: zero_pow_eq
slogan: Zero to the power of n equals one if n is zero, and zero otherwise, in any algebraic structure that has both a zero element and a multiplicative identity. This means raising zero to a positive exponent gives zero, while zero to the zero power is defined as one. The result is determined by a simple if-then-else rule based on whether the exponent is zero.

label: zeta_eq_tsum_one_div_nat_cpow
slogan: When the real part of a complex number s is greater than 1, the Riemann zeta function at s equals the infinite sum of 1 divided by n to the power of s, where n runs through all positive integers. This sum converges only when the real part of s is greater than 1. Outside this range, the zeta function is defined differently to extend its domain.

label: zmodMulEquivOfGenerator
slogan: If a group is cyclic and generated by one element, then the integers modulo the group's size can be matched exactly to the group elements so that adding numbers modulo n corresponds to multiplying elements in the group. This matching preserves the group operation and is a perfect one-to-one correspondence. The result is a multiplicative version of the modular integers being structurally identical to the cyclic group.

label: zorn_le
slogan: If every totally ordered subset (chain) in a preordered set has an upper bound, then the set contains a maximal element—a value that is not less than any other comparable element.

label: zorn_le_nonempty_Ici₀
slogan: If every chain (totally ordered subset) above a given element a in a preordered set has an upper bound, then starting from any element x that is greater than or equal to a, there exists a maximal element m such that x is less than or equal to m and no element is strictly greater than m.

label: zpow_add
slogan: For any element a in a group and any integers m and n, a raised to the power of m plus n equals a to the m times a to the n.

label: εNFA
slogan: An εNFA is a machine with a set of states, a transition function that moves between states using alphabet symbols or empty (ε) steps, a starting state, and a set of accepting states; it can have infinitely many states, but to be a proper εNFA, the state type must be finite, as ensured by the Fintype requirement. The transition function allows multiple next states for a given input, including on no input (none), enabling nondeterminism and ε-moves. This structure models automata that recognize regular languages with the added flexibility of silent transitions.

label: εNFA.accepts
slogan: M.accepts is the set of all strings that, when processed by the epsilon nondeterministic finite automaton M, can lead to at least one of the accept states in M's state space. It uses M's transition rules and starting states to evaluate whether a string is accepted. A string is in the language if any path it generates ends in an accept state.

label: εNFA.toNFA_correct
slogan: Converting an epsilon nondeterministic finite automaton (εNFA) to a standard nondeterministic finite automaton (NFA) results in an automaton that accepts the same language. The language accepted by the original εNFA is identical to the language accepted by the converted NFA. This means the transformation preserves correctness with respect to the strings each machine recognizes.

label: εNFA.εClosure
slogan: The εClosure of a set of states in an εNFA is the collection of all states reachable by following zero or more empty (ε) transitions from any state in the set. It includes the original states and any others that can be reached using only ε-moves. This operation is defined for any subset of states in the machine.
